papers.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the Betti numbers of all powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs.

papers.title: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract:
In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $\xi$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $\zeta$ of $p$ such that $
  |\xi-\zeta|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

papers.title: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
papers.abstract: Let $c(\Omega)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $\lambda$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $\Delta u=0$ in $\Omega\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=\lambda$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(\Omega)\ge c(\Omega^*)$, where $\Omega^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $\Omega\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $\lambda\ge\mu/R$, where $\pi R^2=|\Omega|$ and $\mu\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(\Omega)\ge 0.9142\,c(\Omega^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(\Omega)\ge\max\{\sqrt{\theta(\Omega)},\kappa_N\}\,c(\Omega^*)$, where $\theta(\Omega)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $\kappa_N$ is an explicit constant with $\kappa_3\approx0.650$ and $\kappa_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

papers.title: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
papers.authors: Barry Mazur, Karl Rubin, Alexandra Shlapentokh
papers.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

papers.title: NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
papers.authors: Shanghua Zheng, Chenyu Qiu, Xigou Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

papers.title: The Contact Process with Temporary Immunity on $\mathbb{Z}$
papers.authors: Thomas Mountford, Rafael Santos, C\'elio Terra, Maria Eul\'alia Vares
papers.abstract: We develop a regeneration scheme for the one-dimensional contact process with temporary immunity, also known as the spatial SIRS process, a non-attractive interacting particle system. The key ingredient is a one-sided space-time shielding mechanism, constructed from infinite infection paths of an auxiliary process. These paths separate the evolution of the infection front from the configuration and graphical history left behind, allowing us to construct regeneration times without relying on attractiveness. The same shielding mechanism also provides coupling arguments for processes started from different initial configurations. Using this approach, we establish a law of large numbers and a functional central limit theorem for the right edge, existence and uniqueness of an invariant law for the process seen from the edge, and complete convergence. We also prove survival from every nonempty finite infected set for sufficiently large immunity-loss rates and derive an explicit extinction criterion.

papers.title: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
papers.abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $\pi$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

papers.title: Psyquandle Fares
papers.abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

papers.title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
papers.authors: Elizabeth Mili\'cevi\'c, Petra Schwer, Anne Thomas
papers.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.authors: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata
papers.abstract:
In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter.
  As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract:
Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean
  local field $F$ of characteristic zero.
  We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth
  representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by
  $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$.
  These are precisely the trivial representation and the
  irreducible normalized parabolic inductions
  $\one_{n-2}\times\tau$, where $\tau$ is an infinite-dimensional
  irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished
  by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$.
  The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor
  with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.title: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
papers.authors: Yan-Cheng Lv, Gui-Dong Li, Chun-Lei Tang

papers.title: Mean-field Token Steering
papers.authors: Md Zulfiqur Haider, Asmaa Eldesoukey, Abhishek Halder, Yongxin Chen
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schr\"odinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

papers.title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
papers.authors: Aiden Corcoran, Erik Lundberg, Elisabeth Rodriguez
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

papers.title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of ratios of Ferrers and conical functions related to a Riemannian nonlocal eigenvalue problem
papers.authors: \'Arp\'ad Baricz, Manjunatha M. Rudrappa, Sanjeev Singh
papers.abstract: Recently, for a given Riemannian manifold with certain curvature constraints, S. Kaj\'ant\'o and A. Krist\'aly [KK24] formulated a variational problem (on either positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces) and computed the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in terms of the radii, curvature and weight. Moreover, they conjectured that a saturation phenomenon exists also in the case of positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces (not only in the Euclidean case), and this is based entirely on the incompatibility of a system of nonlinear equations involving special functions, like Ferrers functions of the first kind and conical functions of the first kind. In this paper, we provide a partial solution for both positive and negative curvature case.

papers.title: P\'olya inequalities on thin planar networks
papers.abstract: We construct thin planar domains on which the Dirichlet and the Neumann P\'olya inequalities both hold strictly. For the neighborhoods of a given finite connected embedded polygonal graph (branches and cycles are allowed) there is a single radius threshold below which both inequalities hold for every eigenvalue index. We also show that every nonempty bounded connected open set in the plane can be approximated, in measure and in the Hausdorff distance, by smooth simply connected domains satisfying both inequalities. Along the same sequence, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue tends to infinity, while each Neumann eigenvalue of fixed positive index tends to zero. In the special case of rectangular frames our estimates lead to explicit sufficient conditions, with no restriction on the aspect ratio.

papers.title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
papers.authors: Hamidul Ahmed, Mainak Bhowmik, B. Krishna Das, Haripada Sau
papers.abstract:
We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $
u$-Schur functions.
  In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $
u$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data.
  Finally, we introduce $
u$-inner functions - $
u$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $
u$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $
u$-inner functions are dense in the $
u$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

papers.title: Intersection Cuts for Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programs via Decision-Diagram-Free Sets
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel decision-diagram-based framework for generating intersection cuts to strengthen polyhedral relaxations of bounded mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) with general nonlinear constraints. Building on decision diagrams (DDs) that provide outer approximations of MINLP feasible regions, we propose the concept of DD-free sets, which are convex regions whose interiors do not intersect the sets represented by the DDs. By exploiting the underlying graphical structure, we develop efficient methods for constructing these regions without requiring restrictive assumptions on the functional form of nonlinear constraints or access to distance oracles. We investigate the maximality properties of DD-free sets and devise algorithms for obtaining maximal forbidden regions within several structured classes. The resulting intersection cuts exploit geometric information retained in DD representations, enabling further strengthening of relaxations beyond what can be achieved through conventional DD-based convexification. We also introduce interval DDs to facilitate the representation of general nonlinear constraints and establish convergence results for intersections of constraint-specific DDs, providing a theoretical foundation for their integration into global optimization frameworks. Computational experiments on challenging open instances from MINLPLib, encompassing a broad range of nonlinear and nonconvex structures, demonstrate that the proposed approach can substantially improve dual bounds and achieve greater optimality-gap closure than state-of-the-art global optimization solvers. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting graphical representations of infeasible regions to develop stronger cutting planes for general MINLPs.

papers.title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
papers.abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

papers.title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
papers.authors: Aymeric Baradat, Jean-David Benamou, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Vialard
papers.abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $\rho_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_t\rho=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2\rho)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/\rho$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $\Gamma$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,\xi)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

papers.title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: For an irreducible parabolic flat vector bundle of rank $r < 2\sqrt{g}$ on a genus $g$ curve, we prove that an analytically general isomonodromic deformation is stable. This refines Landesman-Litt's semistability result for bundles of rank $< 2\sqrt{g+1}$. The proof applies the non-generically globally generated (non-GGG) lemma to establish infinitesimal obstructions to extending destabilizing subbundles of semistable bundles.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness for One-Dimensional Quantile-Dependent SDEs with H\"older-Continuous Diffusion
papers.abstract:
We establish strong well-posedness for one-dimensional stochastic differential equations whose drift and diffusion coefficients depend on a prescribed quantile of the solution's marginal law. The diffusion coefficient is uniformly non-degenerate and H\"older continuous in space. The drift is the sum of a non-increasing H\"older-continuous component and a globally Lipschitz component of at most linear growth. Both components are Lipschitz continuous in the quantile variable. The main obstacles are the limited spatial regularity of the diffusion and the quantitative control of quantiles in terms of the $L^1$-distance between densities.
  We freeze the quantile path and combine uniform H\"older estimates for the resulting densities with a cancellation argument for the second-order diffusion perturbation. This yields an $L^1$-stability estimate for the frozen density flows and, together with uniform tail bounds and positive lower density bounds, a Volterra-type estimate for the frozen quantile map. An exponentially weighted supremum norm makes this map a strict contraction on $[0,T]$, giving a unique self-consistent quantile path and hence a unique strong solution. When the diffusion coefficient is independent of the quantile variable, the Yamada--Watanabe approximation also yields stability with respect to the initial condition.

papers.title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
papers.abstract: A (finite or infinite) connected graph is called \textit{cactus-like} if every pair of distinct maximal cliques has at most one vertex in common and its clique graph is a tree. Equivalently, a cactus-like graph is a block graph whose clique graph is a tree. We prove that a finite connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is cactus-like if and only if its quadratic embedding constant satisfies $\mathrm{QEC}(G)<-1/2$. Moreover, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{QEC}(G)$ in terms of the clique degree of a block graph $G$. For the proofs, we develop a method for constructing a conditionally negative definite kernel on a block graph by concatenating local kernels along geodesics in the block graph. Concrete examples include free products of complete graphs and trees.

papers.title: Sum of Powers with Matrix Coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We consider polynomial maps with constants $\omega(x,y)=A_1x^k+A_2y^k$ on $M_n(F)$, where $A_1$ is invertible and $k\geq2$. We show that the necessary condition for surjectivity obtained by Saini and Singh (Polynomial maps with constants on matrix algebra, Linear Algebra Appl. 752 (2027), 256-277) is not sufficient in any dimension $n\geq6$. We also completely characterize surjectivity for $n=5$ and $6$.

papers.title: Fundamental group and $Q$-curvature on open four-manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete, connected, and non-compact four-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and nonnegative $Q$-curvature. If $g$ is not Ricci-flat, we show that both the fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ and the integral of $Q$-curvature are finite, satisfying $$|\pi_1(M)|\int_MQ_g d\mu_g\leq 8\pi^2$$ with the equality holding if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^4, e^{2u}|\mathrm{d}x|^2)$ with vanishing isoperimetric ratio.

papers.title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
papers.authors: Yajun Wang, Eric T. Chung, Lijian Jiang
papers.abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(\eta\), while a small material eigenvalue \(\epsilon\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $\epsilon+ \eta^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

papers.title: Global dynamics and the diffusive limit of the one-species non-cutoff Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system
papers.authors: Shuangqian Liu, Yuan Xu, Fujun Zhou
papers.abstract: The rigorous derivation of incompressible plasma equations from kinetic plasma models is a fundamental problem in kinetic theory. For the one-species Vlasov--Maxwell--Boltzmann system without angular cutoff, global well-posedness and the diffusive limit have remained largely open in the soft-potential regime. We resolve both problems for $0<s<1$ and $\max\{-3,-\frac32-2s\}<\gamma<-2s$. For sufficiently small initial perturbations, we construct unique global classical solutions with energy and time-decay estimates uniform in the Knudsen number $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$. The key analytical contribution is a family of coercivity and trilinear estimates for the non-cutoff collision operators with time-dependent quadratic exponential velocity weights. Exploiting conservation of energy in collisions, these estimates combine with weighted interpolation to control the high-order electromagnetic terms despite the slow decay of the electric field. For well-prepared initial data, we prove strong convergence to the incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier--Maxwell system as $\varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
papers.abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

papers.title: On the Power-Law Duality in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: In this work we first revisit the Hooke-Newton duality and its generalisation to arbitrary power laws in classical and quantum mechanics. We then consider Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics on the real line, which is a deformation of standard Heisenberg-Schr\"odinger quantum mechanics closely related to Dunkl's differential-difference operator formalism. We consider the corresponding eigenvalue problem for the harmonic potential and a Coulomb-like potential. We observe that the Hooke-Newton duality is also applicable to these deformed quantum systems allowing us to solve the eigenvalue problem of one by mapping it onto the other system. This approach is then generalised to arbitrary power-law potentials in Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics. Whereas in standard quantum mechanics the classical re-scaling of angular momenta has to be applied to Langer-modified quantum angular momenta, Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics requires a rescaling of deformation parameters similar to the Langer-type modification but involving the reflection operator. The energy coupling-constant exchange, however, remains the same in all three cases, classical mechanics, quantum mechanics and Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Classification problems for diassociative and dendriform algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: Diassociative algebras (associative dialgebras) and dendriform algebras are vector spaces with two binary operations, introduced by J.-L. Loday in the study of Leibniz algebras; their operads are Koszul dual to each other. We survey the classification problem for these two classes, including the Zinbiel algebras, the commutative dendriform algebras, which are Koszul dual to Leibniz algebras. We recall the definitions, the main examples and the Loday diagram with its extension by left-symmetric algebras and dialgebras, and describe the methods used to classify algebras of small dimension: direct computation from lists of associative algebras, annihilator (central) extensions and geometric classification by degenerations. We then collect, by dimension, the known algebraic classifications of diassociative algebras, dendriform algebras and their commutative case, the Zinbiel algebras, point out lists that later work corrected, and summarise the cohomological results that the methods rely on. We close with a list of open problems.

papers.title: Many faces of integer semidefinite programming
papers.abstract: We first establish several properties of integer positive semidefinite matrices, extending known results for binary and ternary positive semidefinite matrices. We then show how to reformulate an integer quadratic program (IQP) as an equivalent integer semidefinite program (ISDP). We distinguish three cases, namely IQPs with two, three, or more than three distinct integer values, and provide several ISDPs for each case. Each reformulation yields either a binary ISDP, a ternary ISDP, or a rescaled version of one of these. The results show that ternary SDP formulations for problems with three distinct integer values provide SDP relaxations with fewer constraints and, in the case of equally spaced integers, also smaller matrix variables than binary-based SDP relaxations. For quadratic problems whose variables can take more than three distinct integer values, one can choose among three formulations based on the size of their matrix variables, the number of constraints, and the strength of the resulting SDP relaxations. We also show how to reformulate a mixed-integer QP as a mixed-integer SDP.

papers.title: Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
papers.abstract: For every claw-free $C_4$-free planar graph, we prove the sharp weighted bound $\alpha_w(G)\ge (10/31)\sum_v w(v)$, equivalently $\chi_f(G)\le31/10$. The proof uses a line-graph representation and the matching polytope; the exceptional small roots are excluded analytically by planar duality and degree-four neighborhood analysis in triangulations. We also prove that, in every $2$-connected $C_4$-free graph of minimum degree at least four, an independent selection of claw centers leaves a compatible subgraph of noncenters with fractional chromatic number at most three; planarity is not required. We apply these results to the conjecture $\alpha(G)\ge5|V(G)|/16$. A minimum-order counterexample without degree-three vertices has at least forty-nine vertices. When all degree-three components of a minimum counterexample are triangle trees, we derive exact boundary states and a joint matching formula. We identify the remaining deficiency estimate and the additional component types that must be addressed to extend this approach. The general conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

papers.title: Half-factorial generating sets and the realization of Dedekind class groups
papers.abstract: We prove a cardinality obstruction to realizing an abelian group as the ideal class group of a half-factorial Dedekind domain. If an abelian $p$-group $P$ satisfies $\bigcap_{r\ge1}p^rP=0$ and admits a half-factorial generating subset, then $|P|\le\max\{\aleph_0,|P/pP|\}$. The proof separates generators of equal order by finite quotients. Its group-theoretic ingredient is a direct summand generated by selected members of an arbitrary finite generating set. The torsion subgroup of $\prod_{j\ge1}\mathbb{Z}/p^j\mathbb{Z}$ is uncountable and $p$-adically separated, but has countable quotient modulo $p$; hence it has no half-factorial generating subset. This gives a negative answer to the universal half-factorial Dedekind realization problem for every prime. Pure subgroups give counterexamples of every uncountable cardinality at most the continuum, so the least cardinality of a counterexample is $\aleph_1$. We also study free-kernel lifting, order-preserving lifts across torsion kernels, character-compatible generators, and the failure of compatibility under unions and contraction. These results distinguish global realizability from half-factoriality on bounded subgroups and from integrality of cross numbers.

papers.title: Lipschitz bounds and gradient continuity for the Trudinger equation
papers.authors: Verena B\"{o}gelein, Frank Duzaar, Ugo Gianazza, Naian Liao, Christoph Scheven
papers.abstract: We establish local spatial Lipschitz and gradient H\"older estimates for general nonnegative weak solutions to Trudinger's equation $\partial_t u^{p-1}=\Delta_pu$, $p>1$. The estimates are uniform across the zero set. The proofs combine Bernstein-type estimates for power transformations, smooth approximation, and comparison with exponential barriers near the zero set.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

papers.title: Entropy-Based and Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics for Informed Dynamic Scheduling of Belief-Propagation Decoding for LDPC Codes
papers.authors: Tofar Chih-Yuan Chang, Chia-En Liu, Ying-Ren Jian, Di-Chun Liang
papers.abstract: We propose two enhanced conditional innovation (CI) metrics for informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) in belief-propagation (BP) decoding of LDPC codes. The CI-based residual BP (CIRBP) algorithm uses the CI metric to guide the selection of the variable node (VN) to be updated and has been shown to outperform several existing IDS-based BP decoders, especially at the early decoding stage. However, the original CI metric uses only the absolute difference between the current and precomputed posterior probabilities and does not separately account for the reliability associated with each probability. By reformulating the CI metric relative to the decision boundary, we separate each posterior probability into its decision side and a linear-distance term reflecting reliability. Replacing the latter with the binary entropy complement yields the proposed entropy-based CI (E-CI) metric. Moreover, the proposed quadratic CI (Q-CI) metric is derived from the leading quadratic term in the local expansion of the entropy complement, avoiding the logarithmic operations required for direct E-CI evaluation. We apply both proposed metrics to the CIRBP decoder and its node-wise variant. Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally provide lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with their relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.

papers.title: DLR variational principle for the one-dimensional log-gas and another proof of existence of Sine-beta
papers.abstract:
We show that every stationary solution of the Dobrushin--Lanford--Ruelle (DLR) equations for the one-dimensional log-gas with a quantitative control on its number variance minimizes the free energy functional. This yields a DLR variational principle for this continuous long-range system.
  Moreover, we show that any limit point of the finite-volume log-gases is stationary and satisfies this condition. This allows us to give a new, physical proof of the existence of a microscopic limit for the Gaussian Beta Ensembles, known as the Sine-beta point process.

papers.title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Tur\'an numbers and beyond
papers.authors: Wenchong Chen, Gennian Ge, Yang Shu
papers.abstract: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$. To deduce further bounds, we establish a transfer argument from upper bounds on the sizes of sufficiently general-positioned subsets of high-dimensional integer grids to lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. Two methodologies are adopted to derive the former: one connects rainbow Tur\'an theory and general-positioned grid sets, and the other uses full spark linear reduction of tuples with bounded-size preimages. As a combinatorial ingredient, we describe the rainbow Tur\'an behavior under suspension operations, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract:
We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other.
  For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

papers.title: Repairing actuator schedules under graph constraints
papers.abstract: We consider a discrete-time linear system in which each actuator is assigned to one time slot. A graph $H$ records which pairs of actuators cannot share a slot. We seek to remove conflicts by exchanging actuators between slots, while preserving all tail reachability spaces. These spaces describe the terminal corrections available from each time slot onward. We give a sufficient condition based on the number of exchanges that preserve the required bases. The condition guarantees repair from every compatible starting schedule. Two bounds for checking it use failed basis tests and dependent column selections. Each accepted exchange reduces the conflict count, so the procedure uses at most as many exchanges as there are initial conflicts. An explicit family with unequal rank increments admits repair when $3N>4\Delta(H)+4$, where $\Delta(H)$ is the largest number of forbidden partners of any actuator. We also give a family of two-slot examples with only one forbidden partner per actuator and two initial conflicts. The basis constraints force every strict improvement to move arbitrarily many actuators, although one exchange suffices without those constraints. A second example has a connected conflict graph and one initial conflict.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
papers.authors: Haiyun He, Yepeng Liu, Zhuoer Shen, Ziqiao Wang, Yongyi Mao, Yuheng Bu
papers.abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

papers.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
papers.abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $\pi_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.

papers.title: The Common-Color Spectrum of Endpoint Set-Coloring Ramsey Numbers
papers.authors: Guantao Chen, Qiong Fan, Chunxiang Wang
papers.abstract:
The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to each edge of $K_N$ contains a $K_n$ whose edge labels have at least $t$ common colors. Motivated by the work of Erd\H{o}s and Szemer\'edi on $R(n;r,r-1,1)$, we write $R(n;r,r-1,t)=\exp\bigl(nf_{r,n}(t)\bigr)$ and study $f(t):=f_{r,n}(t)$ as $t$ ranges from $1$ to $r-1$.
  For fixed integers $r\ge2$ and $1\le t<r$, we prove that, as $n\to\infty$, \(
  \frac12\log\frac{r}{r-t}+o(1)
  \le f(t)
  \le \frac{r}{r-t}\log\frac{r}{r-t}
  +C+O_{r,t}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \) where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. Comparisons between different numbers of colors show that the rates $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$, defined for fixed $r$ and $t$, each have a limit as $r\to\infty$ and $\frac{t}{r}\to\alpha\in(0,1)$ from above. The resulting two functions of $\alpha$ are finite, positive, nondecreasing, and right-continuous. Writing $\Delta_t=f(t+1)-f(t)$, we further prove that, as $r\to\infty$, uniformly for $n\ge r^2$, at least $\frac{(1-o(1))\log r}{\log\log r}$ indices $1\le t<\frac{r}{2}$ satisfy $\Delta_t\ge\frac{1-o(1)}{2r}$. For $r,n\ge3$ and $2\le h\le r-1$, the final $h-1$ increments account for at least $1-\frac{1}{\left\lceil h/2\right\rceil}$ of the total increase $f(r-1)-f(1)$. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the last increment has a positive lower limit as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, for $r,n\ge3$, it exceeds the sum of all preceding increments whenever $r$ is even or $n=3$.

papers.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Positive Bounded Solutions for Semilinear Dirichlet Problems in Exterior-Star Domains
papers.abstract: We prove the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive bounded solutions for the Dirichlet problem $$-\Delta u=f(u)\,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \Omega, \ \ u=0\,\ \ \text{on}\ \ \partial\Omega,$$ where $f$ is a positive reaction and $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a uniformly $C^{2,\gamma}$ domain with a star-shaped complement. Our uniqueness result gives a positive answer to Open Question 1 of [H. Berestycki and C. Graham, ARMA, 2026].

papers.title: An ancient diophantine problem of Brahmagupta
papers.abstract: In the seventh century CE, Brahmagupta gave a parametric solution to the problem of finding two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x+y, x-y$ and $xy+1$ are all squares. We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. The complete solution of the problem still remains elusive.

papers.title: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
papers.abstract: We study the \emph{structural dimension} of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
papers.authors: Fei Wen, Kai Wang, Tao Wang
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$. In this paper, we show that for fixed integers $n\ge \big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil$ and $k\geq0$, if $G$ is a $k$-cyclic graph of order $n$, then \begin{equation*} \displaystyle m_{G}(1)\leq n-\big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil \end{equation*} and moreover, we completely characterize all extremal graphs attained the upper bound.

papers.title: On divisible domains of the flat affine space with parallel volume
papers.authors: Farid Diaf, Blandine Galiay, Malek Hanounah
papers.abstract: We consider a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ divisible by a discrete subgroup $\Gamma$ of the unimodular affine group $\operatorname{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^d$ if $\Gamma$ is virtually solvable or if its linear holonomy is virtually contained in a semisimple Lie subgroup of real rank one. In particular, we establish the Kleinian Markus conjecture in both cases.

papers.title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
papers.authors: Anastasios Fragkos, Ben Krause, Michael Lacey, Nazar Miheisi, Yu-Chen Sun

papers.title: Global Hyperbolicity Criterion for Regular Sub-Lorentzian Manifolds
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global hyperbolicity of regular sub-Lorentzian manifolds. We establish a criterion for global hyperbolicity on complete Riemannian manifolds, formulated in terms of a smooth time function and an admissible growth function. The proof relies on the theory of differential inclusions. The proposed condition relaxes the classical requirements on the differential of the time function. The effectiveness of the obtained criterion is illustrated on classical nonholonomic structures: the Grushin space, the Heisenberg group, and step-2 Carnot groups, for which we find explicit asymptotic bounds on the expansion rate of causal cones that guarantee the preservation of global hyperbolicity.

papers.title: Weak--type $(1,1;\frac{1}{2})$--estimate for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index
papers.abstract: We prove the weak-type estimate at the end-point $\big(1,1,\frac{1}{2}\big)$ for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index $\alpha_c=n-\frac{1}{2}$ in all dimensions $n\geq 1$. Our proof is motivated by Christ's method for the linear Bochner--Riesz operator at the critical index. We develop a bilinear analogue of the $TT^*$ method to address the end-point boundedness of the bilinear Bochner--Riesz operator. This approach provides a useful tool in addressing the end-point issues for bilinear operators.

papers.title: On the nodal set of the second eigenfunction of the Laplacian in convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$. We prove that the closure of the interior nodal set of any second Dirichlet eigenfunction of $\Omega$ intersects $\partial\Omega$. The proof combines the ground-state derivative and the quantitative log-concavity estimate of Andrews and Clutterbuck with a variational argument.

papers.title: Motivic Borel-Moore Homology is Borel-Moore Motivic Homology
papers.abstract: This paper studies the higher Chow groups of arbitrary finite type separated schemes using motivic homotopy theory, serving as a Borel-Moore counterpart to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology of Bachmann-Elmanto-Morrow. We construct a filtration on the G-theory spectrum of a finite type separated scheme $X$, inducing an Atiyah-Hirzebruch style spectral sequence whose associated graded pieces are a complex computing the higher Chow groups of $X$. We prove that this complex is representable in the stable motivic homotopy category, and is a module over the $\mathbb{A}^1$-motivic complex, giving rise to an action of $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology on the Bloch-Levine cycle complex. This generalizes some results of Bloch and Levine relating higher Chow groups and motivic cohomology to the case of schemes over an arbitrary base, and which need not be smooth or equidimensional.

papers.title: Nonparametric Classification under Adversarial Attacks: Decision-Boundary Geometry and Optimal Rates
papers.authors: Yanhang Zhang, Jingfu Peng, Yuhong Yang
papers.abstract: Unlike in continuous regression, a small input perturbation in classification can move an input across a decision boundary and flip the predicted label. Decision-boundary geometry is therefore essential to understanding adversarial classification risk. Under anisotropic smoothness and margin conditions, we quantify this geometric contribution and establish sharp minimax rates for adversarial excess risk relative to the ordinary Bayes risk. These rates comprise a statistical term governed by the harmonic mean smoothness and a geometric cost of adversarial perturbations governed by the least smooth direction. As smoothness and the margin exponent vary, the adversarial term exhibits a phase transition from a fractional power of the attack radius to linear scaling, with a logarithmic correction in a critical regime. In addition, we construct an adaptive classifier that attains these rates over a range of smoothness and margin classes. We further characterize the minimax rate for adversarial excess risk under a budget on ordinary excess risk, yielding an explicit trade-off curve. The curve identifies attack regimes where ordinary minimax optimality entails a suboptimal adversarial rate. Finally, numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

papers.title: A Kreiss theorem for fractional Cauchy problems with a finite slow component
papers.authors: Vladimir R. Kosti\'c, Jo\~ao Pedro Mangi, Ilja Uzelac Buji\v{s}i\'c
papers.abstract: Fractional Cauchy problems with a Caputo derivative of order bounded by one are solved by Mittag-Leffler operator families that lack the semigroup property but remain bounded for classes of sectorial generators, even with spectrum in the right half-plane. To study their transient growth we introduce the fractional Kreiss constant via the Laplace transform of the propagator family. For a closed generator on a Banach space with a time-scale separation and a finite spectral component, that is, a finite-rank projector commuting with the generator whose complement carries a bounded family, we prove that the projected part of the propagator (typically slow spectral part carrying dynamics that is pertinent at mid and long time-scales) is comparable to a deflated Kreiss constant up to a factor linear in the rank, uniformly in fractional order and independently of the dimension. The analytic core of this result is a Bernstein-type inequality for a class of non-rational functions on vertical lines proved by bounding the turning of the derivative. This is a fundamentally different technique from the classical one used in Kreiss theorem for Markov semigroups based on counting intersections of algebraic curves. Importantly, we show that the rank dependence cannot be removed while keeping the Kreiss constant upper bound. Finally, we show that in Hilbert spaces, generators whose numerical range avoids the sector of instability obey the sharp bound of normal operators, which no spectral-set estimate improves. To conclude, we discuss how subdiffusion driven by a self-excited oscillator, the time-fractional Schr\"odinger equation, and time-changed Markov dynamics illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
papers.abstract:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$. Let $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{F})$ denote the size of a smallest subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $N^2[D]$ intersects the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G - N^2[G]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). For $k \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{E}_k$ denote the set of connected graphs that have at least $k$ edges (and at least one vertex if $k = 0$). By a well-known result of Meir and Moon, $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_0) \leq n/3$ if $n \geq 3$. We show that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_1) \leq n/4$ if $n 
eq 2$, $n 
eq 3$ and $G$ is not a $7$-cycle. Hua and Liu recently showed that if $G$ is not a $4$-vertex path or a $4$-cycle or a $9$-cycle, then there exists a subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $|D| \leq n/5$ and each component of $G-N^2[D]$ has a universal vertex. We strengthen this result by showing that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_2) \leq n/5$ if $n 
eq 3$, $n 
eq 4$ and $G$ is not an $8$-cycle or one of five $9$-vertex graphs. It follows that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_3) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph or a $9$-cycle. This also implies the result of Hua and Liu, and that if $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of cycles, then $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{C}) \leq n/5$ unless $G$ is a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph containing a cycle. All these bounds are sharp.

papers.title: Singular Birth-Death model
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a one-dimensional singular birth-death model constructed from It\^o's Brownian excursion measure. In this model, particles are born at the origin at infinite rate, evolve as Brownian excursions away from the origin, and are killed upon returning to the origin. Although the number of particles alive at any fixed deterministic time is almost surely finite, we prove that the set of exceptional times at which infinitely many particles are alive is almost surely dense and has Hausdorff dimension $1/2$. We further investigate the spatial structure of the particle system at such exceptional times. In particular, we identify the critical near-origin profile of the infinite particle cloud, which is governed by a scale of order $\log\log(1/|x|)^{-1}$ as $x\downarrow0$. Finally, we establish laws of large numbers and central limit theorems for two natural observables of the system: the $\alpha$-power sum of the positions of all alive particles and the top particle position.

papers.title: Local limit theorem for branching processes with immigration
papers.authors: Sadillo Sharipov, Alexander Tarasov, Vitali Wachtel
papers.abstract: Let $\{Y_{n}, n\geq 0\}$ be a critical branching process with immigration. Under the minimal moment restrictions, namely, assuming finite variance for the number of particles of the offspring and finite mean for the number of immigrating particles, we obtain a local limit theorem for the process $\{Y_{n}\}$.

papers.title: On complemented skew braces
papers.authors: Yangming Li, P. P\'erez-Altarriba, L. A. Kudrachenko, A. Ballester-Bolinches
papers.abstract: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

papers.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
papers.abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

papers.title: Bumpless pipe dreams for involutions and shifted plane partitions
papers.authors: Eric Marberg, Alejandro H. Morales, Tianyi Yu
papers.abstract: This article studies a triangular variant of bumpless pipe dreams for involutions in the symmetric group. We prove that a natural weight generating function for these objects recovers all involution Schubert polynomials. For vexillary involutions, we derive a $K$-theoretic extension of this result that gives a new formula for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. In the course of showing this formula, we compute a diagonal term order Gr\"obner basis for the defining ideals of symmetric matrix Schubert varieties associated to vexillary involutions. As applications, we prove a conjectured product formula for principal specializations of involution Schubert polynomials. We go on to derive a shifted analogue of the Fomin--Kirillov formula counting bounded plane partitions. This analogue proves the straight-shape case of a conjecture of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova on the Ehrhart positivity for the order polytopes of shifted partitions. We also conjecture a bumpless pipe dream formula for involution Grothendieck polynomials and discuss connections with diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices and asymptotics of principal specializations.

papers.title: A generic $p$-Wasserstein space is isometrically rigid
papers.authors: Zolt\'an M. Balogh, Eric Str\"oher, Tam\'as Titkos, D\'aniel Virosztek
papers.abstract: We prove for any parameter $p \geq 1$ that the $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ of a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X)$ is isometrically rigid, that is, its isometries are precisely the push-forwards of the isometries of $(X,d_X).$ We also study the question whether the isometry class of a $p$-Wasserstein space completely determines the isometry class of the underlying space. We prove for any $p\geq 1$ that for a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X),$ its $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ is isometric to another $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(Y,d_Y)$ if and only if $(Y,d_Y)$ is isometric to $(X,d_X).$ En route we prove that a stronger property, which we call the Dirac preservation property, is also generic.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton
papers.abstract: This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.

papers.title: Markov potential priors for prediction in Gamma models
papers.abstract: We consider Bayesian prediction in independent Gamma scale models with arbitrary known positive shape parameters. When the dimension is at least three, we construct a shrinkage prior toward any prespecified positive scale vector. The resulting predictive density strictly dominates the Jeffreys predictive density under Kullback--Leibler loss and is minimax. The prior is obtained by weighting the Jeffreys prior with a Markov potential. The transition is determined by the beta--gamma decomposition. The domination result is nonasymptotic.

papers.title: On VMO-Type Characterizations of Ball Banach Sobolev Spaces and Independence of Integrable Index of Special John--Nirenberg--Campanato Spaces
papers.authors: Zhexu Bai, Hao Peng, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
papers.abstract: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, $X$ be a ball Banach function space, and $W^{k,X}$ denote the corresponding ball Banach Sobolev space. In this article, we solve six questions in [Math. Z. 311 (2025)]. Specifically, we first prove that the constants in its VMO-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ are sharp uniformly over all ball Banach function spaces satisfying suitable assumptions. Next, we show that the BBM-type formula and the BSVY-type formula involving minimizing polynomials or ball averages fail in general. In contrast, we establish higher-order BBM-type formulas involving Taylor polynomials and further obtain a Taylor-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ under suitable assumptions. Moreover, we construct counterexamples to show that the characterization of $W^{k,X}$ via higher-order minimizing polynomials fails in general. Finally, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for special John--Nirenberg--Campanato spaces defined via congruent cubes to be independent of their integrability exponent $q$.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

papers.title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
papers.abstract:
Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\),
  \[S_n(t)=\Omega_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.

papers.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Stationary Convective Brinkman--Forchheimer Extended Darcy Equations with a Nonlinear Slip Boundary Condition of Friction Type
papers.authors: Wasim Akram, Weimin Han, Manil T. Mohan
papers.abstract: This work develops and analyzes several discontinuous Galerkin methods for a variational inequality associated with the stationary convective Brinkman--Forchheimer extended Darcy (CBFeD) system. The CBFeD model generalizes the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations by incorporating additional damping and pumping terms. The resulting variational inequality characterizes the motion of a viscous, incompressible fluid in a saturated porous medium under a friction-type slip boundary condition. For the CBFeD variational inequality, we first explore the existence of a unique weak solution. Then, we establish the existence, uniqueness, and stability of the numerical solutions obtained using discontinuous Galerkin methods. Optimal error estimates are derived, measured in the broken $H^1$-norm for the velocity and in the $L^2$-norm for the pressure, when linear velocity elements and piecewise constant pressure approximations are employed. Numerical simulations are carried out to confirm the theoretically predicted convergence orders and to highlight key strengths of the method, including its ability to capture discontinuities, effectively resolve shear layers, handle advection-dominated regimes, and operate robustly on general polygonal meshes.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for L\'evy operators on nilpotent and compact Lie groups
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a left-invariant L\'evy operator, with characteristics $(a,b,\mu)$, on a connected
  and simply connected Lie group $G$ that is either compact or nilpotent with $[G,[G,G]]$ relatively
  compact (equivalently, of step at most two). We prove that every bounded distributional solution of $\mathcal{L}u=0$ is right-invariant under
  the closed subgroup $P=\overline{\langle\exp\mathfrak h_0\cup\text{supp}\mu\rangle}$, where
  $\mathfrak h_0=\text{Lie}\langle b,\operatorname{ran}(a)\rangle$, and is constant if and only if $P=G$. In the
  compact case we give three proofs, one through the It\^o--Kawada equidistribution theorem, one by
  propagation of the maximum and one by an application of the Peter-Weyl theorem, while the nilpotent case rests on the Choquet--Deny theorem of B\'enard and Frisch.

papers.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
papers.abstract: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

papers.title: On Block-Primitive Combinatorial Designs
papers.abstract:
We settle a long-standing problem by proving that every block-primitive combinatorial design is point-primitive. Since block-primitivity and point-primitivity coincide for symmetric designs by duality, it remains to treat the non-symmetric $2$-designs. For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic.
  The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. The other is the dihedral block stabilizer $D_{2(q-1)}$, where the block is a union of $a$ of the $q/2$ orbits, so that $v=q(q-1)/2$, $k=a(q-1)$ and $\lambda=2a(aq-a-1)/(q-2)$, the last an integer exactly when $(q-2)/2$ divides $a(a-1)$; this family is exhausted by finite enumeration except at the degrees beyond its range.
  We then determine which of these designs have strength $t\geq 3$. Apart from the inversive planes and the five Witt designs, exactly two Steiner families arise, attached to the exceptional maximal subgroups of $PGL_2(q)$. There is no non-complete design of strength $t\geq 6$.
