Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

papers.title: High-energy asymptotics for the spectral actions of free particles in thermal equilibrium
papers.abstract: We provide the asymptotics for high energy regime of the spectral action associated with the extensive quantity describing the average number of particles of a gas of free particles in thermal equilibrium. We analyse the case of massless particles (the massive non relativistic case being easier and well known) living in a finite volume manifold of arbitrary dimension, and subjected to periodic boundary conditions (i.e. the d-dimensional torus), obeying Bose, Fermi and Boltzmann statistics. We also treat in full generality the case of relativistic massive particles, which is more difficult and presents the appearance of a logarithmic term when the dimension of the underlying manifold is odd. The situation relative to massless and relativistic massive particles living on the 3-sphere is also studied, showing that, even in this case the asymptotics relative to the massive relativistic particles presents an analogous logarithmic term.

papers.title: Associahedra are 8-colourable
papers.abstract: Determining the chromatic number of associahedra is a long-standing open problem. Tan [arXiv:2611.05323] recently proved that associahedra are 12-colourable, which is the first constant upper bound. This paper adapts Tan's argument to show that associahedra are 8-colourable.

papers.title: Minimal time of null-controllability of the multi-dimensional singular Grushin equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the null-controllability of the multi-dimensional Grushin equation with an inverse-square potential on cylinders. In the critically degenerate case, we compute the minimal time of null-controllability from vertical strips, obtaining an explicit formula depending on the distance of the strip to the singular set and on the strength of the singular potential. To do so, after a Fourier and spherical harmonic decomposition of our control system, we use the moments method for radial problems to construct controls on annuli. For this purpose, we prove a uniform spectral gap and uniform localization estimates for the eigenfunctions of the infinite family of radial operators that arise. We then reduce the control zone using spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method. In the weakly degenerate case, we prove null-controllability in arbitrarily small time from any open set. This is done using the transmutation method and quantitative observability estimates for radial waves, which yield a cost of null-controllability from annuli for the Fourier components of our system that is uniform with respect to the frequency. We conclude again with spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method.

papers.title: Spectral coincidence and generalized Hua inversion in rings and Banach algebras
papers.abstract: For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inverses with Harte-quasinilpotent remainders, without Noetherianity. This gives input-core coincidence under intertwining. If the central subring is Noetherian, every Harte-quasinilpotent element also has separated left and right powers. For common-core data in the finite-central class, the candidate is a strict output inverse exactly when the residual parallel sum is Harte-quasinilpotent. In the Banach setting, uniform input spectral gaps characterize continuity of the core and candidate along convergent input pairs, with intertwining and quasinilpotent input remainders at every term and at the limit. The output gap is equivalent when the residues of the sequence and limit are also quasinilpotent. Exact defect identities give local estimates on augmented inverse data. At an exactly intertwined base with invertible coefficient operators, we determine the feasible first-order defect space and its sharp norm constant, with a norm-specific matrix calibration.

papers.title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal. As a further consequence, the Durfee square side length of a uniformly chosen partition of $n$ has the same distribution as $1$ plus a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables.

papers.title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
papers.abstract: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

papers.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
papers.abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we derive formulas involving finite sums and generating functions. The arguments use images and fibers, homomorphisms between functional digraphs, and isomorphism types of iterates. A common construction decomposes weighted allocations of fibers into trees and cycles, yielding determinant expressions for several generating functions. Colored functional digraphs provide further formulas. As a by-product, for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$, we derive an inclusion--exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite plane-to-plane germs
papers.abstract: We show that the bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite holomorphic map germs $(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ admits continuous moduli, already among finitely determined polynomial germs of corank one and degree five. The moduli come from a new invariant of finite germs: for two tangent branches of the critical set whose images are tangent, the limit of the ratio of the norms of the images of nearby points is preserved by bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence. For germs $(F,H)$ with quasihomogeneous components the invariant is computed from the height functions of $F$ and $H$: it is given by the moduli of the values of the height function of the component of lower weighted degree at the roots of a weighted Wronskian. As a first application we obtain a continuous invariant for the germs $(Y^3+3tYX^4+X^6,\,X^N)$, $N\ge7$, built from the Henry--Parusi\'nski family.

papers.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
papers.abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

papers.title: Maximal dissipativity for the Dirichlet operator associated to the dynamical $\Phi^4$ model on the plane
papers.abstract: We consider the Dirichlet/Kolmogorov operator associated with the stochastic quantization of the $\Phi^4$ model on the plane whose domain is restricted to the space of smooth cylindrical functions. We prove that its closure is maximally dissipative in $L^p$. Our result implies the so-called $L^p$-uniqueness of the Dirichlet operator for every $1\le p<\infty$. In particular, essential self-adjointness and Markov uniqueness follow. The key ingredient is an estimate for the linearized equation for the dynamical $\Phi^4_2$ model. The proof is based on techniques from singular SPDE theory and the stopping time argument introduced by Kunick and Tsatsoulis.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

papers.title: A discontinuous time to collision feedback: well posedness, regularity of the collision-time map, and residual stability of its Hamilton Jacobi approximations
papers.authors: Hossein Nick Zinat Matin, Yuneil Yeo, Maria Laura Delle Monache
papers.abstract: We analyze a finite-horizon time-to-collision map generated by an optimal-velocity prediction with bounded measurable leader acceleration and a feedback law that uses this map. The prediction describes nominal motion without the additional collision-avoidance feedback. Its first-contact geometry can produce discontinuities of the capped collision time at grazing, so smooth-feedback theory does not apply globally. For a prescribed leader--follower pair, we prove existence of Filippov solutions and exclusion of contact with negative relative velocity for every solution; a zero-speed touch is not excluded. Under explicit nondegeneracy hypotheses, trajectories cross the grazing set and uniqueness persists through the crossing. On the domain of transversal first contacts, the collision-time map is locally Lipschitz, continuously differentiable in the state, and differentiable in time outside a common null set. We quantify its sensitivity to the transversality margin and to jumps of the forcing. Characteristic and coarea arguments give boundary-plus-interior residual estimates for Hamilton--Jacobi approximations. An endpoint/age change of variables yields a stability coefficient controlled by flight time and terminal normal velocity, without inverse-transversality blowup. The estimates imply convergence conditional on vanishing continuum loss and pointwise identification under the stated trace and regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments on thirteen prescribed forcing profiles investigate boundary-error transport, sampling effects, and regularity predictions; a separate first-contact experiment numerically demonstrates post-threshold sensitivity sign changes. The guarantees concern the exact feedback and value-function approximation. Learned-feedback safety and convergence of a training algorithm remain open.

papers.title: Inequality-Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode Control
papers.authors: Rawan Hoteit, Veronica Centorrino, Efe C. Balta, John Lygeros
papers.abstract: We present COSMIC (Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode for Inequality Constraints), a continuous-time solver for inequality-constrained optimization. COSMIC couples primal gradient-flow dynamics with multiplier dynamics derived from sliding mode control laws on a manifold defined by the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister function. We prove that COSMIC's trajectories reach this manifold in finite time from any primal initial point, after which the dynamics reduces to the gradient flow of a logarithmic barrier function. This yields a control-theoretic interpretation of barrier methods while allowing infeasible initialization. For strongly convex problems, we further establish exponential convergence to the minimizer. To address the numerical stiffness that arises in discretization, we develop a modified discrete-time algorithm. We validate COSMIC across various machine learning applications, demonstrating its ability to solve optimization problems accurately while scaling effectively to high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Cholesky with Error Guarantees
papers.authors: Sudhanva Kulkarni, James W. Demmel, Laura Grigori
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators increasingly support low-precision formats such as 8-bit floats and integers to speed up machine learning. We show that a Cholesky factorization in which both GEMM and TRSM are implemented using the fixed-point Ozaki 1 scheme satisfies the same backward error bounds as the standard floating-point Cholesky factorization, and that the same holds for a Cholesky factorization computed using a low-precision MicroScaled GEMM. We then use our error analyses to construct an adaptive precision Cholesky factorization that exploits low-precision formats while respecting a prescribed element-wise error bound, as long as the factorization succeeds. We test it in two settings. First, we use it to choose the number of Ozaki 1 slices at each iteration, with SYRK/GEMM and TRSM emulated in INT8 fixed-point arithmetic to attain double-precision accuracy. Second, we use it to build a low-precision Cholesky preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method (PCG), in which SYRK/GEMM take low-precision inputs and accumulate in high precision, with the input format selected adaptively for each panel; if the factorization breaks down, diagonal perturbation still yields a valid preconditioner, at the cost of the error bound guarantees. On an NVIDIA GH200, the adaptive Ozaki 1-based factorization is up to 29% faster than a right-looking Cholesky using a fixed slice count of 7, and up to 69% faster than one using cuBLAS' Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP), while maintaining the same error guarantees. For PCG, FP8 factorizations with diagonal perturbation form effective preconditioners on the 13 tested SuiteSparse matrices, reducing the number of PCG iterations by up to $12\times$ over CG on the same matrix diagonally scaled by powers of two. For synthetic matrices with arithmetic spectra, and geometric spectra with $\kappa \le 10^4$, FP8 preconditioners also reduce the number of CG iterations.

papers.title: The structure of varieties with nef anticanonical divisor in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a regular projective variety with nef anticanonical divisor over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $f:X\to A$ be a surjective morphism to an abelian variety. We prove that there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $f': X\times_AA' \to A'$ admits a Zariski locally trivial structure. If moreover $-K_X\equiv D$ for some semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D$, then $-K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}D$, and there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $ X\times_AA' \cong X_0\times A'$ where $X_0$ is the fiber over the identity $0\in A'$.

papers.title: Boundary regularity, finiteness and stability of energy-maximizing vortex patches
papers.authors: Daomin Cao, Guodong Wang, Yuchen Wang
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for energy-maximizing vortex patches of the 2-D incompressible Euler equations in a bounded Jordan domain. These results resolve Turkington's free-boundary regularity question throughout the full range of admissible parameters. For bounded convex domains, we further prove that the set of energy maximizers is finite at each prescribed patch area. When the domain is smooth, the number of maximizers is uniformly bounded over all admissible patch areas, and every maximizer is Lyapunov stable in $L^p$ for any $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and B\'etermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of B\'etermin--\v{S}amaj--Trav\v{e}nec [SAM 2023].

papers.title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

papers.title: A simplified temporal logic completeness proof
papers.abstract: A temporal logic discussed in the author's book "Logics of Time and Computation" is given a simpler proof of semantic completeness, eliminating some flaws in the original.

papers.title: The automorphism group of the super Jordan plane
papers.authors: W. de Araujo, D. Bagio, R. Baltazar, A. Santana, R. Vinciguerra
papers.abstract: We complete the description of the automorphism group of the super Jordan plane $\mathcal B$ over a field of characteristic zero, extending the classification of super-automorphisms obtained by N. Andruskiewitsch and F. Dumas in \cite{AD}. We characterize a subgroup $\mathbb L$ stabilizing two one-dimensional vector spaces and obtain two semidirect product decompositions of it. This subgroup contains all super-automorphisms and its structure motivates our main result. Precisely, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}\mathcal B=\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$, where $\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$ denote, respectively, the groups of inner automorphisms and super-automorphisms of $\mathcal B$. We also characterize the nilpotent elements of $\mathcal B$ and prove that every nonzero nilpotent has nilpotency index two. Furthermore, we give a geometric interpretation of three distinguished families of nilpotent elements. After degree truncation and projectivization, two of these families yield projective linear subspaces, while the third yields quadratic Veronese varieties of arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: On Semi-interval and Para-interval Graphs
papers.authors: Chenxi Lv, Yiming Lei, Chunlei Xu
papers.abstract: Bau and Johnson introduced semi-interval graphs and asked whether one of the two extremal sets can always be replaced by a single vertex. A negative answer to this question is given by a tree which has no such representation. It is also shown that a finite connected graph with at least two vertices is a semi-interval graph if and only if it is bipartite. Para-interval graphs, for which one extremal set consists of a single vertex, are characterized by necessary and sufficient conditions on their distance matrices. A characterization of para-interval trees is obtained, and a relation between para-interval graphs and shortest-path interval graphs is established by identifying the vertices of an extremal set. Finally, leveled graphs and the corresponding Hasse diagrams of finite partially ordered sets are considered.

papers.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
papers.abstract: We develop a methodology for set-based state estimation from noisy input-output trajectories, without a predefined model structure for the unknown state dynamics or access to training state measurements. We derive a bound on the state set diameter that depends on the sensor map and leverage it as a surrogate to formulate a tractable linear program balancing state set tightness against output trajectory coverage. Combining this certificate with deterministic or probabilistically certified measurement noise sets and leveraging the results from scenario optimization with relaxation, we provide joint a posteriori probabilistic guarantees for state inclusion and state set diameter. Numerical simulations corroborate our developed theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
papers.abstract: We prove Thouless's bandwidth conjecture for the critical rational Harper operator: the denominator times the total bandwidth tends to $32G/\pi$, uniformly in the reduced numerator, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. We identify a universal limit of the normalized even coarea density. Positive real part and evenness give an integrable endpoint bound, so the local law determines the bandwidth. An exact finite-matrix formula reduces the local law to one normalized period for each fixed odd numerator. Explicit boundary polynomials, point blowups, and intersections determine a compact genus-one family. Nodal-annulus calculations fix its period equation and hence the universal density. An exact rational Fourier identity and uniform closed-path bounds extend the result to all reduced numerators and both denominator parities. The singular matrix limit, including its subtraction and normalization, is proved separately in detail.

papers.title: Exact Redundancy under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints
papers.abstract: We characterize the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, we establish the asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under the average distortion constraint, the coefficient is half of the minimum probability that an output reveals information about the source, among all rate-distortion optimal channels. Under the almost-sure distortion constraint, the coefficient is either $1/2$ or $1$, depending on whether the $D$-tilted information is constant or not. Both converse results follow from a common change-of-measure inequality. Finally, we verify the required conditions under both distortion requirements always hold for finite alphabets.

papers.title: Behavior of the Caputo time fractional equations as the order $\alpha\rightarrow 0^+$: the resolvent limit and its stochastic interpretation
papers.abstract: We study the behavior, as the fractional order $\alpha\rightarrow0^+$, of the Caputo time derivative and of the solutions of $D_t^\alpha u=Au$ in a Banach space. The solutions converge for every $t>0$ to the time-independent resolvent value $(1-A)^{-1}\phi$. A single bounded fractional resolvent family already forces the sectoriality of $A$ and yields operator-norm convergence with rate $O(\alpha)$ and a full expansion in powers of $\alpha$. The engine is an expansion of the Mittag-Leffler function in its order, $E_\alpha(z)=(1-z)^{-1}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_k\alpha^k\mathrm{Li}_{-k}(z)+O(\alpha^{K+1})$ on sectors away from $[1,\infty)$, the corresponding qualitative limit going back to Mittag-Leffler's summability of the geometric series. We also develop stochastic interpretations using inverse $\alpha$-stable subordinators, and establish connections with probabilistic potential theory, the Feynman--Kac formula, and degenerate elliptic equations.

papers.title: Relax-and-Sparsify Approximation Algorithms for Sparse Ridge Regression
papers.abstract: This paper studies sparse ridge regression in the low-rank, high-dimensional setting that often arises when data collection is expensive. By exploiting the low-rank structure, we develop approximation algorithms within a relax-and-sparsify framework: solve a convex relaxation and then sparsify its solution to satisfy the original sparsity constraint. Specifically, we establish a tight rank-dependent sparsity bound for the convex relaxation by decomposing its support into two parts. This decomposition in turn motivates two approximation strategies, parameter reduction and binary redistribution, each exploiting a different part. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the binary redistribution algorithms outperform the benchmarks in most instances.

papers.title: On the continuity of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula
papers.abstract: We establish the continuous extension of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula to a natural space of test functions, which are not necessarily compactly supported, for reductive algebraic groups. The continuity of the geometric side of the (untwisted) Arthur trace formula was established by Finis--Lapid. Subsequently, Parab generalized their result to the twisted trace formula under a certain restriction on the truncation parameter and an additional assumption. In this paper, we remove his restriction and assumption, and prove the continuous extension for the twisted trace formula. We also give a revised form of Parab's decay estimate for the geometric side.

papers.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
papers.authors: Minjia Shi, Xinguang Dai, Patrick Sol\'e
papers.abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

papers.title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges
papers.abstract: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we give a complete classification of the asymptotic behavior of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ satisfying $\chi(H)>\chi$ and $\chi(H-e)>\chi$ for every $e\in E(H)$, where $\chi\ge 2$ and $R$ is an arbitrary fixed edge-critical graph with $\chi(R)=\chi+1$. We show that this quantity is of quadratic order, asymptotic to $\frac{2n}{\chi}$, or zero, according to the existence and structure of $\chi$-critical two-edge sets of $H$. In particular, we resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. ({\it J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} 159 (2023), 42-60).

papers.title: Fourier Ratio Bounds and Sensitivity to Sensor Placement
papers.authors: Nico Alberti, Christopher Housholder, Alex Iosevich, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson
papers.abstract: We study how the regularity of a continuous function controls the Fourier ratio of its sampled values, and how errors in sensor placement affect recovery from incomplete measurements. For a periodic function on the square sampled on an $N$ by $N$ grid, we show that H\"older regularity $C^{0,\gamma}$ with $0<\gamma<1$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-\gamma}$, that Lipschitz regularity leads to the critical bound $\sqrt{1+\log N}$, and that fractional Sobolev regularity $W^{s,p}$ with $0<s<1$ and $sp>2$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-s}$, where both polynomial exponents are sharp. A common translation of the grid removes the hypothesis on the sampled mass needed on a fixed grid and yields an estimate in terms of the $L^2$ norm of the gradient, and with two derivatives the bound is independent of the grid size. We extend the energy argument behind these results to compact Riemannian manifolds and prove that the critical square-root logarithm is necessary on every compact surface. Finally, we treat separate sensor displacements as measurement error and combine the analytic bounds with random sampling to obtain stable recovery of the sampled vector on the square and of bandlimited functions on compact manifolds, where the number of samples depends on the suprema of the chosen eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Isolated Singularities Not Resolved by Iterated Nash Blowups
papers.abstract: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-\'Alvarez, and Liendo asked whether iterating ordinary Nash blowups in characteristic zero or normalized Nash blowups in arbitrary characteristic can fail to resolve isolated singularities arXiv:2511.17862. We answer this question affirmatively with two constructions of isolated singularities, one nonnormal and one normal, both giving counterexamples to normalized Nash iteration in every characteristic.

papers.title: The Fourier Ratio on Resistance Spaces and Applications to Electrical Networks
papers.authors: Christopher Housholder, Alex Iosevich, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson
papers.abstract: We study the Fourier Ratio for spectral expansions of nonnegative self-adjoint operators. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz estimates turn eigenvalue counting bounds into Fourier Ratio bounds for spectrally regular functions. On a compact measured resistance space, Kasue's identity expresses the reciprocal eigenvalue sum as one half of the average resistance distance. We use this identity to obtain a sharp coefficient estimate for every finite-energy function, with no spectral cutoff. Bounded orthonormal system recovery theorems then yield reconstruction estimates whose sample counts depend on both the Fourier Ratio and the pointwise size of the chosen eigenfunctions. We distinguish these estimates from the weaker diameter-only bounds and give an interval example with a sample count logarithmic in the dimension of the spectral subspace for fixed accuracy and energy ratio. Resistance also controls errors caused by displaced sensors. We apply the estimates to standard self-similar fractals and finite electrical networks, where the geometric constant becomes the normalized square root of the Kirchhoff index. A separate observation describes Fourier Ratios of coefficient families with a limiting distribution.

papers.title: Routing Information and Stationary Limits in Many-Server Load Balancing
papers.abstract: We study how routing information determines stationary congestion in many-server systems with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous exponential servers. We consider policies that prioritize idle servers and select a queue stochastically no longer than a uniformly sampled queue. In nondegenerate slowdown, where spare capacity is fixed, we identify population laws from the fraction of queues with waiting jobs at each population level. We establish these laws for one-job priority, join-idle-queue, and idle-first sampling. One-job priority attains the join-the-shortest-queue population law and mean delays; further queue information can improve limiting delays in convex order without changing their means. In the super-Halfin-Whitt and Halfin-Whitt regimes, every such policy has the same stationary limits. Our estimates bound idleness-weighted occupancy tails in terms of ordinary tails, uniformly over queue-length thresholds and policies. They also yield process convergence and limit interchange for initial laws uniformly dominated by stationarity, with convergent scaled initial states.

papers.title: Moderate deviations for semilinear stochastic evolution equations in fast Markovian environments
papers.abstract: This work establishes moderate deviation principles for semilinear stochastic evolution equations with coefficients depending on fast Markov environments. The environment is either an exponentially ergodic Markov process on a Polish space, independent of the noise, or a finite-state Markov chain whose transition rates depend on time and on a finite-dimensional observation of the state. The rate function is quadratic in the residual of the linearized dynamics. Its covariance is the sum of the averaged covariance of the Wiener noise and the asymptotic covariance generated by the environment, given by a Green--Kubo formula in the independent case and by a Poisson equation in the switching case. The rate function is written with the Moore--Penrose inverse of the square root of this covariance and requires the residual to lie in its range, not merely in the closure. This allows degenerate covariances and nonclosed ranges. In the switching case, the dependence of the invariant distribution on the slow state adds an extra term to the linearized drift. Since the stochastic convolution is not a semimartingale, the proofs combine the regeneration split chain technique with Galerkin approximation. The assumptions are verified for stochastic reaction--diffusion equations, including space-time white noise in one spatial dimension.

papers.title: Efficient Recursive Evaluation of Gaussian, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian Tail Probabilities
papers.abstract: Accurate computation of tail probabilities motivates efficient high-order implementations of the $G_n^{(1)}$ extrapolation transformation. We derive finite recurrence relations in the transformation order for Gaussian, gamma, and inverse Gaussian tail approximations. The Gaussian and inverse Gaussian numerator and denominator sequences satisfy four-term recurrences, whereas the gamma sequences satisfy a three-term recurrence. The derivation exploits the structure of the underlying differential operator and shows that the reduced numerator and denominator obey recurrences with identical coefficients. This construction avoids the repeated evaluation of higher-order derivatives and nested sums required by the explicit formulations. As a result, generating the approximation sequence through order $n$ requires $O(n)$ arithmetic operations, compared with $O(n^3)$ for the Gaussian and gamma distributions and $O(n^4)$ for the inverse Gaussian distribution. The recurrence algorithms also require only a fixed number of previously computed quantities at each order. Numerical results for the three distributions are in excellent agreement with values reported in the literature

papers.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under H\"older Growth
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{\"o}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{\"o}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

papers.title: Explicit geometric integrators for Langevin equations with superquadratic potentials
papers.authors: Chuchu Chen, Xinyu Chen, Jialin Hong, Michael V. Tretyakov
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of explicit methods for Langevin equations with a superquadratic potential that simultaneously preserve the conformal symplecticity and ergodicity as well as achieving high-order convergence. The construction is based on a mollified potential approach, in which the original potential is truncated to quadratic growth at infinity and globally mollified to control the superquadratic behavior while maintaining the underlying properties of the original dynamics. By appropriately choosing the cut-off radius, the far-field quadratic coefficient, and the step size, we obtain the coercivity of the mollified potential and derive its derivative estimates. These estimates allow us to prove uniform-in-time weak convergence for the proposed (including higher-order) explicit conformal symplectic numerical methods. Since the mollified potential is identical to the original one in a ball whose radius grows as the step size decreases, the computational cost of the new methods is essentially the same as that of the usual schemes (e.g., BAOAB) applied to the original potential. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces
papers.authors: Tristan Collins, Jason Lo, Yun Shi, Shing-Tung Yau
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the Bridgeland stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces. We obtain a complete description of the region where the tangent bundle is (un)stable with respect to the standard Bridgeland stability conditions associated to the anticanonical polarization.

papers.title: Word complexity cutoffs for mixing properties of subshifts
papers.abstract:
Investigating word complexity cutoffs for partial and light mixing in subshifts, we construct partially mixing rank-one subshifts whose word complexity functions $p(q)$ satisfy $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q<2+\epsilon $
for any prescribed $\epsilon>0$ and, conversely, we prove that every lightly mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q>2, $
establishing $2$ as the optimal limiting threshold in the rank-one setting. More quantitatively, we show that every $\alpha$-partially mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $
\liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q\geq 2+\frac{\alpha}{(1+\alpha)}. $
Our constructions are a combination of staircase and Chacon-like rank-one stages; we introduce the independently interesting notion of mixing spans and meshes to establish partial mixing while retaining low word complexity.

papers.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the K\"unneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.

papers.title: An improved lower bound for piercing the chessboard by lines
papers.abstract: Let $p_n$ be the least number of lines meeting the interior of every cell of an $n\times n$ board. We prove that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n/n\ge0.7520517>\frac34$. The previous bound was $0.7$. The proof is computer-assisted. It identifies a non-negative polynomial on the unit square and bounds its integral along every line.

papers.title: Optimal first order global regularity for fractional harmonic maps into spheres
papers.authors: Yu He, Chang-Lin Xiang, Gao-Feng Zheng
papers.abstract: This paper is a continuation of our previous work on global regularity theory for the sphere-valued fractional harmonic maps which was initialized by several authors such as Millot-Pegon-Schikorra and Millot-Sire. By adapting the powerful quantitative stratification approach developed by Naber-Valtorta on harmonic mappings, we establish a corresponding stratification theory for fractional harmonic maps, from which an optimal first order global regularity theory and the rectifiable structure of singular sets follow.

papers.title: The Erd\H{o}s similarity problem for polynomials and analytic maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem by replacing affine copies with images of polynomial maps or analytic maps. This is inspired by a connection between a partial converse of Szemer\'edi's theorem and the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem and its variants, as well as a version of polynomial Szemer\'edi's theorem by Bergelson and Leibman. In particular, we strengthen several known results in the literature. We show that a large class of sequence are not polynomially universal in this sense. First, for sequences satisfying suitable gap hypotheses, an explicit Cantor-type witness is constructed. Second, for sets satisfying certain growth conditions, a random Cantor-type witness is constructed, extending work of Kolountzakis. This also extends certain results in recent work of Cu\'ellar-Iosevich-Kulkarni-Aravena-Yavicoli to the polynomial setting. Finally, we show for arbitrary sequences $A$ with zero as an accumulation point that the $(d+3)$-fold sumset $(d+3)A$ is not polynomially universal when restricted to polynomials of degree at most $d$; this complements classical work of Bourgain.

papers.title: Error-correcting codes without parity-check bits
papers.authors: Boris Ryabko, Ivan Baksheev, Vyacheslav Zhuravlev
papers.abstract:
We are developing a new approach to the problem of error correction in communication channels, in which the input sequence is transformed in such a way that the interdependence of symbols increases significantly. Then, after the sequence is transmitted over the channel, this property is used for error correction, so that the residual error rate is significantly reduced. A natural example of its application is the transmission of binary sequences whose entropy (per symbol) is less than one, since in this case the length of the transmitted sequence remains constant during encoding and decoding.
  An algorithm has been developed to implement the maximum likelihood method, in which the encoding and decoding times are linear. This algorithm was used to experimentally investigate its effectiveness on popular channel models, and it was found that there are certain sets of parameters for which the proposed method is quite effective.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the three-color Hadwiger-Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: The Hadwiger-Ramsey number $R_h(k;\ell)$ is defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that for any edge coloring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices in $\ell$ colors at least one of the color classes induces a graph with a $K_k$ minor. We show that $R_h(k;3) = \left(\beta^{-1} + o(1)\right)k \sqrt{\ln k}$, where $\beta^{-1} = 2/\sqrt{-\ln(10-4\sqrt6)} = 1.58149\ldots$. This resolves the first open case of a problem by Axenovich and Steiner, who determined the asymptotic behavior of $R_h(k;2)$ and asked about the asymptotics of $R_h(k;\ell)$ for $\ell \geq 3$.

papers.title: Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
papers.authors: Changqing Xu, Yan Yang, Junxue Zhang
papers.abstract: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family. Assume that every member of $\mathcal F$ has at least $8$ vertices, minimum degree at least two, and no triangle containing two vertices of degree two. We give explicit sufficient conditions under which $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_t\vee\mathcal F) =\binom{t}{2}+t(n-t)+\operatorname{sat}(n-t,\mathcal F),$ and characterize all extremal graphs. For the family $\mathcal C_{\ge r}=\{C_\ell:\ell\ge r\}$ of subdivisions of $C_r$, this identity holds for fixed $t\ge1$ and $r\ge4t^2+8t+29$ and all sufficiently large $n$. For $K_t\vee C_k$ with $k\ge2t^2+3t+4$, we establish the corresponding identity for saturation when $n\ge2(k+t-2)^3$ and for semi-saturation when $n\ge56k^3+t-1$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
papers.abstract: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture.

papers.title: Splitting of separatrices in generalized standard maps
papers.authors: Inmaculada Baldom\'a, D\'idac Gil-Rams, Pau Mart\'in
papers.abstract: We consider generalized standard maps, that is, maps $F_h:(x,y) \mapsto (x+y+f(x;h),y+f(x;h))$ under quite general assumptions. These maps are area preserving. In particular, the Chirikov standard map, the area preserving H\'enon map and the case $f(x;h)= \varepsilon(x-x^n)$, $n\ge 2$, where $\varepsilon = 4 \sinh^2(h/2)$ satisfy our hypotheses. For all these cases, the problem of the existence of transverse homoclinic points arises. We prove that, for a wide class of generalized standard maps, the primary homoclinic points are transverse, provided that some constant is different from 0.

papers.title: Enhancing Exploration in Ensemble Kalman Inversion via Covariance Inflation and Projected Dropout
papers.authors: Baojun Che, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Xinying Mao, Weijie Wang
papers.abstract: Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) is a derivative-free and parallelizable method for parameter estimation in Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive forward models. It adapts Kalman filtering by repeatedly assimilating the observation data through an artificial dynamical system with identity state evolution and the parameter-to-observation map as its observation operator. However, its performance can be limited by ensemble collapse and confinement to the affine span of the initial ensemble. We propose an exploration-enhanced EKI framework that combines multiplicative covariance inflation with a projected-dropout correction of the ensemble mean. Inflation helps maintain ensemble spread, while projected dropout enables the mean to explore directions beyond the initial affine span. For linear inverse problems, we provide a discrete-time, finite-ensemble analysis of the resulting method and prove the least-squares objective converges exponentially to its minimum in expectation. Within the initial ensemble subspace, the contraction factor is independent of the conditioning of the inverse problem, and the limiting ensemble covariance provides a low-rank representation of the posterior covariance. Experiments on ill-conditioned linear systems, 100-dimensional nonlinear benchmarks, and a PDE-constrained barotropic flow inverse problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todor\v{c}evi\'{c}.

papers.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<\theta<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

papers.title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
papers.abstract: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.

papers.title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Li\'enard systems
papers.authors: Hebai Chen, Yuhuan Lu, Qian Wang Rui Zhang
papers.abstract:
This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Li\'enard system
  $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where
  $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$,
  with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$.
  It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that
  every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting
  for $a_2<0$; this system has
  no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar
  arcs obtained in potential coordinates.
  This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of
  Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).

papers.title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
papers.authors: Hebai Chen, Jie Jin, Zhijie Li, Jueliang Zhou
papers.abstract: We study the polynomial Li\'enard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].

papers.title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
papers.abstract:
We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated.
  The proof constructs angular minima via quadratic regularization, matching the regularization coefficient to the leading inertial term. A free forcing coefficient allows continuation past bounded accumulations of correction orders. For polynomial potentials, this produces a complete Hahn-series solution, and differential algebraicity gives a common Puiseux denominator. A fixed-denominator continuation estimate together with a finite Taylor transfer extends the construction to analytic potentials. The realization theorem for the resulting invariant formal phase curve then yields a genuine trajectory. We also exhibit an isolated polynomial singularity for which an exact Euler-field identity admits no relatively differentiable solution on the negative set of the potential.

papers.title: Weighted bisections of triangle-free subcubic graphs
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo, and Zhou: for every finite triangle-free subcubic graph other than the claw and every nonnegative edge weighting, there is a bisection whose weight is at least $11/15$ of the total edge weight. This bound is best possible, as shown by the Petersen graph. The proof uses matching-based local distributions, weighted induction, and convex separation to establish the edgewise cut guarantees while maintaining global balance.

papers.title: Certified Algorithms for Gaussian Location Mixture NPMLEs via Discretized Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: We study the computation of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLEs) for Gaussian location mixtures in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 1$ via the Fisher-Rao gradient flow. We provide a certified algorithm based on an entropic proximal discretization of the flow which, given a sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, returns an absolutely continuous mixing measure $\tilde\mu$ admitting an exact finite-dimensional representation and satisfying $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\tilde\mu})\le\varepsilon$. For almost every dataset $X_1,\cdots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $n>2(d+1)(m+1)^2$, where $m$ is the number of support points of the NPMLE, the algorithm requires $O(n\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d+2}(1/\varepsilon))$ time. En route, we also establish results on the well-posedness and convergence properties of the continuous-time Fisher--Rao flow. In particular, initializing the flow at the uniform probability measure on a ball containing the convex hull of the observations, we show that $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\mu_t})=O(\log t/t)$. We also establish that, for almost every dataset satisfying the same condition on $n$ as above, the set of global maxima of the optimal score is the same as the support of the NPMLE, and the Hessian of the optimal score is nondegenerate at these points, extending a result of (Polyanskiy-Sellke, 2025) to higher dimensions.

papers.title: First-order smoothed exact-penalty methods for equality-constrained regularized nonconvex optimization
papers.authors: Shiji Zuo, Qihang Lin, Wei Liu, Yangyang Xu
papers.abstract: We consider regularized nonconvex optimization over a closed convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, which involves a convex nonsmooth regularizer $r$ in the objective and $n$ smooth equality constraints. To find a near-KKT point of the problem, we propose a prox-linear first-order method, named as SEPi-Prox, based on a smoothed exact-penalty formulation. At each outer iteration of SEPi-Prox, a strongly convex prox-linear subproblem is formed and solved inexactly to a sufficient accuracy. Under a local non-singularity condition that is weaker than some other commonly used regularity conditions or constraint qualifications, SEPi-Prox finds an $\epsilon$-KKT point within $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ first-order oracle calls, matching the lower bound for unconstrained smooth nonconvex optimization. We employ Nesterov's accelerated proximal-gradient method (APG) and a dual cutting-plane method (DCP) for the prox-linear subproblems. Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}}$ and $\mathcal{C}_r$ denote the numbers of arithmetic operations of evaluating one first-order oracle and one proximal mapping of $r$ over $\mathcal{X}$, respectively. Then SEPi-Prox requires $\widetilde{O}(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}}\epsilon^{-2} + (dn + \mathcal{C}_r)\epsilon^{-5/2})$ and $\widetilde{O}((\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{FO}} + dn^2 + n\mathcal{C}_r + n^{3.373})\epsilon^{-2})$ total arithmetic operations to produce an $\epsilon$-KKT point, respectively by using APG and DCP as the subsolver. The latter result is preferable when $n$ is small and nearly matches the optimal dependence on $\epsilon$. Numerical experiments on instances of the multi-class Neyman-Pearson classification demonstrate the efficiency of SEPi-Prox with both subsolvers.

papers.title: Antisymmetry Breaking for Critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev Extremals in the Three Dimensional Ball
papers.abstract: We study extremal functions for Poincar\'e-Sobolev inequalities in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. At the critical exponent $q=6$, we prove that no minimizer is antisymmetric with respect to any hyperplane through the origin. We obtain a positive gap between the general and antisymmetric optimal constants. Continuity of these constants yields antisymmetry breaking for exponents sufficiently close to $6$. We introduce two critical indices to describe the onset of antisymmetry breaking and prove that global minimizers are antisymmetric at both indices.

papers.title: Exact multiplicity for a Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem with a step weight
papers.abstract: The DEG1 challenge asks whether positive solutions of a super-exponential Minkowski-curvature equation are unique for step weights with a single sign change and negative mean. In this paper, we give a Neumann counterexample by studying $\left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + \lambda a_{\mu,h}(t)(e^{u^2}-1)=0$ with $u'(0)=u'(2h)=0$, where $a_{\mu,h}=1$ on $(0,h)$ and $a_{\mu,h}=-\mu$ on $(h,2h)$, with $\mu>1$. Using the shooting method, we prove that the positive solution curve has exactly two nondegenerate folds for $(\lambda,h)$ in a nonempty open region. As $\mu$ increases through the corresponding critical values, the number of positive solutions is successively $1$, $2$, $3$, $2$, and $1$.

papers.title: Frege's logic in Grundgesetze is nonclassical
papers.abstract: I show that the axioms and rules of inference about the horizontal in the subsystem of Grundgesetze without value-ranges fail to capture its intended interpretation. That is, I build a nonstandard model in which $-a$ is the true iff $a$ is not the false, thereby confirming a conjecture made by Landini that $a \to (-a) = a$ is not provable in this subsystem. This motivates our main result, namely, soundness and completeness proofs for the first-order fragment without value-ranges with respect to a new nonclassical semantics of boolean truncation. Simply put, the widespread assumption that Grundgesetze's first-order logic is classical first-order logic is mistaken.

papers.title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
papers.abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

papers.title: Minimal sets of countable group actions on regular curves
papers.authors: Enhui Shi, Suhua Wang, Yifei Yu
papers.abstract: We study minimal sets of countable groups acting by homeomorphisms on regular curves. If the ambient action has a finite orbit, every infinite minimal set is an equicontinuous Cantor system. If there is no finite orbit, the minimal set is unique and remains minimal for every finite-index subgroup. A minimal set supporting an invariant probability is a finite orbit, an equicontinuous Cantor system, a circle isometry action, or a Cantor extension obtained by splitting a countable invariant subset of such a circle. Without an invariant probability, infinitely many nondegenerate components can occur. Their homeomorphism types determine the underlying space, and every nonempty countable family of types is realized. The two-generator free group admits an example with arc components on a dendrite, whereas its restricted wreath product with the integers admits none on any regular curve.

papers.title: A simple proof of the characterization of $\ell_\infty^n$ by norm-one projections and a stability estimate
papers.abstract: We give a short and elementary proof of a classical fact that an $n$-dimensional real or complex normed space with the absolute projection constant equal to one is linearly isometric to $\ell_\infty^n$. The proof uses only finite-dimensional convexity and linear algebra, with no infinite-dimensional ingredients. The same approach yields a quantitative stability estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when the absolute projection constant is at most $1+\varepsilon$. This improves Zippin's estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{8}}$ in each fixed dimension as $\varepsilon \to 0$. The real and complex cases are treated by the same arguments.

papers.title: A remark on the entropy numbers of mixed smoothness classes
papers.abstract: We find the right orders of both the entropy numbers and the Kolmogorov widths of classes of multivariate functions with bounded mixed derivative, when the class is defined by the restriction in the uniform norm and the error of approximation is measured in the uniform norm. The case of functions of two variables was settled about 30 years ago and the case of three or more variables stayed open.

papers.title: The maximum length of a Hamiltonian path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$
papers.abstract: Label the $mn$ vertices of the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ bijectively by $1, \dots, mn$ and read the labels in increasing order; this produces a Hamiltonian path whose length in the Manhattan metric is denoted $M(P_m \times P_n)$. McNeil conjectured, on the basis of computer evidence, that $M(P_n \times P_n) = n^3 - 3$ for even $n$ and $n^3 - n - 1$ for odd $n$. Fried recently determined $M(P_m \times P_n)$ up to an additive error of one. We determine it exactly, which settles McNeil's conjecture. The proof rests on the cut-counting bound for multisets. Fried states that bound for multiplicities at least two; we give a form valid for every multiplicity, with a correction term that is invisible in the planar case but not in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
papers.authors: Shuixin Fang, Xuerui Wang, Hang Zeng, Tao Zhou
papers.abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives in high dimensions by automatic differentiation can be costly in both computation and memory. Stein's identity offers an alternative through Gaussian smoothing, but the variance of the resulting estimators can diverge as the step size tends to zero, even with antithetic sampling. We propose a variance stabilization technique that extends antithetic sampling from a reflection pair to $n$ equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane. Under local analyticity, we prove that, when $n$ is at least the derivative order, the bias is of order $O(\sigma^n)$ and the variance remains bounded as the smoothing step size $\sigma$ tends to zero. Numerical experiments support these predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the estimator in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for polyharmonic and Cahn--Hilliard equations. The technique mitigates the bias-variance trade-off in smoothing-based derivative estimation and is useful for PINNs solving high-order partial differential equations.

papers.title: Uniqueness of invariant measures for mean-field stochastic damped wave and heat equations
papers.abstract: We study invariant measures for a Wick-renormalized mean-field stochastic damped wave equation on the two-dimensional torus and for the corresponding stochastic heat equation. With Wick ordering relative to the massive Gaussian free field with covariance $(1-\Delta)^{-1}$, we prove uniqueness among invariant laws whose renormalized second moment belongs to $H^{-\sigma}(\mathbb T^2)$, where $0<\sigma<\tfrac12$. Stationarity reduces the mean-field equation to a linear equation with a deterministic distribution-valued potential. We show that self-consistency forces this deterministic potential to vanish. The damped wave equation therefore has invariant law $\mathcal N(0,(1-\Delta)^{-1})\otimes\mathcal N(0,\varepsilon^{-2}I)$, with covariance understood distributionally, while the heat equation has the Gaussian free field as its invariant law. This resolves self-consistency for spatially varying distribution-valued potentials and establishes uniqueness in the specified class. As the inertia parameter tends to zero, the position marginal remains equal to the invariant law of the corresponding stochastic heat equation, whereas the velocity marginal assigns vanishing probability to every bounded subset of $H^{-1-\sigma}(\mathbb T^2)$, establishing Smoluchowski-Kramers type behavior.

papers.title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
papers.abstract:
We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$.
  Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Geh\'er and \v{S}emrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Geh\'er for $p=2$.

papers.title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Amenable Discrete Quantum Groups with Modified Rapid Decay
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an amenable discrete quantum group with the modified rapid decay property relative to a proper central length $\ell$. We construct a modularly corrected commutator seminorm on $C_r^*(G)$ and prove its right invariance. Averaging over the coproduct yields a regular bi-invariant Lip-norm. For the spectral projections $P_R=\chi_{[0,R]}(D_\ell)$, we equip the finite-dimensional operator systems $A_R=P_RC_r^*(G)P_R$ with the Lip-norms induced by the compressed left and right coactions. We prove quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and obtain an explicit approximation estimate. These spectral compressions are length-filtered Peter--Weyl truncations of the compact dual. The resulting regular bi-invariant Lip-norm also places the family within Leimbach's operator Gromov--Hausdorff convergence theorem. The construction applies to non-unimodular discrete quantum groups, including discrete duals of standard deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Characterisation of first passage locations for two-dimensional lattice random walks
papers.abstract: Consider a diagonal random walk $(X_n,Y_n)$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with transition probabilities depending only on the second coordinate. We characterise the distributions of first passage locations, $X(\tau_a)$, where $\tau_a$ is the first time $Y_n$ reaches level $a$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a given distribution to be realised as a rescaled first passage location from some starting level. The proof extends Bondesson's method for one-dimensional first passage times. It combines a transformation of generating functions based on Pick functions with a construction using barriers. We also study maximal representations of generating functions of first passage locations and show that analogous converse results for standard and honeycomb random walks require additional restrictions.

papers.title: Calabi flow in the controlled K\"ahler cone
papers.authors: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng
papers.abstract: We prove that the geometric limit of a global Calabi flow in a real class of the controlled K\"ahler cone is independent of the initial metric. Under cohomological K-polystability, the limit is a smooth cscK metric in the original class and complex structure. We also establish varying-class closedness and an equivariant continuity method. We apply this method to construct a smoothly varying family of cscK metrics throughout an explicit interval of symmetric real K\"ahler classes on the blow-up of the projective plane at four points in general position.

papers.title: Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
papers.abstract: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes. Starting from the asymptotic expansion of a real branch at infinity, we retain its non-decaying terms in order to construct an algebraic surrogate, which is then used as an adaptive far-field model outside a sufficiently large compact region. We introduce explicit discrepancy indicators and a switching radius that determine when the exact branch may be replaced by its generalized asymptotic predictor. The framework recovers the classical linear asymptote whenever the latter exists, while remaining effective for branches with polynomial or Puiseux-type dominant behavior. In the implicit setting, we prove algebraicity and compatibility properties of the predictor and derive asymptotic error estimates from the first neglected term of the expansion. A residual certificate distinguishes guaranteed finite-tail replacement from asymptotic radius estimates. Tangential tails, slow decay, and a smooth transition rule clarify the limitations of truncation. Reproducible finite-window tests compare the predictors with fitted polynomial baselines; these tests are not a benchmark of a complete plotting system.

papers.title: Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calder\'on-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
papers.authors: Xinpeng Huang, Zhengyong Ren, Jingtian Tang
papers.abstract: Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.

papers.title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
papers.abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: A new formula for Moore-Penrose inverses of rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new formula for the Moore-Penrose inverses of the rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices, based on the quasi-direct decompositions of Toeplitz matrices. Numerical examples are presented to verify the validity and the efficiency of our method.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Lin, Yufeng Lu, Rong Yang, Chao Zu
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property.
