We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Counting integral points of fixed degree and given height over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a finite extension of the rational function field in one variable over a finite field, and let $\mathcal{O}_k$ be its ring of integers. Let $\overline{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. For integers $e \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$, we study the number of points in the affine space $\overline{k}^n$ whose coordinates are integral over $\mathcal{O}_k$, have absolute logarithmic Weil height equal to $m \geq 0$, and generate an extension of degree $e$ over $k$. More precisely, we derive an asymptotic formula for this quantity as $m \rightarrow \infty$ whenever $n > e$, except in the cases $(n,e)\in \{(3,2),(4,3),(5,4)\}$. When $k$ is the rational function field, however, we use Weierstrass semigroups to obtain asymptotic formulas for the cases $(n,e)\in \{(1,2),(2,2),(3,2)\}$, thereby completing the picture in the setting $e=2$. As an application, we also derive asymptotic estimates for the number of certain decomposable forms with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}_k$.

papers.title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation
papers.authors: Ailing Zheng, Qingqing Wu, Xiyuan Liu, Wei Feng, Wen Chen, Guoying Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a sparse rotatable array (SRA)-enabled cell-free multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Under a network-wide antenna activation budget, distributed access points (APs) select active antenna elements from their installed arrays and adjust panel orientations, enabling joint control of sparse array apertures and antenna directivity. To avoid frequent hardware reconfiguration in response to instantaneous channel variations, we formulate a two-timescale stochastic optimization problem to maximize the expected minimum-user rate. Long-term antenna activation and panel orientations are optimized based on user spatial distributions and statistical channel state information (CSI), while short-term precoders adapt to instantaneous CSI. Under line-of-sight (LoS) propagation, we derive the optimal single-user antenna allocation, characterize the two-user max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and establish conditions for discrete activation and panel rotation to attain the continuous-position benchmark, and obtain a closed-form multi-AP zero-forcing (ZF) allocation benchmark under a continuous antenna-count relaxation. For the general mixed-integer nonconvex stochastic problem, we develop an alternating algorithm based on sample-average approximation (SAA), integrating uplink-downlink (UL-DL) duality for short-term precoding, weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) surrogates for panel-orientation optimization, and multi-start greedy search for antenna activation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms the fixed-array benchmark, improves all-user service reliability with fewer active antennas, and adapts effectively to nonuniform user spatial distributions.

papers.title: Concircular Sections Along Submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce an equation which generalises that of a concircular vector field to sections of the ambient tangent bundle along submanifolds. Totally umbilic hypersurfaces and various overdetermined systems (such as Obata's and Tashiro's equations) are obtained as specific cases. Given an ambient manifold $M$ and a connected submanifold $P$ of dimension at least $2$, the solution space $W(P;M)$ is shown to have dimension at most $\mathrm{dim } M+1$ with all solutions being of `special type' whenever it exceeds $\mathrm{codim } P+1$. This bound is shown to be sharp. When the submanifold $P$ is simply connected we show the maximum dimension is attained exactly when $P$ has constant sectional curvature $\kappa$ relative to the ambient manifold $M$. In the case of maximum dimension we introduce a bilinear form $\mathbb{I}$ on $W(P;M)$ which is Riemannian, degenerate or Lorentzian, depending on the sign of $\kappa$ and show $P$ immerses into $(W(P;M),\mathbb{I})$'s unit quadric. Hence our main result shows that whenever $P$ is simply connected, has dimension of at least $2$, and has constant curvature $\kappa\neq0$ relative to its ambient manifold $M$, there is an isometric immersion (which we construct explicitly) of $P$ with its metric induced from $M$, into the $\mathrm{dim } M$-dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$.

papers.title: All unital reversible nonsymmetric rings of order 256
papers.authors: Jos\'e Mar\'ia Grau Ribas, Antonio M. Oller-Marc\'en
papers.abstract: A ring is reversible if $ab=0$ implies $ba=0$, and symmetric if $abc=0$ implies $acb=0$. Szabo proved that the smallest order of a unital reversible nonsymmetric ring is $256$. We classify all such minimal rings: up to isomorphism there are exactly $186$ of them, $19$ of characteristic $2$ and $167$ of characteristic $4$, and there are none of characteristic $8$ or higher. All of them are local with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$, the nilpotency index of the Jacobson radical is $4$ or $5$, and $120$ of them form $60$ pairs $R$, $R^{op}$ of non-isomorphic rings. The classification is obtained by a general method of deformation of graded algebras over $\mathbb{Z}/2^e\mathbb{Z}$, whose completeness is proved, and it is checked against the known examples: $\mathbb{F}_2Q_8$, Szabo's example and the ten rings in the family of generalized quaternion rings studied by Grau, Oller-Marc\'en and Szabo. The presentations of the $186$ rings and the code are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Diagnosis and Recovery in AI Workflows with Scarce Expert Capacity
papers.authors: Ruihan Zhou, Jiheng Zhang, Yijie Peng
papers.abstract: We study sequential decisions in AI workflows and other automated execution systems where failures of uncertain origin require recovery under limited shared expert capacity. Recovery choices affect future diagnostic demand, while expert availability changes which recovery actions are worthwhile. We coordinate diagnostic requests, expert dispatch, and checkpoint-based recovery to maximize expected net operating value. A finite-horizon model tracks uncertain error locations, remaining time, and shared expert capacity. Structural analysis shows how competition for diagnosis changes unaided recovery. When a full rebuild from checkpoint 0 is the best unaided fallback after failure, a larger expert pool can justify retaining more work despite a lower chance of immediate success. Capacity can also raise net operating value before fixed staffing costs while reducing diagnostic hours when advice is requested only after a failed trial. Our Diagnosis-Resource-Recovery Control (DRRC) policy coordinates these decisions through local recovery lookahead and estimates of service requirements and remaining time; its learning-augmented variant uses task-specific quality and duration estimates. In controlled simulations, larger pools draw more requests before repair, and selective diagnosis raises net value chiefly by reducing recovery costs. In a digital twin based on 177 software defects, DRRC with reference-assisted diagnosis increases mean timely completion by 3.27 percentage points and mean net value by 1.85% relative to automated recovery, although the net-value advantage remains uncertain across repositories. Expert capacity changes when workflows seek advice and how much work they preserve. Expansion may raise or lower diagnostic hours, so capacity and recovery design should be assessed jointly by their contribution to net operating value.

papers.title: Boundary singularities for weak solutions of semilinear elliptic problems throughout the subcritical range
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial \Omega$. We construct positive very weak solutions for the problem $\Delta u + u^p = 0$ in $\Omega$ for all $p \in [(N+1)/(N-1),(N+2)/(N-2))$ when $N \ge 3$ and for all $p \ge (N+1)/(N-1)$ when $N = 2$. These solutions vanish in a suitable trace sense on $\partial \Omega$ but are singular at prescribed isolated points. This gives a completely affirmative answer to a conjecture of del Pino-Musso-Pacard.

papers.title: Fano blowups of Grassmannians along sub-Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup of the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n+1)$ with $n\ge3$, in arbitrary characteristic, along sub-Grassmannians of codimension $r_1,\dotsc,r_s\ge2$ that meet transversely. We prove that, if $d\ne2$, then $\tilde X$ is Fano if and only if $\sum_i(r_i-1)\le n$, and we give a similar criterion for $d=2$. As applications, we prove that the successive blowup of $\mathbb{P}^4$ along $s$ planes that meet transversely is Fano if and only if $s\le4$. We also determine when the successive blowup of a smooth quadric fourfold along planes of one family that meet transversely is Fano.

papers.title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
papers.authors: Pramod Kumar Das, Manoj B. Prajapati
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms. Each of the chain transitive sub-systems obtained by Shin can be further decomposed into chain mixing systems by using the ideas of Richeson and Wiseman. Next, we use a probabilistic argument to recover both Smale-like and Bowen-like spectral decompositions for expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. Moreover, we investigate inter-relations among several variants of the shadowing property including the eventual shadowing property, the thick shadowing property, the ergodic shadowing property, the mean ergodic shadowing property and the $M_{\alpha}$-shadowing property.

papers.title: Subwavelength resonances and localization in finite resonator chains with a size defect
papers.authors: Yihao Gong, Haigang Li, Junhua Zhang
papers.abstract: We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $\tau\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $\tau_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<\tau<\tau_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $\tau\to\tau_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(\tau_*-\tau)^{-1/2}$. As $\tau\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $\tau^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $\tau$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

papers.title: Two Quintic Diophantine Equations and Fifth Powers in Fibonacci Sums at Distance Five
papers.abstract:
Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. We study the Diophantine
  equation $$
  F_{n+5}+F_n=y^5 $$ in positive integers $n$ and $y$. We prove that this equation has no solutions. The proof uses a recurrence identity to reduce the problem to the two equations $$
  X^2-5Z^5=44,\qquad X^2+44=5Z^5. $$ We show that the first equation has exactly the solutions $(X,Z)=(\pm7,1)$ for $Z>0$, and that the second has no such solutions. To obtain these results, we use ideal factorization in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11})$ and $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-11})$ and reduce the problem to six quintic Thue equations. Their complete solution sets are computed with the Magma Online Calculator and independently verified with PARI/GP.

papers.title: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce linearized multiplicity codes, which are a common generalization of linearized Reed--Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. We also introduce the ordered sum-rank metric, which is a common generalization of the sum-rank metric and the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric (or ordered Hamming metric). We provide a Singleton bound for the ordered sum-rank metric and show that linearized multiplicity codes attain it. That is, they are maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes. We introduce the support lattice for the ordered sum-rank metric and study duality, support distributions and weight distributions of MOSRD codes. We also show that MOSRD codes are ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under some divisibility conditions, MSRD (and thus MDS). For linear MOSRD codes, we give lower bounds on the field extension degree by the number of matrix columns, and upper bounds on the block length by the base field size. We conclude by showing that linearized multiplicity codes attain such bounds exactly in almost all cases, and the same growth order in all cases.

papers.title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: A Critical Choquard Problem for a Quasilinear Schr\"odinger Operator with Singular Discontinuous Nonlinearity
papers.authors: Ankit Mishra, Sarika Goyal, Divya Goel
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the quasilinear Schr\"odinger equation $-\Delta u - \Delta \bigl(|u|^{2\alpha}\bigr)\,|u|^{2\alpha-2}u =\lambda \left(\chi_{\{u<b\}} u^{-\beta}+\left(\int_\Omega \frac{H(y,u)}{\left|x-y\right|^\mu} dy\right)h(x,u)\right)$ in $\Omega$, $u>0$ in $\Omega$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded domain, $b>0$, $0<\mu<2$, $\alpha>\frac12$, $0<\beta<3$, and $h$ has critical exponential growth with primitive $H$. We show that there is $\lambda^*_b\in(0,\infty)$ such that the problem has a positive solution if and only if $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^*_b]$. For $\lambda<\lambda^*_b$, this solution is $g(v_\lambda)$, where the change of variables $g$ makes the problem semilinear and $v_\lambda$ is a local minimizer of the transformed energy in $H^1_0(\Omega)$. If $h$ satisfies a lower bound at the critical scale $\exp\bigl(2\alpha\,g^{-1}(u)^2\bigr)$, we obtain a second positive solution for every $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^*_b)$. The level estimate for this solution must be done at this scale, and not at the scale $e^{u^{4\alpha}}$ used for semilinear problems. This bound excludes $h=f\,e^{u^{4\alpha}}$ with $f$ of polynomial growth. For $\alpha>1$, we obtain a second solution for $h=u^{4\alpha-1}e^{u^{4\alpha}}$, provided that the maximum of the first solution exceeds a constant depending only on $\alpha$. For $\alpha\leq1$, this question remains open.

papers.title: Hidden symmetries and echolocation
papers.authors: Shilei Fan, Shi-Lei Kong, Yakun Xi
papers.abstract: We study the echolocation problem: whether local spectral data determine a point up to isometry. We characterize cospectrality by the existence of a spectral symmetry exchanging the two point evaluations and introduce a pointwise analogue of Sunada's method for constructing such symmetries. This yields cospectral, non-similar points on closed hyperbolic surfaces of every genus at least three and on round lens spaces. We also obtain Neumann examples on a scalene triangle and on a planar slit domain, and reinterpret a known Dirichlet example of Dixon, Miah, Safronov, Snyder, Vakaryuk, and Wyman through the same framework.

papers.title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
papers.abstract: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;\Lambda^k\right)$, where $\Lambda^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;\Lambda^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);\Lambda^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:\Lambda^{k+1}\rightarrow \Lambda^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.

papers.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
papers.authors: Youngae Lee, Haoyu Li, Juncheng Wei, Wen Yang, Lei Zhang
papers.abstract:
We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4\pi m,4\pi(m+1))\times(4\pi k,4\pi(k+1))$, then \[
  \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k
  =(1-x)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-y)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-xy)^{\chi(M)}, \] where $\chi(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block.
  At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4\pi,0)$ and $(8\pi,4\pi)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

papers.title: Dirichlet problems and Green functions for the octonionic Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.authors: Xi-Nan Ma, Wangzhe Wu, Jingyong Zhu
papers.abstract:
We study the Dirichlet problem for the octonionic Monge-Ampere equation on smooth bounded domains in the octonionic plane $\mathbb{O}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^{16}$. For a smooth positive density that is nondecreasing in the unknown function, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution whenever there is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution with the prescribed boundary values. The result also holds on relatively compact domains with smooth boundary in flat translation quotients.
  On smooth bounded strictly octonionic pseudoconvex domains, we construct the unique Green function with zero boundary values and singularity $-|q-a|^{-6}+O(1)$ at an interior pole $a$. We prove $C^{1,1}$ regularity locally up to the boundary away from the pole, together with sharp bounds for the gradient and the full real Hessian. The proof combines boundary estimates based on translations and spin rotations with weighted estimates obtained by differentiating along rotations and dilations.

papers.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.

papers.title: Projective Models of Genus 21 K3 Surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct projective models for general primitively polarized K3 surfaces $(S,h)$ of genus $21$ (degree $h^2=40$) inside the 12-dimensional fine quiver moduli space $X = N(3;3,4)$ parameterizing stable representations of the $3$-Kronecker quiver with dimension vector $(3,4)$. As a corollary, we show that the corresponding moduli space $\mathscr{M}_{21}$ is unirational and prove O'Grady's generalized Franchetta conjecture for genus $21$. Then we investigate the geometry of $(S,h)$ through its Fourier--Mukai partner $S' = M_{S}(4,h,5)$ and construct an explicit isomorphism $f : S^{[2]} \xrightarrow{\sim} S'^{[2]}$ together with a common closed embedding into the projectivization $\mathbb{P}^{17}$ of the space of global sections of the normalized universal bundle, using the polarization $H_2 - 4\delta_2$. Finally, we identify the Brill--Noether locus $\mathfrak{B} = \{Z \in S^{[3]} : h^0(F \otimes I_Z) \ge 2\}$ scheme-theoretically with the $\mathbb{P}^2$-bundle $Y' = \mathbb{P}_{S'}((F')^*)$ and exhibit an isomorphism $S^{[3]} \xrightarrow{\sim} M_{S'}(3,h',6)$.

papers.title: Two approaches of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift
papers.abstract: We investigate the problem of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift of the form: $X_t=\mu t + \sigma B_{H,\lambda}(t)$, for all $t\geq 0$. Based on discrete observations of $X$ and by using the method of moments with the ergodic theorem, we construct estimators of the drift parameter $\mu\in\R$ and noise parameters $ \sigma^2,H,\lambda \in(0,\infty)$. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, including convergence in probability, almost sure convergence, and asymptotic normality. Finally, by using Gladyshev's results \cite{gladyshev1961new} we provide some consistent alternative estimators of $\sigma^2$, $H$ and $\lambda$, when $\mu=0$ and $H\in (0,1)$.

papers.title: Weighted unit equations in cyclic cubic orders
papers.abstract: We study nonrational integral units $u,v$ satisfying $au+sv=1$, with integers $1<a<s$, in varying cyclic cubic fields. The ratio $u/v$ generates the joint order $R=\mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and gives effective finiteness for each fixed first weight and each fixed gap. Consecutive weights yield exactly seven simultaneous-isomorphism classes, at $a=2,4,13$; in every proper order among them, $\{-1,u,v\}$ generates $R^\times$.

papers.title: Stochastic Multivariate Taylor Measure Functions
papers.abstract: We introduce stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions (SMTMFs), which extend the multivariate Taylor measure function framework through random Taylor coefficients and a possibly random Taylor parameter. We establish their measurability properties and derive sufficient conditions for the associated processes to be martingales, including criteria based on conditional covariance and continuous semimartingale decompositions. We construct standard Brownian motion as an almost surely uniformly convergent limit of finite SMTMFs using the Levy-Ciesielski representation. We also show that the completion of the finite stochastic MTMF space under the expected uniform norm contains Brownian motion, Brownian bridges, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with integrable initial conditions. Our main result characterizes this completion as the Bochner space, under an admissibility condition on jointly measurable stochastic Taylor coefficients. The proof uses dyadic piecewise linear interpolation to approximate integrable continuous stochastic processes in the expected uniform norm. Thus, the completed SMTMF space encompasses the full class of integrable continuous random functions on a compact time interval.

papers.title: Dependence measures as spectral risk measures
papers.abstract: For a bivariate copula $C$ with $(U,V)\sim C$, the conditional distribution functions $L_t=\partial_1C(U,t)$ are random variables with means $t$, so that measures of directed dependence become risk functionals. The absolute Lorenz curves of the variables $L_t$ form the rearranged copula $C^\uparrow$. In this picture Chatterjee's rank correlation $\xi$ is a squared Sobolev seminorm and the rearranged Spearman correlation an $L^1$ norm of $C^\uparrow-\Pi$, and both arise from one spectral risk measure, applied either to the conditional laws of $V$ or to the laws of $L_t$. The resulting classes $\omega_\phi$ and $\kappa_\phi$ of spectral dependence measures have mirror-image axiomatic properties. For every spectrum we determine the exact upper bound of $\kappa_\phi$ in terms of $\xi$, and we prove sharp inequalities between $\xi$, $\kappa_\phi$ and the values of $C^\uparrow$, which show how little global measures say about the tails. For plug-in estimators based on the empirical checkerboard copula we obtain consistency, rates and a resolution limit, and a simulation study shows that tail-localised measures separate copulas with identical $\xi$. An application to large credit portfolios illustrates the results.

papers.title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
papers.authors: Sebastian Gwizdek, Sergiusz Ku\.zel, Witold Majdak
papers.abstract: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foia\c{s} dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is on explicit constructions, direct proofs, and a common framework for known results.

papers.title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.

papers.title: Fundamental groups of closed four-manifolds with positive biorthogonal curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a group is the fundamental group of a closed, connected, oriented smooth four-manifold admitting a metric of positive biorthogonal curvature if and only if it is finitely presented. This answers a question of Bettiol. The manifold can be chosen to be stably parallelizable, hence spin with vanishing signature, and with Euler characteristic $2(1-p+q)$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of generators and of nontrivial relators in a given finite presentation. Moreover, we show that the class of closed oriented four-manifolds admitting positive biorthogonal curvature is closed under surgery along embedded circles. As applications, we obtain metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on the boundary of every compact oriented five-manifold that has a handle decomposition with handles of index at most two, which includes every oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. We also obtain such metrics on $Y\times S^1$ for every closed orientable three-manifold $Y$ of positive scalar curvature and, after connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$, on a large class of four-manifolds with arbitrary fundamental group. Finally, we show that for the fundamental group of a finite aspherical two-dimensional complex $X$ the minimal Euler characteristic of such manifolds equals $2\chi(X)$.

papers.title: Simple abelian varieties with prescribed endomorphism ratio
papers.abstract:
Let $A$ be a simple abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, and set $m(A)=2\dim A/[\operatorname{End}^0(A):\mathbb Q]$. We prove that, for every prime $p$ and every positive rational number $\mu$, there exist simple abelian varieties of characteristic $p$ with endomorphism ratio $\mu$, both of $p$-rank zero and of positive $p$-rank. In particular, we answer a question of Oort in a stronger form.
  Our construction combines Honda-Tate theory with explicit deformations of $p$-divisible groups using Breuil windows. An explicit Frobenius matrix, realized in a window with quaternionic multiplication, gives two reduced generic slopes with coprime denominators. Their coprimality, together with specialization and constancy of dimension, determines the full geometric endomorphism algebra. Polarized Serre-Tate theory and Grothendieck algebraization lift these deformations to abelian schemes. A related construction with an additional etale factor yields the positive-$p$-rank result.

papers.title: On the planar four-junction solution to a vector-valued Allen-Cahn system
papers.authors: Nicholas D. Alikakos, Giorgio Fusco, Zhiyuan Geng
papers.abstract: This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

papers.title: A Graph Theory Assisted Method for Determining Limiting Probability Distributions of Higher Order Markov Chains
papers.abstract: This paper presents a graph theory assisted method that checks a sufficient condition for the existence of the limiting probability distribution of a higher order Markov chain and identifies this distribution when the condition is satisfied. This method is more effective as compared to the direct verification of the condition since the latter hinges wholly on computations of the full spectrum on a large-size transition matrix. Even though the graph theoretic tools employed here are well known, their utilization in the context of a higher order Markov chain is new. This method is also implemented as an easy-to-use MATLAB function {\tt gtam}. Several illustrative examples are provided too.

papers.title: Isometries for Hilbert's metric on vector lattices of continuous functions
papers.abstract: In this paper Hilbert's projective metric on the interior of the positive cone of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong order unit is studied. We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of H\"older continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric completion, but that no two of them are isometric.

papers.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $\xi \in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$.

papers.title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
papers.abstract:
Let $\phi_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|\phi_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[
  \Phi\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right)
  \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a)
  \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

papers.title: Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift: process limits, estimated weights and efficiency
papers.abstract: Weighted split conformal prediction handles covariate shift by reweighting calibration scores with the likelihood ratio $v=dQ_X/dP_X$; its training-conditional coverage is a functional of the self-normalized weighted empirical distribution function $\hat F_m$, and we study the process $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$. It converges in $\ell^\infty$ to the Gaussian process $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$, with $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ and $K^2=1+\chi^2(Q\|P)$, if and only if $\chi^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ (for non-degenerate scores); $\sup v$ plays no role. The limit gives the joint law of the coverage across levels, consistent bootstraps, inflations asymptotically exact uniformly in the level, and Berry-Esseen-type rates. With estimated ratios, a uniform expansion remains valid when the estimate uses the calibration covariates; the estimation error enters through a covariance term that can reduce the variance below the oracle's, and a pairs bootstrap reproduces it. When the ratio is known, the weighted conformal threshold is semiparametrically efficient if and only if the ratio and the coverage indicator are uncorrelated under the test distribution, with an explicit efficient correction otherwise. When $\chi^2(Q\|P)=\infty$, the ratio has a regularly varying tail of index $p\in(1,2)$ and the score decouples from it in the far tail, the finite-dimensional limits are $p$-stable at the rate $m^{1-1/p}$ up to a slowly varying factor.

papers.title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $\mu$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $\mu$) admit a common minimal model.

papers.title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
papers.abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

papers.title: Controllability of Acoustic Waves by Point Sources: Reachable States and Stable Reconstruction
papers.abstract:
We study the terminal controllability of the three-dimensional acoustic wave equation driven by finitely many fixed point sources, with zero initial data and time-dependent amplitudes supported in a finite interval. Although finitely many fixed sources cannot control the whole energy space, we establish the following results:
  (i) For source amplitudes in the first-order Sobolev space in time, the terminal state has finite energy if and only if all amplitudes vanish at both endpoints of the control interval.
  (ii) We derive an exact frequency-domain identity for the terminal energy involving a Gram matrix whose diagonal entries are one and whose off-diagonal entries are given by the sinc function, depending on frequency and source separation.
  (iii) For every positive control time, the terminal control operator is bounded below and is an isomorphism onto its closed reachable range, which has infinite codimension even among states satisfying the finite-propagation support condition.
  (iv) We establish a necessary and sufficient radiation-field criterion for reachability, provide stable reconstruction of the unique controls, and characterize the best approximation of non-reachable targets.
  The optimal coercivity constant equals one before the shortest source travel time. At long times, it decays as the inverse square of the control time for two sources and as the inverse fourth power for three equally spaced collinear sources. We also obtain upper bounds for general configurations and illustrate the theoretical results through reproducible Galerkin computations.

papers.title: A DGLA approach to global extensions and deformations of Lie algebras
papers.authors: Jun Jiang, Chuijia Wang, Kanghe Xu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global extension problem of Lie algebras from the perspective of dgLas and the Maurer--Cartan formulism. We propose a new equivalence relation of global extensions, generalizing the early work of Agore and Militaru. This new concept can be better adopted in the study of classical contraction and deformation problems for Lie algebras. Meanwhile, we construct dgLas that control based formal deformations of global extension structures under these equivalences. As byproducts, we obtain the classification of infinitesimal deformations in terms of the cohomology of the controlling dgLas and the corresponding obstruction theory. We relate the dgLa controlling deformation of global extensions under framed equivalence to that of non-abelian extensions constructed by Fr\'egier, obtaining a geometric interpretation of the decomposition of global cohomology into as a disjoint union of non-abelian cohomology. As an application, we study a particular family of an In\"on\"u--Wigner contraction from $\g\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ to $V_{\mathrm{ab}}\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ in the framework of global extension, deformation, and the dgLa approach.

papers.title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
papers.authors: Askar Tuganbaeva, Unsal Tekir, Suat Koc, Gulsen Ulucak
papers.abstract: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

papers.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$\lambda:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Deligne pairing isomorphisms for projective duals and higher-rank associated hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Given a family \pi:X\to S of complex projective varieties, polarised by a (sufficiently) relatively very ample L, we give an isomorphism between a Deligne pairing involving higher relative cotangent Chern classes, and the relative projective dual line X^\vee(L). As a consequence, we obtain explicit Deligne pairing isomorphisms for all of the higher associated hypersurfaces of Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky, including mixed polarisations, as well as higher-rank versions of such hypersurfaces involving sufficiently positive vector bundles.

papers.title: Stability of Plasma Echo Growth and the Sharp Sobolev Stability Threshold for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau Equation
papers.abstract:
We establish stability of growing plasma echo cascades for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau equation with Coulomb collisions near a global Maxwellian. The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $
u^{1/3}[\log(1/
u)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $
u^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.

papers.title: Multiplicity of sign-changing solutions to higher-order $Q$-curvature equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we employ the dual cone method to establish the existence of infinitely many sign-changing solutions to the $Q$-curvature problem involving $GJMS$-operators of arbitrary order $m$ on closed Riemannian manifolds of dimension $n > 2m$, under the assumptions that the operators are coercive and positivity-preserving and that the manifold admits appropriate symmetries. To demonstrate the applicability of our framework, we provide explicit examples on both closed Einstein manifolds and closed special Einstein products. Notably, one of the major contributions of this work is deriving explicit conditions that guarantee the coercivity of $GJMS$-operators on closed special Einstein products.

papers.title: Test of p-rationality of a number field--pari/gp programs
papers.abstract: We give a new computational approach of p-rationality of a number field k, when the method using ray class groups is out of reach in a reasonable time when the degree of k and p are too large. The method is based for a part on the utilisation of the Logp-function that we have defined in the 80's. The general pari/gp program makes no assumptions about k and p. For quadratic fields, we give other programs giving more information (surprisingly these programs, with many instructions, are much faster).

papers.title: Structure of gaps and generalized Wilf's conjecture
papers.authors: Om Prakash Bhardwaj, Carmelo Cisto, Priyavrat Deshpande
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the gaps, the maximal gaps, and the pseudo-Frobenius elements of generalized numerical semigroups of minimum embedding dimension. For these semigroups, we give an explicit description of the set of gaps, explicit formulas for the genus and the number of maximal gaps, and an explicit description of the set of pseudo-Frobenius elements in terms of the blocks of consecutive gaps of an associated numerical semigroup. In particular, we obtain an explicit formula for the type. As a consequence, we show that the type is unbounded even in minimum embedding dimension. Further, we prove that every generalized numerical semigroup with minimum embedding dimension has at least as many non-gaps below its gaps as gaps, and therefore satisfies the generalized Wilf's conjecture. We also prove the conjecture for generalized numerical semigroups in $\mathbb{N}^2$ graded by two-generated numerical semigroups, and asymptotically in higher dimension. For an arbitrary generalized numerical semigroup we bound the number of non-gaps below the gaps in terms of the genus and the type. Finally, we introduce nearly-symmetric generalized numerical semigroups and classify them in minimum embedding dimension. Although the type is unbounded in minimum embedding dimension generalized numerical semigroups, nearly-symmetric ones have type at most two.

papers.title: On Win's Conjecture for Edge-Disjoint Perfect Matchings
papers.authors: Yufei Chang, Yangyang Cheng, Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei
papers.abstract: In 1982, Win conjectured that, for every even integer $n$ and every integer $k$ $1\le k\le n-2$, any graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $d_G(x)+d_G(y)\ge n+k-2$ for every pair of nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings. In this paper, we prove a stronger result for all sufficiently large even $n$. More precisely, we show that under the same degree-sum condition, $G$ contains $\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, together with an additional perfect matching when $k$ is odd, all pairwise edge-disjoint. Consequently, we confirm Win's conjecture for all sufficiently large even $n$, with a threshold independent of $k$.

papers.title: Weighted composition operators between Qp spaces: Boundedness and compactness
papers.authors: Wujun Cao, Zhouyuan Jiang, Songxiao Li
papers.abstract: We characterize boundedness and compactness of weighted composition operators $W_{u,\varphi}:Q_{p_1}\to Q_{p_2}$, where $W_{u,\varphi}f=u(f\circ\varphi)$, $p_1>0$, and $0<p_2<1$. A separation theorem for the two terms in $(W_{u,\varphi}f)'$, together with value and derivative embedding theorems, gives two capacity conditions on $u$ and $\varphi$. For $p_1=1$ and $p_1>1$, the derivative condition has a maximal-integral and an area-integral form respectively.

papers.title: A Solution to the Birkhoff Problem
papers.abstract: For a commutative uniserial ring $R$ of length $n$ we describe the indecomposable objects in the monomorphism category of $R$ independent of the specific ring for $n\leq 5$ and only dependent on the residue field for $n = 6$. Thus, the classification problem for the monomorphism category of $\mathbb{Z}/p^6 \mathbb{Z}$ reduces to the known case of $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^6)$, resolving the Birkhoff Problem.

papers.title: Interacting Brownian Particles with Local Time Driven Jumps and Memory
papers.abstract: We study a system of Brownian particles on the real line whose jump intensities are excited by pairwise collision local times and decay exponentially between encounters. For every finite number of particles and every interaction strength, we construct a global solution and prove uniqueness in law. Under mean-field scaling, exchangeable chaotic initial data, and uniform integrability of the initial intensities, we prove propagation of chaos on path space. The limit is a nonlinear jump-diffusion whose intensity is driven by the density of its own position; it is unique among such processes with locally bounded mean intensity. The proof combines uniform intensity and local-time estimates, tightness of particle and pair empirical measures, identification of conditional collision local times, and a coupling argument for nonlinear uniqueness. No moment assumptions are imposed on the initial positions or the jump-size distribution.

papers.title: Stability of Carath\'eodory Outer Measures Generated by Spatial Gauges
papers.authors: Ren\'e Erlin Castillo, H\'ector Camilo Chaparro
papers.abstract: We study outer measures generated by covering costs that depend on both the diameter and the location of a covering set. After establishing the metric and Borel-regularity properties of this construction, we investigate its stability under perturbations of the spatial gauge. For power gauges, we prove a uniform logarithmic criterion: if the exponent perturbation multiplied by $\log(1/r)$ converges uniformly to $\lambda$, then the induced measure is multiplied by $e^{-\lambda}$. Pointwise asymptotic equivalence, however, is insufficient: on $[0,1]$ we construct bounded gauges whose ratio is eventually equal to one at every fixed point, although their induced measures differ by a prescribed factor. In the converse direction, continuity of the ratio in the spatial variable on a Baire space yields equality of the measures on every compact subset of a suitable dense $G_\delta$ set. The results identify a concrete obstruction to pointwise-to-measure stability and a localization principle, while leaving open the corresponding question for all Borel sets.

papers.title: Embedding of Barnes-Wall lattices into Cayley-Dickson algebras
papers.abstract: The family of Barnes-Wall lattices includes the balanced Barnes-Wall lattice $M_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ and two ordinary Barnes-Wall lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, which are geometrically equivalent to each other. Embedding of these lattices into the Cayley-Dickson algebras of an appropriate dimension is considered. It is shown that for all $n \geq 2$ the lattices $M_n$ and $L_n$ are closed under multiplication and are generated by the sets of pairwise products of their elements. The lattices $L_n \cdot L'_n$, $L'_n \cdot L_n$, and $L'_n \cdot L'_n$, generated by pairwise products of elements of the lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$, also are studied.

papers.title: The dual of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is an infinitary variety of algebras
papers.abstract: A metric compact Hausdorff space is a Lawvere metric space equipped with a compatible compact Hausdorff topology (which does not need to be the induced topology). These spaces maintain many important features of compact metric spaces, but the resulting category is much better behaved. We prove that the category of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is dually equivalent to a variety of infinitary algebras.

papers.title: An abstract observability criterion via translation hulls, with applications to transport systems
papers.abstract: We establish an observability criterion for translation-covariant families of operators on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$. Under continuity of the observed cell energies, a common summable localization bound, and reconstruction up to a locally collectively compact error, observability is equivalent to the absence of nonzero uniformly local invisible states on every configuration in the full translation hull. For one-dimensional transport systems satisfying the Kalman rank condition, this yields localized observability in the intrinsic Kalman--Jordan energy space for arbitrary real Jordan structure and nonzero speeds. For unions of observed intervals with a uniform positive lower length bound, the sharp condition is that the slowest characteristic travels farther than the gap supremum. Observability fails at equality even when this supremum is not attained. Duality gives exact controllability in the dual energy space. We also obtain sharp criteria for translating observation regions and scalar transport with an integrable convolution kernel. The reconstruction hypothesis is also necessary for observability. An anisotropic heat-flux example shows that it applies beyond coercive multiplication-plus-compact Gramian decompositions.

papers.title: Totally Positive Interpolation and Critical Sampling of Positive Operator Orbits
papers.abstract: How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous functional calculus, including explicit resolvent bases. In the case of normal operators, we give a single-orbit frame for which every admissible weighted design has sampling count growing faster than the radial spectral count.

papers.title: Gordan-Rankin-Cohen brackets on $1|n$-dimensional superstrings with a contact structure for $n\leq 6$
papers.authors: Sofiane Bouarroudj, Dimitry Leites, Oleksandr Lozhechnyk, Irina Shchepochkina
papers.abstract:
The binary projectively $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant differential operators between spaces of weighted densities on the 1-dimensional manifold are called Gordan transvectants or Rankin-Cohen (GRC) brackets. For the two contact series (with an even and an odd ``time'' variable) on the supercircle or superstring of dimension $1|2$, we describe analogs of GRC brackets. We have discovered many new operators. For $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|2)$, the space of invariant binary operators of every given order is $2$-dimensional for all weights of the densities, not only for the weights considered so far. For $\mathfrak{pe}(2)\subset\mathfrak{m}(1)$, there are three independent binary operators of order $2$, not two. While classifying them, we correct an earlier result on the unary operators: the order-$2$ Bol operator over $\mathfrak{m}(1)$ is only one member of a $1$-parameter family invariant for all weights, which corrects Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:2110.10504.
  We correct earlier findings in the $1|3$-dimensional case and consider $\mathfrak{osp}_a(4|2)$-invariant (GRC) brackets in $1|4$-dimensional case, where the order-$2$ bracket is independent of the parameter $a$ and is invariant under the whole of $\mathfrak{k}(1|4)$. In the $1|5$-dimensional case, the analogs of Bol operators are odd, of order $5+2k$, where $k=0,1,2,\dots$, and so is the first GRC bracket of odd order, which is of order $5$. We also settle the exceptional case $\mathfrak{as}\subset\mathfrak{kas}\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|6)$.

papers.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
papers.abstract: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(\tau)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $\tau$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

papers.title: Augmented Lagrangian methods with Nesterov acceleration for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop Nesterov accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods for composite convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints. The methods are derived through a compatible discretization of inertial primal-dual dynamics, yielding a unified framework that couples difference extrapolation of the constraint mapping with a projected multiplier. Under convexity and weighted summability of the primal stationarity errors, we prove boundedness of the primal-dual iterates and simultaneous $\mathcal O(k^{-2})$ last-iterate rates for the objective residual and constraint violation. Under strict parameter conditions, the primal-dual sequence converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker pair, and both residuals improve to $o(k^{-2})$. These results require no strong convexity of the objective or constraints. Numerical experiments examine the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.abstract:
We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity.
  In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

papers.title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
papers.abstract: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

papers.title: The Estermann Problem with Almost Proportional Summands
papers.abstract:
We obtain a family of estimates for short Weyl sums $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2\pi i\alpha m^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{s-1}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}} \bigl(\log(qy)\bigr)^{ \frac{(n-1)^s+s-2}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}}, $$ where $n\ge3$ and $s\ge2$ are fixed integers, $x\ge y\ge2$, $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $a\in\mathbb Z$, $q\in\mathbb N$, $(a,q)=1$, and $\left|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}\right|\le\frac{1}{q^2}$.
  For $n\ge4$, we also derive from the modern form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem the estimate $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2\pi i\alpha m^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{n(n-1)+2}} \log y. $$
  Using these estimates, repeated Dirichlet approximation, and an estimate in the intermediate range, we establish an asymptotic formula for the number of representations $$ p_1+p_2+m^n=N,\quad |p_i-\mu_iN|\le H,\quad i=1,2, \quad |m^n-\mu_3N|\le H, $$ where $p_1,p_2$ are primes, $m$ is a positive integer, and $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ are fixed positive numbers whose sum is $1$. The asymptotic formula holds in the range $$ N^{1-\theta_n}(\log N)^{A_n}\le H\le N^{1-\delta}, \qquad \theta_n=\min\left\{\frac{1}{2n},\frac{2}{n^2}\right\}, $$ where $0<\delta<\theta_n$ is fixed, $A_3=3$, $A_4=\frac{61}{4}$, and $A_n=6n-12+\frac{22}{n}-\frac{12}{n^2}$ for $n\ge5$. In the cubic case, the logarithmic exponent in the previously known lower bound for $H$ is reduced from $10$ to $3$. For $n\ge4$, the exponent of $N$ is reduced from $1-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}$ to $1-\frac{2}{n^2}$.

papers.title: Arc connected continua and the double commutant property
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact metrizable space. For $f\in C(K)$ let $M_f$ be the largest lower semicontinuous map with $k\in M_f(k)\subseteq f^{-1}(f(k))$. We say that $K$ has the double commutant property if for every $f\in C(K)$ every continuous function that is constant on all sets $M_f(k)$ is constant on the fibres of $f$; this is exactly the condition that the double commutant of every multiplication operator on $C(K)$ is the closed algebra generated by the operator and the identity. We show that an arc connected continuum has this property if the points having an open locally connected neighbourhood are dense, and we extend this to some continua that are not arc connected. We then develop new techniques that work when such points are not dense, or do not exist at all, and prove that several well-known continua have the property: the Cantor comb, the Cantor fan and, more generally, the cone over every compact metrizable space, every smooth fan with a closed set of end points, and the Cantor grid $(C\times[0,1])\cup([0,1]\times C)$. The property passes to open images. Examples show that the hypotheses cannot be weakened in several directions. For individual functions we show that, on a continuum all of whose arc components are dense, every function that is constant on no arc satisfies the double commutant condition, and that on every smooth dendroid and every fan the functions satisfying it are dense.

papers.title: Causality and order restricted inference in the Aalen additive hasard model
papers.abstract:
We study a graphical model (DAG) with time to event as a response variable. We use the Aalen additive hazard model for modelling the effect on the response variable of covariates, combined with a multiple linear regression for earlier layers in a DAG. This enables modelling covariates affecting the event process both directly and indirectly. The indirect component effect is represented by a product $\theta_1(t)\beta_2(t)$, where $\theta_1(t)$ describes the effect of the independent covariate on the dependent covariate and $\beta_2(t)$ is the effect of the dependent covariate on the final time to response variable, in the additive hazard model. We estimate $\beta_2(t)$ by the order-restricted estimator recently introduced in Anevski and Merai (arXiv:2606.23882v2), thereby enabling disease models with early onset or late onset covariate effects. Combining our previously obtained results with the DAG allows for modelling early onset or late onset covariate effects together with direct and indirect covariate effects, which should be of particular interest for studying causality for complex diseases.
  We present a nonparametric plug-in estimator of the indirect effect. We derive the limit distribution of the plug-in estimator of the indirect component, and show that it has $n^{1/3}$ pointwise asymptotic rate and a limit distribution which is proportional to the Chernoff distribution.

papers.title: Joint quadratic base changes of elliptic surfaces with torsion Z/4Z and Z/2Z x Z/6Z
papers.abstract:
We study elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ obtained from an elliptic surface by imposing two quadratic conditions, each of which produces a new point. By the Kani-Rosen decomposition, the joint cover is rational only when the branch loci of the two conditions meet; for two quadratic conditions this means that they share a root. We apply this to two surfaces.
  For Elkies's rank-four K3 surface with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, a catalogue of $194$ quadratic conditions contains exactly two such pairs. One recovers the rank-six curve of the authors; the other gives a second, inequivalent curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank six.
  For the universal curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$, $42$ conditions give exactly $21$ rational joint covers, which yield seven curves of rank two. Two more arise from a tower of conditions. Five of these nine curves are the curves of Dujella, Kazalicki and Peral; the other four are not equivalent to any of them.
  In both cases we determine the Mordell-Weil groups over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ exactly, and we prove that the curves are pairwise inequivalent under invertible changes of parameter, even over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

papers.title: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set. This improves on known results for independent sets in uniform hypergraphs; in particular, in a linear uniform hypergraph of large bounded degree, we find an independent set of explicit asymptotic size. Among the applications, we obtain complete arcs in finite projective spaces that come within logarithmic factors of the counting lower bound, improving the known results on Segre's complete arc problem. We also show that, for a wide class of multivariable polynomials, there is a maximal set in a finite field avoiding solutions of the polynomial whose size lies within logarithmic factors of the elementary lower bound.

papers.title: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.

papers.title: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
papers.abstract: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

papers.title: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
papers.authors: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Marcela Ribeiro, Nancy Saravia-Molina
papers.abstract: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in dimension three. Using the theory of higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of foliations in dimension two, we introduce these invariants for pairs of plane germs. For every order, we show that the higher-order Milnor number of a pair is determined by the Milnor number of the pair and the algebraic multiplicity of the associated foliation, and we compute the difference between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of the pair. Finally, we establish a bifurcation formula comparing the higher-order Milnor number of a pair with that of the product of the germs. As a consequence, we characterize semitame meromorphic germs as those for which these two numbers agree at some order, or equivalently at every order.

papers.title: Phase Transitions in Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation under $\ell_p$ Norms
papers.authors: Ishaq Aden-Ali, Yeshwanth Cherapanamjeri, Mikael M{\o}ller H{\o}gsgaard, Kasper Green Larsen, Nikita Zhivotovskiy
papers.abstract: We study the problem of estimating the mean of a random vector in $\mathbb R^d$ under $\ell_p$ norms, assuming only the existence of a covariance matrix. In the Euclidean norm, the sample mean is already optimal in expectation, and robust estimators are usually needed only to obtain high-probability tails. Our results show that this picture changes for $\ell_p$ norms with $p>2$: robustification is already necessary even for the expected risk. We prove that the minimax risk exhibits a sharp phase transition, controlled by the interaction between the sample size $n$, the dimension $d$, and the norm parameter $p$. In the large-sample regime, the classical Gaussian rate remains achievable. In the complementary regime, heavy-tailed distributions create a genuinely non-Gaussian obstruction. Furthermore we show that the simple estimator: coordinate-wise median of means whose number of buckets chosen according to the geometry of the loss, optimally tracks this phase transition in its expected risk minimax. We also show that natural projection-based median-of-means estimators for general norms, despite achieving the optimal confidence trade-off relative to the sample-mean benchmark of Lugosi and Mendelson (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2019), can be polynomially suboptimal for $\ell_p$ norms even in the constant-probability regime.

papers.title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
papers.abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.

papers.title: Unirationality of Meromorphic Differential Strata
papers.abstract: We prove that all components of the meromorphic differential strata are unirational in genus $2\le g\le 5$ and with relatively low number of poles. In particular, it follows that the moduli space of pointed even spin curves $\mathcal{S}_{5;1}^+=\mathcal{S}_5^+\times_{\mathcal{M}_5}\mathcal{M}_{5,1}$ is unirational.

papers.title: Two categorifications of the Kekul\'e relations
papers.authors: Jernej Grlj, Ziyi Lei, Emmanuel Wagner
papers.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelul\'e relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

papers.title: Curves in $\PP^{3}$ are Complete Intersections or Golod
papers.abstract: Let $I\subset S$ be an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal in a regular local ring, or an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal that is homogeneous in a positively graded polynomial ring over a field. We prove the statement of the title when $\pd_{S}(S/I) \leq 3$, and conjecture that this dichotomy holds in codimension 2 with any projective dimension.

papers.title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Yu Gao, Jiayu Qiu
papers.abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.

papers.title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
papers.authors: Claudiu G. Pop, George C. Rad, George C. \c{T}urca\c{s}
papers.abstract: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$.
