  For a nilpotent $\mu\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we present algorithms that construct $C(\mu)$, its subset of idempotents, and its subsemigroup of nilpotents, thereby determining their cardinalities. We also describe the nilpotents whose centralizers consist only of idempotents, of nilpotents together with the identity, or of nilpotents and idempotents. We extend these descriptions to arbitrary elements of $\mathcal{C}_n$.
  To obtain our results, we represent $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$ as a sequence $\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle$ of rooted trees. The sets of vertices of the trees form a partition of $X_n$. Each tree is level-ordered, which means that it can be drawn in such a way that moving from the root down, level by level, from left to right at each level, we pass through an increasing sequence of consecutive elements of $X_n$.

papers.title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
papers.abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, {\O}bro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

papers.title: The random analyst
papers.abstract: Modern data-analysis pipelines increasingly involve searching among candidate analyses before reporting an estimate. We investigate the replicability of the resulting conclusions by studying independent repetitions of the entire search-and-report procedure on new samples. Can the reported estimates become increasingly similar across studies while remaining systematically displaced from the scientific target? We first show that this can happen in a simple Gaussian model. Although every prespecified candidate estimator is unbiased and consistent, searching over exponentially many candidates within each study yields a selected estimator converging to a limit different from the target, a selection-induced pseudotruth. Across independent repetitions, the reported estimates thus become replicable but systematically inaccurate, while the selected candidates differ with probability tending to one. We then study dependent Gaussian candidates, including marginal regression coefficients, and show that Gaussian width governs the displacement, which persists when squared width is of the same order as sample size. Metric entropy and generic chaining reveal that the effective complexity of the search is determined by the geometry of statistically distinguishable analyses rather than by their nominal number. Large-deviation arguments further extend the phenomenon beyond Gaussian models. Numerical agreement between independent studies therefore need not indicate either a stable analytical path or proximity to the scientific target.

papers.title: A hyperhamiltonian approach to symmetry of the Dirac equation
papers.abstract: The Dirac equation is the simplest wave equation invariant under the Poincar\'e group, and was indeed determined by Dirac precisely by requiring this invariance. Moreover it is invariant under dilations of the wave function, as follows by its linear character. It is known that the Dirac equation possesses, besides these, other symmetries, which in this sense are the special part of the Dirac equation's full symmetry. In previous work we have shown that the Dirac equation can be cast in hyperhamiltonian terms. Here we show that the symmetries can also be described in hyperhamiltonian terms.

papers.title: Stochastic control representations for extremal solutions of HJB Dirichlet problems with measurable coefficients
papers.authors: David Criens, Hyungbin Park, Jongjin Park
papers.abstract: We study stochastic control problems for uniformly elliptic controlled diffusions on bounded domains whose coefficients are merely measurable in the state variable and whose drift is dominated by an $L_d$-function. The associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) Dirichlet problems may have more than one $L_p$-viscosity solution, so that the equation alone does not determine the value function. We show that the control problem selects the minimal solution: for all $p$ in a range $(d_0,d)$ determined by the spatial dimension, the ellipticity constant and the drift bound, the value function is the minimal $L_p$-viscosity supersolution of the HJB Dirichlet problem. In particular, every continuous $L_p$-viscosity supersolution bounds the optimal cost from above, which yields a one-sided verification theorem without regularity assumptions. We further prove the existence of optimal relaxed control rules for running costs dominated by an $L_p$-function, and the lower semicontinuity of the value function under perturbations of the coefficients. An example shows that upper semicontinuity may fail even when the coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in the control variable and the approximating coefficients are smooth, so that regularization may overestimate the optimal cost. The proof approximates arbitrary supersolutions from below by Sobolev supersolutions of HJB equations whose coefficients are modified only on sets of vanishing measure, and passes to the limit by means of Krylov estimates and martingale problem techniques.

papers.title: Design of an optimal positive state observer for a diffusion system with point observation
papers.abstract: An optimal state observer design problem for a diffusion system with point observation is studied. As the considered system is positive, the analysis takes into account this additional condition. The solution of the optimization problem is derived by means of a discretization approach, which consists in considering the analogous problem adapted for a spatially discretized version of the pure diffusion system.

papers.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
papers.abstract: We prove that $G$-Fano threefolds which are given by the blow-up of a smooth quadric along a twisted quartic curve are $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. We also prove that the action of $G$ is linearisable if and only if $G$ does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

papers.title: Explicit Tartakowsky theorem and universality criterion sets over totally real number fields
papers.authors: Vitezslav Kala, Siu Hang Man, Robin Visser, Pavlo Yatsyna
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit version of Tartakowsky's theorem over all totally real number fields. Namely, a positive definite integral lattice of rank at least five represents every totally positive integer that it represents locally, provided that the norm of the integer exceeds an explicit bound, exponential in powers of the volume of the lattice and of the discriminant of the field. As an application, we give explicit criterion sets for universal quadratic forms over all but finitely many real quadratic fields. Finally, we determine the minimal criterion sets for an infinite family of real quadratic fields.

papers.title: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

papers.title: N\'eron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We express N\'eron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate N\'eron functions to local N\'eron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic N\'eron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the N\'eron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

papers.title: Policy Iteration Convergence for Exploratory Two-State Mean-Field Control Problems
papers.authors: Zhenhua Wang, Xiaoli Wei, Xiang Yu
papers.abstract: This paper studies the theoretical policy iteration convergence for two-state mean-field control (MFC) problems with Wright--Fisher common noise under entropy regularization. The population dynamics lead to a degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation of Kimura type. After an arcsine transformation, the degeneracy becomes a singular Bessel drift whose coefficients and weights depend on the feedback stochastic policy. This policy dependence prevents a direct application of estimates for a fixed operator. We establish weighted Sobolev estimates and H\"older embeddings uniformly over the admissible policy class. Combining these estimates with logarithmic entropy bounds and boundary estimates that remain valid when the policy changes, we prove the well-posedness, monotone improvement and convergence of policy iteration to the optimal solution. We also establish the convergence to the original MFC problem when the entropy parameter $\lambda$ tends to zero. Both the regularization error and the performance loss of the regularized optimal policy are bounded by $O(\lambda(1+|\ln\lambda|))$ in a weighted H\"older norm. An epidemic containment example of MFC is presented to illustrate the policy iteration convergence and the vanishing entropy convergence.

papers.title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
papers.authors: Vyacheslav M. Boyko, Oleksandra V. Lokaziuk
papers.abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

papers.title: Vanishing Dissipation Limit to Planar Euler Shock for the Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove the vanishing dissipation limit to a weak planar Euler shock for the full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The viscosity and heat conductivity are proportional to $\varepsilon$, with their ratio fixed. The conservative initial perturbation may depend on all three spatial variables and is assumed small only in the scaled $H^2 \cap \dot H^{-1}$ norm. No $L^1$ bound or zero-mass condition is required. For these data, we obtain a unique global strong solution and an energy estimate uniform in time and in $\varepsilon$. On every cylinder with a measurable transverse section of finite positive area, the $L^2$ error has an explicit leading term, yielding the sharp rate $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$. The remainder has order $\varepsilon^{3/2}$ times the scaled initial norm; both estimates are uniform for $t \geq 0$. If this norm tends to zero, convergence away from the shock front is uniform in time, including at $t=0$. The entropy production measures converge locally weakly to the measure carried by the Euler shock. Low frequencies are controlled by an entropy-weighted elliptic estimate. At second order, integration by parts in the pressure and viscous heating terms leaves at most two derivatives on the density, while third derivatives of velocity and temperature enter only through the time-integrated dissipation.

papers.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
papers.abstract: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

papers.title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $\Phi:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$\alpha\big((\Phi(A)-\Phi(B))\Phi(C)\big) =\alpha\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $\alpha$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.

papers.title: Sums of Integers with Small Prime Factors
papers.abstract:
Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$, with $P^+(1)=1$. We prove that, for every $\beta>103/(256\sqrt e)$, there is a constant $C=C(\beta)>0$ such that every sufficiently large integer $N$ can be written as $N=a+b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and
  $$
  P^+(a)\leq N^\beta,\qquad P^+(b)\leq(\log N)^C.
  $$
  This strengthens Balog's result, which gives two $N^\beta$-smooth summands for $\beta>4/(9\sqrt e)$. The proof combines Balog's argument with convolution estimates that are uniform in the residue class.

papers.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
papers.authors: Cisca Kalmijn, Walter D. van Suijlekom
papers.abstract: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

papers.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

papers.title: Cassini ovals, translated polynomials, and the arithmetic of their discriminants and resultants
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $f$, $a>0$ and $b,\omega\in\mathbb{C}$, consider the translate $J^{(a,b,\omega)}f(z)=f(z/a)-\omega f(b/a)$. We show that for $f(x)=(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ and $\omega=\pm1$ every zero of $J^{(a,b,\omega)}f$ lies on the Cassini oval $|z^{2}-a^{2}|=|b^{2}-a^{2}|$. We call these translates \emph{Cassini polynomials} and give their zeros explicitly, prove that the zeros for $\omega=1$ and $\omega=-1$ strictly interlace on each component of the oval, and evaluate their discriminants and resultants in closed form. We then prove the reduced monic polynomials $Q_{n}=a^{2n}J^{(a,b,\omega)}f/(z^{2}-b^{2})$ factor into homogenized cyclotomic polynomials, satisfying $\operatorname{Res}(Q_{m},Q_{n})=(b^{2}-a^{2})^{2(m-1)(n-1)}$ for coprime $m,n$, and have discriminants governed by a Lucas sequence. We then prove a comparison principle: if $f$ is even or odd with all zeros in $[-1,1]$, $b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $|\omega|\le1$, then every zero of $J^{(a,ib,\omega)}f$ satisfies $|z^{2}-a^{2}|\le a^{2}+b^{2}$, and the symmetry hypothesis cannot be removed. As an application, every solution of $\det(A(P_{n})-\lambda I)=F_{n+1}$, where $A(P_{n})$ is the adjacency matrix of the path on $n$ vertices and $F_{n+1}$ is a Fibonacci number, satisfies $|\lambda^{2}-4|\le5$. This disproves, for every $n$, a conjecture of Gullerud, Johnson and Mbirika that the real parts of these solutions are unbounded.

papers.title: Resolution of ladder representations
papers.abstract: Let $\pi$ be a ladder representation of $\mathbf{GL}_m(F)$, $F$ a non-Archimedean local field. We construct an exact sequence of costandard modules, indexed by a lower Bruhat interval of a symmetric group and graded by the length, whose Euler characteristic is the determinantal formula of Tadi\'c and Lapid--M\'inguez. This is an analogue of the dual Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand resolution. The proof is combinatorial, through Jacquet modules and the Bruhat order; we also interpret the coresolution as a Cousin complex on Zelevinsky's space, which extends it to the balanced representations of Lapid--M\'inguez.

papers.title: Orbifold Morse Handles I. Morse Indices and Isomorphism Classes of Ordered Handles
papers.abstract: We classify the Morse indices and ordered handles arising from nondegenerate critical points of smooth functions on effective orientable four-dimensional orbifolds. Let $\rho\colon G\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$ be a faithful representation of a finite group. Let $V\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the negative eigenspace of a nondegenerate Hessian that is invariant under $\rho(G)$. The splitting $\mathbb R^4=V\oplus V^\perp$ determines an ordered quotient handle. Two such ordered handles admit an orientation-preserving isomorphism if and only if their negative eigenspaces lie in the same orbit under $N_{\mathrm{SO}(4)}(\rho(G))$. We determine the possible Morse indices and the normalizer orbits for every family in the completed Du Val list.

papers.title: On the Matlis duals of $\mathcal D$-modules in characteristic zero
papers.abstract: Let $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be a formal power series ring over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(R,k)$ be the ring of $k$-linear differential operators. We prove that if $\mathcal M$ is a nonzero left $\mathcal D$-module with $(0)\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(\mathcal M)$, then $(0)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R D(\mathcal M)$, where $D(-)$ denotes Matlis duality, without assuming holonomicity or finite generation over $\mathcal D$. As a significant consequence of this result, we establish the Lyubeznik--Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m conjecture in equicharacteristic zero. We also obtain a criterion for the Matlis dual of a $\mathcal D$-module to be non-holonomic.

papers.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization of convex bodies always converges in shape
papers.abstract: We prove that every sequence of iterated Steiner symmetrals of a convex body converges in shape. That is, every such sequence can be corrected by a sequence of rotations to achieve convergence in Hausdorff distance. Moreover, for a fixed corresponding family of subspaces, the same rotations can be used for every initial convex body, and their successive increments can be chosen to be square-summable.

papers.title: Long-time asymptotics of advection-diffusion of finite element differential forms
papers.authors: Kaibo Hu, Jindong Wang, Umberto Zerbinati
papers.abstract: This paper establishes global numerical analysis for the long-time behavior of Lie advection--diffusion of differential forms discretized by finite element exterior calculus (FEEC). For potential flows we prove a weighted Hodge decomposition implying convergence to harmonic forms of dimension equal to the Betti number, yielding a differential-form antidynamo theorem. For general advection, a mixed FEEC scheme is introduced and shown to preserve key structural properties: the dimension of closed stationary discrete $k$-forms is at least $b_k$. Under verified spectral-preservation assumptions (satisfied for small $h$ by spectral approximation and for arbitrary $h$ by a lowest-order exponential-fitting $M$-matrix discretization), discrete antidynamo theorems are obtained. In particular, on two-dimensional manifolds the numerical $1$-forms converge exponentially to a uniquely determined closed stationary form for every diffusion coefficient $\eta>0$, rigorously excluding spurious dynamo growth. The results guarantee that FEEC faithfully inherits the topological long-time asymptotics of the continuous system.

papers.title: Precise Analytic Boundaries and Positive Symplectic Paths in the Stability Diagrams of Elliptic Relative Equilibria
papers.abstract: We investigate the dependence of the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibria on the mass parameter and eccentricity. Using a periodic matrix Riccati decomposition, we derive explicit analytic curves separating hyperbolic--hyperbolic and complex--saddle spectra. The construction applies to the Lagrangian, Euler--Robe, and $(2+2)$-body families. A Hermitian Riccati factorization also yields an eccentricity-independent sufficient condition for positivity of the associated operators under every unit-circle boundary condition, and hence for hyperbolicity of the monodromy matrix. Finally, we construct an explicit lower bound for the second antiperiodic degeneracy curve by a finite trigonometric test function. This bound agrees with the value and tangent of the degeneracy curve at the circular limit. Together, these results provide analytic descriptions and estimates for distinct spectral boundaries in the stability diagrams.

papers.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
papers.abstract:
We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions.
  We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

papers.title: On the regularity of branching loci for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-harmonic spinors
papers.authors: Yang Li, Davide Parise, Yichen Zhang
papers.abstract: We show that the branching locus of a $\mathbb Z_2$-harmonic spinor is smooth (resp. real-analytic) near every point of frequency $\frac{1}{2}$ for smooth (resp. real-analytic) ambient defining data. This partially strengthens the previous regularity results obtained by Clifford Taubes and Boyu Zhang.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for nonautonomous pressureless gas dynamics
papers.authors: Richard De la cruz, Rakib Mondal, Wladimir Neves
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for one-dimensional pressureless gas dynamics with a continuous positive transport coefficient $\alpha(t)$ and a continuous nonnegative linear damping coefficient $\sigma(t)$, for every nonnegative locally finite Radon measure $\rho_0$ as initial density and every $u_0\in L^\infty(d\rho_0)$ as initial velocity. A central contribution of this paper is a new and direct proof of uniqueness under the original assumptions of Huang and Wang. It is carried out on the generalized potentials, and the energy condition enters only through the vanishing of the velocity dispersion at the initial time. The proof applies on every finite time strip and requires neither finite mass nor finite moments. We then show that time-dependent transport and damping act on entropy solutions only through an effective time, so that the nonautonomous system is the homogeneous one observed on a time interval $[0,A_\infty)$. Together with uniqueness on strips, this yields a global entropy solution, unique in density and momentum at every time, for all such coefficients. We also show that the energy condition cannot be dropped, and that its defect equals the mass of an atom times the variance of the velocities into which it splits. As consequences, we obtain an explicit representation of the solution by a generalized potential, the Riemann solutions with delta shocks, and the vanishing-damping limit.

papers.title: Average character degree below 14/3
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

papers.title: A note on meromorphicity in infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: In this note we develop the notion of a meromorphic mapping between infinite-dimensional complex manifolds. We restrict ourselves with second countable Hilbert manifolds modelled on a separable Hilbert space.

papers.title: Coalescing and annihilating random walks on the ring
papers.authors: A. M. Povolotsky, R. Tribe, O. V. Zaboronski
papers.abstract: We study correlation functions in the model of coalescing and annihilating random walks on the one-dimensional periodic lattice $\mathbb{Z}_N$. We prove that, for a special class of initial conditions, the $n$-point correlation function can be represented as a linear combination of two Pfaffians of $2n\times 2n$ matrices constructed from $2\times2$ matrix kernels, which in turn can be expressed in terms of two scalar kernels. This is an analogue of the single-Pfaffian form exhibited by correlation functions of the same model on $\mathbb{Z}$, where it serves as a signature of a Pfaffian point process. We derive equations for the kernels and construct their solutions. We also show that a particular example of an initial condition leading to bi-Pfaffian correlation functions is the inhomogeneous Bernoulli point process, which includes a fixed initial configuration as a particular limiting case.

papers.title: Linear Network Coding for Sum All-Reduce over Ring Networks
papers.authors: Yi Chen, Zhuoqi Tu, Shenghao Yang
papers.abstract: Sum All-Reduce is a fundamental collective communication primitive in which each node holds a local vector and every node must recover the componentwise sum of all vectors. In distributed training, this operation is often implemented over a ring topology using a reduce--multicast scheme. We study sum All-Reduce on directed rings via linear network coding, which includes reduce--multicast as a special case. We give a necessary and sufficient feasibility condition in terms of the coding matrices. For a ring with $N\geq 3$ nodes and unit-capacity links, where each node holds a vector containing $K$ symbols, we prove that the number of time units $T$ required by any feasible linear code satisfies $T\ge\max\bigl\{K+N-2,\ \lceil\frac{2(N-1)}{N}K\rceil\bigr\}$, giving a rate $K/T$ of at most $N/(2(N-1))$. The bound is tight over every field. When $K\ge N$, an interleaved reduce--multicast code achieves the bound; when $K<N$ and $K$ divides $N$, a reduce--partial-multicast code does. When $K<N$ and $K$ does not divide $N$, no coordinate-wise code---in particular, no reduce--multicast code---achieves the bound, while an explicit linear network code does.

papers.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
papers.authors: Sebastian Debus, Kurt Klement Gottwald, Nils Gubela
papers.abstract: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

papers.title: Borel--Serre Callias Classes and Cuspidal Localization
papers.abstract: We construct equivariant Callias classes on the Borel--Serre space of a Hilbert modular group and prove a Kasparov product formula. For torsion-free normal congruence subgroups and twists by powers $m_j\geq2$ of the holomorphic cotangent line bundles, we identify the image of the maximal higher index in the representation ring of the finite quotient with the equivariant index of the cuspidal Dolbeault operator on total forms. The comparison uses a Fredholm homotopy that separates an invertible noncuspidal block. As an application, we compute the $A_5$-equivariant index on the principal level-two Hilbert modular surface over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ for all parallel powers $m\geq2$. The resulting class in $R(A_5)$ is $15$-periodic in $m$ and has virtual dimension four. We express this class as an alternating sum of Hilbert cusp-form representations and deduce dimension identities for the full Hilbert modular group.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for the Nodal Measure of Clamped Plate Eigenfunctions in Smooth Domains
papers.authors: Hairong Liu, Long Tian, Xiaoping Yang
papers.abstract: We investigate measure estimates for the nodal sets of nonzero real eigenfunctions $u$ of the biharmonic operator, satisfying $\Delta^2u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ with clamped boundary conditions $u=\partial_\nu u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. We establish the optimal upper bound of order $\lambda^{1/4}$ for the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of their nodal sets on general bounded connected $C^\infty$ domains. Our approach combines an enhanced annular Carleman estimate with propagation of mass along a finite chain of balls, these yield a doubling index bounded uniformly up to the boundary.Interior analyticity then gives the nodal measure away from the boundary. To estimate the measure near the boundary, we develop a subdivision argument using the boundary values of $\Delta u$ and $\partial_\nu\Delta u$. Estimates from these data reduce large doubling indices and control the nodal measure in the region associated with a selected child cube whenever both the doubling index of the parent cube and $r\lambda^{1/4}$ are bounded, where $r$ is the side length of the parent cube.

papers.title: On Mean Field Games with Focusing Logarithmic Local Couplings
papers.abstract: In this note we study the existence theory of classical solutions to a second order stationary discounted Mean Field Games (MFG) system with focusing logarithmic local coupling in one space dimension. We then show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of the work of Bardi--Cardaliaguet.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
papers.authors: Marian Aprodu, Gavril Farkas, Jinhyung Park
papers.abstract: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

papers.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{E}=\{E_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$, indexed by a linearly ordered set $I$ with no greatest element. We call a nonnegative finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $G$ admissible if it takes finite values on the sets in $\mathscr{E}$ and these values are not bounded above. Every admissible measure $\mu$ can be normalized to have total mass one by applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{\mu(B\cap E_\alpha)}{\mu(E_\alpha)}\right\}_{\alpha\in I}$, defined for all sufficiently large $\alpha$. We study invariant finitely additive measures obtained by normalizing admissible measures. We show that every invariant measure constructed in this way can be obtained by normalizing a measure of a special form. An example is given showing that not every measure of the type under consideration can be obtained by normalizing a countably additive measure. We obtain a generalization of the Yosida-Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measures.

papers.title: Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
papers.abstract: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

papers.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
papers.abstract:
It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward.
  We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat \v{C}ech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed.
  We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

papers.title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract:
In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves.
  The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach
papers.authors: Thomas Bonnafont (ENSTA, Lab-STICC\_PIM), Fabien Caubet (LMAP), Nicolas Grima (LMAP), Jason Tridon (LMAP)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{\`e}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.

papers.title: Weak error of approximation of a L\'evy-type process using dynamic cutting
papers.abstract: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two L\'evy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

papers.title: Infinite projections and failure of pure infiniteness in simple nuclear $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a separable, unital, simple, nuclear $C^*$-algebra in the UCT class such that every nonzero projection in its stabilization is infinite, while it contains a nonzero projectionless hereditary subalgebra. The construction gives a negative answer to the question whether infiniteness of all nonzero projections in a unital simple nuclear $C^*$-algebra implies pure infiniteness.

papers.title: Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
papers.authors: Reinis Cirpons, Luna Elliott, Alex Levine, James D. Mitchell
papers.abstract: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

papers.title: Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning Coding for Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
papers.authors: Leonardo Roque, Louis-Adrien Dufr\`ene, Quentin Lampin, Gr\'egoire Lefebvre, Mohamad Assaad
papers.abstract: Transmitting quantized semantic embeddings over a bit-flip channel requires a binary mapping that minimizes expected reconstruction distortion. The classical Binary Switching Algorithm (BSA) ($\mathcal{O}(K^3 \log K)$ for $K$ centroids) yields locally optimal assignments but ignores hierarchical bit significance, making it incompatible with Unequal Error Protection (UEP). We propose Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning (RSGP), which recursively bisects the centroid affinity graph along the Fiedler eigenvector so that early bits separate semantically distant groups while later bits refine local structure. RSGP runs in $\mathcal{O}(K^3)$ with no iterative outer loop, and is the only method studied to show a systematic positive UEP gain: protecting early bits over later ones improves accuracy for RSGP, while being neutral or harmful for unstructured assignments. Experiments on the Banking77 dataset and the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) confirm that RSGP consistently matches or exceeds BSA accuracy across codebook sizes and error profiles.

papers.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
papers.abstract:
Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $\Sigma$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehat{\mu}_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $\mu_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression.
  Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

papers.title: Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
papers.authors: Benyin Fu, Kang Li, Jiawen Zhang
papers.abstract: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry. Such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, and if and only if the canonical map from its maximal Roe algebra to its reduced Roe algebra is injective. Both characterisations hold in the uniform and ordinary Roe settings. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that strong quasi-locality is equivalent to norm approximability by finite-propagation operators. In particular, the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property, and that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced crossed-product functor precisely for exact discrete groups.

papers.title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
papers.authors: Samuel Fiorini, Stefan Kober, Caleb McFarland
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomass\'e (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.

papers.title: Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
papers.authors: Pham Viet Hai, Vu Nhat Huy, Pham Trong Tien
papers.abstract:
We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_\sigma^p$, $\sigma>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations.
  As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{\psi,\varphi}:B_\sigma^p\to B_\tau^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $\sigma,\tau>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $\tau-\sigma|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-norm estimates, characterize differences of weighted composition operators via a no-cancellation principle for distinct symbols, and determine the connected and path-connected components of the corresponding operator spaces.

papers.title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
papers.abstract: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $\pi_0$ of $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $\pi_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)})$.

papers.title: Singular Global Compactness for Logarithmically Coupled \(p\)-Laplacian Systems
papers.abstract: We establish global compactness for logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on RN, where p=N>4 and bounded positive potentials converge to positive constants at infinity. The finite-energy domain need not be closed under subtraction, obstructing direct profile subtraction. We develop a scalar localisation method using slowly expanding cutoffs and residual commutator estimates uniform in the regularisation parameter. As the regularisation vanishes, residual Palais-Smale sequences split into a solution of the original system and finitely many separating autonomous profiles, with a strongly vanishing remainder and splitting of the logarithmic densities. A converse construction characterises all levels of compactness failure. Applications include convergence of ground-state levels, a compactness-escape alternative for minimising sequences, and a directional response formula for the ground-state energy.

papers.title: Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
papers.authors: Pengwei Wang, Na Li, Jiacheng Fan, Tielong Shen, Zuo Quan Xu
papers.abstract: This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Optimal Ordering-Free Two-Dimensional Insdel Reed-Solomon Codes via Cross-Ratios
papers.authors: Runqing Qiu, Shixin Zhu, Yang Li, San Ling
papers.abstract: Insertion-deletion (insdel) codes correct synchronization errors. By the half-Singleton bound, an ${[n,2]}_q$ code has minimum insdel distance at most $2n-4$. The smallest field size of two-dimensional Reed--Solomon (RS) codes attaining this bound is $\Theta(n^3)$. Unlike the minimum Hamming distance, the minimum insdel distance of an RS code depends on the ordering of its evaluation points. An evaluation set is called ordering-free if every ordering of its points gives an RS code attaining the half-Singleton bound. In this paper, we first show that for $n\ge6$ every ${[n,2]}_q$ code attaining the half-Singleton bound is an RS code, and hence $q\ge\binom{n}{3}+2$. Secondly, we show that an ordering-free evaluation set with $n\ge6$ points in $\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfies $n<q^{1/3}+2$, and that it has at most $r+1$ points if $q=r^3$ for a prime power $r\ge3$. Finally, by using cross-ratios, we construct an ordering-free evaluation set with $r+1$ points in $\mathbb{F}_{r^3}$ for every prime power $r$. Hence, the bound $r+1$ is attained for $r\ge3$. Moreover, the constructed set is even robust against permutations combined with insdel errors.

papers.title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
papers.abstract: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

papers.title: Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
papers.abstract:
In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category.
  We apply these results to contractions of relative dimension one, resolutions of nodal varieties, and blowups of smooth projective varieties along smooth centers. For projective surfaces with ADE singularities, we identify the discrete factor through a simply transitive braid group action. When the minimal resolution is a K3 surface, every weak stability condition obtained by lifting a numerical stability condition from the singular surface is the limit of a continuous, quasi-convergent family of numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the resolution with the same heart.

papers.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $\mu(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((\kappa^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

papers.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
papers.abstract: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

papers.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
papers.authors: Benjamin Joseph, Tam\'as Keleti, M\'ark K\"ok\'enyesi, Andr\'as M\'ath\'e, Andrew Schmidt
papers.abstract: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

papers.title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
papers.authors: Sharan Nurani Ramesh, Lea Sa{\ss}mannshausen, Axel Klawonn, Daniel Balzani
papers.abstract:
This paper presents a computational model integrating transmural drug transport, smooth muscle cell contraction, nonlinear anisotropic material behavior, and residual stresses to investigate the effects of calcium channel blockers~(CCBs) on local stress distributions in atherosclerotic arteries.
  The balance of linear momentum is coupled with a three-dimensional reaction-diffusion equation for the drug transport.
  Smooth muscle contraction is modeled phenomenologically based on a chemo-mechanical model that incorporates the effects of stretch on intracellular calcium dynamics and calcium sensitization.
  A novel drug-tissue interaction model is proposed to capture the effects of CCBs on intracellular calcium and thus on smooth muscle contraction.
  Material parameters are identified by fitting to experimental data from the literature and finite element simulations are conducted on five exemplary atherosclerotic arterial geometries reconstructed from histological cross-sections.
  Simulation results show that although CCBs reduce the stresses in the media through reduced smooth muscle contraction, they shift load to the fibrous cap, whose stress increases in all five geometries (median of up to 28.9~kPa).
  This increase varies strongly between plaque morphologies and becomes smaller with lower smooth muscle tone before treatment, lower drug concentrations in the arterial wall and increasing axial pre-stretch.
  A blood pressure reduction of 10~mmHg already lowers it to a median of at most 3.8~kPa in four of the five geometries.
  Our findings suggest that CCBs may increase the rupture risk of vulnerable plaques with highly loaded fibrous caps under insufficient blood pressure reduction, which remains to be confirmed experimentally and clinically.

papers.title: The pinched Veronese has no Koszul filtration
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that the pinched Veronese subalgebra $k [x^3,x^2y,xy^2,x^2z,xz^2,y^3,y^2z,yz^2,z^3] \subset k[x,y,z]$ has no Koszul filtration regardless of the field $k$, despite it being a Koszul algebra. We do this by showing that no ideal $(f,g)$ minimally generated by two linear forms can belong to a Koszul filtration. By the definition of a Koszul filtration this, in turn, implies that no Koszul filtration can exist.

papers.title: A scaling approach to double phase equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the double phase equation $-\Delta_p u - \operatorname{div}(|x|^{-b}\,|\nabla u|^{q-2}\nabla u) = f(|x|,u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, whose operator admits a scaling that acts on both phases simultaneously. Our first main result is a sharp description of the continuous and compact embeddings of the radial energy space into weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^s(\mathbb{R}^N;|x|^{-c})$ with an explicit characterization of their admissible regions in the $(s,c)$-plane. The two critical edges reflect the two phases: on the edge attached to the $p$-phase compactness is lost by spreading to infinity, while on the edge attached to the weighted $q$-phase it is lost by concentration at the origin. Our second main result concerns equations with one critical term on each edge. We show that bounded Palais-Smale sequences either converge or lose at least the energy $\beta^\ast = \min\{\beta_1,\beta_2\}$, where $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are the explicit single-phase thresholds, and that this level is optimal when the critical terms are unweighted. Thus, the two mechanisms cannot combine to lower the compactness threshold. Combining these results with a Poho\v{z}aev identity, variational methods for scaled functionals and the Fadell-Rabinowitz cohomological index, we prove nonexistence results, obtain an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues on the scaling line and infinitely many solutions for pure power equations, and show that large superscaled and small subscaled perturbations of the doubly critical equation yield multiple solutions.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: Convex polynomial approximation on the unit ball
papers.authors: Andriy Bondarenko, Andriy Prymak, Igor Shevchuk
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{B}^d$ be the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge1$. We prove that, for every convex $f\in C(\mathbb{B}^d)$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a polynomial $P_n$ of total degree at most $n$, convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\|f-P_n\|_{C(\mathbb{B}^d)}\le c\,\omega_2(f,n^{-1};\mathbb{B}^d)$. Here $\omega_2$ is the ordinary second modulus of smoothness and $c=c_d$ depends only on $d$. In particular, we obtain the rate $O(n^{-2})$ for convex functions with uniformly bounded second derivatives.

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

papers.title: Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $\Pi$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $\chi(k^{-1}\Pi P\Pi)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\int\chi(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2\pi^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse K\"ahler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. For $(n,0)$-forms on complete Sasakian manifolds, a cut-off by the self-adjoint generator of the Reeb flow, which avoids the self-adjointness question for the Toeplitz operator, gives the same results with twisted coefficients.

papers.title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
papers.abstract: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{\sigma(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{\sigma(d)}\}$, $\sigma\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $\lambda_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_i\lambda_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $\lambda_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $\Theta(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

papers.title: On the blow-up of the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two
papers.abstract: We establish three-term asymptotics for the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two as $\gamma\to 0$ and identify, up to rescaling and symmetries, the profile of the asymptotically worst potential. The proof uses the well-known relation between the one-particle constant and an integral moment of optimizers of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Through the optimizers' characterization as positive, vanishing solutions of the nonlinear elliptic equation $-\Delta Q + Q = Q^{s}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the essence of the proof lies in the asymptotic analysis of solutions $Q$ as $s\to\infty$.

papers.title: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
papers.abstract:
We study $K$-out-of-$N$ oblivious transfer (OT) between a server and a client over a discrete memoryless channel, under an honest-but-curious model. The client must retrieve $K$ out of $N$ messages stored by the server while learning nothing about the remaining $N-K$ messages, and the server must not learn the client's selection. For a binary erasure channel (BEC) with parameter $\epsilon$, we show that the $K$-out-of-$N$ OT capacity is $\min\Big(\frac{K\epsilon}{N-K},1-\epsilon\Big)$. This characterization generalizes the known capacity results for $1$-out-of-$2$ OT and for $1$-out-of-$N$ OT when $\epsilon\ge\tfrac{N-1}{N}$. We also investigate OT reductions, specifically, we show that constructing a $K$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol from repeating $K$ times an optimal $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be suboptimal, but we also identify certain ranges of $\epsilon$ and $M < N$ for which a $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be optimally realized via the repetition of a $1$-out-of-$M$ OT protocol.
  Finally, we discuss extensions of our results to a generalized erasure channel (GEC).

papers.title: An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

papers.title: Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
papers.authors: Luis Brice\~no-Arias, Fernando Rold\'an, Adrien Taylor
papers.abstract: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm is a classical method for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators. In its standard form, both operators are reflected in the same manner and are activated with the same step-size. In this article we break this symmetry by replacing the reflected resolvents by relaxed resolvents, letting the two operators be activated with different step-sizes. We show that this additional freedom is available precisely when the operators are cocoercive, the admissible range of the parameter being determined by their cocoercivity constants and reducing to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Within this range we quantify the averagedness of the resulting operator, which yields the weak convergence of the method together with relaxation steps beyond those allowed in the classical case, and, when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, a strict contraction. We compute in closed form the parameters minimizing the contraction factor and we exhibit instances attaining it, so that the resulting linear rates are tight. The optimal rates are strictly smaller than the best rates available for the classical Douglas--Rachford algorithm in the monotone inclusion and convex optimization settings, which are studied separately. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

papers.title: \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G)\) for \(0\leq\alpha<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_{\alpha}(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_{\alpha}\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution. The structural function solves an ill-posed operator equation whose conditional expectation operator need not be injective, and whose solutions need not belong to the hypothesis space. We analyse a two-stage kernel estimator that extends kernel instrumental variable regression to $\mathbb{Y}$-valued outcomes and allows spectral regularisation in both stages, including Landweber iteration and Showalter's method in the second stage. We show that the second stage is a regularisation method in the Hilbert scale generated by the inverse of the kernel integral operator. This viewpoint identifies the solution towards which the estimator converges: the minimum-norm solution in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space in the well-specified case and, in the misspecified case, the unique solution in the range of the continuous extension of the projection operator associated to the well-specified setting. Under source conditions and link conditions expressed through general index functions, we derive non-asymptotic bounds in a scale of interpolation norms that hold with high probability in terms of the first-stage error, with or without identification and in the well- and misspecified settings. For polynomial link conditions, we recover the rate of scalar kernel instrumental regression and extend it to targets outside the hypothesis space; for exponential link conditions, we obtain logarithmic rates in the severely ill-posed regime.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of Channel Coding
papers.abstract: We introduce a new framework for the study and evaluation of the fundamental limits of channel coding, emphasizing genuinely nonasymptotic results. The {\em channel coding sample complexity} $n^*({\cal W},\epsilon)$ of a channel ${\cal W}$ is defined as the smallest blocklength at which it is possible to transmit information through that channel with error probability below $\epsilon$ and at a rate at least as high as that given by an appropriate constraint also in terms of $\epsilon$. This formulation follows analogous developments in statistics, computer science and, more recently, in lossless source coding. For any discrete memoryless channel we derive nonasymptotic bounds on the sample complexity, with explicit constants. These bounds show that the sample complexity is characterized not by the usual channel capacity, but by the channel's Augustin--Csisz\'{a}r capacity of order $1/2$, which coincides with the cutoff rate as well as with the channel's Sibson capacity of order $1/2$. The proof is partly based on a new channel-coding one-shot converse in terms of hypothesis testing. We also examine extensions of the sample complexity framework to general target rates. Moreover, we derive corresponding results for the sample complexity of the additive white Gaussian noise channel with a quadratic power constraint. Their proof relies on new, explicit upper bounds on the best achievable error probability, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
papers.authors: Aleksa Milojevi\'c, Patryk Morawski, Benny Sudakov, Istvan Tomon
papers.abstract:
A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. This was recently resolved by Sadhu and, independently, by Pach, Tardos, and Zeng, based on a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich. These papers showed that $k$-quasiplanar graphs have at most $k^{O(k)}n$ edges.
  In this note, we greatly improve the dependence on $k$ and show that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. The proof is based on a geometric charging scheme and Erd\H{o}s-Szekeres type combinatorial arguments.

papers.title: Sumsets modulo ideals: Baire category and descriptive complexity
papers.abstract:
Given an ideal $\mathcal I$ on the nonnegative integers, we study the family $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ of all sets for which every $\mathcal{I}$-small modification is not a nontrivial sumset $A+B$.
