Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.

papers.title: A separation criterion for chiral systems and its application to Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski perturbations
papers.abstract: We give a constructive criterion for local separation of first-order chiral systems coupling two complex doublets. It combines a Gram decomposition of the coupling sources with separate coordinate dependence and a differential transport test. For recoverable, nondegenerate source families, the criterion is necessary and sufficient within the specified class of mode-independent complex matrix transformations with unit determinant. For a fixed differential operator and admissible Gram decomposition, we identify conditions under which the sources uniquely determine the Hermitian coefficient matrix required for separation. As an application, we construct an explicit algebraic transformation and derive separated radial and angular equations for coupled radiative Einstein--Maxwell perturbations of rotating, charged Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski backgrounds with acceleration, NUT charge, and a cosmological constant, on specified local patches. Its Gram decomposition is unique under additional generic assumptions. We also derive angular endpoint indices for Bonnor and Misner identifications with conical deficits or excesses. Under the stated regularity assumptions, each specified self-adjoint angular realization at fixed real mode parameters has a discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis.

papers.title: Formalism of operators for Laguerre-Gauss modes
papers.authors: A. L. F. da Silva, A. T. B. Celeste, M. Pazetti, C. E. F. Lopes
papers.abstract: In this work apply the algebra of operators of quantum mechanics in the Helmholtz wave equation in cylindrical coordinates in paraxial approximation to describe the raising and lowering operators for the Laguerre-Gauss modes.

papers.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
papers.authors: R. Callejas-Bedregal, M. F. Z. Morgado, J. Seade
papers.abstract: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusi\'{n}ski-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global L\^e cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

papers.title: Bessel Integrals, Periods and Zeta Numbers
papers.abstract: We present a summary of recent and older results on Bessel integrals and their relation with zeta numbers.

papers.title: Arithmetical Foundations - Recursion. Evaluation. Consistency
papers.abstract:
We fix constructive foundations for Arithmetic on a map theoretical, algorithmic level. In contrast to elementhood and quantification based traditional foundations such as Principia Mathematica PM, Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, or v. Neumann-Goedel-Bernays set theory NGB, our fundamental primitive recursive theory PR has as its basic "undefined" (not further defined) terms just terms for objects and maps. Goodstein's axiomatic uniqueness rules are derived as theorems in PR - with equality definability as a side result -, S is obtained by predicate comprehension, and the equivalence of the theory of partially defined maps and the categorical theory of mu-recursion identifies mu-recursive maps and while-loops with partially defined maps.
  Keywords: Goedel theorems, primitive recursion, categorical free-variables Arithmetic, mu-recursion, totality

papers.title: Critical binomial ideals of Northcott type
papers.authors: P. A. Garc\'{\i}a-S\'anchez, D. Llena, I. Ojeda
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a family of binomial ideals defining monomial curves in the n-dimensional affine space determined by $n$ hypersurfaces of the form $x_i^{c_i} - x_1^{u_{i1}} \cdots x_n^{u_{1n}}$ in $\Bbbk[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ with $u_{ii} = 0$, $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$. We prove that the monomial curves in that family are set-theoretic complete intersections. Moreover, if the monomial curve is irreducible, we compute some invariants such as genus, type and Frobenius number of the corresponding numerical semigroup. We also describe a method to produce set-theoretic complete intersection semigroup ideals of arbitrary large height.

papers.title: Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles
papers.abstract: We prove global Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles, combining arguments from M.Ikawa (1982,1988) with more recent ones inspired by N.Burq, C.Guillarmou, and A. Hassell (2010) and O. Ivanovici (2010). This is to be contrasted with the loss in the smoothing estimate for the Schr\"odinger equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in the presence of a trapped geodesic.

papers.title: The classification of $2$-dimensional rigid algebras
papers.authors: Antonio Jes\'us Calder\'on, Amir Fern\'andez Ouaridi, Ivan Kaygorodov
papers.abstract: Using the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional algebras, we give the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional rigid, conservative and terminal algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. We have the geometric classification of the variety of $2$-dimensional terminal algebras, and based on the geometric classification of these algebras we formulate some open problems.

papers.title: The set of numerical semigroups of a given multiplicity and Frobenius number
papers.authors: Manuel B. Branco, Ignacio Ojeda, Jos\'e Carlos Rosales
papers.abstract: We study the structure of the family of numerical semigroups with fixed multiplicity and Frobenius number. We give an algorithmic method to compute all the semigroups in this family. As an application we compute the set of all numerical semigroups with given multiplicity and genus.

papers.title: $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras
papers.authors: Bruno Leonardo Macedo Ferreira, Ivan Kaygorodov, Viktor Lopatkin
papers.abstract: A relation between $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras has been established. Some non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a certain Lie algebra (Witt algebra, the algebra $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$, the thin Lie algebra and a solvable Lie algebra with abelian nilpotent radical) have been done. In particular, we have developed an example of the transposed Poisson algebra with associative and Lie parts isomorphic to the Laurent polynomials and the Witt algebra. On the other side, it has been proved that there are no non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a Lie algebra part isomorphic to a semisimple finite-dimensional algebra, a simple finite-dimensional superalgebra, the Virasoro algebra, $N=1$ and $N=2$ superconformal algebras, or a semisimple finite-dimensional $n$-Lie algebra.

papers.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.

papers.title: On Iwasawa invariants of modular forms with reducible and non-$p$-distinguished residual Galois representations
papers.abstract:
Let $f$ be the ordinary $p$-stabilization of the weight-one Eisenstein series, where $\chi$ is odd and $\chi(p)=1$. Under a Gorenstein hypothesis on the cuspidal Hecke algebra, we prove a factorization of the even branches of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function of $f$ by evaluating a cup product of cyclotomic units via local reciprocity. The odd branches follow from the Eisenstein specialization formula of Fukaya and Kato with a minor modification for the exceptional character considered here. We then obtain results on the $\mu$- and $\lambda$-invariants. On the algebraic side, we compute the Selmer characteristic ideals at $f$ and the Iwasawa invariants of the higher-weight specializations. For every nontrivial twist of $f$, the ordinary characteristic ideal is generated by the corresponding $p$-adic $L$-function.
  On the untwisted branch it has one additional factor, the cyclotomic augmentation parameter. Imposing the strict local condition at $p$ removes this factor. For higher-weight specializations coming from newforms of level prime to $p$, Kato's divisibility then gives the cyclotomic main conjecture after inverting $p$.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on Galilean and solvable Lie algebras
papers.authors: Ivan Kaygorodov, Viktor Lopatkin, Zerui Zhang
papers.abstract: Transposed Poisson structures on complex Galilean-type Lie algebras and superalgebras are described. It is proven that the principal Galilean Lie algebras and superalgebras do not admit nontrivial transposed Poisson structures. We also prove that each complex finite-dimensional solvable Lie algebra of dimension greater than one admits a nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivation and a nontrivial ${\rm Hom}$-Lie structure, and that each complex finite-dimensional non-abelian solvable Lie algebra admits a nontrivial transposed Poisson structure.

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: Satellite knots that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists
papers.abstract: A positive braid with at least one full twist is known to be a minimal braid, i.e, it achieves the braid index for its closure. In this paper we find knots that are the closure of positive minimal braids that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists. More precisely, we show that some satellite knots with companions and patterns given as the closure of positive braids cannot be represented as the closure of positive braids with full twists. As a consequence, we find infinitely many satellite knots with companions and patterns being Lorenz knots that are not Lorenz knots. This gives an answer to the question whether a satellite knot having Lorenz pattern and companion is also a Lorenz knot, originally addressed by Birman and Williams in a special case in the 1980s.

papers.title: Lower bounds on the measure of the support of positive and negative parts of trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: The measure of the positivity set $\{ x \in [0; 2\pi] \mid f(x) > 0 \}$ of a trigonometric polynomial $f$ is bounded from below by the Motzkin density. We generalize the bound to polynomials in several variables and almost periodic functions. We then use these generalizations to extend known results on Taikov's problem.

papers.title: Cartesian Gray-Monoidal Double Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we present cartesian structure for symmetric Gray-monoidal double categories. To do this we first introduce locally cubical Gray categories, which are three-dimensional categorical structures analogous to classical, locally globular, Gray categories. The motivating example comprises double categories themselves, together with their functors, transformations, and modifications. A one-object locally cubical Gray category is a Gray-monoidal double category. Braiding, syllepsis, and symmetry for these is introduced in a manner analogous to that for 2-categories. Adding cartesian structure requires the introduction of doubly-lax functors of double categories to manage the order of copies. The resulting theory is algebraically rather complex, largely due to the bureaucracy of linearizing higher-dimensional boundary constraints. Fortunately, it has a relatively simple and compelling representation in the graphical calculus of surface diagrams, which we present.

papers.title: The Brauer-Manin obstruction on algebraic stacks
papers.abstract: For algebraic stacks over number fields, we define their Brauer-Manin sets, Brauer-Manin pairings, and extend the descent theory of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and Sansuc. By extending Sansuc's exact sequence, we show the torsionness of Brauer groups of stacks that are locally quotients of varieties by linear groups. With mild assumptions, for stacks that are locally quotients or Deligne-Mumford, we show that the Brauer-Manin obstruction coincides with some other cohomological obstructions such as obstructions given by torsors under connected groups or abelian gerbes. For Brauer-Manin sets of these stacks, we show the properties such as descent along a torsor, product preservation are still correct. These results extend classical theories of those on varieties.

papers.title: Faster Algorithms for Structured Linear and Kernel Support Vector Machines
papers.authors: Yuzhou Gu, Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang
papers.abstract:
Many machine learning problems are quadratic programs, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs). A general quadratic program has input size $\Theta(n^2)$, and assuming the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH), no $O(n^{2-o(1)})$ time algorithm exists when the objective matrix is positive semidefinite (Backurs, Indyk, and Schmidt, NeurIPS'17). SVMs, however, are given by $n$ data points of dimension $d$, often much smaller than $n$, and have only $O(1)$ equality constraints.
  In this work, we design the first nearly-linear time algorithm for solving quadratic programs whenever a low-rank factorization of the quadratic objective matrix is given, the number of linear constraints is small, the coefficients of the objective and some optimal solution are bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(n)$, and some feasible point has all entries between $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and $\mathrm{poly}(n)$. For linear SVM on $d$-dimensional data, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $\widetilde O(nd^{(\omega+1)/2}\log(n/\epsilon))$ when $(d+1)^{\omega-1}\le n$ and the data points have norms at most $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and margin at least $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$, where $\omega<2.258$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Its output satisfies the equality constraint only approximately. For Gaussian kernel SVM, when $d=O(\log n)$, the squared dataset radius is $o(\log n/\log\log n)$ and the dual variables lie in a box $[0,R]^n$ with $R\le\mathrm{poly}(n)$, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $n^{1+o(1)}$ for any accuracy $\epsilon\ge 1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$. We also prove that, assuming SETH, when the squared dataset radius is $\Omega(\log^2 n)$, $\Omega(n^{2-o(1)})$ time is required on some inputs to reach error $\exp(-\Theta(\log^2 n))$ for the program without the bias term. This improves upon the prior best lower bound in both the dimension $d$ and the squared dataset radius.

papers.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
papers.authors: Bin Pei, Robert Hesse, Bjoern Schmalfuss, Yong Xu
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.

papers.title: Discrete and Continuous Concentration of Measure: Geometric Obstructions, Predictive Gowdy Evolution, and Observable Limits
papers.abstract:
We compare concentration in increasing dimension with geometric and metric--measure degeneration of compact Cauchy hypersurfaces.
  For vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy developments we establish an exact law for redistribution of normalized spatial volume, without imposing polarization. An explicit strict bound on the \emph{initial} spatially averaged wave-map energy guarantees divergence of the transverse circle length $L(\tau)$. Under this expansion hypothesis, we classify \emph{all convergent distance-scaling regimes}: if $a_\tau L(\tau)\to\ell$, the rescaled sections concentrate to a point for $\ell=0$, to the uniformly measured circle of circumference $\ell$ for $0<\ell<\infty$, while for $\ell=\infty$ their associated pyramids converge to the maximal pyramid. The classification applies to Ringstr\"om's generic non-polarized class, including nondegenerate true spikes, and requires no uniform geometric control at spike points.
  The argument compares orbit metrics with their initial values outside an exceptional set of probability at most $L(\tau_0)/L(\tau)$. The normalized Laplacian splits into periodic one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators indexed by toroidal Fourier modes; its non-invariant sectors satisfy a uniform spectral gap $\Lambda_\tau\ge cL(\tau)^2$. Thus only torus-invariant modes persist at bounded spectral energy, with quantitative heat-semigroup and resolvent estimates. Separately, an initial-data perturbation criterion yields strictly monotone transfer toward a prescribed region in a relatively open low-velocity non-polarized class. Explicit high-velocity solutions exhibit contrasting point-collapse and unbounded-diameter geometries governed by the torus marking.

papers.title: A biregular classification of smooth quotients of abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify smooth projective surfaces that are quotients of abelian surfaces by finite groups. We also record the orbifold boundary associated to a quotient map and describe its structure explicitly in the case of augmented irregularity one.

papers.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
papers.abstract:
We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group.
  As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{\tau_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $\tau_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on solvable and perfect Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We described all transposed Poisson algebra structures on oscillator Lie algebras, i.e., on one-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; on solvable Lie algebras with naturally graded filiform nilpotent radical; on $(n+1)$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; and on $n$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $n$-dimensional algebra with trivial multiplication. We also answered one question on transposed Poisson algebras, posted in a paper by Beites, Ferreira and Kaygorodov. Namely, we found that the semidirect product of ${\mathfrak sl}_2$ and an irreducible module gives a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with non-trivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations, but without non-trivial transposed Poisson structures.

papers.title: Prescribed projections and efficient coverings by curves in the plane
papers.authors: Alan Chang, Alex McDonald, Krystal Taylor
papers.abstract: Davies efficient covering theorem states that an arbitrary measurable set $W$ in the plane can be covered by full lines so that the measure of the union of the lines has the same measure as $W$. This result has an interesting dual formulation in the form of a prescribed projection theorem. In this paper, we formulate each of these results in a nonlinear setting and consider some applications. In particular, given a measurable set $W$ and a curve $\Gamma=\{(t,f(t)): t\in [a,b]\}$, where $f$ is $C^1$ with strictly monotone derivative, we show that $W$ can be covered by translations of $\Gamma$ in such a way that the union of the translated curves has the same measure as $W$. This is achieved by proving an equivalent prescribed generalized projection result, which relies on a Venetian blind construction.

papers.title: Existence, uniqueness, and universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model
papers.authors: Ruoyuan Liu, Nikolay Tzvetkov, Yuzhao Wang
papers.abstract: We study the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure (with order $\alpha > 1$) and the dynamical problem of its canonical stochastic quantization: the three-dimensional stochastic damped fractional nonlinear wave equation with a cubic nonlinearity, also called the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model. We first construct the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure via the variational approach by Barashkov-Gubinelli (2020). When $\alpha \leq \frac{9}{8}$, this fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure turns out to be singular with respect to the base Gaussian measure. We then prove almost sure global well-posedness of the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model and invariance of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure for all $\alpha > 1$ by further developing the globalization framework due to Oh-Okamoto-Tolomeo (2024) on the hyperbolic $\Phi^3_3$-model. Furthermore, when $\alpha > \frac{9}{8}$ , we prove weak universality of the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model by utilizing the convergence of Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Monodromy of rational singularities on surfaces in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the monodromy on the $\ell$-adic cohomology of smooth proper surfaces over complete discrete valuation fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with algebraically closed residue field and $p>5$. When the surfaces admit proper models whose special fiber has at worst a rational double point, we show that the monodromy action of inertia is finite, depends on an \'etale neighborhood of the singularity and its nontrivial part coincides with a restriction of the reflection representation of a Weyl group naturally associated with the singularity. We extend this description for degenerations into general rational singularities whose deformations lie in the Artin component: the monodromy is described by restricting the reflection representation of the Weyl group associated with the exceptional $(-2)$-curves in the minimal resolution of the special fiber. Moreover we determine minimal finite extensions over which such surfaces have good reduction. The proof relies on a mixed-characteristic extension of Grothendieck--Springer simultaneous resolutions and an identification of monodromy and Springer representations via relatively perverse nearby cycles.

papers.title: Inverse Gram Matrix Methods for Prioritization in Analytic Hierarchy Process: Explainability of Weighted Least Squares Optimization Method
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Inverse Gram Matrix (IGM) methods to prioritize Pairwise Reciprocal Matrices (PRMs) in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The IGM methods include Pseudo-IGM, Normalized-IGM, and Lagrangian-IGM. Interestingly, the proposed IGM methods achieve the minimum Weighted Least Squares (WLS) error. Since clarity, explainability, usability, and verification of the closed-form solutions of WLS appear to be incomplete in the literature, comprehensive mathematical proofs, detailed computational demonstrations, and intensive simulation verification to extend the prior studies are offered in this study. After a simulation of one million random PRM instances was performed to verify the equivalence of the IGM methods, another simulation of ten thousand random PRM instances was performed to verify that any one of the proposed IGM methods is the exact closed-form solution to the WLS optimization problem. The proposed IGM methods under the WLS framework provide the promising alternatives to Saaty's Eigenvector method in AHP. The open-source R package igm4ahp, along with its user manual, tutorials, and simulation datasets, is publicly available on GitHub and permanently archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: On the role of dense ideals on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and associated $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets
papers.abstract: This article is a continuation of the work done in [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289] on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and concerns in addition the generalized version of Arbault sets, namely, $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets that is generated from this collection. A special class of ideals, namely, non-$snt$ ideals was introduced in 2023 ($snt$ stands for ``strongly non translation invariant") which was found to be effective in understanding ``Eggleston's dichotomy". Here we introduce another new class of ideals $\mathcal{H}$, a subclass of non-$snt$ ideals. We are able to establish a (new) necessary and sufficient condition for a $P$-ideal to be dense in Theorem 2.8 using the condition used to define the class $\mathcal{H}$ from which it follows that $\mathcal{H}$ coincides with dense $P$-ideals. Furthermore the important fact is established that the class of non-$snt$ ideals strictly contains the class of dense $P$-ideals. Subsequent investigation leads us to Theorem 2.14 which establishes the novelty of $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups for ideals coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$ and arbitrary arithmetic sequences showing that these are not even Arbault sets. Before all these, we also present a correct and revised proof of the main result of [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289], namely Theorem 3.8 (which had a gap in the proof). Finally we extend the results of [Das et al., Bul. Sci. Math. 179 (2022), 103157] for generalized version of Arbault sets and primarily show that for each ideal coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$, the class of $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets not only properly contains the class of classical Arbault sets but also a large subfamily of sets of absolute convergence while being contained in the class of weak Dirichlet sets.

papers.title: The transversal game
papers.abstract: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.

papers.title: On Some Infinitary Logics
papers.abstract: We define a new class of infinitary logics $\mathscr L^1_{\kappa,\alpha}$ generalizing Shelah's logic $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ defined in \cite{MR2869022}. If $\kappa=\beth_\kappa$ and $\alpha <\kappa$ is infinite then our logic coincides with $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$. We study the relation between these logics for different parameters $\kappa$ and $\alpha$. We give many examples of classes of structures that can or cannot be defined in these logics. Finally, we give a different version of Lindstr\"{o}m's Theorem for $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ in terms of the $\phi$-submodel relation.

papers.title: Fractional Calculus Operator Emerging from the 2D Biorthogonal Hermite Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we introduce a method to construct two variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. By using this new technique, we define 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and we investigate several properties of them such as biorthogonality property, operational formula and integral representation. We further inverstigate their images under the Laplace transformations, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function and obtain the similar properties for them. In order to establish new fractional calculus, we add two new parameters and consider 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function. We introduce an integral operator containing the modified bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function in the kernel. We show that it satisify the semigroup property and obtain its left inverse operator, which corresponds to its fractional derivative operator.

papers.title: A sharper observability for diffusion equations in $\mathbb R^N$
papers.abstract: We establish that for any small constant $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a nontrivial equidistributed set (with an unbounded complement) such that the observability cost in the short time $(0,T)$ of diffusion equations over $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ can be improved to a sharper exponential form of $Ce^{\varepsilon/T}$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $T$.

papers.title: Control of the Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^3$: The critical case
papers.authors: Pablo Braz e Silva (UFPE), Roberto de A. Capistrano-Filho (UFPE), Jackellyny Dassy do Nascimento Carvalho (UFPE), David dos Santos Ferreira (IELC)
papers.abstract: This article deals with the $H^{1}$--level local null controllability for the energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Firstly, we demonstrate that the problem under consideration is well-posed using Strichartz estimates. Moreover, through the Hilbert uniqueness method, we prove the linear Schr\"{o}dinger equation to be controllable by means of a control force supported in the exterior of a ball. Finally, we use a perturbation argument and show local controllability for the critical nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation.

papers.title: Nontrivial Massey products on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.authors: Giovanni Placini, Jonas Stelzig, Leopold Zoller
papers.abstract: We show that the bigraded quasi-isomorphism type of the bigraded, bidifferential algebra of forms on a compact K\"ahler manifold generally contains more information than the de Rham cohomology algebra with its real Hodge structure. More precisely, on any closed Riemann surface of genus at least two, there is a nontrivial ABC-Massey product. Furthermore, starting from dimension three, there are simply connected projective manifolds with a nonzero ABC-Massey product of three divisor classes. In particular, compact K\"ahler manifolds are generally not formal in the sense of pluripotential homotopy theory.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and unbounded drift
papers.abstract: We consider controlled SDEs with measurable coefficients, a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient and an $L_d$-drift. In this framework we investigate the relationship among value functions, PDEs, and operator semigroups. First, for a cost with an infinite time horizon on a bounded domain, we identify the value function as an $L_{d_0}$-viscosity solution to an HJB equation and we establish quantitative regularity estimates. The constant $d_0 \in (d/2, d)$ only depends on the space dimension $d$, the ellipticity constants of the diffusion coefficient and the $L_d$-bound of the drift. To illustrate applications of these results, we provide a uniqueness theorem under an additional assumption on the diffusion coefficient, showing a stochastic representation, and we discuss stability of value functions. Second, we consider a cost with a finite time horizon, terminal and running terms, assuming an $L_{d + 1}$-drift. We show that the value function indexed over the terminal cost is a nonlinear semigroup on $C_b (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we establish a regularization by noise effect, which shows that the semigroup regularizes lower semicontinuity to local H\"older continuity. We also establish quantitative regularity estimates for the semigroup that are local in time and global in space. Lastly, under an additional $L_{d + 2, loc}$-assumption on the drift, we relate the semigroup to a parabolic PDE, showing that the associated value function is an $L_{d + 1}$-viscosity solution. Our proofs of the regularity of the value functions, the $C_b$-Feller property of the semigroup and its regularization by noise effects are based on a strong Markov selection principle and analytic estimates for linear diffusions that were recently established by N. V. Krylov in a series of papers. We highlight that our method covers frameworks without uniqueness of the controlled SDEs, as well as the associated PDEs.

papers.title: On Elliptical and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions
papers.authors: Imen Ayadi, Florent Bouchard, Fr\'ed\'eric Pascal
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions, which play a major role when handling covariance matrices. Similarly to multivariate elliptical distributions, these form a large family of covariance distributions, encompassing, \textit{e.g.}, the Wishart or $t$-Wishart ones. Our first major contribution is to derive a stochastic representation for Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart matrices. This later enables us to obtain various key statistical properties of these distributions such as expectations, variances, and Kronecker moments up to any order. The stochastic representation provides an efficient method for generating random matrices from these distributions. Additionally, Elliptical Wishart distributions have a specific dependence structure - a random scale shared by all columns - which strongly influences their asymptotic behavior. Lastly, the practical relevance of Elliptical Wishart distributions, particularly the $t$-Wishart distribution, is demonstrated through a fitting experiment conducted on real electroencephalographic data. This experiment highlights their effectiveness in accurately modeling real covariance matrices.

papers.title: Secure Distributed Matrix Multiplication with Precomputation
papers.authors: Ryann Cartor, Rafael G. L. D'Oliveira, Salim El Rouayheb, Daniel Heinlein, David Karpuk, Freeman Slaughter, Alex Sprintson
papers.abstract:
We consider secure distributed matrix multiplication, in which a user computes the product of two matrices with the help of honest-but-curious servers, any $T$ of which may collude. Using the outer-product partition, the matrices are split into $K$ and $L$ blocks and hidden by random masks. Assuming the user has precomputed the products of the random matrices, we develop methods that use this precomputation to reduce the number of servers required.
  Polynomial codes are designed through degree tables, whose distinct entries count the servers. We show that precomputation can reduce the minimum number of servers by designing degree tables specifically for this setting. For Gap Additive Secure Polynomial (GASPr) codes, we give a precise formula and show that it is monotone in the chain length $r$, so only the extremes GASP_small and GASP_big matter. We also prove lower bounds attained by GASP_small in several regimes. Consequently, any fraction of colluding servers below one can be tolerated, compared to the threshold of one half without precomputation, and the order of the total computational complexity decreases when the colluders are a fixed fraction of the servers. We show that no existing construction uses fewer servers than the better of GASP_small and GASP_big once the mask products are precomputed.
  We introduce Gap-Reduced Additive Secure Polynomial (GRASP) codes, which retain a single interval for the mask degrees while selecting the information degrees carefully. For $K = T = 4$ and every $L \geq 3$, we give an explicit GRASP code that uses one fewer server than every GASPr code and is within two servers of optimal. For large $T$, the configuration becomes an integer packing problem independent of $T$, and the number of servers saved by GRASP over GASPr grows quadratically in $K$ and $L$.

papers.title: Quantitative asymptotics for polynomial patterns in the primes
papers.authors: Lilian Matthiesen, Joni Ter\"av\"ainen, Mengdi Wang
papers.abstract:
We prove quantitative estimates for averages of the von Mangoldt and M\"obius functions along polynomial progressions $n+P_1(m),\ldots, n+P_k(m)$ for a large class of polynomials $P_i$. The error terms obtained save an arbitrary power of logarithm, matching the classical Siegel--Walfisz error term. These results give the first quantitative bounds for the Tao--Ziegler polynomial patterns in the primes result.
  The proofs are based on a quantitative generalised von Neumann theorem of Peluse, a recent result of Leng on strong bounds for the Gowers uniformity of the primes, and analysis of a ``Siegel model'' for the von Mangoldt function along polynomial progressions.

papers.title: On Bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: Recently, \"Ozarslan and Elidemir (2023) introduced a methodology for constructing two-variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one-variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. The primary objective of the paper is to introduce novel class of two-variable biorthogonal polynomials namley bivariate Jacobi Konhauser polynomials. We investigate several fundamental properties of these polynomials including their biorthogonality property, operational formula, generating function, and integral representation. Furthermore, We inverstigate their images under the Laplace transform, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Mittag Leffler (JKML) function and obtain the similar properties for them.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: Finding pure Nash equilibria in large random games
papers.authors: Andrea Collevecchio, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Ziwen Zhong
papers.abstract: Best Response Dynamics (BRD) constitute a family of strategy update rules designed to identify Pure Nash Equilibria (PNEs) in strategic games. In each iteration, a player is selected uniformly at random and adopts a best response strategy, maximising their payoff given the current strategies of the other players. If no improvement is possible for the selected player, another is chosen. The process terminates upon reaching a state where no player wishes to deviate, corresponding to a PNE. However, convergence is not guaranteed as either PNEs may not exist, or the dynamics may become confined within substructures of the game, which we call traps, that admit no PNEs. We investigate this behaviour in the context of random games with $N$ players, each choosing between two actions and receiving independently and identically distributed payoffs. The payoff distribution is permitted to have atoms, allowing for the possibility of ties. The induced dynamics define a class of random walks on the $N$-dimensional hypercube, where the landscape includes two types of absorbing sets: PNEs and traps. Our analysis encompasses BRD, simple random walks, and a broad class of nearest-neighbour processes. We prove that, with high probability, these dynamics reach a PNE before encountering any trap. Our results complete and generalise the ones by Amiet, Collevecchio, Scarsini and Zhong (2021), using a different approach.

papers.title: Harary's Sum and Integral Sum Graphs -- A Survey in detail
papers.authors: V. Vilfred Kamalappan, Lowell W. Beineke
papers.abstract: Harary introduced the concepts of sum and integral sum graphs. A graph $G$ is a {\em sum graph} if the vertices of $G$ can be labeled with distinct positive integers so that $e = uv$ is an edge of $G$ if and only if the sum of the labels on vertices $u$ and $v$ is also a label in $G$. An {\em integral sum graph} is also defined just as sum graph, the difference being that the labels may be any distinct integers. This survey presents results obtained by different authors, in detail, on sum and integral sum graphs.

papers.title: Quantum inverse scattering for the 20-vertex model up to Dynkin automorphism: 3D Poisson structure, triangular height functions, weak integrability
papers.abstract: We initiate a novel application of the quantum inverse scattering method for the 20-vertex model, building upon seminal work from Faddeev and Takhtajan on the study of Hamiltonian systems. In comparison to a previous work of the author in late 2023 which characterized integrability of a Hamiltonian flow for the 6-vertex model from integrability of inhomogeneous limit shapes, formalized in a work of Keating, Reshetikhin and Sridhar, notions similar to those of integrability can be realized for the 20-vertex model by studying new classes of higher-dimensional L-operators. Such L-operators provided by Boos and colleagues have algebraic, combinatorial, and geometric, qualities, all of which impact leading order approximations of correlations, products of L-operators, the transfer matrix, and the quantum monodromy matrix.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision Lloyd's Algorithm for k-means Clustering
papers.authors: Erin Carson, Xinye Chen, Xiaobo Liu
papers.abstract: As low-precision arithmetic becomes more widely available on modern hardware, we develop mixed-precision variants of Lloyd's algorithm for k-means clustering, with a family of mixed-precision kernels for Euclidean distance computation as the main ingredient. These kernels are guided by rounding-error analysis and use a simple reliability test to decide whether the expanded distance formula can be evaluated safely with low precision or a higher-precision correction by the direct distance formula is required. Thus, most distance computations can be carried out with low precision, while high-precision arithmetic is used selectively when cancellation may lead to a loss of accuracy. We evaluate the proposed methods on large-scale distance-computation benchmarks, synthetic clustering problems, and image-segmentation tasks. The experiments verify that the mixed-precision kernels on GPUs can substantially improve performance while retaining accuracy and convergence behavior of higher-precision baselines. In particular, our implemented distance computation in CUDA achieves speedups of up to $4\times$ over the \texttt{PyTorch} baseline that evaluates the expanded formula in FP64 on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, with overall maximum relative errors of order $10^{-3}$, while providing increased numerical robustness in cancellation-prone calculations. The resulting mixed-precision kernels show efficiency for clustering and image segmentation, although the observed gains depend on factors such as feature dimension, and number of clusters. The mixed-precision kernels offer a favorable trade-off between performance and accuracy for clustering, and suggest that similar ideas may be beneficial for other distance-based machine learning methods.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Asymptotics of a Gauss hypergeometric function related to moments of symmetric square L-functions I
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for a special case of the Gauss hypergeometric function, which arises in the explicit formula for the second moment of Maass form symmetric-square $L$-functions.

papers.title: Shift associative algebras
papers.authors: Hani Abdelwahab, Ivan Kaygorodov, Bauyrzhan Sartayev
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of algebras satisfying the identity $(xy)z=y(zx),$ named as shift associative algebras. Our research shows that these algebras are related to many interesting identities. In particular, they are related to anti-Poisson-Jordan algebras and algebras of associative type $\sigma$. We study algebras of associative type $\sigma$ to be Koszul and self-dual. A basis of the free shift associative algebra generated by a countable set $X$ was constructed. An analog of Wedderburn-Artin's theorem was established. The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $4$-dimensional shift associative algebras are given. In particular, we proved that the first non-associative shift associative algebra appears only in dimension $5$.

papers.title: ARMAr-LASSO: Mitigating the Impact of Predictor Serial Correlation on the LASSO
papers.authors: Simone Tonini (L'EMbeDS and Institute of Economics, Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies, Pisa), Francesca Chiaromonte (L'EMbeDS and Institute of Economics, Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies, Pisa, Dept. of Statistics, The Pennsylvania State University), Alessandro Giovannelli (University of L'Aquila)
papers.abstract: We explore estimation and prediction accuracy for sparse linear models, focusing on scenarios where both predictors and errors carry serial correlations. We establish a clear link between predictor serial correlation and the performance of the LASSO, showing that even orthogonal or weakly correlated stationary AR processes can lead to significant spurious correlations due to their serial correlations. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach named ARMAr-LASSO (ARMA residuals LASSO), which applies the LASSO to predictors that have been pre-whitened with ARMA filters and lags of dependent variable. We establish oracle inequalities for the feasible estimator and assess its estimation, selection, and forecasting performance empirically. Our findings are supported by extensive simulations and an application to real-world macroeconomic data, which highlight the superior performance of the ARMAr-LASSO for handling sparse linear models in the context of time series.

papers.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.abstract: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While a standard probabilistic proof uses matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose an elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity: any 1-sub-Gaussian distribution with variance 1 yields the same sufficient target dimension as the Gaussian distribution. We then extend the analysis to sparse projections, with data-dependent sparsity conditions on the pairwise differences of the points, and we quantify the cost of sparsity on the target dimension. A complementary lower bound shows the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

papers.title: Classification of real nodal orders
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study properties of nodal orders defined over arbitrary base fields. In particular we give a classification of complete real nodal orders.

papers.title: A Projective Twist on the Hasse Norm Theorem
papers.authors: Thomas R\"ud, Alan Bu, Kevin Xiao
papers.abstract: A finite extension of global fields $L/K$ satisfies the Hasse norm principle if any nonzero element of $K$ has the property that it is a norm locally if and only if it is a norm globally. In 1931, Hasse proved that any cyclic extension satisfies the Hasse norm principle, providing a novel approach to extending the local-global principle to equations with degree greater than $2$. In this paper, we introduce the projective Hasse norm principle, generalizing the Hasse norm principle to multiple fields and asking whether a line through the origin that contains a simultaneous norm locally in every field must also contain a norm globally in every field. We show that the projective Hasse norm principle is independent of the conjunction of Hasse norm principles in all of the constituent fields in the general case, and that the projective principle holds whenever the fields are all Galois and jointly linearly disjoint, without assuming their individual Hasse norm principles. We also give a criterion in terms of their Galois groups and prove that the implication holds whenever the Galois group of their compositum has fourth-power-free order. A counterexample of Demarche and Wei shows that this bound is sharp. We also prove an analogue of the Hasse norm theorem for the projective Hasse norm principle, namely that the projective Hasse norm principle holds for every finite family of cyclic extensions.

papers.title: Markov-Nash equilibria in mean-field games under model uncertainty
papers.authors: Johannes Langner, Ariel Neufeld, Kyunghyun Park
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a framework for mean-field Markov games under model uncertainty. In this framework, a state-measure flow describing the collective behavior of a population affects the given reward function as well as the unknown transition kernel of the representative agent. The agent's objective is to choose an optimal Markov policy in order to maximize her worst-case expected reward, where worst-case refers to the most adverse scenario among all transition kernels considered to be feasible to describe the unknown true law of the environment. We prove the existence of a mean-field equilibrium under model uncertainty, where the agent chooses the optimal policy that maximizes the worst-case expected reward, and the state-measure flow aligns with the agent's state distribution under the optimal policy and the worst-case transition kernel. Moreover, we prove that for suitable multi-agent Markov games under model uncertainty the optimal policy from the mean-field equilibrium forms an approximate Markov-Nash equilibrium whenever the number of agents is large enough.

papers.title: On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy
papers.authors: Gabriel Goldberg, Jonathan Osinski, Alejandro Poveda
papers.abstract: In the first part of the manuscript, we establish several consistency results concerning Woodin's HOD hypothesis and large cardinals around the level of extendibility. First, we prove that the first extendible cardinal can be the first strongly compact in HOD. Second, answering a question in \cite{CFH}, we prove that the first supercompact cardinal can be the first strongly compact, non supercompact, of HOD. We extend a former result of Woodin by showing that under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible cardinal is $C^{(1)}$-supercompact in HOD. We also show that the first cardinal-correct extendible may not be extendible, thus answering a question by Gitman and Osinski \cite[\S9]{GitOsi}. In the second part of the manuscript, we discuss the extent to which weak covering can fail below the first supercompact cardinal $\delta$ in a context where the HOD hypothesis holds. Answering a question of Cummings et al. \cite{CumFriGol}, we show that under the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis there are many singulars $\kappa<\delta$ where $\mathrm{cf}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(\kappa)=\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ and $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}=\kappa^{+}.$ In contrast, we also show that the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis is consistent with $\delta$ carrying a club of $\mathrm{HOD}$-regulars cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}<\kappa^{+}$. Finally, we close the manuscript with a discussion about the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis and $\omega$-strong measurability.

papers.title: $\delta$-Poisson and transposed $\delta$-Poisson algebras
papers.authors: Hani Abdelwahab, Ivan Kaygorodov, Bauyrzhan Sartayev
papers.abstract: We study two new classes of Poisson-type algebras, namely, $\delta$-Poisson and transposed $\delta$-Poisson algebras. We show that these algebras are related to many interesting identities; in particular, they are related to shift associative algebras, $F$-manifold algebras, algebras of Jordan brackets, etc. We classify simple $\delta$-Poisson and transposed $\delta$-Poisson algebras and find their depolarizations. We study the Koszulity and self-duality of the $\delta$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson operads. Bases of the free $\delta$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson algebras generated by a countable set $X$ are constructed.

papers.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
papers.authors: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Yupeng Li, Jacob P. Matherne
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Br\"and\'en and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

papers.title: Projected gradient methods for nonconvex and stochastic smooth optimization: new complexities and auto-conditioned stepsizes
papers.authors: Guanghui Lan, Tianjiao Li, Yangyang Xu
papers.abstract: We present a novel class of projected gradient (PG) methods for minimizing a smooth but not necessarily convex function over a convex compact set. We first provide a novel analysis of the constant-stepsize PG method, achieving a unified iteration complexity for finding an approximate stationary point for convex and nonconvex problems. We then develop an "auto-conditioned" projected gradient (AC-PG) variant that achieves the same iteration complexity without requiring the input of the Lipschitz constant of the gradient or any line search procedure. The key idea is to estimate the Lipschitz constant using first-order information gathered from the previous iterations, and to show that the error caused by underestimating the Lipschitz constant can be properly controlled. We then generalize the PG methods to the stochastic setting, by proposing a stochastic projected gradient (SPG) method and a variance-reduced stochastic gradient (VR-SPG) method, achieving new unified complexity bounds in different oracle settings. We also present auto-conditioned stepsize policies for both stochastic PG methods and establish comparable convergence guarantees.

papers.title: On statistical and causal models associated with acyclic directed mixed graphs
papers.abstract: Causal models in statistics are often described using acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs), which contain directed and bidirected edges and no directed cycles. This article surveys various interpretations of ADMGs, discusses their relations in different sub-classes of ADMGs, and argues that one of them---the noise expansion (NE) model---should be used as the default interpretation. Our endorsement of the NE model is based on two observations. First, in a subclass of ADMGs called exogenously bidirected graphs (which retain most of the good properties of directed acyclic graphs and bidirected graphs), the NE model is equivalent to many other interpretations, including the ordinary Markov and nested Markov models. Second, the NE model for an arbitrary ADMG is exactly the union of the observed margins of NE models on its exogenously bidirected expansions. This property is referred to as completeness, as it shows that the model does not commit to any specific latent variable explanation. In proving the nested Markov property, we also develop an ADMG-based theory for causality and its complete characterization via the potential outcome calculus. Finally, we compare the NE model with the closely related but different interpretation of ADMGs as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with latent variables that is commonly used in the literature. We argue that the ``latent DAG'' interpretation is mathematically unnecessary, makes obscure ontological assumptions, and discourages practitioners from deliberating over important structural assumptions.

papers.title: Categorical Diffusion of Weighted Lattices
papers.authors: Robert Ghrist, Miguel Lopez, Paige Randall North, Hans Riess
papers.abstract: Quantales are well known in logic and computer science, and categories enriched in them unify ordered, metric, relational, and tropical structures. Problems in dynamic programming, synchronization, and discrete event systems require reconciling local data, represented by objects in a quantale-enriched category, across the edges of a network, represented by an undirected graph. Concurrently, replacing inner products with hom-objects and linear adjoints with adjoint functors initiates a categorification of graph and sheaf Laplacians, with a view toward enrichment in larger monoidal categories and bicategories. To this end, we lay the foundations for an enriched harmonic analysis on graphs through cellular sheaves of quantale-enriched categories and a Laplace operator that we call the Lawvere Laplacian. Over an arbitrary unital quantale, the weighted global sections of such a sheaf are the vertex data that agree across every edge up to the tolerances of a weight function. They form the quantale-enriched category of natural transformations from a weight diagram into the sheaf, which is a weighted limit when the quantale is commutative. When the restriction maps have right adjoints, we prove that the weighted global sections are the suffix points of the Lawvere Laplacian, which are the equilibria of its harmonic flow. Under a continuity hypothesis, the harmonic flow converges to the greatest weighted global section below its initial cochain, and for central weight functions the weighted global sections form a complete coreflective subcategory of the cochains. Instances of the theory include the Bellman--Ford iteration over the Lawvere quantale, the reconciliation of local cost estimates, quantale and clock synchronization, and coupled max-plus discrete event systems.

papers.title: $P$-trivial MMP, Zariski decompositions and minimal models for generalised pairs
papers.abstract: We develop an inductive method for generalised pairs (g-pairs) without the NQC assumption. It is based on $P$-trivial MMPs, whose steps are trivial with respect to a given nef divisor $P$. For klt g-pairs, if $P$ is numerically equivalent to an effective divisor, we perturb the boundary so that any MMP on $K_X+B+M+\alpha P$ is $P$-trivial for $\alpha\gg0$. For lc g-pairs, the components with coefficient one cannot be perturbed, so we use induction on lc centres. If $K_X+B+M-P$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor, then local Cartier indices control the coefficients under divisorial adjunction, and we prove a special termination. This includes the case $P=0$, where $K_X+B+M$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor. As applications, we prove that a projective lc g-pair $(X,B+M)$ of dimension $3$ has a minimal model if $K_X+B+M$ birationally has a Nakayama-Zariski decomposition with nef positive part and either $K_X+B+M\equiv D\geq0$ or $M\equiv D\geq0$. We also prove this for klt g-pairs in arbitrary dimension. In dimension $4$, the last condition can be replaced by the log abundance of the nef data. For usual pairs, this is a theorem of Birkar and the author.

papers.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
papers.abstract:
Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether
  \[
  S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}}
  \]
  converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erd\H{o}s and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].

papers.title: Compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of analytic varieties
papers.authors: Piotr Achinger, Sally Gilles, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}
papers.abstract: We study properties of compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties. In particular, we prove a comparison theorem, in a stable range, with compactly supported syntomic cohomology, which is built from compactly supported Hyodo-Kato and ${\mathcal B}^+_{\rm dr}$-cohomologies. We derive from that a (limited version of a) fundamental diagram.

papers.title: Rational values of the weak saturation limit
papers.abstract: Given a graph $F$, a graph $G$ is weakly $F$-saturated if all non-edges of $G$ can be added in some order so that each new edge introduces a copy of $F$. The weak saturation number $\operatorname{wsat}(n, F)$ is the minimum number of edges in a weakly $F$-saturated graph on $n$ vertices. Bollob\'as initiated the study of weak saturation in 1968 to study percolation processes, which originated in biology and have applications in physics and computer science. It was shown by Alon that for each $F$, there is a constant $w_F$ such that $\operatorname{wsat}(n, F) = w_Fn + o(n)$. We characterize all possible rational values of $w_F$, proving in particular that $w_F$ can equal any rational number at least $\frac 32$.

papers.title: The infinitesimal subgroup of interpretable groups in some dp-minimal valued fields
papers.authors: Yatir Halevi, Assaf Hasson, Ya'acov Peterzil
papers.abstract:
We continue our local analysis of groups interpretable in various dp-minimal valued fields, as introduced in [8]. We associate with every infinite group $G$ interpretable in those fields an infinite type-definable infinitesimal subgroup $
u(G)$, generated by the four infinitesimal subgroups $
u_D(G)$ associated with the distinguished sorts $K$, $	extbf{k}$, $\Gamma$ and $K/\mathcal{O}$.
  To show that $
u(G)$ is type-definable, we show that the resulting subgroups $
u_D(G)$ commute with each other as $D$ ranges over the four distinguished sorts. We then study the basic properties of $
u(G)$. Among others, we show that $
u(G_1	imes G_2)=
u(G_1)	imes 
u(G_2)$ and that if $G_1\le G$ is a definable subgroup then $
u(G_1)$ is relatively definable in $
u(G)$. We also discuss possible connections between $\mathrm{dp	ext{-}rk}(
u(G))$ and elimination of imaginaries.

papers.title: Cardinalities of Ultraproducts of Finite Sets in ZF + DC
papers.abstract: Relative to an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent with ZF + DC that there exists an ultrafilter $U$ on $\omega$ such that two infinite ultraproducts of finite sets, $\prod A_n / U$ and $\prod B_n / U$, have the same cardinality if and only if $0 < \lim_U |A_n|/|B_n| < \infty$. In particular, this holds in $W[U]$, where $W$ is the Solovay Model and $U$ is $[\omega]^\omega$-generic.

papers.title: $C^0$-Contact Anosov flows
papers.authors: Cheikh Khoule, Matheus Manso, Ameth Ndiaye, Khadim War
papers.abstract: We prove that smooth reparametrizations of the geodesic flow on a manifold of constant negative curvature are contact Anosov flows. In particular we give a new class of exponentially mixing Anosov flows. Moreover, this introduces the notion of $C^0$-contact and we prove that the classical Gray stability theorem that is known in the smooth case fails in this setting.

papers.title: Coherent manifolds and quantization
papers.authors: Arnold Neumaier, Phillip Josef Bachler, Arash Ghaani Farashahi
papers.abstract: We study the differential geometry of coherent manifolds modelled on convenient vector spaces and apply it to coherent quantization. A smooth coherent product determines geometric structures on the label manifold. We construct a common invariant domain for the quantizations of coherent vector fields and of coherent diffeomorphisms with smooth diffeomorphic adjoints. These quantizations are distinguished operators on the associated quantum space and satisfy commutator, covariance, and formal adjoint relations. Their coherent matrix elements can be calculated by differentiation and substitution in the coherent product. Extending the operators to the common invariant domain leaves their Hilbert space closures unchanged. Motions in subgroups of diffeomorphisms give rise to Lie algebras of generators without requiring a Lie group structure on the subgroup. Suitable coherent motions recover the infinitesimal quantization by differentiation. We express quantum dynamics through coherent matrix elements and obtain a coherent action principle by restricting the quantum action to coherent states. For Klauder spaces, the construction gives creation and annihilation operators, the canonical commutation relations, Segal fields, Weyl operators, and normal ordering on the common invariant domain.

papers.title: Triangle-free graphs with the fewest independent sets
papers.authors: Pjotr Buys, Jan van den Heuvel, Ross J. Kang
papers.abstract:
Given $d>0$ and a positive integer $n$, let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d$. With an elegant induction, Shearer (1983) tightened a seminal result of Ajtai, Koml\'os and Szemer\'edi (1980/1981) by proving that $G$ contains an independent set of size at least $(1+o(1))\frac{\log d}{d}n$ as $d\to\infty$.
  By a generalisation of Shearer's method, we prove that the number of independent sets in $G$ must be at least $\exp\left((1+o(1))\frac{(\log d)^2}{2d}n\right)$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves upon results of Cooper and Mubayi (2014) and Davies, Jenssen, Perkins, and Roberts (2018). Our method also provides good lower bounds on the independence polynomial of $G$, one of which implies Shearer's result itself. As certified by a classic probabilistic construction, our bound on the number of independent sets is sharp to several leading terms as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: Modeling and Analysis of an Optimal Insulation Problem on Non-Smooth Domains
papers.authors: Harbir Antil, Alex Kaltenbach, Keegan L. A. Kirk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study an insulation problem that seeks the optimal distribution of a fixed amount $m>0$ of insulating material coating an insulated boundary $\Gamma_I\subseteq \partial\Omega$ of a thermally conducting body $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $d\in \mathbb{N}$. The thickness of the thin insulating layer $\Sigma_{I}^{\varepsilon}$ is given locally via $\varepsilon \mathtt{d}$, where $\mathtt{d}\colon \Gamma_{I}\to [0,+\infty)$ specifies the (to be determined) distribution of the insulating material. We establish $\Gamma(L^2(\mathbb{R}^d))$-convergence of the problem (as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$). Different from the existing literature, which predominantly assumes that the thermally conducting body $\Omega$ has a $C^{1,1}$-boundary, we merely assume that $\Gamma_I$ is piece-wise flat. To overcome this lack of boundary regularity, we define the thin insulating boundary layer $\Sigma_{I}^{\varepsilon}$ using a Lipschitz continuous transversal vector field rather than the outward unit normal vector field. The piece-wise flatness condition on $\Gamma_I$ is only needed to prove the $\liminf$-estimate. In fact, for the $\limsup$-estimate is enough that the thermally conducting body $\Omega$ has a $C^{0,1}$-boundary.

papers.title: Multiparameter extensions of the Christ-Kiselev maximal theorem: strong variational bounds
papers.abstract: For a linear operator $T$ bounded from $L^p(Y)$ to $L^q(X)$, the Christ--Kiselev theorem gives $L^p \to L^q$ bounds for the maximal function $T^{*}$ associated to a filtration on $Y$. This result has been extended to the multiparameter setting, establishing bounds for the maximal function associated to a product of filtrations. In this note, we strengthen these results by proving $\rho$-variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations when $\rho>p$. Furthermore, we give a multilinear extension of the Christ--Kiselev theorem, establishing strong variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations for a general multilinear operator.

papers.title: Asymmetric graph alignment and the phase transition for asymmetric tree correlation testing
papers.abstract:
Graph alignment - identifying node correspondences between two graphs - is a fundamental problem with applications in network analysis, biology, and privacy research. While substantial progress has been made in aligning correlated Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs under symmetric settings, real-world networks often exhibit asymmetry in both node numbers and edge densities. In this work, we introduce a novel framework for asymmetric correlated Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs, generalizing existing models to account for these asymmetries. We conduct a rigorous theoretical analysis of graph alignment in the sparse regime, where local neighborhoods exhibit tree-like structures. Our approach leverages tree correlation testing as the central tool in our polynomial-time algorithm, MPAlign, which achieves one-sided partial alignment under certain conditions.
  A key contribution of our work is characterizing these conditions under which asymmetric tree correlation testing is feasible: If two correlated graphs $G$ and $G'$ have average degrees $\lambda s$ and $\lambda s'$ respectively, where $\lambda$ is their common density and $s,s'$ are marginal correlation parameters, their tree neighborhoods can be aligned if $ss' > \alpha$, where $\alpha$ denotes Otter's constant and $\lambda$ is supposed large enough. The feasibility of this tree comparison problem undergoes a sharp phase transition since $ss' \leq \alpha$ implies its impossibility. These new results on tree correlation testing allow us to solve a class of random subgraph isomorphism problems, resolving an open problem in the field.

papers.title: Fermat Distance-to-Measure: a robust Fermat-like metric
papers.authors: J\'er\^ome Taupin (LMO, INRIA), Fr\'ed\'eric Chazal (LMO, INRIA)
papers.abstract: Given a probability measure with density, Fermat distances and density-driven metrics are conformal transformations of the Euclidean metric that shrink distances in high density areas and enlarge distances in low density areas. Although they have been widely studied and have shown to be useful in various machine learning tasks, they are limited to measures with density (with respect to Lebesgue measure, or volume form on manifold). In this paper, by replacing the density with the Distance-to-Measure, we introduce a new metric, the Fermat Distance-to-Measure, defined for any probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We derive strong stability properties for the Fermat Distance-to-Measure with respect to the measure and propose an estimator from random sampling of the same measure, featuring an explicit bound on its convergence rate.

papers.title: Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for unramified maximal parahoric level
papers.abstract: We prove the Kudla--Rapoport conjecture for unramified unitary groups with maximal parahoric level structure. Our approach differs from the local proof of C. Li and W. Zhang. We reduce the conjecture to a global intersection problem using local-global compatibility. Then we apply an inductive procedure based on the modularity of generating series of global special divisors. This strategy follows the framework developed in the proof of the arithmetic fundamental lemma by W. Zhang and Mihatsch--Zhang and arithmetic transfer identities by Z. Zhang and Luo--Mihatsch--Zhang.

papers.title: Regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, $4$-torus, and small covers over $\Delta^2 \times \Delta^2$
papers.abstract: A crystallization is an edge-colored graph encoding a contracted triangulation of a closed PL manifold, providing a combinatorial framework for studying PL-manifold invariants. In this framework, we determine the regular genus of several important $4$-manifolds. We first prove that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=6$, thereby resolving a conjecture on the regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1$. We also establish that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=16$. These computations lead to further observations on the regular genus of the $n$-torus and motivate the conjecture $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{T}^n)=1+\frac{(n+1)!(n-3)}{8}$ for $n\geq 5$. We then apply our combinatorial methods to small covers. For the simple polytope $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$, we classify the corresponding small covers up to Davis-Januszkiewicz equivalence and obtain exactly seven equivalence classes. One of these is $\mathbb{RP}^2\times\mathbb{RP}^2$, while the remaining six are $\mathbb{RP}^2$-bundles over $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We prove that all seven small covers have regular genus $8$. Thus, the paper provides regular genus computations for a collection of $4$-manifolds arising from products and small covers. The approach is purely combinatorial and relies on various combinatorial moves.

papers.title: SDP bounds on the stability number via ADMM and intermediate levels of the Lasserre hierarchy
papers.authors: Lennart Sinjorgo, Renata Sotirov, Juan C. Vera
papers.abstract: We consider the Lasserre hierarchy for computing bounds on the stability number of graphs. The semidefinite programs (SDPs) arising from this hierarchy involve large matrix variables and many linear constraints, which makes them difficult to solve using interior-point methods. We propose solving these SDPs using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). When the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy for a given graph is intractable for the ADMM, we consider an intermediate-level relaxation of the hierarchy. To warm-start the ADMM, we use an optimal solution from the first level of the Lasserre hierarchy, which is equivalent to the well-known Lov\'asz theta function. Additionally, we use this solution to determine which degree two monomials to add in the Lasserre hierarchy relaxation to obtain an intermediate level between 1 and 2. Computational results demonstrate that our approach yields strong bounds on the stability number, which are computable within reasonable running times. We provide {improved} bounds on the stability number of various graphs from the literature.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.
