papers.title: Structure and asymptotic preserving deep neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in multiscale kinetic equations
papers.authors: Wei Chen, Giacomo Dimarco, Lorenzo Pareschi
papers.abstract: The high dimensionality of kinetic equations with stochastic parameters poses major computational challenges for uncertainty quantification (UQ). Traditional Monte Carlo (MC) sampling methods, while widely used, suffer from slow convergence and high variance, which become increasingly severe as the dimensionality of the parameter space grows. To accelerate MC sampling, we adopt a multiscale control variates strategy that leverages low-fidelity solutions from simplified kinetic models to reduce variance. To further improve sampling efficiency and preserve the underlying physics, we introduce surrogate models based on structure and asymptotic preserving neural networks (SAPNNs). These deep neural networks are specifically designed to satisfy key physical properties, including positivity, conservation laws, entropy dissipation, and asymptotic limits. By training the SAPNNs on low-fidelity models and enriching them with selected high-fidelity samples from the full Boltzmann equation, our method achieves significant variance reduction while maintaining physical consistency and asymptotic accuracy. The proposed methodology enables efficient large-scale prediction in kinetic UQ and is validated across both homogeneous and nonhomogeneous multiscale regimes. Numerical results demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency compared to standard MC techniques.

papers.title: On the Residue Sequence in Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology
papers.abstract: Algebraic K-theory participates in localization sequences, as first established by Quillen. We identify their boundary maps with the \emph{residue} map from logarithmic TC under the cyclotomic trace, resolving a conjecture of Rognes. As a consequence, we obtain e.g. a trace map from the K-theory of periodic complex K-theory to the logarithmic TC of connective complex K-theory. Moreover, we find that there exists a stable infinity-category C such that TC(C) realizes logarithmic TC for specific log structures, such as the natural ones on discrete valuation rings, connective complex K-theory, and truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. This provides evidence for the existence of a category of modules in the context of logarithmic geometry. We conjecture that such a category can be chosen to reflect additional structure on logarithmic TC, and we give evidence for this for discrete valuation rings.

papers.title: Large deviations for Generalized Polya Urns with non-binary increments
papers.abstract: In this paper we show how to extend the large deviation principle for the paths of the Hill, Lane and Sudderth urn model to the case in which the urn increment is not a binary variable. In particular, we extend Theorem 1 of [Stochastic Processes and their Applications, 127 (2017), 3372-3411] to urn processes with integer increments from zero to $K$. The increment probabilities depend on the mean of the preceding increments and are continuous and strictly positive on the entire state interval. We derive the terminal entropy and uniform estimates for the probabilities of individual attainable final values. We identify the zero-cost states and paths. We prove the existence and strict convexity of the normalized limiting cumulant generating function and provide conditions for duality with the entropy. We characterize the realizable continuous concave entropies and construct the corresponding urn probabilities.

papers.title: Geometrically formal Hermitian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study geometrically formal Hermitian metrics on compact complex manifolds, focusing on Dolbeault, Bott-Chern, and Aeppli cohomologies. We establish topological and cohomological obstructions to their existence and we provide a detailed analysis for several classes of compact complex manifolds. We prove that on any blow-up of a K\"ahler manifold no K\"ahler metric can be geometrically formal, and that K\"ahler metrics with nonnegative curvature operator are necessarily geometrically formal.

papers.title: Convergence of a finite-volume scheme for aggregation-diffusion equations with saturation
papers.abstract: In [Bailo, Carrillo, Hu. SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2023] the authors introduce a finite-volume method for aggregation-diffusion equations with non-linear mobility. In this paper we prove convergence of this method using an Aubin--Simons compactness theorem due to Gallou\"et and Latch\'e. We use suitable discrete $H^1$ and $W^{-1,1}$ discrete norms. We provide two convergence results. A first result shows convergence with general entropies ($U$) (including singular and degenerate) if the initial datum does not have free boundaries, the mobility is Lipschitz, and the confinement ($V$) and aggregation ($K$) potentials are $W^{2,\infty}_0$. A second result shows convergence when the initial datum has free boundaries, mobility is just continuous, and $V$ and $K$ are $W^{1,\infty}$, but under the assumption that the entropy $U$ is $C^1$ and strictly convex.

papers.title: Adaptive direct search for blackbox optimization
papers.authors: Charles Audet, Th\'eo Denorme, Youssef Diouane, S\'ebastien Le Digabel, Christophe Tribes
papers.abstract: Two families of directional direct search methods have emerged in derivative-free and blackbox optimization (DFO and BBO), each based on distinct principles: Mesh Adaptive Direct Search (MADS) and Sufficient Decrease Direct Search (SDDS). MADS restricts trial points to a mesh and accepts any improvement, ensuring that none are missed, but at the cost of restricting the placement of trial points. SDDS allows greater freedom by evaluating points anywhere in the space, but accepts only those yielding a sufficient decrease in the objective function value, which may lead to discarding promising points. This work introduces a new class of methods, Adaptive Direct Search (ADS), which uses a novel acceptance rule based on the so-called punctured space, avoiding both mesh and sufficient decrease conditions. ADS enables flexible search while addressing the limitations of MADS and SDDS, and retains the theoretical foundations of directional direct search. Computational results in constrained and unconstrained settings highlight its performance compared to both MADS and SDDS.

papers.title: The pure $Y=X^{d}$ truncated moment problem
papers.abstract: Let $\beta \equiv\beta^{(2n)}$ be a real bivariate sequence of degree $2n$. We study the existence of representing measures for $\beta$ supported in the curve $y=x^{d}$ ($d\ge 1$) in the case when all column dependence relations in the moment matrix $M_n(\beta)$ are generated by the relation $Y=X^{d}$. We prove that the core variety of $\beta$, $\mathcal{CV}(L_{\beta})$, is nonempty (equivalently, representing measures exist) if and only if $C$, the partially defined \textit{core matrix} of $\beta$, admits a positive, recursively generated completion $C[A]$. Moreover, $\mathcal{CV}(L_{\beta})$ is the entire curve $y=x^{d}$ if and only if there is a positive definite completion $C[A]$. In the remaining case, if there is a measure, it is unique and finitely atomic. For $d = 3$, we use these results to compute the core variety of $\beta$ and give new characterizations of the existence of representing measures, which complement a result of the first author.

papers.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the unit disc
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with canonical bundle $K_X$ and holomorphic tangent bundle $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. For each integer $r\geq 2$, each $q\in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of a square root of $K_X$, we obtain a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\ldots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate Hermitian metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. We call $h$ complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\ldots,H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki proved that if $q$ is nonzero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete harmonic metric on the corresponding cyclic Higgs bundle satisfying $\det(h)=1$. The Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for general subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$ whose exponentials are $C^2$ outside a compact subset of $X$. On the unit disc $\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, we also prove that a real complete solution exists for every subharmonic weight function. We further establish a monotone approximation theorem. If $\varphi_\epsilon$ are smooth subharmonic weight functions on the discs $\mathbb D_\epsilon=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1-\epsilon\}$ decreasing to $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the corresponding complete solutions $h_\epsilon$, normalized by $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$, converge monotonically to a complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$.

papers.title: Reversible birth-and-death dynamics in continuum: free-energy dissipation and attractor properties
papers.authors: Benedikt Jahnel, Jonas K\"oppl, Yannic Steenbeck, Alexander Zass
papers.abstract: We consider continuous-time birth-and-death dynamics in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting infinite-volume Gibbs point processes as reversible measures. The birth rates are translation invariant, have finite range, and are uniformly bounded from above and away from zero. For all translation-invariant initial measures, we show that the specific relative entropy is non-increasing along trajectories and that, if the entropy is initially finite, then every long-time weak limit point is a Gibbs point process for the same interaction. Our proofs rest on a lower bound for entropy dissipation in terms of the reduced Palm measure of the evolved law.

papers.title: Embeddability of right-angled Artin groups into hierarchically hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: For a hierarchically hyperbolic group, we give sufficient conditions ensuring that suitable powers of a finite collection of elements generate a right-angled Artin subgroup; under an additional condition, this subgroup is undistorted. We verify these hypotheses in two natural situations: one modeled on mapping class groups, using structural assumptions on the ambient HHG, and one modeled on RAAGs, requiring the chosen elements to be rigidly fully supported. Our results recover known embedding theorems for mapping class groups and extend the non-annular undistortion theorem of Clay--Leininger--Mangahas, while also recovering the Kim--Koberda extension graph theorem for RAAGs.

papers.title: The linear minimal 4-chart with three crossings
papers.abstract:
Charts are oriented labeled graphs in a disk. Every simple surface braid ($2$-dimensional braid) can be described by a chart. Moreover, a chart represents an oriented closed surface embedded in four-space. In this paper, we study such embedded surfaces using charts.
  Let $\Gamma$ be a chart. Let ${\rm Cross}(\Gamma)$ denote the set of all the crossings of $\Gamma$, and let $\Gamma_m$ denote the union of all the edges of label $m$. A 4-chart $\Gamma$ is said to be ${\it linear}$ if every connected component of $$(\Gamma_1\cup \Gamma_3)-{\rm Cross}(\Gamma)$$ is acyclic. In this paper, we prove that after deleting free edges and hoops, every linear minimal $4$-chart with three crossings is lor-equivalent (equivalent under label changes, orientation reversals, and reflections) to the chart describing a $2$-twist-spun trefoil knot.

papers.title: Orlicz spaces and the uncertainty principle
papers.authors: A. Iosevich, I. Li, Z. Li, E. Yu
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a finite signal. The classical uncertainty principle tells us that the product of the support of $f$ and the support of $\hat{f}$, the Fourier transform of $f$, must satisfy $|supp(f)|\cdot|supp(\hat{f})|\geq |G|$. Recently, Iosevich and Mayeli improved the uncertainty principle for signals with Fourier supported on generic sets. This was done by employing the Fourier restriction theory in $L^p$ spaces. In this paper, we extended the $(p,q)$-restriction setting to Orlicz spaces. Then we apply uncertainty principles to the problem of exact recovery, which again extends and recovers the result that Iosevich and Mayeli obtained in Lebesgue spaces.

papers.title: Projective geodesic extensions by conformal modifications in nonholonomic mechanics
papers.abstract: Projective geodesic extensions are reparametrizations of the trajectories of a nonholonomic mechanical system (with only a kinetic energy Lagrangian), in such a way that they can be interpreted as part of the geodesics of a Riemannian metric. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of these extensions, in the case where the constrained Lagrangian remains preserved up to a conformal transformation. When the nonholonomic system has a symmetry group (a Chaplygin system), we clarify the relation between projective geodesic extensions and closely related concepts, such as ${\phi}$-simplicity, invariant measures and Hamiltonization. Throughout the paper, new and relevant examples illustrate the key differences between all these concepts.

papers.title: Infinite Euclidean Distance Discriminants
papers.abstract: We study infinite Euclidean distance discriminants of algebraic varieties, defined as the loci of data points whose fibers under the second projection from the Euclidean distance correspondence are positive-dimensional. In particular, these discriminants contain all data points with infinitely many critical points for the nearest-point problem. We present computer code that computes the infinite Euclidean distance discriminant, and use it to present numerous varieties with nonempty such discriminants. Moreover, we prove that for any data point, the fiber under the second projection is contained in a finite union of hyperspheres centered at that point. For curves, we include a complete characterization; their infinite Euclidean distance discriminants turn out to be affine linear spaces. Finally, we introduce and characterize skew-tube surfaces in three-dimensional space. By construction, these have a one-dimensional infinite Euclidean distance discriminant. We further demonstrate that many skew-tubes have significantly lower Euclidean distance degrees than generic surfaces of the same degree.

papers.title: Functor-induced isomorphisms and $G$-matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore how functor-induced isomorphisms are encoded by $G$-matrices. We first show that the Grothendieck group isomorphism induced by a tilting module can be realized via the $G$-matrix of this tilting module. Building on this, we compare $g$-vectors for a tilted algebra and its associated hereditary algebra, and provide $G$-matrix interpretations of the Coxeter transformation, the Nakayama functor, and the Auslander-Reiten translation for suitable algebras. Furthermore, we demonstrate the geometric representations of any Weyl group can be realized by the $G$-matrices of tilting modules or support $\tau$-tilting modules arising from generalized preprojective algebras. Consequently, the group generated by the transpose of these $G$-matrices is isomorphic to the corresponding Weyl group. Finally, we show that the Grothendieck group isomorphism induced by a $2$-term silting complex can also be realized via the $G$-matrix of this $2$-term silting complex.

papers.title: Absolutely Summing Toeplitz operators on Fock spaces
papers.abstract:
For $1\le p<\infty$, let $F^p_\varphi$ be the Fock spaces on ${\mathbb C}^n$ with the weight function $\varphi$ that \(\varphi \in {\mathcal{C}}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right)\) is real-valued and satisfies
  $
  m{\omega }_{0} \leq d{d}^{c}\varphi \leq M{\omega }_{0}
  $
  for two positive constants \(m\) and \(M\), \({\omega }_{0} = d{d}^{c}{\left| z\right| }^{2}\) is the Euclidean K\"{a}hler form on \({\mathbb{C}}^{n}\), \({d}^{c} = \frac{\sqrt{-1}}{4}\left( {\bar{\partial } - \partial }\right)\). In this paper, we completely characterize those positive Borel measure $\mu$ on ${\mathbb C}^n$ so that the induced Toeplitz operators $T_\mu$ is $r$-summing on $F_{\varphi}^{p}$ for $r \ge 1$.

papers.title: Linking numbers and triple linking numbers for periodic tangles
papers.abstract: Periodic tangles are 1-dimensional submanifolds in the 3-space with translational symmetry. In this paper, we define the linking numbers for singly, doubly, and triply periodic tangles using appropriate motifs and show that they are well-defined and invariant under link-homotopy. Furthermore, we extend the notion to the triple linking numbers for singly, doubly, and triply periodic tangles, and the higher order linking numbers for singly periodic tangles under certain assumptions.

papers.title: Topological Vector Spaces
papers.abstract: Motivated by applications to duality theorems for $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of rigid analytic spaces, we study the category of Topological Vector Spaces in the setting of condensed mathematics. We prove that it contains, as full subcategories, both the category of (topologically) bounded algebraic Vector Spaces and the category of perfect complexes on the Fargues-Fontaine curve. Vector Spaces coming from $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties are examples of sheaves belonging to the former category.

papers.title: A Block-Activated Decomposition Algorithm for Multi-Stage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: We develop a block-activated decomposition algorithm for multi-stage stochastic variational inequalities with nonanticipativity constraints. The algorithm features two computational novelties: (i) At each iteration, it activates only a user-chosen subset of scenarios. (ii) For each activated scenario, it employs the resolvent of the cost operator and the projector onto the constraint set separately. These reduce computational load and enhance tractability, in contrast with existing approaches, which often require evaluating the resolvent of the sum of the cost operator and the normal cone operator of the constraint set. As an application, we demonstrate that in risk-averse stochastic programming with conditional value-at-risk objective functions, our method requires only projecting onto constraint sets, together with solving univariate equations involving the proximity operators of the cost functions, thereby avoiding solving high-dimensional constrained subproblems as required by existing methods.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
papers.abstract:
Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $\nu\neq\kappa$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally.
  Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

papers.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Simultaneous Conjugacy Classes
papers.authors: Jyotirmoy Ganguly, Digjoy Paul, Amritanshu Prasad, K N Raghavan, Velmurugan S
papers.abstract: A Kronecker coefficient is the multiplicity of an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ in a tensor product of irreducible representations. We define Kronecker Hecke algebras and use them as a tool to study Kronecker coefficients in finite groups. We show that the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes in a finite group $G$ is equal to the sum of squares of Kronecker coefficients, and the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes that are closed under elementwise inversion is the sum of Kronecker coefficients weighted by Frobenius-Schur indicators. We use these tools to investigate which finite groups have multiplicity-free tensor products. We introduce the class of doubly real groups, and show that they are precisely the real groups which have multiplicity-free tensor products. We show that non-Abelian groups of odd order, non-Abelian finite simple groups, and most finite general linear groups do not have multiplicity-free tensor products.

papers.title: Exploring the Scaling Crossover of Generalized Jeffreys-Type Law: Modeling, Analysis, and High-Accuracy Numerical Computation
papers.abstract: The generalized Jeffreys-type law is formulated as a multi-term time-fractional Jeffreys-type equation, whose dynamics exhibit rich scaling crossover phenomena associated with different diffusion mechanisms. In this work, we provide a microscopic stochastic interpretation of the MT-TFJE through a continuous-time random walk (CTRW) framework with a generalized waiting-time distribution, elucidating the physical mechanisms underlying the scaling crossover. Based on the Laplace-Volterra formulation and spectral analysis, we establish the well-posedness and stability of the MT-TFJE and derive Sobolev regularity estimates under appropriate assumptions on the initial data and source term. We further develop a high-accuracy numerical scheme, termed CIM-CLG, which combines a contour integral method for temporal approximation with a Chebyshev-Legendre Galerkin method for spatial discretization. The proposed method achieves exponential temporal convergence under the stated regularity of the governing equation, together with high-order spatial accuracy. The temporal approximation involves $\mathcal{O}(N)$ independent contour evaluations, while FFT-based transforms have a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(M^n\log M)$ for spatial dimensions $n=1,2$. The resulting algorithm is naturally parallelizable. Detailed implementation procedures and rigorous error estimates are presented. Extensive numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate the efficiency, accuracy, and robustness of the proposed method, providing a computationally effective framework for generalized nonlocal diffusion problems.

papers.title: Lectures on stochastic sewing with applications
papers.abstract: These are lecture notes for a mini-course on stochastic sewing, taught at the University of Edinburgh and Beijing Institute of Technology in Spring/Summer 2025. The aim is to introduce the reader to stochastic sewing techniques and to show how they can be successfully applied to study various problems in stochastic analysis, including: regularization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by Brownian motion, a L\'evy process or fractional Brownian motion, the study of averaging operators, and the analysis of numerical algorithms.

papers.title: The geometry of magnitude for finite metric spaces
papers.abstract: The main result of this article is a geometric interpretation of magnitude, a real-valued invariant of metric spaces. We introduce a Euclidean embedding of a (suitable) finite metric space $X$ such that the magnitude of $X$ can be expressed in terms of the `circumradius' of its embedding $S$. The circumradius is the radius of the unique sphere that goes through $S$. We give three applications: First, we describe the asymptotic behaviour of the magnitude of $tX$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, in terms of the circumradius. Second, we develop a matrix theory for magnitude that leads to explicit relations between the magnitude of $X$ and the magnitude of its subspaces. Third, we identify a new regime in the limiting behaviour of $tX$, and use this to show submodularity-type results for magnitude as a function on subspaces.

papers.title: Rank 1 phenomena for groups of positive deficiency
papers.abstract: We examine second bounded cohomology and mod p homology in finite index subgroups of 1-relator groups and groups with a presentation of positive deficiency. We use this to determine exactly which subgroups of 1-relator groups are boundedly generated.

papers.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
papers.authors: Luxuan Li, Xiao Wang, Chunfeng Cui
papers.abstract: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.

papers.title: Incomplete U-Statistics of Equireplicate Designs: Berry-Esseen Bound and Efficient Construction
papers.abstract: U-statistics are a fundamental class of estimators that generalize the sample mean and underpin much of nonparametric statistics. Although extensively studied in both statistics and probability, key challenges remain: their high computational cost - addressed partly through incomplete U-statistics - and their non-standard asymptotic behavior in the degenerate case, which typically requires resampling methods for hypothesis testing. This paper presents a novel perspective on U-statistics, grounded in hypergraph theory and combinatorial designs. We identify the dependency graph of an incomplete U-statistic with the line graph of its design hypergraph and use Stein's method to derive Berry-Esseen bounds for deterministic designs under full degeneracy. We further extend these results to studentized statistics using a variance estimator tailored to the fully degenerate setting. The resulting bounds establish Gaussian limits for superlinear design sizes with fixed kernel order and accommodate diverging order under separate conditions. We also develop efficient algorithms for constructing equireplicate designs, a subclass of deterministic designs, which yield minimum-variance incomplete U-statistics in the second-order case. Beyond its theoretical contributions, our framework provides permutation-free alternatives to tests based on fully degenerate U-statistics, as demonstrated in experiments with the two-sample Maximum Mean Discrepancy test and a one-sample mean test based on a higher-order U-statistic.

papers.title: Sharp angle estimates for second order divergence operators
papers.abstract: This article is about the (minimal) sector containing the numerical range of the principal part of a linear second-order elliptic differential operator defined by a form on closed subspaces $V$ of the first-order Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$ incorporating mixed boundary conditions. We relate the angle of sectoriality and the $\mathcal{H}^\infty$-angle of realizations of the elliptic operator to two reference angles: the optimal angle of the $L^2$-realization and the optimal angle of the coefficient function. We thereby consider the operator in several scales of Banach spaces: the Lebesgue space, the negative Sobolev space, and their interpolation scale. For the latter two types of spaces, we rely on recent results regarding the Kato square root property. We focus on minimal assumptions on geometry, and we consider both real and complex coefficients, in particular aiming at explicit estimates built on readily accessible problem data. New results include an explicit estimate for the angle of sectoriality for the elliptic operator on $L^p(\Omega)$ with complex coefficients without any assumptions on geometry, which reduces to the known sharp angle for real coefficients, a new estimate on the angle of the sector containing the numerical range of a linear, continuous and coercive Hilbert space operator, and an estimate on the $\mathcal{H}^{\infty}$-angle for the elliptic operator on $L^p(\Omega)$ with real coefficients.

papers.title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a weak Asplund space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space, then $X\times\mathbb R$ is also a weak Asplund space. This resolves an open problem posed by D. G. Larman and R. R. Phelps in 1979 (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 20 (1979), 115-127). The proof combines the Banach-Mazur game, properties of maximal monotone operators, and the G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability of Minkowski functionals. Specifically, we introduce an iterative perturbed Minkowski convex cone approximation game method, and establish a theoretical framework to verify the existence of dense differentiability sets for convex functions on product spaces. By relating the properties of convex functions on the base space and the product space via projection mappings, and constructing dense $G_\delta$ subsets using sequences of dense open cones, we demonstrate that the product space satisfies the definition of a weak Asplund space.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Difference Equation and Affine Laumon Space III: Generalization to $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$
papers.authors: Hidetoshi Awata, Koji Hasegawa, Hiroaki Kanno, Ryo Ohkawa, Shamil Shakirov, Jun'ichi Shiraishi, Yasuhiko Yamada
papers.abstract: In a series of papers, we have considered a non-stationary difference equation which was originally discovered for the deformed Virasoro conformal block. The equation involves mass parameters and, when they are tuned appropriately, the equation is regarded as a quantum KZ equation for $U_q\bigl(A_{1}^{(1)}\bigr)$. We introduce a $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ generalization of the non-stationary difference equation. The Hamiltonian is expressed in terms of $q$-commuting variables and allows both factorized forms and a normal ordered form. By specializing the mass parameters appropriately, the Hamiltonian can be identified with the $R$-matrix of the symmetric tensor representation of $U_q\bigl(A_{N-1}^{(1)}\bigr)$, which in turn comes from the 3D (tetrahedron) $R$-matrix. We conjecture that the affine Laumon partition function of type $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ gives a solution to our $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary difference equation. As a check of our conjecture, we work out the four-dimensional limit and find that the non-stationary difference equation reduces to the Fuji-Suzuki-Tsuda system.

papers.title: A new proof of the Murnaghan--Nakayama-type rule for stable Grothendieck polynomials of Grassmannian type
papers.abstract: In this article, we present a new proof the Murnaghan--Nakayama-type rule for the stable Grothendieck polynomials of Grassmannian type, which was originally established by Nguyen--Hiep--Son--Thuy.

papers.title: Dirac - von Neumann axioms in the setting of Continuous Model Theory
papers.abstract: We recast the well-known axiom system of quantum mechanics used by physicists (the Dirac calculus) in the language of Continuous Logic. For the basic version of the axiomatic system we prove that along with the canonical continuous model the axioms have approximate finite models of large sizes, in fact the continuous model is isomorphic to an ultraproduct of finite models. We analyse the continuous logic quantifier corresponding to Dirac integration and show that in finite context it has two versions, local and global, which coincide on Gaussian wave-functions.

papers.title: Revisiting the $\beta_1$-action on the 3-primary stable homotopy groups of spheres
papers.abstract: Let $\beta_1$ be the first 3-torsion class in the stable homotopy groups of spheres in even degree. Toda showed that $\beta_1^5 \neq 0$, whilst $\beta_1^6 = 0$. Shimomura generalised this to the 144-periodic family generated by $\beta_1$, written as $\{\beta_{1+9s}\}_{s\geq 0}$, and showed that any $5$-fold product $\prod_5 \beta_{1+9s} \neq 0$, whilst all 6-fold products $\prod_6 \beta_{1+9s} = 0$. In this article, we give a simple proof of these results as well as some generalisations to other 144-periodic families. Along the way, we also refine known detection results for these families. Our tools include BP-synthetic spectra, and the well-known Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for the spectrum of topological modular forms at the prime $3$ as well as its Adams operations.

papers.title: Rate-Optimal Streaming Codes Under an Extended Delay Profile for Three-Node Relay Networks With Burst Erasures
papers.abstract: This paper investigates streaming codes for three-node relay networks under burst packet erasures with a delay constraint $T$. In any sliding window of $T+1$ consecutive packets, the source-to-relay and relay-to-destination channels may introduce burst erasures of lengths at most $b_1$ and $b_2$, respectively. Let $u = \max\{b_1, b_2\}$ and $v = \min\{b_1, b_2\}$. Singhvi et al. proposed a construction achieving the optimal rate when $u\mid (T-u-v)$. In this paper, we present an extended delay profile method that attains the optimal rate under a relaxed constraint $\frac{T - u - v}{2u - v} \leq \left\lfloor \frac{T - u - v}{u} \right\rfloor$ and it strictly cover restriction $u\mid (T-u-v)$. %Furthermore, we demonstrate that the optimal rate for streaming codes is not achievable when $0< T-u-v<v$ under the convolutional code framework.

papers.title: A General Theorem for Non-Simultaneous Hat Guessing Puzzles
papers.abstract: The prisoners and hats puzzle, or simply the hat puzzle, is a family of games in which a group of prisoners are each assigned a colored hat and are asked to guess the color of their own hat. Various versions of the puzzle arise depending on the number of prisoners, the number of possible hat colors, and the information available to them before and after the game begins. These puzzles are broadly classified according to whether the prisoners' declarations are made simultaneously or non-simultaneously. In this paper we present a general theorem concerning the existence of a winning strategy when the declarations are non-simultaneous. We also discuss the relationship between the construction of such strategies and the Axiom of Choice, as well as their connection to the simultaneous-declaration case.

papers.title: Automorphisms of the Worm Domain
papers.abstract: The Diederich--Forn\ae ss worm domain, an important example of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain without a Stein neighborhood basis, provides key counterexamples in the theory of several complex variables. In this paper, we examine its automorphism group and observe that its boundary is locally spherical everywhere except at the exceptional locus and the closure of the caps.

papers.title: Log-Averaged Mirror Prox for Fast, Large-Scale Optimal Transport in Linear Space
papers.abstract: We propose Log-Averaged Mirror Prox (LAMP), a linear-space primal-dual method for large-scale optimal transport. LAMP implements primal mirror prox updates by tracking an averaged dual sequence, reducing storage complexity from $\mathcal{O}(nm)$ to $\mathcal{O}(n+m)$ while preserving dense, GPU-friendly reductions. Consequently, LAMP preserves the last-iterate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\|C\|_\infty nm\varepsilon^{-1})$ arithmetic complexity of conservatively parameterized primal-dual mirror prox. We further analyze LAMP as a direct optimal transport solver in a more performant parameter regime, providing a last-iterate sub-optimality certificate dependent on infeasibility and an explicit $\mathcal O(\|C\|_\infty\log (m)/t)$ term. Moreover, we give a computable sufficient condition for ergodic convergence. Numerical experiments with an optimized CUDA implementation show that LAMP outperforms first-order baselines in several high-accuracy (entropic) optimal transport problems. LAMP is further shown to scale up to problems with $n=m=2^{18}$ marginal supports, which were previously beyond the reach of primal-dual first-order methods.

papers.title: Dynamics of Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group
papers.abstract: We study Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group through the doubled handlebody, a connected sum of copies of the product of a circle and a two-sphere, in which the Dehn twist along a primitive torus is induced by twisting a regular neighborhood of the torus. Our main result states that sufficiently large powers of the Dehn twists along a compatible collection of primitive tori generate a right-angled Artin group. The proof is a ping-pong argument in the universal cover, the complement of a Cantor set in the three-sphere, where intersection numbers become counts of orbits of lifts. Along the way we show that commuting Dehn twists along primitive tori have tori whose lifts never cross, and that a Dehn twist determines the oriented cyclic splitting dual to its torus. Finally, we construct a compact space of primitive curves on which multitwists act parabolically and fully irreducible outer automorphisms act with north--south dynamics.

papers.title: Almost-simple algebraic supergroups
papers.abstract: We investigate certain almost-simple algebraic supergroups over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or odd characteristic. Beyond those whose Lie superalgebras are simple and appear in Kac's classification, we construct new families of almost-simple supergroups whose Lie superalgebras are either non-simple or simple but fall outside Kac's classification.

papers.title: A convex approach for Markov chain estimation from aggregate data via inverse optimal transport
papers.authors: Michele Mascherpa, Axel Ringh, Amirhossein Taghvaei, Johan Karlsson
papers.abstract: We address the problem of identifying the dynamical law governing the evolution of a population of indistinguishable particles, when only aggregate distributions at successive times are observed. Assuming a Markovian evolution on a discrete state space, the task reduces to estimating the underlying transition probability matrix from distributional data. We formulate this inverse problem within the framework of entropic optimal transport, as a joint optimization over the transition matrix and the transport plans connecting successive distributions. This formulation results in a convex optimization problem, and we propose an efficient iterative algorithm based on the entropic proximal method. We illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the method in two numerical setups, considering estimation from independent snapshots and estimation from a time series of aggregate observations, respectively.

papers.title: Quadratic Mean-Field BSDEs and Exponential Utility Maximization
papers.authors: Yining Ding, Kihun Nam, Jiaqiang Wen
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of real-valued mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with generators of quadratic growth in the control variable and the mean-field term. For bounded terminal conditions satisfying suitable structural regularity, we establish existence and uniqueness under two complementary quadratic regimes; the uniformly continuous path-dependent case additionally requires a uniform quadratic bound on the normalized generator. Our approach for these results combines Malliavin calculus with refined BMO and stability estimates, and bridges the gap between the quadratic BSDE results of [Ann. Probab. 45 (2017), pp. 3795--3828] and [Ann. Appl. Probab. 35 (2025), pp. 2128--2174]. Motivated by a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, we further extend our framework to terminal conditions without imposing continuity or Markovian structure on the terminal condition. Under a suitable smallness condition on the oscillation of the terminal value around its mean, the associated quadratic BSDE admits a unique solution in a suitable small solution class. We then apply the extended theory to solve a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, thereby extending the constrained exponential utility framework of Hu et al. [Ann. Appl. Probab. 15 (2005), pp. 1691--1712] to a mean-field setting.

papers.title: On the Iterates of Endomorphisms of Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of certain notions related to the algebraic dynamics of endomorphisms of projective varieties. Our main results include: (i) a characterization of projective varieties that occur as iterated images of endomorphisms of normal projective varieties; (ii) exploring stability behavior in the Stein factorizations of the iterates; and (iii) a structure result concerning endomorphisms whose iterates lie in a finite union of connected components of the endomorphism scheme, thereby completing a result of Brion.

papers.title: Mutual arc presentations and braided open books
papers.abstract: We show that every canonically fibered link in $S^3$ is the binding of a braided open book in $S^3$, addressing a question of Montesinos and Morton. We introduce mutual arc presentations as our main technical tool, which we consider to be of independent interest. We prove that any fibered link admitting such a presentation is the binding of a braided open book.

papers.title: Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
papers.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

papers.title: On the future cover of a sofic shift
papers.abstract: The paper contains a new proof of the theorem by Krieger which establishes the canonicity of the future cover of a sofic shift. In addition the paper describes a method to produce new canonical covers from a given one, resulting in canonical covers related to, but generally different from the future cover.

papers.title: On the Green's functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a discontinuous layered medium
papers.authors: Sandro Franceschi, Irina Kourkova, Maxence Petit
papers.abstract:
We consider a two-dimensional diffusion process in a two-layered plane, governed by distinct covariance matrices in the upper and lower half-planes and by two drift vectors pointed away from the $x$-axis. We first analyze the case where the generator of the process is in divergence form, that is, when the flux is continuous across the interface. Then we extend the study to a broader class of processes whose behavior at the interface forms an oblique two-dimensional analogue of the skew Brownian motion.
  We provide a detailed theoretical analysis of this transient process. Our main results are as follows: (i) we derive explicit Laplace transforms of the Green's functions; (ii) we compute exact asymptotics of the Green's functions along all possible trajectories in the plane; (iii) We determine all positive harmonic functions, identifying the full and minimal Martin boundaries, which turn out to be distinct. The nonminimality of the Martin boundary is a noteworthy phenomenon for diffusions with regular coefficients.
  To obtain an analytical description of the process, we fully develop a three-variable version of the so-called kernel method by deriving and exploiting a functional equation involving unknown Laplace transforms of Green's functions and two known kernels $\gamma_+(x,y)$ and $\gamma_{-}(x,z)$. The introduction of independent auxiliary variables $y$ and $z$, associated with each half-plane, is a key idea.

papers.title: An unfitted divergence-free higher order finite element method for the Stokes problem
papers.authors: Michael Neilan, Maxim Olshanskii, Henry von Wahl
papers.abstract: The paper develops and analyzes a higher-order unfitted finite element method for the incompressible Stokes equations, which yields a strongly divergence-free velocity field up to the physical boundary. The method combines an isoparametric Scott-Vogelius velocity-pressure pair on a cut background mesh with a stabilized Nitsche/Lagrange multiplier formulation for imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions. We construct finite element spaces that admit robust numerical implementation using standard elementwise polynomial mappings and produce exactly divergence-free discrete velocities. The key components of the analysis are a new inf-sup stability result for the isoparametric Scott-Vogelius pair on unfitted meshes and a combined inf-sup stability result for the bilinear forms associated with the pressure and the Lagrange multiplier. The finite element formulation employs a higher-order Lagrange multiplier space, which ensures stability and mitigates the loss of pressure robustness typically associated with the weak enforcement of boundary conditions for the normal velocity component. The paper provides a complete stability and convergence theory in two dimensions, accounting for the geometric errors introduced by the isoparametric approximation. The analysis shows optimal-order velocity convergence in both the $H^1$ and $L^2$ norms and establishes optimal $H^1$-convergence and nearly optimal $L^2$-convergence of a post-processed pressure. Numerical experiments illustrate and confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Duality Relations of Graph Polynomials
papers.abstract: The duality theorem of Lass relates the matching polynomials of a simple graph $G$ with the matching polynomials of its complement $\bar G$. In particular, this relation gives rise to Godsil's result, which offers a nice interpretation of the Lebesgue integral associated with the Hermite orthogonality measure. In this work, we show that similar to matching polynomials, the path-cover polynomials also satisfy duality relations and give combinatorial interpretations of the Lebesgue integral and the inner product in the space of associated Laguerre polynomials. Similar duality relations hold for clique-cover polynomials and chromatic polynomials. As applications, we find an efficient algorithm that computes these graph polynomials for cographs. We also give explicit formulas to compute the number of Hamiltonian paths and cycles in complete multipartite graphs.

papers.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

papers.title: Fiberwise criteria for Fourier--Mukai equivalences
papers.authors: El\'ias Guisado Villalgordo, Pat Lank, Kabeer Manali Rahul, Nebojsa Pavic
papers.abstract: We prove fiberwise criteria for full faithfulness and equivalences of integral transforms between proper flat families of schemes over a separated Noetherian base. The kernels are bounded pseudocoherent complexes which are relatively perfect over each factor, and need not be perfect. A key ingredient is the calculus of mates, which controls the units and counits of adjoint integral transforms under base change. In particular, we give a complete argument for a fiberwise criterion of Hern\'{a}ndez Ruip\'{e}rez--L\'{o}pez Mart\'{i}n--Sancho de Salas, and extend it to arbitrary separated Noetherian bases. As applications, we extend a result of Orlov on field extensions to singular varieties, and show that over a Noetherian local ring these properties can be detected on the special fiber.

papers.title: The Narrow Corridor of Stable Solutions in an Extended Osipov--Lanchester Model with Constant Total Population
papers.abstract: This paper studies a modification of the classical Osipov-Lanchester model in which the total population of the two sides, $N=R+B$, stays constant. In this model the ratio $y=R/B$ obeys the Riccati equation $\dot y=\alpha y^2-\beta$, which is solvable in elementary functions for all values of the parameters. The main result is a complete classification of the stable regimes. An asymptotically stable invariant set in the quadrant $R,B\ge 0$ exists only in three cases: $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ gives a stable interior equilibrium; $\alpha=0,\ \beta<0$ makes the boundary $B=0$ stable; $\alpha<0,\ \beta=0$ makes the boundary $R=0$ stable. If $\alpha>0$ or $\beta>0$, every solution except one unstable equilibrium reaches a boundary of the quadrant in finite time, where the model stops being applicable. If the parameters vary in time, a fixed distance from the boundaries is kept when $\alpha(t)$ and $\beta(t)$ obey buffer dynamics that push them away from zero. Finally, in the case $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ the original system grows exponentially, while in the two degenerate cases it grows at most linearly. Growth demanded of a given cost, the sum of the two channels, bounds their imbalance and, with the perturbation bound, confines the parameters to an explicit wedge about $|\alpha|=|\beta|$ truncated near the origin: the narrow corridor of the model.

papers.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
papers.abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.

papers.title: Differential calculus on bigraded spaces and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: Koszul duality for superalgebras involves both the intrinsic super parity and the degree shift introduced by suspension. We study this duality while keeping the two gradings separate, using a $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z$-graded refinement of the commutativity convention of Deligne and Morgan. In this setting, the Koszul suspension preserves the parity degree and raises the independent weight by one. We realize the polynomial superalgebr $\mathcal O(k^{m|n})$ and its Koszul dual as function algebras on bigraded spaces and construct an isomorphism between their differential calculi of polyvector fields and mixed differential forms. For admissible quadratic Poisson structures, whose bivectors have bidegree $(0,2)$, this isomorphism descends to the differential calculi on Poisson cohomology and mixed Poisson homology. With respect to the corresponding mixed volume forms, Koszul duality preserves unimodularity and, in the unimodular case, identifies the induced Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structures on Poisson cohomology.

papers.title: On Oscillatory Integral Operators Satisfying the cinematic curvature condition
papers.abstract: We establish improved $L^r\mapsto L^p$ estimates for oscillatory integral operators satisfying the positive cinematic curvature condition. In ambient dimension $n\geq4$, the output range is $p>2+8/(3n-4)$, with the full Knapp-admissible input range $r'\leq (n-2)p/n$. The proof combines a transverse covering $L^2$ estimate, Wolff's two-ends reduction, and refined decoupling. In dimension $n=3$ we retain the range $p>4$.

papers.title: On construction of differential $\mathbb Z$-graded varieties
papers.abstract:
Given a commutative unital algebra $\mathcal O$, a proper ideal $\mathcal I$ in $\mathcal O$, and a positively graded differential variety over $\mathcal O/\mathcal I$, we provide a $\mathbb Z$-graded extension, whose negative part is an arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution of $\mathcal O/ \mathcal I$. This extension is obtained through an algorithm exploiting the explicit homotopy retract data of the arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution, so that the number of homological computations in the construction is significantly reduced. For a positively graded differential variety over $\mathcal O$ that preserves the ideal $\mathcal I$, the extension admits a manifest description in terms of decorated trees and computed data.
  As a by-product, to every Lie-Rinehart algebra over the coordinate ring of an affine variety $ W \subseteq M = \mathbb{C}^d$, one associates an explicit differential $\mathbb{Z}$-graded variety over $M$ whose negative component is the arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution of the coordinate ring $\mathbb C[x_1, \ldots, x_d]/\mathcal I_W$ of $W$, and whose positive component is the universal dg-variety of the given Lie-Rinehart algebra. Concrete examples are given.

papers.title: Approximate Computation via Le Cam Simulability
papers.abstract:
We propose a decision-theoretic framework for computational complexity, complementary to classical theory: moving from syntactic exactness (Turing / Shannon) to semantic simulability (Le Cam). While classical theory classifies problems by the cost of exact solution, modern computation often seeks only decision-valid approximations. We introduce a framework where "computation" is viewed as the efficient simulation of a target statistical experiment within a bounded risk distortion (Le Cam deficiency).
  We formally define computational deficiency ($\delta_{\text{poly}}$) and use it to construct the complexity class LeCam-P (Decision-Robust Polynomial Time), characterizing problems that may be syntactically hard but semantically easy to approximate. We show that classical Karp reductions can be viewed as zero-deficiency simulations, and that approximate reductions correspond to bounded deficiency. Furthermore, we establish the No-Free-Transfer Inequality, showing that strictly invariant representations inevitably destroy decision-relevant information. This framework offers a statistical perspective on approximation theory, bridging the gap between algorithmic complexity and decision theory.

papers.title: Completeness of closed Kleinian flat Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds of Signature (2,2)
papers.authors: Farid Diaf, Blandine Galiay, Malek Hanounah
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ denote the model space of flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds of signature $(2,2)$. We prove that the only domain divisible by a discrete subgroup of the isometry group of $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ is $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ itself. In the Kleinian setting, this provides the first completeness theorem of closed flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds beyond the Euclidean and Lorentzian cases.
  Along the proof, we show as a result of independent interest concerning the existence of syndetic hulls in semidirect products $R \ltimes G$, where $G$ is a homothety Lie group. This construction generalizes earlier constructions in affine geometry due to Carri\`ere and Dal'bo.

papers.title: Importance sampling of unbounded random stopping times: computing committor functions and exit rates without reweighting
papers.authors: Carsten Hartmann, Annika J\"oster, Christof Sch\"utte, Alexander Sikorski, Marcus Weber
papers.abstract:
Rare events in molecular dynamics are often related to noise-induced transitions between different macroscopic states (e.g., in protein folding). A common feature of these rare transitions is that they happen on timescales that are on average exponentially long compared to the characteristic timescale of the system, with waiting time distributions that have (sub)exponential tails and infinite support. As a result, sampling such rare events can lead to trajectories that can be become arbitrarily long, with not too low probability, which makes the reweighting of such trajectories a real challenge.
  Here, we discuss rare event simulation by importance sampling from a variational perspective, with a focus on {the computation of committor functions and mean first exit times that both play a prominent role in molecular dynamics}. The idea is to design importance sampling schemes that (a) reduce the variance of a rare event estimator while controlling the average length of the trajectories and (b) that do not require the reweighting of possibly very long trajectories. In doing so, we study different stochastic control formulations for committor and mean first exit times, which we compare both from a theoretical and a computational point of view, including numerical studies of some benchmark examples.

papers.title: Topological classification of certain nonorientable 4-manifolds with cyclic fundamental group of order 2 mod 4
papers.abstract: The classification up to homeomorphism of closed topological nonorientable 4-manifolds with fundamental group of order 2 due to Hambleton-Kreck-Teichner can be used to classify a large set of 4-manifolds with $\pi_1 = \Z/2p$ for odd $p > 1$. It is plausible that this set comprises all homeomorphism classes of such 4-manifolds. This is done through a cut-and-paste construction, which is then used to calculate an extension of the Hausmann-Weinberger invariant for every cyclic group of even order and to produce 4-manifolds that are not homotopy equivalent to a connected sum and which need not be smoothable.

papers.title: Orthogonal Vector-Valued Rational Functions with Applications in Rational Approximation
papers.abstract: We present two algorithms for constructing orthonormal bases of vector-valued rational functions with respect to a discrete inner product. \rev{Every pole is prescribed together with a tangential direction, which fixes the direction of the residue at that pole.} Building on the pencil formulation of the inverse eigenvalue problem for scalar rational functions by Van Buggenhout, Van Barel and Vandebril (2022), we show that, for functions with $k$ components, the recurrence relations are represented by a pencil of $k$-Hessenberg matrices, i.e., matrices with at most $k$ nonzero subdiagonals, \rev{and that the poles are the ratios of the entries on the $k$th subdiagonal. This extends the banded Hessenberg structure of orthogonal vector-valued polynomials to rational functions, and it replaces the semiseparable-plus-diagonal representation of Delvaux and Van Barel (2005), in which every pole belongs to a single component, by a pencil.} We derive an updating algorithm based on rotations and a Krylov-type algorithm \rev{that orthogonalizes a tangential rational Krylov subspace, and we compare their accuracy. Finally, we show that the lightning method and the AAA algorithm fit in our framework; for AAA, the barycentric weights follow from a singular value decomposition of a small block of the pencil.} The approximation of $\sqrt{z}$ on $[0,1]$ with exponentially clustered poles and sample points serves as a stress test for our methods.

papers.title: Domino tilings of black-and-white Temperleyan cylinders
papers.abstract: We consider the dimer model in cylindrical domains $\Omega_\delta$ on square grids of mesh size $\delta$ with two Temperleyan boundary components of different colors. Assuming that the $\Omega_\delta$ approximate a cylindrical domain $\Omega$ as $\delta\to 0$, we prove the convergence of height fluctuations to the Gaussian Free Field in $\Omega$ plus an independent discrete Gaussian multiple of the harmonic measure of one of the boundary components. The limit of the dimer coupling functions on $\Omega_\delta$ is holomorphic in $\Omega$ but not conformally covariant. Given this, we determine the limiting structure of height fluctuations from general principles rather than from explicit computations. In particular, our analysis justifies the inevitable appearance of the discrete Gaussian distribution in the doubly connected setup.

papers.title: A geometric approach to the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points
papers.authors: Zhuchao Ji, Jiarui Song, Junyi Xie
papers.abstract:
We prove that for a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth curve, the genus of a generic sequence of multi-sections with small heights tends to infinity.
  As an application, we give a new proof of the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points on fibers of an abelian scheme over a smooth curve, a result originally proved by Cadoret and Tamagawa. Furthermore, our approach allows us to reprove a conjecture of Cadoret and Tamagawa without additional assumptions.
  Our approach is based on the theory of Betti foliations and the arithmetic equidistribution theorem.

papers.title: Length Spectrum Rigidity and Flexibility of Spheres of Revolution with One Equator
papers.abstract: We define a notion of marked length spectrum for $S^1$-symmetric Riemannian metrics on the two-sphere having only one equator. We prove that isospectral metrics in this class have conjugate geodesic flows. Under a further ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetry assumption, we show that the marked length spectrum determines the metric. Finally, we show that every isospectral class of metrics contains a unique ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetric metric and give an explicit description of this isospectral class as an infinite-dimensional convex set, generalizing the known description of $S^1$-symmetric Zoll metrics. This paper contains also two appendices, in which we provide an elementary proof of the fact that a $C^2$ real-valued function on an interval is determined by the set of tangent lines to its graph, and we classify a class of $S^1$-invariant contact forms on three-manifolds.

papers.title: Mutually c-Conjugate Potentials in Multimarginal Optimal Transport: Dual Representation and Stability
papers.authors: Yehya Cheryala, Mokhtar Z. Alaya, Salim Bouzebda
papers.abstract: We establish dual representation and stability results for multimarginal optimal transport (MOT) with bounded continuous costs. Our approach uses mutually $c$-conjugate potentials: each component is the largest function compatible with the dual constraint when the others are fixed. A single sweep of successive component updates produces such a family from any real-valued feasible family while preserving contact points. The resulting potentials are bounded and upper semicontinuous. On fixed compact metric spaces, normalization at fixed reference points yields a compact class of continuous potentials in the product uniform norm. This class is independent of the marginals and contains a dual maximizer for every marginal tuple. We prove its Lipschitz dependence on the cost in Hausdorff distance. Under uniform cost convergence and weak marginal convergence, transport values converge. The corresponding normalized optimizer sets are upper stable in the product uniform norm, without uniqueness assumptions. We also obtain value bounds in total variation and, for coordinatewise Lipschitz costs, Wasserstein distance. For coordinatewise Lipschitz reference costs, a power-growth condition on the dual objective gives one-sided H\"older estimates for optimizer sets under joint perturbations. On finite spaces, polyhedral structure yields linear growth and one-sided Lipschitz estimates with reference-dependent constants. On Polish spaces, total boundedness of the coordinate cost profiles in the uniform norm yields a compact normalized representation. For a fixed cost satisfying this condition, value continuity and upper stability of normalized conjugate optimizer sets hold under weak marginal convergence.

papers.title: A Local Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Dirichlet Boundary Control Problems
papers.authors: Peter Benner, Michael Hinze, Hamdullah Y\"ucel
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider control constrained $L^2-$Dirichlet boundary control of a convection-diffusion equation on a two dimensional convex polygonal domain. We discretize the control problem based on the local discontinuous Galerkin method with piecewise linear ansatz functions for the flux and potential. We derive a priori error estimates for the full as well as for the variational discrete control approximation. We present a selection of numerical results to demonstrate the performance of our approach and to underpin the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Log canonical thresholds at infinity
papers.abstract: The paper considers a global version of the notion of log canonical threshold for plurisubharmonic functions $u$ of logarithmic growth in $\mathbb{C}^n$, aiming at description of the range of all $p>0$ such that $e^{-u}\in L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$. Explicit formulas are obtained in the toric case. By considering Bergman functions of corresponding weighted Hilbert spaces, a new polynomial approximation of plurisubharmonic functions of logarithmic growth with control over its singularities and behavior at infinity (a global version of Demailly's approximation theorem) is established. Some application to tame polynomial maps are given.

papers.title: Function-on-function nonlinear autoregressive model (F2NARX) for probabilistic surrogate modeling of stochastic dynamical systems
papers.authors: Zhouzhou Song, Marcos A. Valdebenito, Styfen Sch\"ar, Stefano Marelli, Bruno Sudret, Matthias G. R. Faes
papers.abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally efficient surrogate models for predicting dynamical system responses is critical in many engineering domains, yet remains challenging due to the strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional mapping from external excitations and system parameters to system responses. This work introduces a novel Function-on-Function Nonlinear AutoRegressive model with eXogenous inputs (F2NARX), which reformulates the recently proposed $\mathcal{F}$-NARX method from a function-on-function regression perspective. The proposed framework substantially improves predictive efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. By combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression, F2NARX further enables probabilistic predictions of dynamical responses via the unscented transform in an autoregressive manner. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through case studies of varying complexity. Results show that F2NARX outperforms state-of-the-art NARX model by orders of magnitude in efficiency while achieving higher accuracy in general. The probabilistic prediction capability of F2NARX is further demonstrated by combining it with active learning for first-passage probability estimation, showing its potential for reliability-oriented applications.

papers.title: On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in K\"ahler Families with Projective Central Fiber
papers.authors: Christopher D. Hacon, Yi Li, Sheng Rao
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in K\"ahler families. Based on recent developments in the K\"ahler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for K\"ahler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth K\"ahler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for K\"ahler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth K\"ahler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

papers.title: On Busemann subgradient methods for stochastic minimization in Hadamard spaces
papers.abstract: We study the recently introduced Busemann subgradient method due to Goodwin, Lewis, L\'opez-Acedo and Nicolae, extending it to minimize the mean of a stochastic function over general Hadamard spaces. We prove a strong convergence theorem under a local compactness assumption and further prove weak convergence of the method over separable Hadamard spaces. The proof is based on a general (weak) convergence theorem for stochastic processes in Hadamard spaces which confine to a stochastic variant of quasi-Fej\'er monotonicity, together with a nonlinear variant of Pettis' theorem, which are of independent interest. Lastly, we provide best function value estimates as well as a strong convergence result under a strong convexity assumption, and in that latter case in particular derive explicit rates of convergence. We illustrate the practical use of the general mean minimization problem and the associated Busemann subgradient method through statistical models for phylogenetic inference via the Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann tree space.

papers.title: Equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials of Thagomizer Matroids with a Hyperoctahedral Group Action
papers.authors: Matthew H. Y. Xie, Philip B. Zhang, Michael X. X. Zhong
papers.abstract: We compute the equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig and inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of the thagomizer matroid $T_n=M(K_{1,1,n})$ under the action of the hyperoctahedral group $\Bn$. For $n\ge2$, this action identifies $\Bn$ with the full automorphism group of $T_n$. For every $n\ge0$, we give multiplicity-free decompositions of all coefficients of both polynomials into irreducible representations and prove that both coefficient sequences are strongly induced log-concave with respect to induction from $\Bn\times\Bn$ to $\B{2n}$. The formulas for Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials follow from the palindromicity of the equivariant $Z$-polynomial and the known equivariant formulas for the graphic matroids of cycle graphs under the action of $\Sn$. The inverse formula follows from Proudfoot's equivariant inversion identity. For $n\ge2$, we also obtain explicit formulas for both polynomials of $M(K_{2,n})$ under the inherited action of $\Bn$, again with multiplicity-free coefficients.

papers.title: Deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields \`a la Fedosov. We provide an explicit construction to quantize each symplectic vector field as a derivation of the deformed star algebra. This recovers a result of M\"uller-Bahns and Neumaier with an explicit formula of higher total degree terms. Moreover, we show that this quantization yields a non-abelian $2$-cocycle on the Lie algebra of symplectic vector fields with values in the deformed star algebra. For a Fedosov deformation quantization with vanishing first characteristic class, this non-abelian $2$-cocycle can provide a formal deformation of the crossed-product algebra generated by the action of symplectic vector fields. In this sense, we can quantize any Lie algebra action by symplectic vector fields.

papers.title: Real-Time Dynamic N-1 Screening: Identifying High-Risk Lines and Transformers After Common Faults
papers.authors: Ayrton Almada (Misha), Laurent Pagnier (Misha), Igal Goldshtein (Misha), Saif R. Kazi (Misha),  Michael (Misha),  Chertkov
papers.abstract: Power system operators routinely perform N-1 contingency analysis, yet conventional tools provide limited guidance on which lines or transformers deserve heightened attention during fast post-fault transients. In particular, static screening does not reveal whether (1) the same faulted line repeatedly triggers severe downstream overloads, or (2) a specific transformer emerges as vulnerable across many distinct fault scenarios. This paper introduces a real-time dynamic N-1 screening framework that addresses this gap by estimating, for each counterfactual single-phase transmission fault, the probability of transient overcurrent on critical grid elements. The output is an operator-facing dashboard that ranks (a) faulted lines whose outages most frequently lead to dangerous transformer overloads, and (b) transformers that consistently overload across top-risk scenarios, both of which are actionable indicators for real-time situational awareness. The approach models post-fault electromechanical dynamics using a linear stochastic formulation of the swing equations with short-lived, fault-localized uncertainty, and combines analytic transient evaluation with cross-entropy based importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare but high-impact events. All N-1 contingencies are evaluated in parallel with linear computational complexity. The framework is demonstrated on the IEEE 118-bus system, where it reveals latent high-risk lines and transformers that remain invisible under deterministic dynamic or static N-1 analysis. Results show orders-of-magnitude computational speedup relative to brute-force Monte Carlo, enabling practical deployment within real-time operational cycles.

papers.title: On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
papers.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed K\"ahler class $[\omega]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal K\"ahler metric in $[\omega]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $\Delta$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $\Delta$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $\Delta$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[\omega]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

papers.title: Max-Min Bilinear Completely Positive Programs: A Semidefinite Relaxation with Tightness Guarantees
papers.authors: Sarah Yini Gao, Xindong Tang, Yancheng Yuan
papers.abstract: We study max-min bilinear completely positive (CP) programs and their associated min-max programs. We establish reformulations of these problems as linear optimization over the product of the CP cone and the copositive (COP) cone, namely, the COP-CP programs. A hierarchy of coupled Moment-SOS type semidefinite relaxations is proposed to solve these COP-CP programs. We show that this approach has asymptotic convergence under mild assumptions. Moreover, we use the coupled flat truncation conditions (FTCs) to certify tightness of semidefinite relaxations, and we give sufficient conditions for finite convergence of the hierarchy, under which the FTCs hold at every optimal solution of all sufficiently high-order relaxations. Numerical experiments are presented to show the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title: A Fully Discrete Nonnegativity-Preserving FEM for a Stochastic Heat Equation
papers.authors: Owen Hearder (Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Claude Le Bris (\'Ecole des Ponts, INRIA), Ana Djurdjevac (Freie Universit\"at Berlin, University of Oxford)
papers.abstract: We consider a stochastic heat equation with nonlinear finite-rank space-coloured multiplicative noise that admits a unique nonnegative solution when given nonnegative initial data. Inspired by existing results for fully discrete finite difference schemes and building on the convergence analysis of semi-discrete mass-lumped finite element approximations, a fully discrete numerical method is introduced that combines mass-lumped finite elements with a Lie-Trotter splitting strategy. This discretization preserves nonnegativity at the discrete level and is shown to be convergent under suitable regularity conditions. A rigorous convergence analysis is provided, highlighting the role of mass lumping in ensuring nonnegativity and of operator splitting in decoupling the deterministic and stochastic dynamics. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the convergence rates and the preservation of nonnegativity. In addition, we examine several numerical examples outside the scope of the established theory, aiming to explore the range of applicability and potential limitations of the proposed method.

papers.title: A Super Version of a Theorem of Fricke-Klein
papers.abstract: We start studying the character variety of the algebraic supergroup OSp(1|2) from the algebraic perspective. We do this by first investigating the specific case of the character variety of the free group on two letters and try to describe the ring of invariants with respect to the conjugation action. The explicit description of the corresponding character variety for SL(2) was done by Fricke and Klein, so this can be seen as a variant of this theorem for its supergeometric counterpart OSp(1|2) and briefly touch upon the character stack for OSp(1|2)

papers.title: Functional central limit theorem for superdiffusive SDEs with stable noise
papers.authors: Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Andrey Pilipenko, Isao Sauzedde
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a functional stable central limit theorem for a class of superdiffusive solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by an $\alpha$-stable process.

papers.title: Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
papers.authors: Tijs Buggenhout, Mathias Stout, Lisa Vandebrouck
papers.abstract: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak.
