papers.title: Height functions on the $m \times n$ Miura-ori flip graph: degree sequence and diameter
papers.abstract: Miura-ori is an origami grid of parallelogram faces whose creases carry mountain or valley folds. Its flip graph joins locally flat-foldable assignments differing by a legal face flip. Local flat-foldability does not require the whole sheet to fold flat. Earlier two-row formulas and small-flip counts left a uniform rectangular counting law unresolved, while the known maximum shortest-path distance left its attaining pairs unclassified. Integer face functions with adjacent values differing by one identify legal flips with local extrema and determine shortest-path distances through their differences. For a fixed number $d\ge3$ of legal flips, the assignment count on an $m\times n$ face grid with $m,n\ge2$ is a symmetric polynomial once $m,n\ge d-1$. Its degree is $d-2$ in each variable and in total, with leading part proportional to $m^{d-2}+n^{d-2}$ except at $d=4$. Exact computation identifies formulas through ten flips. For fixed $2\le m\le d-2$ and $n\ge d-1$, a finite construction gives correction polynomials of degree at most $d-3$ in $n$. At $m=d-2$, an exact linear correction involving Baxter permutations proves the threshold sharp for $d\ge4$. Computer assistance enters the four-flip total-degree proof and a cubic correction-degree bound. A sharper uniform correction-degree bound remains open. Interior-face flips first become possible with five legal flips on grids at least $3\times3$. Classifying face-function differences that maximize their minimum total absolute deviation from a constant and reconstructing every realizing assignment pair gives all farthest pairs. Outside $2\times2$, these lie among four minimum-flip assignments with two legal flips each, with four unordered pairs when one dimension is two and the other even, and two otherwise. The counts and pair classification describe available moves and maximal separation without enumerating the full flip graph.

papers.title: Structural functional identifiability and model discovery in differential equation models
papers.authors: Torkel E Loman, Alexander P Browning, Ruth E Baker
papers.abstract: Differential equation models are widely used to describe, interpret, and predict dynamical phenomena across science and engineering. In practice, however, the governing dynamics are rarely fully known and must be inferred from observational data. Traditionally, inverse problems in differential equation modelling have focused on estimating unknown parameter values. In this setting, structural identifiability determines whether parameter values can, in principle, be uniquely recovered from ideal observations and is, therefore, a prerequisite for meaningful inference. More recently, the integration of machine learning with mechanistic modelling has enabled the discovery of unknown equations, functions, and constitutive relationships, substantially expanding the space of admissible models. This raises a fundamental question: under what conditions can unknown functional components be uniquely recovered from data? In this paper, we generalise the classical notion of structural parameter identifiability to functional identifiability. We first identify broad classes of models for which unique functional recovery is impossible. We then show how functional identifiability can be assessed for differential equation models using differential algebra-based techniques which are well-established as a means of assessing structural identifiability for ordinary differential equation models. Our framework reveals new phenomena that arise in the transition from parametric to function inference and have no analogue in the classical setting. Finally, we characterise functional identifiability in several common model classes. Taken together, our results demonstrate that functional identifiability provides a theoretical foundation for modern inverse problems in differential equation modelling, particularly those that use machine learning representations of unknown system components.

papers.title: Axes of null Cartan normal helices with applications to isophotic and silhouette curves in Minkowski space-time
papers.authors: Derya Sa\u{g}lam, Umut Selvi, Sevgi Esen Almal{\i}
papers.abstract:
We study null Cartan curves in Minkowski space-time $\E$ that are normal helices with respect to C-constant normal fields $V=\lambda T+\mu N+
u B_2$, whose components in the Cartan frame are constant. If $\kappa_3$ has no zeros, the constant vectors $W$ for which $\ip{V}{W}$ is constant correspond to common solutions of two linear differential equations, of orders four and at most two. Hence they form a space of dimension at most two, $B_2$ is never an axis field, and the normal helices with any other axis field $V$ and prescribed $\kappa_3$ are obtained by two quadratures, explicitly for $V=\lambda T\pm B_2$. For null Cartan helices, $V$ admits an axis if and only if one of three explicit linear conditions on $(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ holds; then $\ip{V}{W}=0$, and the axes are spanned by the invariant null lines and spacelike plane of the boost--rotation group generating the helix. For fields with $\mu
u
eq0$ we obtain a Riccati criterion and determine all fields moving in a fixed plane; for fields $\lambda T+N$ we find non-helical curves with two linearly independent axes, unlike in dimension three. Finally, we introduce a normalized Darboux frame for null curves on timelike hypersurfaces and characterize the isophotic and silhouette curves with C-constant normal.

papers.title: On perturbations that preserve the connectivity properties in tree percolations
papers.abstract:
We consider a general bond percolation on an infinite locally finite tree, where the edge retention probabilities $p_e$ are replaced by $\min\{1,q_{|e|}p_e\}$, where $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of positive perturbation factors and $|e|$ denotes the distance between the edge $e$ and the root. If the original percolation model admits infinite clusters, it is of interest to investigate under which perturbations $0<q_n\le 1$ this connectivity property is preserved. Conversely, if the original percolation does not admit infinite clusters, we are led to study the stability of such a property under perturbations satisfying $q_n\ge 1$.
  In both cases, under minimal assumptions on the original model, we show that the percolative behaviour is stable against certain quantitative non-trivial perturbations. We also discuss an application of our results to the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture for Cantor sets.

papers.title: Categorical structures of Kuranishi spaces with $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce $L_{\infty}$-Kuranishi spaces by associating, to each chart, $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras defined on open neighborhoods of points in the zero locus of the Kuranishi section. We show that these objects collectively form a category into which the category of smooth manifolds naturally embeds. Some notions in \cite{FOOO1} are modified to achieve the desired categorical structures; for instance, the tangent bundle condition for chart embeddings is replaced by a quasi-isomorphism condition for the $L_{\infty}[1]$-structures.

papers.title: A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes
papers.authors: Anastasios Fragkos, Ben Krause, Nazar Miheisi, Yu-Chen Sun
papers.abstract:
Let $\Lambda$ denote the von Mangoldt function; we prove that for each $r > 2$, there exist constants \[ r' < \mathbf{c}(r) < 2 < \mathbf{C}(r), \qquad \lim_{r \to \infty} \mathbf{c}(r) = 1, \ \lim_{r \to \infty} \mathbf{C}(r) = \infty \] so that the discrete variational Carleson operator along the primes \begin{align} \mathcal{V}^r \Big( \sum_{n \neq 0} f(x-n) \Lambda(|n|) \frac{e^{2\pi i \lambda n}}{n} : \lambda \in \mathbb{T} \Big) \end{align} is bounded on $\ell^p$ for all $\mathbf{c}(r) < p < \mathbf{C}(r)$, while the variation is unbounded when $p \leq r'$. At the non-variational endpoint, the same argument gives the sharp maximal result: the prime Carleson operator \[ \sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb T} \Big|\sum_{n\neq0} f(x-n)\Lambda(|n|)\frac{e^{2\pi i\lambda n}}{n}\Big| \] is bounded on $\ell^p(\mathbb Z)$ for the full expected range $1<p<\infty$.
  The proof gives a new mechanism for treating modulation-invariant singular integrals after arithmetic sparsification. It combines higher-order Fourier uniformity, a variable-coefficient multi-frequency principle in the spirit of Bourgain, and an additive-combinatorial inverse argument. A key step is a reduction to finite periodic models, where the Ramanujan structure of the major arcs is converted into a sharp estimate for structured atoms by elementary number theory.

papers.title: Local linear convergence of the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm for semidefinite programming
papers.abstract: Primal-dual first-order methods are widely used for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP), but their ability to compute highly accurate solutions is not explained by global convergence theory alone. We study the local convergence of the primal--dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method for SDP. We first show that PDHG converges linearly, uniformly for all starting points near a KKT point, if and only if the KKT mapping is metrically subregular at that point. We then show that PDHG eventually converges linearly whenever the limit KKT point is strictly complementary, even with multiple solutions. The asymptotic rate admits a bound computable from the eigenvalues of the linearized PDHG map and matching the observed rates in our experiments. As a byproduct of the analysis, strict complementarity implies metric subregularity. Finally, we prove that PDHG can converge sublinearly even when started arbitrarily close to a solution, which cannot happen for linear programming. Numerical experiments support the theory and exhibit SDP instances on which PDHG struggles to reach high accuracy.

papers.title: Exterior power operations on relative K-theory
papers.abstract: We algebraically construct exterior power operations on higher relative algebraic K-groups and prove their desired properties such as the expected behaviour with respect to (tensor) products and composition. This builds on Grayson's description of relative K-groups in terms of explicit generators and relations and on work by Harris, the first author and Taelman for (absolute) K-groups. Among the new features in our approach is the observation that the product axiom in the classical notion of a lambda-ring is redundant.

papers.title: A Direction Adaptation Evolution Strategy for Noisy Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.abstract: In noisy derivative-free optimization (DFO), methods based on the matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES) often mistakenly identify points with spuriously good function values, undermining selection and leading to unreliable search directions. To address this, we develop a novel direction adaptation evolution strategy (DAES) that targets the algorithmic phases prone to noise propagation, combining selected-population search with complexity analysis. Fixing the transformation matrix to the identity, DAES employs a structured direction-generation mechanism consisting of symmetric sampling, joint sorting--selection of noisy values, partitioning of all sampled directions into three ranked groups, and construction of a heuristic search direction. Along this direction, a noisy derivative-free sufficient descent condition with extrapolation is applied. Using a probabilistic angle condition preserved through our proposed framework, we obtain, to the best of our knowledge, the first high-probability evaluation-complexity bounds for a noisy MAES-type method across nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex objectives, under bounded noise. Finally, experiments on 230 BARON BCP problems across eight noise levels compare DAES with five DFO solvers, notably MADFO, showing greater robustness at intermediate-to-small budgets.

papers.title: A Ramanujan Pell K3 Surface and Cube Representations
papers.abstract: We classify all polynomial representations of $K(u)=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3$ as a sum of two cubes over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without an a priori degree bound. The displayed representation is unique up to interchange and independent multiplication by cube roots of unity. On the elliptic K3 surface $y^2=x^3-432K(u)^2$, the resulting eighteen sections are exactly those of minimum positive Shioda height $4/3$. The proof combines an exact root-pairing calculation with the degree-height relation on the genus-four cover $w^3=K(u)$; it does not require the full Mordell-Weil rank. For the rational representations arising from multiples of the displayed section, we determine the reduced degrees and prove strong divisibility of their common denominators, including an exact formula for each primitive part. We also prove nontorsion at every rational parameter and explain the Pell origin of the sextic. The associated integral lattices and symplectic quotient are treated in appendices. All proofs are in characteristic zero.

papers.title: On Milnor and Tjurina numbers of Pairs of Holomorphic Function Germs
papers.authors: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'ia Barroso, Nancy Saravia-Molina
papers.abstract: Motivated by the bifurcation formula for the Milnor number of pairs of holomorphic function germs, we introduce, via foliation theory, the Tjurina number of such pairs. We define it as the generic value of the Tjurina number of the foliation associated with the pair, with respect to a specified family of balanced divisors of separatrices. We prove that this value is well defined and that it is an analytic invariant, we derive an explicit formula for it, and we establish a bifurcation formula. As an application, we characterize semitame pairs in terms of this invariant. We also prove a version of Teissier's lemma for pairs and an upper bound for the Milnor number of a pair, and we apply these results to generic pencils of algebraic curves.

papers.title: Flexibility of the isometric immersion system in arbitrary dimension and codimension and the energy scaling of prestrained thin films
papers.abstract: We prove that, for a given $C^{r,\beta}$-regular Riemann metric posed on a $d$-dimensional domain, every short immersion into the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{d+k}$, can be uniformly approximated by exact isometric immersions of regularity $C^{1,\alpha}$ for any $\alpha<\alpha_0=\min\{\frac{r+\beta}{2}, \frac{1}{1+d(d+1)/k}\}$. Our theorem recovers several previously known results as special cases. The novelty thereof lies in providing a unified flexibility statement for arbitrary dimensions $d$ and codimensions $k$, while also treating the so far uncharted range $k\in (1, \frac{d(d+1)}{2}-d+1)\setminus \{d\}$, where no corresponding general result was previously available. Our threshold flexibility exponent $\alpha_0$ agrees with that previously obtained for the closely related Monge-Amp\`ere system. As an application, we prove a new estimate in the quantitative immersability of thin prestrained films, setting the scaling exponent of the infimum of non-Euclidean energies in presence of an arbitrary prestrain metric, and in the limit of the film's vanishing thickness, at $\frac{4\alpha_0}{\alpha_0+1}$.

papers.title: Transmit Coefficients and Receive Combining Vector Design for OTA-FL with Imperfect CSI
papers.authors: Xiaoyan Ma, Shahryar Zehtabi, Yinan Zou, Taejoon Kim, Christopher G. Brinton
papers.abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.

papers.title: The Liouville equation on Riemannian surfaces: the role of volume growth in classification and rigidity results
papers.authors: Giulio Ciraolo, Alberto Farina, Michele Gatti
papers.abstract: We study the Liouville equation $-\Delta_g u = e^u$ on a complete, connected, non-compact, boundaryless Riemannian surface $(M, g)$ with non-negative Ricci curvature. Assuming only some asymptotic lower bound on the solution, we establish classification results for both the solutions and the ambient manifold, discussing also their optimality. Our results reveal a close connection between the volume growth of the manifold and the classification of both the solutions and the underlying manifold.

papers.title: An infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs with a bisimplicial vertex
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs $G_t$, each with a bisimplicial vertex $v_t$ of degree four and a cutvertex. Thus the same family disproves Ho\`ang's conjectures excluding bisimplicial vertices and clique cutsets from such graphs. For every integer $t\geq1$, the graph $G_t$ has clique number three and satisfies \[ |V(G_t)|=93+30(t-1),\qquad |E(G_t)|=320+104(t-1). \] Deleting $v_t$ gives a perfectly divisible graph $H_t$ with an edge whose endpoints both lie outside the perfect part of every perfect division. This gives a negative answer to the prescribed-vertex question of Hu, Xu and Zhuang. The same graphs answer their second question affirmatively: each $H_t$ is perfectly divisible but not perfectly weight divisible. The cutvertex and weighted consequences were pointed out by Hu, Xu and Zhuang, who also observed that replacing one endpoint of the edge by two adjacent twins gives a minimally nonperfectly divisible graph with a homogeneous set.

papers.title: Counterexamples, Spectral Obstructions, and Deletion Stability for WOW-284
papers.abstract:
WOW-284 is a Graffiti conjecture asserting that every connected graph of order at least three and girth at least five has minimum dual degree at most $-\lambda_{\min}(D)$, where $D$ is the distance matrix and the dual degree of a vertex is the average degree of its neighbors. We refute it with exact counterexamples on $38$, $39$, $40$, $42$ and $50$ vertices and study the structure of regular counterexamples. For a connected $k$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least five and diameter three, we prove that $\delta^*(G)+\lambda_{\min}(D)=2k-2-\max_\theta(\theta+1)^2$, the maximum being over the nonprincipal adjacency eigenvalues, so strict failure is a spectral window condition. The closed window $|\theta+1|\le\sqrt{2k-2}$ alone, without any diameter assumption, forces $|V(G)|<(k+2)(k^2+3)/6$ when $k\ge4$, and an integral excess matrix derived from the optimal polynomial sharpens this bound for diameter-three counterexamples. Every regular strict counterexample has degree at least six and diameter at most four, and in degree six it has at most $50$ vertices.
  Under vertex deletion, the Hoffman-Singleton graph remains a strict counterexample after the removal of any five vertices, while an explicit six-vertex deletion destroys strictness. A degree-$57$ Moore graph, if one exists, remains a connected strict counterexample after the removal of any $56$ vertices. Every strict counterexample has at least $15$ vertices, and an exhaustive search excludes orders up to $19$. The strict induced subgraphs of the Hoffman-Singleton graph of orders $36$ to $50$ are classified up to automorphism; among them are three further irregular counterexamples of order $40$.

papers.title: Uniform Airy expansions for Ramanujan's function and the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel
papers.abstract: For $q=e^{-\varepsilon}\to1^-$, we obtain an Airy expansion for Ramanujan's entire function $A_q(\sqrt q\,x)$, uniformly for $x$ in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of $1/4$. After an explicit exponential normalization, the expansion has analytic coefficients and a nonlinear Airy argument. We calculate the first corrections and bound the remainder by $\varepsilon^2$ times an Airy envelope. The estimate is valid at Airy zeros and retains exponential decay on the real interval below $1/4$. The proof uses a Gaussian integral representation and an odd analytic change of variable that reduces the phase to cubic form. The compact turning-point expansion follows as a corollary. For each fixed positive zero $\rho_n(q)$, we obtain an expansion of $\log(4\rho_n(q))$ through order $\varepsilon^2$, with remainder $O_n(\varepsilon^{8/3})$. A zero-free interval identifies the zeros by their global indices. We also calculate the $\varepsilon^{2/3}$ correction to the known Airy limit of the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel, with an $O(\varepsilon^{4/3})$ remainder uniformly on compact sets, including the diagonal.

papers.title: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval
papers.authors: Yuchen Chen, Yandi Shen, Xingyu Xu
papers.abstract: Randomly initialized first-order iterative algorithms are simple, widely used, and empirically effective across many high-dimensional inference problems, yet their theoretical behavior remains far less understood than that of algorithms started from more elaborate, problem-specific initializations such as spectral initialization. This paper takes a step toward closing this gap by studying randomly initialized approximate message passing (AMP) for noiseless phase retrieval, a canonical nonconvex inference problem. We give a non-asymptotic, growing-horizon characterization of the AMP trajectory from random initialization, and show that it achieves both the information-theoretic weak recovery threshold $\delta_{\rm weak}=1/2$ and the AMP strong recovery threshold $\delta_{\rm str}\approx1.13$, matching the recovery thresholds established for spectrally initialized AMP. The key technical ingredients are twofold: (i) a non-asymptotic coupling that decomposes the AMP iterates as a signal component, a linear combination of independent Gaussian vectors, and an approximation error, and (ii) a second-order analysis of the Onsager correction error built around a non-asymptotic version of Bolthausen's condition. These allow us to analyze the $O_\delta(\log n)$ steps required for weak recovery, and to faithfully track the asymptotic state evolution up to $n^{1/3}/\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps in the intermediate recovery regime $\delta\in(\delta_{\rm weak},\delta_{\rm str})$, both beyond the $O(1)$-iteration horizon of classical AMP theory. Above the strong recovery threshold, AMP reaches any prescribed fixed recovery accuracy within $O_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\log n)$ iterations. Both the coupling and the error analysis are developed for a broad class of generalized AMP dynamics and may be of independent interest for general single-index models.

papers.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
papers.abstract: We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.

papers.title: Speculative Successive Cancellation Decoding of Polar Codes
papers.authors: Ryan Seah, Marvin R\"ubenacke, Warren J. Gross
papers.abstract: Polar codes achieve channel capacity as block length increases, but this asymptotic advantage comes at the cost of decoding speed: the conventional \ac{SC} algorithm is inherently sequential, which limits its practicality for high-throughput applications. This work addresses that limitation by introducing the \emph{\ac{Spec-SC}} framework, which incorporates speculative execution into the \ac{SC} decoding process. While \ac{sp-node}-based decoders enable partial parallelism for specific, predefined structures, \ac{Spec-SC} extends this capability by permitting parallel execution in general nodes that do not match any \acs{sp-node} pattern. A built-in verification mechanism ensures that this speculation does not compromise decoding correctness. Simulation results show that \ac{Spec-SC} achieves the same \acs{BER} and \acs{FER} performance as conventional \ac{SC} decoding, while reducing the average number of sequentially traversed nodes by up to $69\%$ for a polar code of length $N=4096$. A cycle-level analysis further shows that, for $\Pc(4096,3584)$ at $5\,\mathrm{dB}$, a heterogeneous four-core configuration achieves a $1.57\times$ decoding speedup using a total of $2944$ processing lanes, representing a $43.75\%$ increase over the $N_{\mathrm{lane}}=2048$ one-core \ac{SC} baseline. The speedup increases to $2.5\times$ at $7\,\mathrm{dB}$, demonstrating the increasing effectiveness of speculation at higher $\EbNo$. These results demonstrate that \ac{Spec-SC} enables additional algorithm-level parallelism beyond conventional \ac{sp-node}-based decoding, motivating its further investigation for high-throughput and high-reliability communication systems. achieve, paving the way for speculative hardware decoder implementations.

papers.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum system on the real line obeying a deformed Heisenberg algebra. This deformation was originally proposed by E.P. Wigner in 1950 when establishing the non-uniqueness of the canonical commutation relations implied by the equations of motion. An explicit coordinate representation was subsequently provided by L.M. Yang in 1951 and in essence is identical in form with Dunkl's difference-differential operator introduced in 1989 in connection with root systems of reflection groups when limited to the group $Z_2$ acting on the real line. Under certain conditions such quantum systems exhibit a supersymmetric (SUSY) structure where the reflection operator acts as the grading operator. We present a generalisation of Yang's representation by first considering only one of the two equations of motion in phase space. The corresponding non-interacting system is found to represent Witten's model of SUSY quantum mechanics. Imposing also the second equation of motion the original result of Wigner and Yang is reconsidered by extending their discussion to general symmetric potentials on the real line. As explicit example we discuss the harmonic oscillator and an attractive Coulomb-like potential $V(x) = - \gamma / |x|$. We also establish a Hooke-Newton duality between this Coulomb-like system and the original Wigner-Yang harmonic oscillator system.

papers.title: Time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with a general external force in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.authors: Renjun Duan, Jinkai Ni, Tong Yang
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-
abla_{x}\phi \cdot 
abla_{v}f +  rac{1}{2}v \cdot 
abla_{x}\phi f$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.

papers.title: The universal cover of the second-type locus of a cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the surface of second-type lines on a general cubic fourfold has fundamental group of order two. Its universal cover, constructed by Huybrechts, is obtained by considering the two ramification points of the Gauss map along each second-type line.

papers.title: Quantum Bicycle LDPC Codes with High $kd^2/n$ from Divisor-Driven Search
papers.authors: Liangdong Lu, Guanmin Guo, Yang Liu, Ruipan Yang
papers.abstract: Bicycle (two-block circulant) quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC)codes include some of the best known small quantum codes, yet their design has relied on group-algebra formulations in which the dimension and distance are accessible only through matrix computation. We show that in the cyclic case the construction collapses into the polynomial ring $\F_2[x]/(x^{l}-1)$: self-orthogonality is automatic, the quantum dimension is read off from a polynomial gcd, and the minimum distance is certified exactly through the Calderbank correspondence to additive codes over $\F_4$, turning code search into an algebraically pre-filtered enumeration that reaches parameter regimes poorly covered by existing tables. A computer search based on this framework recovers the short codes $[[42,12,4]]_2$ and $[[62,12,4]]_2$ and produces a family of codes with competitive figure of merit $kd^2/n$, including $[[66,20,7]]_2$ with $kd^2/n=14.85$, above the bivariate bicycle code $[[144,12,12]]_2$ ($kd^2/n=12$) at less than half the block length, together with $[[46,2,8]]_2$, $[[66,2,9]]_2$, $[[66,4,8]]_2$, $[[66,6,8]]_2$ and, at $n=90$, $[[90,16,7]]_2$, $[[90,18,6]]_2$, $[[90,20,6]]_2$. An exhaustive census at $n=48$ delineates the boundary of this picture: we exhibit a $[[48,10,6]]_2$ code from a minimal $48$-element group (the Aydin--Tamo--Barg realization uses $72$ elements), and prove that distance $5$ forces a stabilizer-rank loss, which excludes $[[48,10,5]]_2$ from the weight-$8$ symmetric coset family. The framework thus opens a systematic route to bicycle-type quantum LDPC codes beyond the reach of group-theoretic searches, and identifies exactly where genuinely coset-theoretic phenomena begin.

papers.title: From algebraic orthogonality to RAAG embedding obstructions in hierarchically hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We extend the Kim--Koberda obstruction arguments for embeddings of right-angled Artin groups (RAAGs) to a class of hierarchically hyperbolic groups (HHGs). To this end, we isolate algebraic conditions on HHGs relating domain orthogonality to the decomposition and commutation of group elements. Under these conditions, we obtain a clique-graph obstruction to RAAG embeddings into such HHGs using the \emph{expanded core graph}, which we introduce as a counterpart of both the extension graphs of RAAGs and the disjointness graphs of curves on surfaces. When the HHG structure has rank at most two, the expanded core graph itself gives a complete embedding criterion.

papers.title: On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category
papers.abstract:
We develop an $\infty$-categorical framework for internal homotopy theory (truncations, homotopy groups, and Eilenberg-MacLane objects) of an accessible localization of an $\infty$-topos. For the motivic localization over a perfect field $k$, we show that a motivic space has trivial motivic $n$-truncation iff it has trivial Nisnevich $n$-truncation ($n\geq-2$), identifying internal $n$-Eilenberg-MacLane objects with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of groups when $n=1$ and strictly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of abelian groups when $n\geq2$. We further prove that a generically free Nisnevich group sheaf is strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff it is birational (which for the free group sheaf $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ holds iff $A$ is birational), whereas for an \'etale-weakly unramified sheaf of sets $A$, $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff $A$ is itself $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Non-birational, \'etale-weakly unramified motivic sheaves of sets (such as $\mathbb{G}_m$) thus generate (non-abelian) $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves that are not strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Combining this obstruction with essentially smooth base change, we prove that for a qcqs scheme $S$, $\mathcal{H}^{mot}(S)$ is an $\infty$-topos iff $S=\emptyset$.
  We also study relative truncation and connectivity under a localization. Over a qcqs scheme $S$, this identifies external $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings with internal motivic $n$-coverings via pullback along the localization unit, yielding a motivic $n$-Galois correspondence over $k$. For connective morphisms over $k$, we establish a higher $\mathbb{A}^1$-Van Kampen theorem and a Nisnevich-local-to-global $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-connectivity criterion; in particular, a $k$-scheme is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected iff it admits a Nisnevich cover by $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected schemes whose pairwise fiber products have $k$-points.

papers.title: Spectral and Isoperimetric Bounds on Flat Tori
papers.abstract:
We record several elementary relations between spectral and isoperimetric parameters of a flat torus $\mathbb{T}_\Lambda = \mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$ and the covariance structure of a fundamental domain $K$ for the lattice $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. For every measurable fundamental domain $K$ and nonzero vector $\xi$ in the dual lattice $\Lambda^*$, we observe the sharp directional variance estimate \[ \left\langle \operatorname{Cov}_K \xi,\xi\right\rangle \geq \frac{1}{12}. \] This yields a lower bound on the torus spectral gap $\lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda)$ (equivalently, the length of the shortest nonzero dual vector $\lambda_1(\Lambda^*)$) in terms of the maximal covariance of $K$: \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda) = 4\pi^2 \lambda_1(\Lambda^*)^2 \geq \frac{\pi^2}{3\left\|\operatorname{Cov}_K\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}. \] Analogous sharp results are obtained for the isoperimetric profile and the Cheeger constant $D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda)$ using an old argument of Hadwiger.
  In particular, when the Voronoi cell $K_\Lambda$ of a lattice with $\det \Lambda = 1$ is isotropic, the recent resolution of the Slicing Problem by Klartag and Lehec implies that \[ D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda),\quad \lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda),\quad \lambda_1(\Lambda^*) \geq c > 0, \] where $c > 0$ is a universal constant independent of dimension $n$; this may be thought of as a positive resolution of the Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits conjecture for all flat tori.
  While there are lattices $\Lambda$ and corresponding Voronoi cells $K = K_\Lambda$ for which no dimension-independent converse inequality to the spectral-gap bound above can hold, we show that under a certain sectional tiling hypothesis, this inequality is in fact an equivalence (up to numerical constants).

papers.title: Bogomolny Monopoles on Asymptotically Cylindrical 3-Manifolds
papers.abstract:
We construct irreducible smooth SU(2)-monopoles on asymptotically cylindrical 3-manifolds with vanishing first and second Betti numbers, using a gluing construction. Their Higgs fields grow linearly along the end, and their Yang-Mills-Higgs energy is infinite.
  We also construct singular U(1)-Dirac monopoles on arbitrary asymptotically cylindrical 3-manifolds whenever a topological obstruction determined by the singularities and the charges vanishes; this is automatic if the first or second Betti number vanishes.

papers.title: On biharmonic equations with $p$-Laplacian and indefinite potentials or critical nonlinearity
Structural and Dynamical Properties of Subfactor Commuting Squares
papers.abstract: This paper explores the algebraic invariants and ergodic behavior of the finite-index inclusions forming commuting squares of $\text{II}_1$ factors. We begin by establishing how regularity, intermediate-subfactor lattices, and Weyl groups transfer across the commuting square under relative commutant and irreducibility conditions. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization, via a novel factorization theorem, of the unitary normalizers of the upper inclusion when the lower inclusion is regular. Applying these findings to crossed-product inclusions induced by discrete groups, we introduce a relative eigenbasis property that preserves regular inclusions. Finally, we contrast this by proving that a relative weak mixing condition on the group action forces the crossed-product inclusion to be singular.

papers.title: Locally finite fixed points of branching Brownian motion
papers.authors: Xinxin Chen, Arnab Chowdhury, Atul Shekhar, Shuo Zhu
papers.abstract: We give a full characterization of the fixed points of Branching Brownian motion with critical and supercritical drifts under no additional assumptions besides it being locally finite almost surely. In particular, we do not assume finite intensity (Kabluchko, 2012) or the finite top particle (Chen-Garban-Shekhar, 2023) conditions. We also give a full characterization of the domain of attraction of the fixed points of BBM.

papers.title: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation and Retry Feedback in LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language model providers are compute constrained, and a common response to congestion is to degrade service: route queries to smaller models, cut reasoning budgets, or shorten context windows. A user who receives an unsatisfactory answer either retries, adding load while the system is busy, or abandons, possibly as churn. We model inference serving as a control problem in which service quality is the provider's decision. A two-regime fluid approximation with retries folded into the service rate gives closed-form trajectories and crossing times, so the dynamic program over quality tiers needs no simulation. We characterize a region in which a weaker tier uses less energy per task but more capacity per task, and show that in the fluid model reactive throttling to such a tier can keep the queue from draining. With heterogeneous customers the problem is a transportation problem with retry-inflated capacity coefficients; optimal routing follows a $c\mu$-type index, and the dual of the capacity constraint gives the marginal cost of one more query by class and time. We illustrate the method on five instances calibrated to public benchmark data.

papers.title: Solution to a McKean-Vlasov forward-backward stochastic difference equation and applications to optimal control with law-delay
papers.abstract: In this paper, motivated by discrete-time McKean-Vlasov optimal control problems with law-delay, a class of forward-backward stochastic difference equations is investigated. The main difficulties come from the absence of Ito's formula in the discrete-time setting, as well as the fully coupled structure in which the coefficients depend on both law-delayed and law-anticipated terms. Under suitable monotonicity conditions, the existence and uniqueness of solutions are established. Furthermore, a new monotonicity condition is introduced to address the associated optimal control problem. As an application, the unique optimal control for linear quadratic systems with law-delay is derived.

papers.title: A Structural Theory of Admissible Transitions in Biological Reaction Networks
papers.abstract:
Biological reaction networks exhibit transient changes that cannot be understood from steady states or long-term persistence alone. We extend Chemical Organization Theory to transitions between species subsets, using stoichiometry and feasible reaction fluxes to characterize structurally admissible changes without specifying kinetic parameters.
  The framework distinguishes algebraic admissibility from feasibility constrained by reactant availability. We relate these transitions to reaction-based ordinary differential equations and identify an asymmetry: closure-building transitions are determined by network structure, whereas subsequent reductions can depend on the realized trajectory. Transitions to terminal organizations are characterized when the relevant species sets occur along that trajectory.
  An HIV-immune response model illustrates how a shared closure-building phase can precede different long-term outcomes. The framework connects continuous dynamics with discrete changes in species composition and supports structural analysis of transient pathways and organization formation in systems biology, while distinguishing structural admissibility from realization under particular kinetics.

papers.title: On the weak Lefschetz property of Artinian Gorenstein algebras of codimension three in arbitrary characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf k$ be a field, $S=\mathsf k[x,y,z]$, and $R=S/I$ be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein $\mathsf k$-algebra of codimension three. The $h$-vector of such an algebra is known to be symmetric and unimodal. Mir\'o-Roig proved that if $\mathsf k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero and the $h$-vector of $R$ has at least three peaks, then $R$ has the weak Lefschetz property. We first observe that this statement holds over any infinite field of arbitrary characteristic, and that it follows from a theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev by an argument which is already used in special cases in the literature. We then give a second, characteristic-free proof, following the strategy of Migliore--Zanello, which is elementary and does not use the theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev, and hence does not use the Buchsbaum--Eisenbud structure theorem.

papers.title: Beyond Procrustes distances: a multilinear Gromov-Wasserstein distance capturing chirality
papers.authors: Cl\'ement Soubrier, Geoffrey Woollard, Andrew Warren, Khanh Dao Duc
papers.abstract: Efficiently and robustly analyzing shape data is critical across many scientific disciplines. While chirality is a fundamental property in numerous applications - most notably in molecular science - existing shape analysis metrics either fail to distinguish enantiomers, or rely on costly alignment. To address this gap, we introduce a multilinear generalization of the Gromov-Wasserstein objective, which yields an alignment-free distance between shapes, represented as probability distributions quotiented by a Lie group $G$. In particular, for $G = SO(d)$, we introduce the Chiral Gromov-Wasserstein ($\mathrm{CGW}$) distance, sensitive to chirality. We establish robustness and sample complexity properties for the multilinear Gromov-Wasserstein distances and develop efficient algorithms to compute them, reformulating the underlying optimization problem by projecting couplings onto a low-dimensional space. We derive algorithms for both local and approximate global solutions, yielding an approximation scheme, which is polynomial in the sample size and precision. We validate the framework through numerical experiments that demonstrate the effectiveness of $\mathrm{CGW}$ as a shape metric for chiral objects.

papers.title: Low-Altitude Fluid Antenna Network with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Tong Zhang, Yanfei Su, Shuai Wang, Wanli Ni, Chengzhong Xu, Huseyin Arslan
papers.abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) integrate terrestrial and aerial platforms to provide ubiquitous communication, sensing, and localization services for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. However, dynamic air-ground and air-air channels, abrupt blockages, and heterogeneous interference hinder the realization of this goal. Nevertheless, fluid antenna (FA), a cutting-edge multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique, overcomes these challenges by reconfiguring antenna positions to unlock additional spatial degrees-of-freedom. In this paper, towards bringing low-altitude FA networks into reality, we study the fast and high-performance FA reconfiguration for low-altitude FA networks with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Specifically, we present an electromagnetic digital twin (EM-DT)-assisted MARL framework. To fill the sim-to-real gap, we introduce a two-stage transfer learning framework. Our case study shows that joint FA positions and beamforming optimization can enhance the system sum-rate by 118.5%, compared to the fixed position baseline. This gain comes from the dynamic millisecond timescale reconfiguration of FA arrays and the adaptive steering of beams toward aerial users with mobility.

papers.title: A Chv\'atal--Erd\H{o}s type condition for supereulerian digraphs with $\alpha_{2}=4$
papers.abstract: A digraph is \textbf{supereulerian} if it contains a spanning closed trail. Let $\alpha_2(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing no 2-cycle. In this paper, we study the supereulerianity of digraphs with arc-strong connectivity at least 2. We identify a family $\mathcal H$ of nonsupereulerian 2-arc-strong digraphs and prove that every 2-arc-strong digraph $D$ with $\alpha_2(D)\leq 4$ is supereulerian if and only if $D\notin\mathcal H$. In particular, every digraph $D$ satisfying $\alpha_2(D) \le 4$ and $\lambda(D) \ge 3$ is supereulerian.

papers.title: A Full-Sequence Quantitative Gap Between the Chromatic and Cochromatic Numbers of a Random Graph
papers.abstract:
The cochromatic number $\zeta(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the least number of parts in a partition of $V(G)$ into cliques and independent sets, so $\zeta(G)\le\chi(G)$. Erd\H{o}s and Gimbel asked whether $\chi(G_n)-\zeta(G_n)\to\infty$ with high probability for $G_n\sim G(n,1/2)$. Heckel answered this affirmatively for about $95\%$ of all integers $n$ and conjectured that the natural order of the difference along the full sequence is $n/(\ln n)^3$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$ through all integers, $\chi(G_n)-\zeta(G_n)\ge0.063\,n/(\ln n)^3$ with high probability. The failure probabilities are summable, so under any coupling of the graphs $G_n$ the bound holds almost surely for all sufficiently large $n$.
  The proof counts partitions of the vertex set into classes of five consecutive sizes, each class declared independent or complete. The two choices per class outweigh the entropy lost by restricting the class sizes, so the expected number of such partitions is large already at a number of classes that lies order $n/(\ln n)^3$ below the first-moment lower bound for the chromatic number, uniformly in the rounding phase. A second-moment argument, which controls all overlaps between two such partitions, including whole shared classes and large intersections of unequal classes, bounds the probability that such a partition exists from below. Vertex-exposure concentration, together with a coloring of the leftover vertices, then raises this to high probability at a cost of $o(n/(\ln n)^3)$ extra classes.

papers.title: On the gonality of Kneser graphs
papers.authors: Luis A. Ballinas, Willoughby Caine, D. Blake Hopkins, Doel Rivera Laboy
papers.abstract: The Kneser graphs $\text{KG}(n,k)$ are a classically studied family of graphs. One known invariant of graphs is gonality (also called divisorial gonality), which is the minimum degree of a rank 1 divisor on the graph. Using known bounds on gonality of simple, connected graphs, one may obtain that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is bounded above by $\binom{n-1}{k}$. In 2014, Harvey and Wood showed that the treewidth (a lower bound on gonality) for $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is $\binom{n-1}{k}-1$ for $n\geq 4k^2-3k+2$. In this paper, using scramble number, another lower bound on gonality, we improve this polynomial bound and show that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is exactly $\binom{n-1}{k}$ for $n\geq \frac{3k^2+k+2}{2}$, and conjecture an even stricter polynomial bound using the uniform edge scramble. We then extend our argument to the family of generalized Kneser Graphs, computing the scramble number and gonality using the same polynomial bound.

papers.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
papers.abstract:
We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$\sigma$-weak topology.
  For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai.
  For $\eta(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $\sigma$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence.
  Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.

papers.title: Relative Fourier--Mukai theory for algebraic spaces
papers.abstract: We study the variation of Fourier--Mukai equivalences in proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. For bounded pseudocoherent kernels, we prove that the equivalence locus is open and commutes with arbitrary Noetherian base change. To do so, we develop a theory of relative perfectness and relative quasi-perfectness for algebraic spaces. This includes a fiberwise criteria for integral transforms with nonperfect kernels. As an application, we construct an explicit autoequivalence for elliptic fibrations.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: The direct moving plane method for weak solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop the method of moving planes entirely in the weak formulation for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in the singular range $1<p\leq2$. We first establish a small region principle for antisymmetric functions and apply it to prove radial symmetry and monotonicity of nonnegative weak solutions of fractional $p$-Laplacian equations in a bounded domain. We also consider the nonlocal quasilinear Lane--Emden equation $(-\Delta)^s_pu=u^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. In the Sobolev critical case, we establish radial symmetry, monotonicity, and precise asymptotic behavior at infinity for finite-energy weak solutions. Under a suitable decay condition, we also obtain radial symmetry for the full range $q>p-1$. Our proofs rely on integral estimates derived directly from the weak formulation, thereby extending the moving plane approach of Chen and Li (Adv. Math. 2018: 735-758) from the pointwise $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ setting to weak solutions.

papers.title: Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts
papers.authors: M. P. Thejitha, S. N. Fathima
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the combinatorial object $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ which counts the colored overpartition $k$-tuples wherein both even and odd parts occurs with $r$ and $s$ colors, respectively. We establish several congruences which extends the results of Chacon and Sellers for infinite families of $r,s$ and $k$. In particular, we prove divisibility properties for $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ modulo prime $p$ and derive new congruences modulo powers of $2$. The techniques involved to obtain our results rely on theta function identities and modular forms.

papers.title: Moments of crosscorrelation demerit factors of binary sequences
papers.authors: Daniel J. Katz, Harmony M. Vargas
papers.abstract: Families of sequences with low mutual aperiodic crosscorrelation assist the design of systems for multi-user asynchronous communications and multiple-input multiple-output radar. The crosscorrelation demerit factor of a pair of sequences is the sum of the squared magnitudes of their crosscorrelation values at every shift when the sequences are normalized to unit Euclidean norm, and the merit factor is the reciprocal of the demerit factor. For each positive integer $\ell$, we endow the $2^{2 \ell}$ pairs of binary sequences of length $\ell$ with uniform probability measure and study the distribution of their crosscorrelation demerit factors. Sarwate showed that the mean value is always $1$ regardless of length $\ell$. We develop a method for finding an exact formula for the $p$th central moment (for any positive integer $p$) as a function of $\ell$. Formulae for the variance and third central moment ($p=2$ and $3$) are then obtained by hand calculations, while the fourth through sixth central moments are obtained by computer-assisted calculations. Our theory also shows that all the central moments must be strictly positive for $p\geq 2$ and $\ell \geq 3$.

papers.title: Nonradial stability of an infinite family of self-similar blow-up profiles for the three-dimensional Keller--Segel equation
papers.authors: Te Li, Yuwei Sun, Kaiqiang Zhang
papers.abstract:
The three-dimensional parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel equation admits infinitely many radial self-similar blow-up profiles. Earlier work established radial and nonradial stability for one explicit profile. We study the non-explicit profiles constructed by inner-outer matching and allow perturbations without any symmetry assumption. For each sufficiently large profile index, we prove that the corresponding blow-up dynamics are asymptotically stable along a Lipschitz manifold of initial data. When the blow-up center and scale are allowed to vary, the codimension of this manifold equals the number of intrinsic unstable radial modes.
  We derive refined inner-outer asymptotics and two-scale estimates for the profiles and analyze the nonlocal, non-self-adjoint linearized operator in each spherical harmonic sector. In the radial sector, a reduced-mass transformation leads to a local Sturm-Liouville problem and gives the exact number of negative eigenvalues. In the $l=1$ sector, we identify the translation modes and exclude any additional unstable spectrum. For every $l\ge 2$, the sharp lower bound on the real part of the spectrum is $1/4$. We then combine the spectral decomposition with modulation equations, higher-order energy estimates, and a finite-dimensional Brouwer argument to obtain the nonlinear stability result.

papers.title: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

papers.title: Network recovery from aggregated relational data: alignment and resolution
papers.abstract: We prove that labeled edge probabilities can be recovered uniformly from complete aggregated relational data (ARD) at a given community composition if and only if the sum of trait alignment and partition resolution diverges. We study a two-community logistic network with fixed known weak signal and $K$ trait groups of size $m$. If $b_k$ is the difference between the two community counts in group $k$, alignment $\Lambda=\|b\|_2^2/m$ measures separation in the mean counts. Resolution $\rho=K/m^2$ measures the information that accumulates across groups through joint count fluctuations. Without knowing $b$, the full count likelihood gives a mean squared error bounded by $Ce^{-c(\Lambda+\rho)}+O((Km)^{-2})$ under bounded-energy activity perturbations. At exact group balance and zero activity, the minimax risk is $\exp\{-\Theta(\rho)\}$ as $\rho\to\infty$. Uniform recovery over all globally balanced community assignments holds exactly when $\rho\to\infty$. At zero activity, when the community assignment is uniform over all balanced assignments, the optimal mean squared error averaged over assignments and networks vanishes exactly when $K\to\infty$. The population count law identifies every edge probability, and full adjacency permits uniform recovery throughout the model.

papers.title: Entropic repulsion to the middle layer
papers.abstract:
We consider $\nabla\varphi$ height functions with even and convex interaction energy $W$ on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, which are restricted to take values in the set $\{-S, \ldots, S\}$ for some integer $S \ge 1$. We study the effect of entropic repulsion, which tends to push the spin values to the middle layer.
  We prove that the model has a unique Gibbs measure, with exponential decay of correlations, in the cases: (a) Dimension $d=2$ at all temperatures. (b) Dimensions $d\ge3$ at all temperatures, for a wide class of $W$ with non-increasing second derivative, including the family $W(x)=|x|^p$ for $p\in[1,2]$. (c) Dimensions $d\ge 3$ at both low and high temperatures, $T\in (0,\frac{W(1)d}{4(\ln d+\ln 8)})\cup(d W(2S),\infty]$, with the normalization $W(0)=0$. At low temperatures, our proof provides an alternative to Pirogov--Sinai methods.
  Conversely, we exhibit a class of even and convex interaction energies $W$ which, in high dimensions and suitable temperature regimes, have multiple Gibbs measures.
  Though uniqueness may fail, we show that the magnetization of every Gibbs measure lies in $(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$. This implies the delocalization of the model restricted to take values in $\{0,1,\ldots\}$ (i.e., conditioned to lie above a floor) for all dimensions, any even and convex $W$, and all temperatures.
  Our methods extend to additional setups: We prove that height functions taking values in the real interval $[-1,1]$ always have a unique Gibbs measure, a result previously proved only for the quadratic interaction. For height functions taking values in $\{-S+\frac{1}{2}, \ldots, S-\frac{1}{2}\}$, $S \ge1 $ integer, we prove that the magnetization of every Gibbs measure lies in $(-\frac12, \frac12)$.
  The special case $W(x)=x^2$ of our results addresses questions left open in the work of Bricmont--El Mellouki--Fr\"ohlich (1986).

papers.title: Positive biorthogonal curvature on $S^2$-bundles over closed surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct an explicitly one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics with positive biorthogonal curvature on $S^2\times T^2$, answering a question raised by Bettiol. The method also yields metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on every smooth oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. Since $\pi_1(S^2\times T^2)=\mathbb Z^2$ is not virtually free, these examples separate positive biorthogonal curvature from positive isotropic curvature at the level of fundamental groups.

papers.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
papers.authors: Yuting Jia, Zongxia Liang, Xiaodong Luo
papers.abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through an effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

papers.title: Conformal boundary rigidity for simple Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the conformal boundary rigidity problem for Finsler metrics on a bounded domain. We establish stability estimates for determining the conformal factors of simple Finsler metrics in the same conformal class from their boundary distance functions. Our results provide the Finslerian version of the well-known stability estimates for Riemannian metrics.

papers.title: Product structures and decompositions of $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the decomposition and product theory of $\Gamma$-symmetric spaces, where $\Gamma$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. These results lead to the local classification of semisimple Riemannian $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces of nontrivial type. Furthermore, we identify notable phenomena specific to $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces: the existence of distinct product structures and that of an example with the trivial infinitesimal isotropy representation.

papers.title: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
papers.authors: Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo, Shengzhao Hou, Yizhou Shao, Qi Zhou
papers.abstract:
We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}}\int_{\theta}^{\theta+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$.
  The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra when $2 \in R^\times$, costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $\pi\colon S \to R$ with $\pi(1) = 1$. In particular, the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over these fields is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ when $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. An implementation for the standard tower over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $q = p^k$ with $p \le 2^{31}-1$ an odd prime and $k \le 12$ is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface pyfastcd, available on PyPI. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method over $\mathbb{R}$, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$ for both single and batched products and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract:
Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness.
  We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: The Auslander--Reiten Conjecture for Igusa--Todorov Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra satisfies the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. More precisely, let $V$ be an $n$-Igusa--Todorov witness, and let $t$ be the number of isomorphism classes of nonprojective indecomposable summands of $V$. If a finitely generated module $M$ satisfies $\Ext_A^i(M,A)=0$ for every $i>0$ and $\Ext_A^q(M,M)=0$ for $1\leq q\leq 2t+1$, then $M$ is projective. As applications, algebras of representation dimension at most three and algebras satisfying $J^{2m+1}=0$ for which $A/J^m$ has finite representation type satisfy the Auslander--Reiten conjecture.

papers.title: Spherical and lacunary maximal operators on rank one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type
papers.abstract: The spherical maximal operator of order $\mu$ was introduced by El Kohen in the setting of real hyperbolic spaces, where its $L^p$-boundedness properties were investigated. In this paper, we extend this operator to rank-one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type and establish sufficient conditions on $\mu$ for its boundedness on $L^p$, $1<p\leq\infty$. We also obtain a necessary condition for $L^p$-boundedness when $\mu$ is real and $1<p<\infty$. For $1<p\leq 2$, the necessary and sufficient conditions coincide, yielding the sharp range of real $\mu$ in this regime. Finally, we establish sufficient conditions for the $L^p$-boundedness of the corresponding lacunary spherical maximal operator for $1<p\leq\infty$.

papers.title: On the Markov semigroup generated in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by linear fractional divergence form operators
papers.abstract:
Let $0<s<1$ and $A$ be a constant symmetric positive definite matrix. Given the quadratic form $$ Q_A(u)=\int_{\R^N} A
abla^s u(x)\cdot 
abla^s u(x)\,dx, $$ where $
abla^s$ denotes the Riesz fractional gradient, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions such that $Q_A$ defines a Dirichlet form. In strike contrast with the local case $s=1$, positive definiteness of a constant matrix is not sufficient for the Markov property when $0<s<1$. We also describe the associated symmetric Markov semigroup and its $L^p$ realizations, prove the existence of a smooth nonnegative heat kernel and establish a bounded $H^\infty$ functional calculus.

papers.title: The Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality for operator monotone functions
papers.abstract: We show that for any positive operator monotone function $f$ the inequality $\int_{[0,\infty)} f(t) \, \mathrm{d} \left\lVert E^{\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}}(t) \xi_\psi \right\rVert^2 + f'_\infty \varphi(1-s(\psi)) \geq \frac{f(1)}{2} \Bigl( \varphi(1) + \psi(1) - \lVert \varphi - \psi \rVert \Bigr)$ holds, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{M}_{*,+}$ are two normal positive linear functionals on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$, and $\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}$ is the associated relative modular operator. Choosing $f(t) = t^s$ with $s \in [0,1]$, the Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality is recovered.

papers.title: An inverse problem on eigenfunction triple products
papers.abstract: On a connected closed smooth Riemannian manifold, the algebraic structure of the Laplace eigenfunctions, as described by eigenfunction triple products, uniquely determines the geometry. We refine this correspondence by introducing the notion of an $N$-product eigenbasis, which consists of eigenfunctions whose pairwise products may be written as linear combinations of at most $N$ basis elements. We prove that a manifold admits a $2$-product eigenbasis if and only if it is a flat torus. We also prove an analogous result for Laplace eigenvectors of bounded-degree graphs.

papers.title: Equilibrium selection and sharp convergence rates for a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with simplex-volume interactions
papers.authors: Dohyun Kim, Hansol Park, Woojoo Shim
papers.abstract: We study a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. The associated free energy is not isplacement semiconvex when the simplex dimension $n$ is at least two. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a noncompact continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. The limit is then selected by the initial covariance, whose eigenvectors and eigenvalue gaps are preserved by the flow. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates. For compactly supported initial data with nonstationary covariance, the sharp rate is the smaller of the covariance relaxation rate and three times the slowest transport rate, provided that the third moments do not vanish along the directions of slowest transport. The skewness of the initial datum, rather than its covariance, may therefore dictate the long-time behavior.

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels--Part I: $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: We study the {\epsilon}-capacity regions of mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with general mixture and cost constraints by the information spectrum method. The starting point is a general formula for the {\epsilon}-capacity region of general MACs with cost constraint, together with the random-coding and converse lemmas from which it is derived. For the quasi-static fading Gaussian MAC, with random fading coefficients and noise variance, we show that the {\epsilon}-capacity region is the {\epsilon}-outage capacity region, which gives the latter a Shannon-theoretic operational meaning. The direct part follows from the general formula, and the converse part from the strong converse property of the Gaussian MAC, which is stronger than the {\epsilon}-strong converse, applied to each component. The {\epsilon}-capacity regions coincide in all four scenarios of availability of channel state information (CSI), and the results extend to K users. With CSI at both terminals, variable-rate coding enlarges the 0-capacity region to the polymatroid whose rank function is the average of those of the components. For mixed MACs with general components and a countable parameter space, CSI at the receiver alone never enlarges the {\epsilon}-capacity region, and the region with CSI at the transmitters is given by an information spectrum formula; unlike the Gaussian case, the regions with and without CSI at the transmitters may differ. For uncountable parameter spaces, only the formula for the region with CSI at both terminals survives in general. Parts II and III treat finite-alphabet mixed MACs and the strong converse for the K-user Gaussian MAC, respectively.

papers.title: Uniqueness of embedded minimal Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{CP}^2$
papers.authors: Yong Luo, Hui Ma, Jiabin Yin
papers.abstract: We prove that any embedded minimal Lagrangian torus in the complex projective plane is congruent to the Clifford torus. This settles the orientable case of Oh's classification conjecture. The proof uses a new two-point function constructed from Hermitian products of normalized horizontal lifts.

papers.title: Percolation Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: We study Percolation Markov Decision Processes (PMDPs), where the decision maker repeatedly moves a token through the d-dimensional integer lattice with deterministic transitions and random payoffs assigned to the edges. Payoffs are revealed before the beginning of the decision process and the decision maker aims to maximize the average accumulated payoff over a fixed horizon. First, we address general asymptotic control-theoretic questions by proving the existence of the uniform value and 0-optimal strategies. Furthermore, we examine the structural properties of optimal strategies: we establish the existence of stationary 0-optimal strategies for a class where the token moves in a fixed direction independent of the player's actions, and we provide low-dimensional examples to illustrate their complexity. Moreover, we introduce a dimensional lifting property that allows PMDPs to be approximated by lower-dimensional PMDPs, offering a representation of the approximation of critical probability thresholds in percolation theory via PMDPs.

papers.title: Norms of Schneider--Teitelbaum Polynomials in $p$-adic Fourier Theory
