papers.abstract: Let $F$ be the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and let $P_n(X)$ denote the Lubin--Tate analogues of the binomial polynomials arising in the $p$-adic Fourier theory of Schneider and Teitelbaum. For a particular choice of Lubin--Tate logarithm, we determine explicitly the norms of the functions $P_n(x\Omega)$ on the Banach spaces of locally $F$-analytic functions of fixed order, where $\Omega$ is a Lubin--Tate period. Our computation is based on a recent valuation formula of Ardakov and Berger for the values $P_n(\Omega)$. As an application, we improve the Bannai--Kobayashi normalization of these polynomials. Each element of the resulting basis has norm one.

papers.title: Perturbed Brownian motion reflected at a time-dependent boundary
papers.abstract:
Let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion, $x\ge 0,\, 
u<1$, and $b:[0,\infty)	o\mathbb R$ be a continuous function locally of finite variation starting from 0. We define the perturbed Brownian motion reflected at the boundary $b$ by establishing strong existence and pathwise uniqueness of a solution to the equation \[
  W_t=(1-
u)x+B_t+
u M_t(W)+ rac12 L_t^0(W-b),
  \qquad W_t\ge b(t), \] where $M_t(W):=\sup_{0\le s\le t} W_s$ and the process $L^0(W-b)$ is the semimartingale local time at 0 of the process $W-b$. We give a positive result under condition (PB) on the boundary $b$ : for every $T>0$, the upward increment $\sup_{0\le s<t\le T,\,t-s\le h}(b(t)-b(s))^+ = o(\sqrt{h})$ as $h\downarrow 0$. The proof splits into two regimes: the case $
u<1/2$ is a consequence of the Skorokhod problem in an orthant proved by [Williams 1995], while the case $
u\ge 1/2$ combines a deterministic comparison estimate and a logarithmic upper bound on the number of completed round-trips, following the strategy of [Chaumont and Doney 1999]. For $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, we also construct an increasing $\alpha$-H"older boundary for which no continuous adapted solution starting from zero exists for any $
u<1$.

papers.title: Principal component error in high-dimensional factor models
papers.authors: Alex Bernstein, Lisa R. Goldberg, Nicholas Gunther, Alec N. Kercheval, Tian Lan, Yian Lin, Dayi Yao
papers.abstract: In a statistical factor model, principal components (or eigenvectors) of a sample covariance matrix serve as estimates of principal directions, the true drivers of co-movement of a collection of observed variables. We write the often substantial error in these estimates as a sum of two interpretable terms, which we show have almost sure asymptotic limits as the number of variables grows with sample size bounded. This scenario is commonplace in financial economics, genomics, machine learning and signal processing. Out-of-subspace error measures the distance from an estimate to the subspace spanned by population factor exposures. It can be expressed in terms of data, providing an estimable floor for asymptotic error. In-subspace error is driven by a rotation error within that subspace, which arises from the fixed sample size of the latent factor returns and cannot be estimated from data alone. We illustrate our error analysis with a three-factor simulation of the US public equity market, showing the dependence of the magnitude of the error and its components on dimension and sample size. In that simulation, out-of-subspace error dominates. Researchers who rely on principal component analysis to estimate factor models can use our results to quantify errors in model-based predictions and attributions.

papers.title: Exact Sign Recovery for PCA Connectivity Analysis in Mixture Models
papers.abstract: We study exact sign recovery for PCA connectivity analysis in mixture models with $K$ components, using the projection onto the first $(K-1)$ principal components. For any fixed number of components with affinely independent means, we derive the oracle signal projection explicitly. Under anisotropic sub-Gaussian noise, with a random number of observations in each component, a rowwise eigenspace bound yields a sufficient condition, governed by the weakest signal direction, for recovering all connectivity signs without requiring a bounded condition number of the nonzero signal spectrum. Under isotropic Gaussian noise, when the configuration of the component means is fixed up to scaling and orthogonal transformations, we identify an asymptotically sharp threshold for the signal strength: exact sign recovery succeeds above the threshold and fails below the threshold, with probability tending to one when the signal strength stays a fixed relative distance from the threshold. For an equally weighted regular simplex, we give an explicit sharp cutoff coefficient and show that optimizing the common entrywise threshold improves the coefficient's dependence on the number of components from linear growth to inverse proportionality.

papers.title: A finite Livshits theorem and local length spectrum rigidity
papers.authors: Jonathan DeWitt, Spencer Durham, James Marshall Reber, Thomas Aloysius O'Hare
papers.abstract: We show that for closed negatively curved Riemannian manifolds whose length spectrum is exponentially separated, the length spectrum is a local isometry invariant. The main tool used in the proof is a finitary version of the Livshits theorem with an exponential tail that improves with the regularity.

papers.title: Selberg sieve weights and sign changes of Kloosterman sums. I. Uniform asymptotics for shifted weights
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for smoothed correlations of divisor sums with independently shifted quadratic cutoff functions. With $Y$ denoting the averaging scale, $R$ the divisor cutoff, and $g$ a fixed smooth averaging weight, the error is $O_g(Y/(\log Y)^2)$, uniformly for $Y^{1/5}\leq R\leq Y^{1/3}$ and shifts $s,u\in[0,1/2]$, including coincident shifts. The main term is an explicit bilinear form in the first and second derivatives of the cutoff functions. The proof uses a fixed zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta-function to evaluate the relevant Mellin integrals by successive contour shifts and residue calculations. We also obtain a mean-square estimate for differences of shifted divisor sums, which is used in Part II to control small prime factors in the study of sign changes of Kloosterman sums.

papers.title: Selberg sieve weights and sign changes of Kloosterman sums. II. Square-free moduli with at most four prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $\operatorname{Kl}(1;q)$ denote the normalized Kloosterman sum modulo $q$. We prove that, for each sign, there are $\gg X/\log X$ square-free moduli $q\in(X,2X]$ with at most four prime factors for which $\operatorname{Kl}(1;q)$ has that sign. The proof combines the Selberg sieve with equidistribution and mean-square estimates for Kloosterman sums; the uniform estimate for shifted sieve weights established in Part I controls the contribution of moduli having small prime factors.

papers.title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter in $\mathbb{Z}_N^d$
papers.authors: Alex Iosevich, Zhihe Li, Ke Yu
papers.abstract:
We study asymptotic spectral synthesis on $\mathbb Z_N^d$ using the Fourier ratio, the quotient of the counting-measure $\ell^1$ and $\ell^2$ norms of the unitary Fourier transform. For supports of cardinality $N^{\alpha+o(1)}$, the Fourier-ratio concentration exponent satisfies $0\leq\kappa\leq\frac{\alpha}{2}$. We prove a finite-scale synthesis estimate that uses either the Fourier ratio of a function or that of its support indicator. In particular, the indicator condition applies uniformly to arbitrary weights on the support. Uniform $\ell^p$ bounds imply decay of the largest Fourier coefficient when $2\leq p<\frac{2(d-2\kappa)}{\alpha-2\kappa}$, with every finite $p\geq2$ allowed at maximal concentration. Random unions of cosets show that the finite critical exponent is sharp for every admissible pair in each prescribed ambient dimension, along prime-power moduli.
  We also determine the exact synthesis constant for sets with a transitive group of affine symmetries. For paraboloids this constant is an explicit divisor sum. The formula proves endpoint synthesis along powers of a fixed odd prime, although the endpoint fails along primes. Along products of distinct small primes, synthesis extends to a larger exponent. These families have the same Fourier-ratio exponent. Finally, we relate Fourier concentration to generalized Salem estimates, additive energy, Fourier algebra norms, and necessary conditions for extension estimates.

papers.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
papers.abstract: In their studies of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola--Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems $S'$ and $S'_T$, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension $T$ of Peano arithmetic ($\mathrm{PA}$), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in $T$, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a $T$-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's $S'$ is the case $T=\mathrm{PA}$. More generally, for consistent $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when $T$ proves every true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$ by G\"odel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if $T$ is $\Sigma^0_1$-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

papers.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
papers.abstract: We implement a program of constructing a reflectionless measure on a Widom set with a nontrivial singular continuous component of Nazarov-Volberg and Yuditskii. The construction is an induction that based on two types of operations: splitting point mass and inserting bands. Each operation is realized by multiplying the Cauchy transform of the measure by some explicit multipliers. We provide necessary estimates on measures and the Green functions after each operation.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Third-Order Langevin Dynamics for Non-Convex Optimization via Simulated Annealing
papers.abstract: We study global convergence guarantees of third-order Langevin dynamics for non-convex optimization via simulated annealing with fixed friction and decreasing noise. An explicit three-block distorted entropy transfers dissipation from the noisy auxiliary variable to the full state. Under dissipativity, regularity, and low-temperature functional-inequality assumptions, logarithmic cooling drives the objective values to the global minimum in probability at the barrier-controlled kinetic rate. For the exact-force-integral and midpoint three-stage discretizations, polynomially decreasing steps preserve this rate on the physical time scale. The cubic local endpoint estimate gives a less restrictive sufficient step-size condition than the available frozen-force kinetic result. A comparison with the one-gradient UBU integrator shows how its centered stochastic local error leads, under the same strong-coupling analysis, to a smaller sufficient iteration exponent. Numerical experiments are conducted to illustrate our theory. For a double well objective, third-order Langevin terminal-success point estimates are higher than UBU at both a common horizon and an equal gradient budget. For a high-dimensional nonconvex neural-network objective using synthetic data, independently tuned UBU and third-order Langevin schemes both outperform overdamped Langevin dynamics; the third-order Langevin point estimate is higher. For the same neural-network objective on real data, we show the same point-estimate ordering for best-basin probability and post-quench test accuracy. Numerical code and associated experiment results are publicly available at https://github.com/gagawjbytw/simulated-annealing-third-order-langevin

papers.title: Recursive Paintboxes and the Martin Boundary of the Hoffman Rooted-Tree Graph
papers.abstract: We determine the Martin boundary of the Hoffman graph on unlabelled non-plane rooted trees and classify the central measures on its path space. Every boundary point is minimal, and the boundary is parametrized by deterministic recursive paintboxes up to equality of their finite sampling laws. The probabilities of sampling trees whose root has a single child determine the root branch masses and their associated boundary points, and characterize convergence on the boundary. Under any central measure, the successive tree shapes converge almost surely to a random boundary point whose law is the unique mixing measure in the extremal decomposition. For recursive Ewens trees, this limit is represented by a random paintbox with independent Poisson--Dirichlet splits at its vertices, and the mixing measure has no atoms. This applies in particular to the uniform recursive-tree law and Fulman's rooted-tree Plancherel law.

papers.title: Common invariant measures for beta-transformations: affine relations and squared bases
papers.abstract: We classify the common invariant probabilities of two beta-transformations in two families. In the first, the bases satisfy $\gamma=a\beta+c>1$ with $\beta>1$ irrational, $a,c\in\mathbb Q$ and $a+c\ne1$. In the second, they are an irrational $\beta>1$ and its square. In both families every common singular invariant probability is the point mass at zero; combining this with the classification of coincident R\'enyi--Parry measures gives all common invariant probabilities, with no entropy, ergodicity or multiplicative-independence hypothesis.

papers.title: Congruences for Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts
papers.authors: M. P. Thejitha, S. N. Fathima
papers.abstract: In recent work, authors defined $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ to be the number of overcolored partition $k$-tuples wherein both even and odd parts are colored with $r$ and $s$ colors, respectively. This function generalizes the overcubic partition $k$-tuples studied by Chacon and Sellers. The present work gives a uniform framework for studying congruences for $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ modulo odd primes. For example, we prove that, for $n\ge 1$, \begin{align*} \bar{b}_{4,2}^4(5n)\equiv 0\pmod{5}. \end{align*}

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract:
In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration.
  Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: Elections, Fractional Dichromatic Number and Domination in Tournaments and Digraphs
papers.abstract:
The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of induced acyclic sets into which its vertex set can be partitioned. The fractional dichromatic number is its fractional relaxation. Bourneuf, Charbit and Thomass\'e showed that the domination number of a tournament can be bounded as an (exponential) function of its fractional dichromatic number. This naturally leads to the question of finding a polynomial bound.
  We show that this bound is linear. To do this, we show a connection between undominated sets in elections and dominating sets in tournaments with bounded fractional dichromatic number. Within this framework, we also connect the well-known question of the existence of small Condorcet winning sets in elections to domination problems in digraphs with fractional dichromatic number less than 2. Thus, we open a new path to investigating these popular open problems in social choice from the perspective of graph theory.

papers.title: Existence of three solutions for parametric $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with a nonlinear elliptic problem in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ involving the $p$-Laplacian operator with $p>N$. Under suitable assumptions on the potential term and on the nonlinearity, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational and relies on two different three critical points theorems. The results extend to higher dimensions some recent multiplicity theorems for one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian equations on the real line, and provide explicit ranges for the parameter $\lambda > 0$ ensuring the existence of multiple solutions, which are nonnegative under additional sign conditions. The nontriviality of the solutions is also discussed. Finally, applications to problems whose nonlinearities have separated variables are presented.

papers.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
papers.authors: Lucas Chen, Joshua Im, Steven J. Miller, Devayani Pradhan
papers.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

papers.title: Boundary Collisions and Weak Excitation in LQR Policy-Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: Closed-loop stability concerns all initial states, whereas an LQR cost evaluates only the directions excited by a prescribed initial-state distribution. We study how this distinction affects Euclidean policy-gradient flows. For every nonzero deficient covariance rank, we construct relatively open families of controllable data and open sets of stabilizing initial gains whose exact gradient trajectories reach the stability boundary in finite optimization time. The state Gramian can remain positive definite at every time before collision. By separating the cost contribution of a critical mode, we obtain a local collision criterion based on direction attraction and motion toward the stability boundary. Adding excitation of strength $\varepsilon$ yields matching $\Theta(\sqrt\varepsilon)$ bounds on the local minimum stability margin for trajectories that would otherwise collide. For a class of single-input, corank-one systems, these bounds hold over the entire trajectory without a common compact-set assumption. Numerical examples further illustrate the dynamics and scaling laws.

papers.title: Strictly positive optimal Hardy weights on manifolds and graphs via Green potential
papers.authors: Ujjal Das, Matthias Keller, Yehuda Pinchover
papers.abstract: Consider a subcritical functional $Q$ associated with a $p$-Schr\"odinger operator defined on a domain $\Omega$ in a noncompact Riemannian manifold. Employing the supersolution construction, we obtain a family of strictly positive-critical Hardy weights for $Q$. The construction is based on the Green potential $G_f$, with a strictly positive charge $f$ such that $G_f$ vanishes at infinity. An interesting new feature of this family, depending on a parameter $0\leq \varepsilon\leq 1$, is the transition from positive-criticality to null-criticality at $\varepsilon=0$. Furthermore, we prove an analogous result on graphs.

papers.title: Rank-One HCIZ Integrals and Multiplicative Convolutions
papers.authors: Beno\^it Collins, Nicolas Delporte, Manasa Nagatsu, Reiko Toriumi
papers.abstract:
We study how spectral averaging interacts with the logarithm in large-dimensional rank-one Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber (HCIZ) integrals. For independent bi-unitarily invariant matrices $A,B$ with uniformly bounded deterministic singular values and weakly convergent empirical spectral measures of their Gram matrices, the integral for $(BA)^*(BA)\otimes\mathbf{1}_N$ has two limiting descriptions at speed $N^2$ for small real parameters: averaging its logarithm gives free multiplicative convolution, whereas taking the logarithm after averaging gives classical multiplicative convolution. We also prove an exact finite-dimensional equality between this annealed integral and the one for $(A^*A)\otimes(B^*B)$. For any fixed $k\ge3$ factors under the hypotheses stated for $A,B$, the annealed limits at speed $N^k$ generally differ for small positive parameters, and we characterize the equality cases.
  For tensor products with any fixed number $k$ of factors, global Haar vectors at speed $N^k$ and product-state vectors at speed $N$ yield classical and free multiplicative convolution, respectively, for small real parameters under the corresponding hypotheses.
  We also derive the known multiplicativity of the $S$-transform.

papers.title: Normalized ground states as sharp dynamical thresholds for the inhomogeneous NLS with an inverse-square potential
papers.abstract: We study the focusing inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with an inverse-square potential, in the mass-supercritical and energy-subcritical regime and in every dimension $N\ge3$. Two lines of research on this model have so far developed separately, namely the scattering theory below the ground state and the variational theory of solutions with prescribed mass. We connect them. We compute explicitly the minimax level $m_a(c)$ of the energy on the Pohozaev manifold of mass $c$ in terms of the sharp constant of the associated Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. We prove that the minimizers of $m_a(c)$ are exactly the optimizers of this inequality lying on the Pohozaev manifold, and that they are ground states of the stationary problem. This answers a question left open in the literature. We then show that $m_a(c)$ is a sharp dynamical threshold. Below it, the sign of the Pohozaev functional is preserved by the flow. If this sign is positive, the solution is global. If it is negative and the datum has finite variance, the solution blows up in finite time. For the three-dimensional cubic model, the global solutions also scatter, by a known scattering criterion read in its scale-invariant form. As consequences, we obtain the strong instability of all normalized ground states, with destabilizing data on the same mass sphere, the strict monotonicity of the threshold with respect to the coupling constant, and a positive lower bound for $m_a(c)$ which is uniform up to the critical Hardy coupling.

papers.title: Compatible Bases and Actuator Scheduling
papers.abstract:
We study a constrained basis-selection problem for an ordered block matrix $B=[ B_1\mid\cdots\mid B_n ].$ The successive tail matrices determine a nested family of column spaces, and we consider bases of representatives which are compatible with this induced flag. Our main linear-algebraic result shows that, among bases of representatives, compatibility with the entire flag is characterized by the intrinsic block quotas $r_k=w_k-w_{k+1}$, where $w_k$ is the rank of the $k$-th tail matrix.
  We then show that the same structure arises naturally in finite-horizon linear control. For the reachability matrix $[A^{N-1}G\mid \cdots\mid G]$, requiring every actuator to be used exactly once turns an actuator schedule into a representative system. Preservation of the complete reachability profile is then equivalent to compatibility with the tail-space flag.
  This correspondence leads to an exact depth-first search with a future-rank pruning criterion. For an explicit structured family and a fixed search ordering, the baseline search visits $3\cdot2^m+m-2$ nodes before the first solution, whereas future-rank pruning reduces this number to $3m+1$. Exact-arithmetic experiments reproduce these formulas for all tested instances.

papers.title: Inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson structures from vector field samples
papers.authors: Jason E. Frank, Georg A. Gottwald
papers.abstract: We present a method for the data-driven inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson dynamical systems from vector-field samples, in which the Hamiltonian and the underlying Poisson tensor are estimated jointly rather than assuming the structure is known. The Hamiltonian is represented as a linear combination of random feature maps with fixed random internal weights, so its estimation is a linear regression problem for any given Poisson structure. We treat three cases of increasing generality: a known Poisson tensor, an unknown constant invertible (symplectic) structure matrix, and Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson structures, with structure matrix linear in the state. In the constant case, the Hamiltonian and structure matrix are recovered jointly from an eigenvalue problem that avoids the trivial zero solution due to the scaling symmetry of Hamiltonian systems. For Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson systems we alternate between an initial Hamiltonian estimate from a generalized eigenvalue problem for an approximate first integral, and a constrained nonlinear least-squares fit of the structure constants that enforces the Jacobi identity and, for affine structures, the cocycle condition, via continuation in a penalty parameter. Orthogonal matching pursuit selects a compact, well-conditioned subset of random features. Because the learned Hamiltonian is a sum of single-feature terms, the model admits an explicit Poisson/symplectic splitting integrator, which we use to validate the learned systems via long-time Poincare sections. We demonstrate the approach on the four- and five-dimensional Lorenz-86 model and a six-dimensional Kirchhoff rigid-body system, recovering Hamiltonians, structure constants and Casimir invariants to high accuracy, and showing the inferred Poincare sections converge to the correct invariant-tori topology as the number of random features increases.

papers.title: Numerical Range Geometry and Sharp Inequalities for Positive Block Matrices
papers.abstract: We give affirmative answers to two questions posed by Bourin and Lee concerning positive block matrices and numerical ranges. We prove that the elliptical width of a fixed off-diagonal block \(X\) is exactly the best correction term in their norm inequality. As a consequence, the corresponding inequality without a correction term holds for every positive completion of \(X\) if and only if \(X\) is essentially Hermitian, proving their Conjecture 3.3. We also show that the radius term in their eigenvalue inequality for normal off-diagonal blocks is best possible at every prescribed eigenvalue level.

papers.title: Presentation of Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local rings
papers.abstract: We obtain presentations of Borel subgroups of certain Chevalley groups and Kac-Moody groups of simply laced type. More precisely, we show that Borel subgroups of simply laced Chevalley groups over a commutative, unital ring (satisfying a minor technical condition), are the amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups, generalising a result of Tits over fields (different from $\mathbb{F}_2$). We moreover show that Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local B\'ezout domains also have a presentation as an amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups as soon as this holds for their rank 3 subgroups. In particular we deduce that Borel subgroups of simply laced Kac-Moody groups over a local B\'ezout domain (with residue field different from $\mathbb{F}_2$) have such a presentation if and only if they are of 3-spherical type.

papers.title: Propagation of Energy Moments for the Plasma--Charge Model
papers.abstract: This paper proves propagation of energy moments for the three-dimensional plasma--charge model, namely, the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system with a moving point charge. For every $K>2$, an initially finite $K$th energy moment remains finite on every bounded time interval, without requiring any initial moment of order greater than $K$, a smallness condition on the plasma mass, or positive initial separation from the point charge. The constructed global weak solution conserves total energy for almost every time. The proof relies on a critical space--time density estimate and a direct control of the electric field along the moving charge.

papers.title: The set-theorist's real numbers
papers.abstract: Descriptive set theorists often refer to elements of the Baire space, $\mathcal{N} = {}^\omega\omega$, as ``reals.'' In this expository article, we present mathematical justification for this practice and highlight the advantages of working with $\mathcal{N}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ in the context of descriptive set theory.

papers.title: Comparing the reliability of coherent systems with heterogeneous, dependent and distribution-free components
papers.abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in comparing the reliability of systems with dependent components. Most of the recent works consider Archimedean copulas to define the dependency structure of systems and examine specific familiy of distributions. In this work, we provide distribution-free results to compare, in the usual stochastic order under some majorization conditions, coherent systems with heterogeneous and dependent components where the dependency structure can be defined by any copula. Applications of our main results for specific copulas and different families of marginal distributions are also given.

papers.title: Uniformly Positive Scalar Curvature on Manifold Interiors
papers.abstract:
We obtain topological obstructions to the existence of a complete Riemannian metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature on the interiors of certain 4-manifolds using Seiberg--Witten theory. In particular, no punctured blowups of a homotopy K3 manifold admit complete metrics of uniformly positive scalar curvature.
  Further, let $X$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n$. We show that if $n=6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of uniformly positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric which is a product near the boundary. In dimension 5, an analogous result holds under additional hypotheses and after possibly changing the smooth structure on $X$. If $n=5,6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric with minimal boundary. One ingredient is a new PSC deformation result.

papers.title: Strong transport noise prevents self-intersection in 2D fluid-structure interaction
papers.abstract: We consider the interaction of a viscous incompressible fluid with a flexible elastic shell occupying the boundary of the fluid's domain in two space dimensions. The shell is modelled by a visco-elastic linearised beam equation. It is an open problem in fluid-structure interaction, if a self-intersection of the structure can be excluded in the long run. We show that by adding a physically well-motived and sufficiently strong transport noise in the structure equation, the self-intersection does not occur before any given end-time with any prescribed probability smaller than 1.

papers.title: Chiral Extensions of Cotangent Yangian
papers.abstract: We construct chiral extensions of the cotangent Yangian using vertex algebroids. At zero level, the construction yields a vertex algebra with a compatible coproduct, whose Zhu reduction recovers the cotangent Yangian of Abedin and Niu. We also construct vertex algebra extensions at non-zero levels and study level-additive coproducts. The zero-level vertex algebra admits two natural quasi-conformal structures. We compute the corresponding sphere one-point conformal blocks and equip each block space with an associative product induced by the coproduct. For the first quasi-conformal structure, the blocks space can be identified with the dual of a certain Lie algebroid homology; for the second, we describe the block algebra and its classical limit in terms of mini-twistor geometry.

papers.title: Beyond LLM-GA: Secure Fluid Antenna Systems with ReEvo-Designed Memetic Algorithm
papers.authors: Hanyong Xu, Zhaolai Dang, Tong Zhang
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) offer significant spatial flexibility, yet securing them against eavesdropping is critical for practical FAS deployment in military, satellite, and internet-of-things networks. Although large language model (LLM)-assisted genetic algorithms (LLM-GAs) can address this secure FAS port selection problem, whether further algorithmic improvement is possible warrants deeper investigation. To this end, we propose a memetic algorithm based on reflective evolution (ReEvo). Unlike the state-of-the-art LLM-GAs, which design only crossover or mutation operators with an LLM, our algorithm leverages an LLM to evolve dedicated crossover, mutation, and local-search operators offline. These operators are then embedded into a memetic search framework, thereby obviating any online LLM queries during execution. Simulation results at equal generation counts demonstrate that our proposed algorithm achieves a higher secure sum-rate than the conventional GA and the state-of-the-art LLM-GAs.

papers.title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
papers.authors: Alexey Naumov, Sergey Samsonov, Vladimir Spokoiny, Vladimir Ulyanov
papers.abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent mean zero random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$ that need not be identically distributed. Let $S_n$ denote the sum, $\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\ne0$, and let $G\sim N(0,\Sigma)$. Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma}{\|\Sigma\|}, \qquad v(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)}{\|\Sigma\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions $r(\Sigma)\le C_\Sigma v(\Sigma)$ and $v(\Sigma)\ge6$, we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(\Sigma)}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The approximation error thus tends to zero when $r(\Sigma)=o(n)$, even if $p$ grows faster than $n$. We also provide an example showing that the order $r(\Sigma)/n$ is sharp in general. The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof combines Esseen smoothing, truncation, covariance partitioning, moment matching, frame/lattice estimates, a second-order endpoint expansion and comparison estimates expressed in terms of the covariance matrices.

papers.title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
papers.abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets
papers.abstract: Recent results [arXiv:2602.04378, arXiv:2602.22608] establish lower bounds for optimization over strongly convex sets, covering specified Frank-Wolfe updates and unrestricted deterministic first-order linear minimization oracle (LMO) methods, respectively. Neither establishes a lower bound for unrestricted randomized methods. We close this gap by proving an $\Omega(L\operatorname{diam}(S)^2/T^2)$ distributional lower bound after $T$ oracle calls for randomized first-order LMO methods over strongly convex sets, with final outputs required to be feasible on every instance and seed. While our construction reuses the family of [arXiv:2602.22608], our proof characterizes the conditional distribution of the hidden permutation after adaptive queries and bounds the expected decrease of a combinatorial statistic controlling optimizer variance. We also show that the same error threshold holds with probability at least $3/4$ and yields a stopping-time tail bound. Our construction uses the same curvature-diameter coupling as [arXiv:2602.22608]. Comparisons with the upper bound [arXiv:1406.1305] must account for this coupling. Separately, we show that prescribed slow exact-line-search Frank-Wolfe trajectories can locally amplify sufficiently small initialization errors, corresponding to roughly one extra bit of initialization accuracy per iteration, and that initializations satisfying a particular eventual slow envelope have planar measure zero.

papers.title: Symmetric two-level preconditioning for the method of reflections for Laplace and Stokes problems
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze symmetric two-level preconditioners for the method of reflections for Laplace and Stokes problems in three-dimensional perforated domains. Both models admit quadratic constrained minimization formulations, with the Stokes velocity restricted to divergence-free functions. We combine parallel reflection corrections with a coarse correction based on constant boundary modes to obtain symmetric positive definite preconditioners for the conjugate gradient method. Under a geometric separation condition, we prove condition number bounds independent of the number and sizes of the holes and the diameter of the ambient domain, with explicit dependence on the separation parameter. The coarse problem has one unknown per hole for Laplace problems and three for Stokes problems. We also derive convergence estimates for the one-level methods.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
papers.abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{{\lambda},\mu}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities (${\lambda}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$). Furthermore, we provide explicit expressions for cocycles generating these spaces.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing and quantitative transversality on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on spetral designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.

papers.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.

papers.title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
papers.abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-H\"older in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(\phi)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity established by Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

papers.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
papers.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and \c{S}avk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite and Borel's theorem, the symmetries of the hyperbolic knot Th(p,q) are the symmetries of its standard diagram once that diagram has no non-trivial flypes (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes in the sense made precise in the paper (a closely related statement is due to Shimizu, Gill and Joshi) and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

papers.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

papers.title: Provable Method of Moments for Cryo-EM
papers.authors: Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory, Dan Edidin, Josh Katz, Shay Kreymer, Nir Sharon
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional volume in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) from noisy tomographic projections acquired at unknown viewing rotations, drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. We show that, in a spherical-shell representation satisfying an explicit shell-separation condition, the first three moments generically determine the underlying real volume up to its intrinsic global $\mathrm{O}(3)$ ambiguity. The proof is constructive and yields a frequency-marching procedure that successively recovers the volume. Consequently, consistent recovery in the high-noise regime has sample complexity $n=\omega(\sigma^6)$, where $n$ is the number of observations and $\sigma^2$ is the noise variance. Numerical experiments validate the constructive recovery scheme under finite sampling and additive noise, and indicate that direct third-moment optimization can succeed beyond the structural assumptions required by the constructive proof.

papers.title: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
papers.abstract:
We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all bounded definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. These beautiful pairs are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields.
  We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields -- considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. Using the non-abelian Hodge correspondence, we show that the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
papers.abstract: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets. We prove that it does. The proof combines direct decompositions with an auxiliary ordering of connected ordered sets and a careful choice of intervals of maximum height. We then extend the reconstruction result to several forms of repeated exponentiation.

papers.title: Brezis--Nirenberg-type results for coupled critical elliptic systems with sign-changing perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish Brezis--Nirenberg-type existence results for elliptic systems with symmetric linear coupling, a radial critical nonlinearity and a subcritical potential. For any dimension $N\ge3$, the potential may change sign, with its negative part bounded by a subquadratic power for some exponent $q_1\in(1,2)$ and no smallness restriction on the coefficient. Under coercivity and suitable near-zero and subcritical growth assumptions, we obtain a nontrivial weak solution if the largest eigenvalue of the coupling matrix is positive when $N\ge4$, or exceeds a positive constant depending on the domain when $N=3$. No homogeneity, convexity or monotonicity along rays is required of the perturbation potential, and either sign of the linear coupling is allowed. The proof combines a variational criterion below the critical Sobolev energy level with estimates showing that the negative part of the potential contributes less than the linear energy decrease. On star-shaped domains, we also obtain a Pohozaev nonexistence criterion.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $\epsilon$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $\epsilon$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $\epsilon$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $\sigma^p$ for some $\sigma\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $\Omega\big(\big(\sigma^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\epsilon^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 \Delta\epsilon^{-2}+L_1\Delta\epsilon^{-1})\big)$, where $\Delta>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1\epsilon^{-1}\Delta$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

papers.title: On the location of mass concentration for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential in bounded domains
papers.authors: Shubin Yu, Chun-Lei Tang, Ziheng Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ Letting $\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ be the ring of global minima of $V(x)$, we focus on a unified geometric setting $\Gamma\cap \Omega\not=\emptyset$, which allows $\Gamma\subset \Omega$ or $\Gamma\cap\partial\Omega\neq\emptyset$. In this setting, we determine the precise location of mass concentration for ground states as the interaction strength approaches the critical value. More precisely, we prove that the mass concentrates at a point $x_0\in\Gamma\cap \Omega$ that has maximal distance from $\partial\Omega$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds on the difference between the minimal energies in the bounded domain and whole space. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of planar graphs
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lu\v{z}ar, Rindo\v{s}ov\'{a} and Sot\'{a}k [Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum colorings of planar graphs with respect to neighborhoods, \emph{Discrete Appl.\ Math.}\ \textbf{324} (2023) 80--92] conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no conflict-free colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a critical planar graph on $25$ vertices and $51$ edges that needs four colours, with a proof that can be checked by hand. Finally, we give an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

papers.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined on Curves of Genus 2
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

papers.title: Complete solutions and subharmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X \rightarrow X$ the canonical bundle, and $T_X\coloneqq K_X^{-1}\rightarrow X$ the dual bundle of the canonical bundle. For each integer $r \geq 2$, each $q \in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of the square root $K_X^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle, we canonically obtain a Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))\rightarrow X$, which is called a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal solution $h = (h_1, \dots, h_r)$ to the Hitchin equation on a cyclic Higgs bundle yields $r-1$ Hermitian metrics $H_1, \dots, H_{r-1}$ on $T_X\rightarrow X$, defined as $H_j \coloneqq h_j^{-1} \otimes h_{j+1}$ for each $j=1,\dots, r-1$, while $h_1$, $h_r$, and $q$ yield a Hermitian metric $H_r$ on $T_X \rightarrow X$ which is degenerate at the zero set of $q$. A diagonal solution is said to be complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\dots, H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki established a theorem stating that, for any Riemann surface $X$ and any $q$ that is non-zero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete solution $h$ to the Hitchin equation for the cyclic Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))$ with $\det(h)=1$. The holomorphic section $q$ induces a subharmonic weight function $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X\rightarrow X$, and the Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through this weight function. In previous work, the author introduced a variant of the Hitchin equation associated with an arbitrary subharmonic weight function $\varphi$. In this paper, we extend the Li--Mochizuki theorem to complete solutions of the extended Hitchin equation associated to any subharmonic weight function $\varphi$ that is not identically $-\infty$ unless $X$ is hyperbolic.

papers.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
papers.abstract:
We consider the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories
  to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. Its even-morphism part is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence, rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems of Shimizu-Yadav, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose M\"uger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We give a self-contained treatment of graded simple current algebras and of the free fermion (Ising) example. We compare our formulation with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

papers.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
papers.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$ of rotation numbers. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotation numbers in $I$ is an ellipse. It suffices to assume these caustics at a suitably chosen family of rotation numbers in $I$ with any prescribed rational point of $I$ as its unique accumulation point. The key linear result classifies real $L^2$ displacements with phase-independent orbit sums at every rational rotation number in $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.authors: Vincenzo Di Gennaro, Antonio Rapagnetta, Pietro Sabatino
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the N\'eron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$. When $X\subset\mathbb P^r$ is not necessarily a complete intersection, assuming that the Picard group of $X$ is generated by the hyperplane section class, we obtain the coarse bound $p_a(C)\leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+\left(\frac{11}{24}n+4\right)$ for $d\gg n$.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.authors: Zhuoni Chi, Shurui Liu, Ping Nie
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: Uniform Confinement for One-Dimensional Pressureless Euler--Poisson: Existence and Asymptotics
papers.authors: Andrew Xie, Emmanuel Alayande, Christopher Chun, Yusen Li, Rohan Mawalkar, Adrian Tudorascu, Adam Van
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are attractive at long ranges serve as simplified models that describe aggregation phenomena. We prove uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system where the potential satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions, requiring the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. When the potential is semiconvex, these bounds yield compactness of time-translated trajectories, which converge to a solution on all of $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ of a simpler equation. Often, these limiting solutions possess substantial rigidity that determines the asymptotic behavior of the original solution, which we explore in a few applications. This method is robust with respect to the choice of potential, and in contrast to previous work does not require the solution operator to have a closed-form expression. As a corollary of our uniform bounds, we also obtain existence of solutions for non-semiconvex potentials, although such solutions may not retain stickiness.

papers.title: The Exhaustive Peres Transform: Extraction and Universal Coding
papers.abstract: Run to exhaustion, Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure yields a bijection of {0,1}^N that splits every string into fair bits and a residual. The residual is self-delimiting and determines the number of ones, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual under every exchangeable law. Each residual one accounts for a power of two of the weight of the input, and the residual of every input of length N has fewer than sqrt(3) N^0.793 ones. This sparsity gives a short proof, with an explicit remainder, that the fair bits per symbol tend almost surely to the entropy for Bernoulli sources and every finite alphabet. The Bernoulli likelihood factorises along the recursion, and code B, which codes the residual at plug-in biases, has the length of the two-part code. Code G gamma-codes the gaps of the residual, with no estimate and no arithmetic coder: on every string its length is at most the logarithm of the type class plus O(N^0.793 log N). What is more, a concatenation of J pieces costs its piecewise empirical entropy plus a term that is sublinear when J = o(N), without the cuts being sent. After a Burrows-Wheeler transform of the reversed string, both codes are universal for stationary ergodic sources: code B through a context tree of growing depth, with regret O(2^k log N) against Markov sources of order k, and code G with no tree, competing on every individual sequence with the empirical conditional entropy of every order. For laws invariant under permutations inside the pieces of a partition, the fair bits not mixed across the pieces are exactly uniform given everything else; after the BWT, the fair bits of every stationary source fall short of their length by o(N) bits of entropy, with an exponential tail for Markov sources. Experiments measure the finite-length price of these guarantees.

papers.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
papers.abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

papers.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
papers.authors: Kenta Kitamura, Mingchang Liu, Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.

papers.title: Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium property is established.

papers.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
papers.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.authors: Dmitriy F. Kuznetsov, Mikhail D. Kuznetsov
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
papers.abstract: For Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes, we develop the first sparse-grid finite element discretizations, for dramatically reducing the number of degrees of freedom used in tensor-product finite elements. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. For the three-dimensional Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes, we construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials, exactness and uniform inf-sup stability of associated mixed methods. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we also prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent algebraic convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to tensor-product finite elements.

papers.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
papers.abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided. Moreover, we show that it is a braided module category over a suitable monoidal subcategory.

papers.title: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
papers.authors: Roberto Nuca, Matteo Parsani, Lisandro Dalcin
papers.abstract: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared weighted reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the weighted-norm optimality and coefficient-space quasi-optimality of local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.authors: Lior Gishboliner, Sepehr Hajebi, Xiangyu Li
papers.abstract: For $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\geq 3$ and an $r$-graph (i.e., an $r$-uniform hypergraph) $H$, the Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every red/blue coloring of the hyperedges of the $N$-vertex complete $r$-graph $K_N^{(r)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(r)}$. For every integer $r\geq 3$, we characterize all $r$-graphs $H$ for which $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$. Explicitly, we prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"{e}te, and Yu, that $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of a lexicographic power of $K_r^{(r)}$. This concludes an extensive line of work initiated by Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal in 1972 on characterizing the polynomial growth of off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers.

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.authors: Xinyu Bai, Wanshan Lin, Xueting Tian
papers.abstract: We consider an attractor $\Lambda$ of a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbf M^d$ with a trapping neighborhood $U$ and an extendable continuous invariant splitting $T_{\overline U}\mathbf M^d=E\oplus F$. Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures on $\Lambda$ that satisfy Pesin's entropy formula and have negative Lyapunov exponents on $E$ and positive exponents on $F$. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures, and the corresponding sets of asymptotically hyperbolic points are covered, modulo Lebesgue null sets, by the basins of at most countably many such measures. We give necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of ergodic SRB measures with these exponent signs in terms of derivative growth and orbit statistics, and characterize the relationship between physical measures, strongly observable measures, physical-like measures and such SRB measures. We also construct examples with unique hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists. We apply these results to matrix cocycles, establishing the existence of invariant measures that realize the joint spectral radius for countable families of matrices.

papers.title: Magnetic billiards: duality and magnetic Radon property
papers.abstract:
We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field.
  We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property.
  These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property.
  In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular.
  We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard.
  Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.

papers.title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
papers.abstract: We propose a parametrization-free method that estimates the principal curvatures and principal directions of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$ from the closest point projections of a few random rays, without coordinate charts or local fitting. The projection of a ray induces a curve on the submanifold, which is a geodesic only in special cases, so its curvature is in general not a curvature of the submanifold. The velocities of these curves, however, relate to the derivative of the closest point projection, whose eigenpairs carry the information of the principal curvatures and directions. Finite differences along $d$ rays can estimate them without relying on the normal information at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections, and we provide error bounds.
