papers.abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\mathrm{deg}( x_p )=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles K\'atai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $\beta_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We reconstruct smooth cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution through classical interpolation of smooth plane conics from five distinct points, or four with their cross-ratio. If the quadratic coefficient map has rank three and the fixed cubic surface has trivial automorphism group, five polarized anti-invariant Jacobian factors of smooth Eckardt sections suffice, or four with their parameters. Both bounds are optimal. By contrast, in rank two we construct two-dimensional families of equivariantly nonisomorphic fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. The factor family also has an integral projective Lagrangian closure in an associated OG10 compactification.

papers.title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, and we call it the Golod threshold for $I$ over $\m$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We also show that when $I$ is homogeneous, under a suitable degree condition, $\m^k I$ is Golod if and only if $k\geq \mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, i.e., once Golodness is achieved, it cannot be lost. In the last section, we work in the setting of a regular local ring of dimension 3, and show that the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this resolves a question posed by Dao and De Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.title: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
papers.abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly. We will also show that two gcd-graphs over the same matrix ring are isospectral if and only if they have the same generating set.

papers.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
papers.authors: D. E. K\k{e}dzierski, D. Koellmer, P. Kraso\'n
papers.abstract:
We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence.
  The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

papers.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
papers.authors: Alessandro Chiesa, Guy Weissenberg, Eylon Yogev, Kai Zhe Zheng
papers.abstract:
Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius.
  We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=\rho n$, fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrt{\rho}+\eta)n\rceil$, with error $O_{\rho,\eta}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding.
  For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{\rho,\eta}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{\rho,\eta,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $\rho,\eta,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

papers.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
papers.abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-S\"oderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $\Psi$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollob\'as's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.

papers.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: A Probabilistic Characterization of the Ideals of Resolvent Algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize the ideal theory of Buchholz for resolvent algebras in probabilistic terms. Regarding closed two-sided ideals as kernels of representations, we pass from representations to the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal representations of states, and describe the singular, trivially regular, and regular parts, which Buchholz gives through the one-particle space, by the behavior of the corresponding probability measures of the fields. On an isotropic subspace, the resolvent algebra is a commutative $C^{\ast}$-algebra whose states correspond to probability measures, and this correspondence carries the description further to sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Starting from Bose--Einstein condensation of the free Bose gas with its direct integral representation and from the treatment of the infrared singularity of the van Hove model, we connect the ideal-theoretic and the probabilistic arguments. Since the ideals carry physical information in these arguments, we show that the corresponding sub-$\sigma$-algebras and their inclusions carry this information in correspondence with the ideals.

papers.title: The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erd\H{o}s problem 521
papers.authors: Zengjing Chen, Xiaodong Liu, Jie Peng, Hanchao Wang, Mingjian Zhang
papers.abstract: We resolve Erd\H{o}s Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\xi_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1\pi,\;\frac1\pi+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/\pi$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|\xi_0|^{2+\delta}<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$.

papers.title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
papers.abstract:
Following G\'abor Cz\'edli, the \emph{congruence density} of a finite lattice $A$ is $\cd(A)=|\Con A|/2^{|A|-1}$, where $\Con A$ is its congruence lattice and $|A|$ is its number of elements. Cz\'edli proved that density cannot increase under several kinds of sublattice extension and asked whether this holds for every sublattice inclusion.
  For a sublattice $S$ of $L$, we prove the stronger inequality $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. The proof follows congruence labels along the chains into which prime intervals of $S$ split in $L$.
  We also prove that $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ if and only if every element of $L-S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of G. Cz\'edli and L.~Szab\'o relating compatible quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding quasiorder-density results.

papers.title: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
papers.authors: Jinping Li, Yueming Zhong, Yangbiao Zhou
papers.abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials $P\in\Z[T]$ for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over $\Q(x)$ for $k\ge1$. For $R_n(y)\in\Z[y]$ satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to $\Z[y][[x]]$ and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For $q\in \Z$, taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verd\'u--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
papers.abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $\zeta$-function $\zeta_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $\zeta$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

papers.title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
papers.abstract: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

papers.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
papers.abstract:
This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $\pi$.
  We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints.
  We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

papers.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger algebras
papers.abstract: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schr\"odinger algebras to have bracket width one.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.authors: Emily M. Palmer, Anil V. Rao
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. We can generalize the first-order Schreier sets recursively to higher orders, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element $2$ and the index shift of a convolution of the Fibonacci numbers (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4\pi$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current.

papers.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess. spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then $\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0$, with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R}_+,r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
papers.authors: Dongjing Ma, Peihe Wang, Hua Zhu
papers.abstract: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \bar{\sigma}_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)-h, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+\delta, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_\mu}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cot\theta, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<\theta\le\pi/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_\mu\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<\theta<\pi$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

papers.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.authors: Dongjing Ma, Qiqi Zhang, Hua Zhu
papers.abstract:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<\theta<\pi/2$, we consider \[
  \sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)
  =
  f(\xi)h^{p-1}\frac{\rho^{k+1}}{\varphi(\rho)},
  \qquad
  \rho=(h^2+|\nabla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $\nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\bar\sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)=f, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+\delta, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Training artificial neural networks predominantly relies on offline, gradient-based backpropagation algorithms. In contrast, biological circuits process and retain information through decentralized, continuous-time adaptation. In this work, we explore an online, gradient-free learning methodology by formulating the tuning of synaptic weights as a closed-loop trajectory tracking problem driven by model-free control principles. Rather than performing global optimization across static parameters, decentralized controllers adjust synaptic interactions in real-time using solely local input-output tracking errors. We present an exploratory benchmark neural architecture, whose purpose is to assess the dynamic resilience of the proposed approach, particularly in tracking target outputs and adapting to abrupt non-stationarities and structural perturbations (such as topological changes or dynamic dropout) without requiring offline retraining. This empirical preliminary study provides a proof-of-concept for control-theoretic learning paradigms and outlines the foundation for scalable, dynamically evolving connectome frameworks.

papers.title: Adventures in Multi-Omics I: Combining heterogeneous data sets via relationships matrices
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose a covariance based method for combining partial data sets in the genotype to phenotype spectrum. In particular, an expectation-maximization algorithm that can be used to combine partially overlapping relationship/covariance matrices is introduced. Combining data this way, based on relationship matrices, can be contrasted with a feature imputation based approach. We used several public genomic data sets to explore the accuracy of combining genomic relationship matrices. We have also used the heterogeneous genotype/phenotype data sets in the https://triticeaetoolbox.org/ to illustrate how this new method can be used in genomic prediction, phenomics, and graphical modeling.

papers.title: Ensemble Modeling for Time Series Forecasting: an Adaptive Robust Optimization Approach
papers.authors: L\'eonard Boussioux, Henry Mao, Dimitris Bertsimas
papers.abstract: Accurate time-series forecasting is critical for many problems involving temporal data. Ensemble modeling is a well-established technique that leverages multiple predictive models to improve accuracy and robustness, since a single predictor's performance can vary widely due to shifts in the underlying data distribution. This paper proposes a new methodology for building robust ensembles of time series forecasting models. Our approach uses Adaptive Robust Optimization (ARO) to construct a linear regression ensemble whose model weights adapt over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through synthetic experiments covering eight disturbance scenarios, from no drift to abrupt regime shifts, and real-world applications, including air pollution management, energy consumption forecasting, and tropical cyclone intensity forecasting. In the real-world applications, our adaptive ensembles outperform the best ensemble member in hindsight by 16-26% in root mean square error (RMSE) and 14-28% in conditional value at risk at the 15% level and improve over the other ensemble methods we compare on most metrics. In the synthetic experiments, they have lower mean RMSE than a rolling-ridge comparator in seven of the eight scenarios, significantly in four, while an abrupt regime shift that first appears after model selection remains a limitation.

papers.title: Selective Inference for Survey-Weighted Generalized Linear Models: Growing Dimension and Average Marginal Effects
papers.abstract: This paper extends the $\ell_1$-penalized likelihood Selective Inference method to survey settings. We establish its asymptotic validity for generalized linear models with an increasing number of covariates and survey weights, allowing inference on pseudo-true parameters of possibly misspecified selected models. Moreover, we generalize the method to facilitate inference on nonlinear functionals, such as the average marginal effect in survey-weighted logit models. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated using simulated data and the 2020 Canadian Internet Use Survey.

papers.title: Stationarity with Occasionally Binding Constraints
papers.authors: James A. Duffy, Sophocles Mavroeidis, Sam Wycherley
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of multivariate threshold autoregressive models, known as censored and kinked structural vector autoregressions (CKSVAR), which are notably able to accommodate series that are subject to occasionally binding constraints. We develop a set of sufficient conditions for the processes generated by a CKSVAR to be stationary, ergodic, and weakly dependent. Our conditions relate directly to the stability of the deterministic part of the model, and are therefore less conservative than those typically available for general vector threshold autoregressive (VTAR) models. Though our criteria refer to quantities, such as refinements of the joint spectral radius, that cannot feasibly be computed exactly, they can be approximated numerically to a high degree of precision.

papers.title: On the enumeration of signatures of XOR-CNF's
papers.authors: Nadia Creignou, Oscar Defrain, Fr\'ed\'eric Olive, Simon Vilmin
papers.abstract: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_m$ over a set of variables $V$, a truth assignment $\mathbf{a} : V \to \{0, 1\}$ generates a binary sequence $\sigma_\varphi(\mathbf{a})=(C_1(\mathbf{a}), \ldots, C_m(\mathbf{a}))$, called a signature of $\varphi$, where $C_i(\mathbf{a})=1$ if clause $C_i$ evaluates to 1 under assignment $\mathbf{a}$, and $C_i(\mathbf{a})=0$ otherwise. Signatures and their associated generation problems have given rise to new yet promising research questions in algorithmic enumeration. In a recent paper, B\'erczi et al. interestingly proved that generating signatures of a CNF is tractable despite the fact that verifying a solution is hard. They also showed the hardness of finding maximal signatures of an arbitrary CNF due to the intractability of satisfiability in general. Their contribution leaves open the problem of efficiently generating maximal signatures for tractable classes of CNFs, i.e., those for which satisfiability can be solved in polynomial time. Stepping into that direction, we completely characterize the complexity of generating all, minimal, and maximal signatures for XOR-CNFs.

papers.title: Transfer Learning for High-dimensional Quantile Regression with Distribution Shift
papers.authors: Ruiqi Bai, Yijiao Zhang, Hanbo Yang, Zhongyi Zhu
papers.abstract: Information from related source studies can often enhance the findings of a target study. However, the distribution shift between target and source studies can severely impact the efficiency of knowledge transfer. In the high-dimensional regression setting, existing transfer approaches mainly focus on the parameter shift. In this paper, we focus on the high-dimensional quantile regression with knowledge transfer under three types of distribution shift: parameter shift, covariate shift, and residual shift. We propose a novel transferable set and a new transfer framework to address the above three discrepancies. Non-asymptotic estimation error bounds and source detection consistency are established to validate the availability and superiority of our method in the presence of distribution shift. Additionally, an orthogonal debiased approach is proposed for statistical inference with knowledge transfer, leading to sharper asymptotic results. Extensive simulation results as well as real data applications further demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed procedure.

papers.title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
papers.authors: Yilie Huang, Yanwei Jia, Xun Yu Zhou
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.

papers.title: Light Edge Fault Tolerant Graph Spanners
papers.authors: Greg Bodwin, Michael Dinitz, Ama Koranteng, Lily Wang
papers.abstract:
There has recently been significant interest in fault tolerant spanners, which are spanners that still maintain their stretch guarantees after some nodes or edges fail. This work has culminated in an almost complete understanding of the three-way tradeoff between stretch, sparsity, and number of faults tolerated. However, despite some progress in metric settings, there have been no results to date on the tradeoff in general graphs between stretch, lightness, and number of faults tolerated.
  We initiate the study of light edge fault tolerant (EFT) graph spanners, obtaining the first such results. First, we observe that lightness can be unbounded if we use the traditional definition (normalizing by the MST). We then argue that a natural definition of fault-tolerant lightness is to instead normalize by a min-weight fault tolerant connectivity preserver; essentially, a fault-tolerant version of the MST. However, even with this, we show that it is still not generally possible to construct $f$-EFT spanners whose weight compares reasonably to the weight of a min-weight $f$-EFT connectivity preserver.
  In light of this lower bound, it is natural to then consider bicriteria notions of lightness, where we compare the weight of an $f$-EFT spanner to a min-weight $(f' > f)$-EFT connectivity preserver. The most interesting question is to determine the minimum value of $f'$ that allows for reasonable lightness upper bounds. Our main result is a precise answer to this question: $f' = 2f$. In particular, we show that the lightness can be untenably large (roughly $n/k$ for a $k$-spanner) if one normalizes by the min-weight $(2f-1)$-EFT connectivity preserver. But if one normalizes by the min-weight $2f$-EFT connectivity preserver, then we show that the lightness is bounded by just $O(f^{1/2})$ times the non-fault tolerant lightness (roughly $n^{1/k}$, for a $(1+\epsilon)(2k-1)$-spanner).

papers.title: Rectifying Conformity Scores for Better Conditional Coverage
papers.authors: Vincent Plassier, Alexander Fishkov, Victor Dheur, Mohsen Guizani, Souhaib Ben Taieb, Maxim Panov, Eric Moulines
papers.abstract: We present a new method for generating confidence sets within the split conformal prediction framework. Our method performs a trainable transformation of any given conformity score to improve conditional coverage while ensuring exact marginal coverage. The transformation is based on an estimate of the conditional quantile of conformity scores. The resulting method is particularly beneficial for constructing adaptive confidence sets in multi-output problems where standard conformal quantile regression approaches have limited applicability. We develop a theoretical bound that captures the influence of the accuracy of the quantile estimate on the approximate conditional validity, unlike classical bounds for conformal prediction methods that only offer marginal coverage. We experimentally show that our method is highly adaptive to the local data structure and outperforms existing methods in terms of conditional coverage, improving the reliability of statistical inference in various applications.

papers.title: On accuracy of density estimation in generative models based on stochastic optimal control
papers.authors: Nikita Puchkin, Denis Suchkov, Alexey Naumov, Denis Belomestny
papers.abstract: We study the statistical accuracy of Schr\"odinger bridge models based on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference process. Given a known, compactly supported initial distribution and independent samples from an unknown target distribution, we estimate a right Schr\"odinger log-potential by minimizing empirical Kullback-Leibler (KL) risk over a prescribed function class. For bounded sub-Gaussian target densities, potentially with unbounded support, we establish a non-asymptotic high-probability oracle inequality for the KL-divergence between the target and estimated terminal marginals. Under additional two-sided Gaussian bounds and smoothness assumptions on the target log-density, we derive approximation guarantees for sparse ReLU networks and establish a KL convergence rate of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-2s / (2s + d)})$ for exact empirical risk minimization. This matches, up to logarithmic factors, the classical nonparametric KL-risk convergence exponent, while allowing target densities on $\mathbb R^d$ whose tails are controlled by Gaussian envelopes.

papers.title: Non-Wellfounded and Labelled Sequent Calculi for Bimodal Provability Logics
papers.abstract: Bimodal provability logics are modal logics where the two modalities are interpreted as two formal provability predicates of arithmetic theories. We present modular labelled calculi for four different bimodal provability logics, whose rules arise from the relational semantics of these logics, while the second-order property of Noetherianity of models is enforced using techniques from cyclic proof theory. Completeness with respect to the semantics is established via proof search and countermodel construction. We further present regular and finite variants of the calculi via proof transformations.

papers.title: Graph-Cover-based Characterization of the Bethe Partition Function of Double-Edge Factor Graphs
papers.abstract:
For standard factor graphs (S-FGs), whose local functions are nonnegative-real valued, a popular approximation of the partition function is given by the Bethe approximation, which is also known as the Bethe partition function. Vontobel gave a combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function with the help of graph covers. The proof of this characterization heavily relied on the method of types.
  In this paper, we study double-edge factor graphs (DE-FGs), whose local functions are complex valued and satisfy certain positive-semidefinite constraints. DE-FGs and their partition functions are particularly relevant to quantum information processing. Approximating the partition function of a DE-FG is more difficult than approximating the partition function of an S-FG because the DE-FG partition function is a sum of complex values rather than nonnegative-real values.
  We develop a Bethe approximation of the partition function of a DE-FG based on sum-product-algorithm (SPA) fixed points. However, one cannot directly apply the method of types to prove a similar graph-cover-based combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function as in the case of S-FGs.
  Despite this, we establish such a combinatorial characterization for a class of DE-FGs that satisfy an easily checkable condition. Towards proving this characterization, we apply a suitable loop-calculus transform (LCT) to DE-FGs. Originally, the LCT was introduced by Chertkov and Chernyak as a special linear transform for S-FGs and later extended by Mori. Our proposed LCT is applicable to both S-FGs and DE-FGs and generalizes prior versions by handling zero-valued SPA fixed-point message components, which are common in DE-FGs.
  Supported by numerical results, we conjecture that the graph-cover-based combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function holds more broadly for DE-FGs.

papers.title: Data-Driven Exploration for a Class of Continuous-Time Indefinite Linear--Quadratic Reinforcement Learning Problems
papers.abstract: We study reinforcement learning (RL) for a class of continuous-time stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) control problems, where volatilities depend on both states and controls while states are scalar-valued and there are no running control rewards, the last feature also leading to the so-called indefinite LQ controls. We propose a model-free, data-driven exploration mechanism that adaptively adjusts entropy regularization by the critic and policy variance by the actor. Unlike the constant or deterministic exploration schedules employed in the existing literature, which require extensive tuning for implementations and ignore learning progress during iterations, our adaptive exploratory approach boosts learning efficiency with minimal tuning. Despite its flexibility, our method achieves a sublinear regret bound that matches the best-known model-free results for this class of LQ problems, which were previously derived only with fixed exploration schedules. Numerical experiments demonstrate that adaptive explorations accelerate convergence and improve regret performance compared to the non-adaptive model-free and model-based counterparts.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Asset-Liability Management
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for Asset-Liability Management (ALM) by employing continuous-time Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a linear-quadratic (LQ) formulation that incorporates both interim and terminal objectives. We develop a model-free, policy gradient-based soft actor-critic algorithm tailored to ALM for dynamically synchronizing assets and liabilities. To ensure an effective balance between exploration and exploitation with minimal tuning, we introduce adaptive exploration for the actor and scheduled exploration for the critic. Our empirical study evaluates this approach against two enhanced traditional financial strategies, a model-based continuous-time RL method, and three state-of-the-art RL algorithms. Evaluated across 200 randomized market scenarios, our method achieves higher average rewards than all alternative strategies, with rapid initial gains and sustained superior performance. The outperformance stems not from complex neural networks or improved parameter estimation, but from directly learning the optimal ALM strategy without learning the environment.

papers.title: Test-Time Search in Neural Graph Coarsening Procedures for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
papers.authors: Yoonju Sim, Hyeonah Kim, Changhyun Kwon
papers.abstract: The identification of valid inequalities, such as the rounded capacity inequalities (RCIs), is a key component of cutting plane methods for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP). While a deep learning-based separation method can learn to find high-quality cuts, our analysis reveals that the model produces fewer cuts than expected because it is insufficiently sensitive to generate a diverse set of generated subsets. This paper proposes an alternative: enhancing the performance of a trained model at inference time through a new test-time search with stochasticity. First, we introduce stochastic edge selection into the graph coarsening procedure, replacing the previously proposed greedy approach. Second, we propose the Graph Coarsening History-based Partitioning (GraphCHiP) algorithm, which leverages coarsening history to identify not only RCIs but also, for the first time, the Framed capacity inequalities (FCIs). Experiments on randomly generated CVRP instances demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in reducing the dual gap compared to the existing neural separation method. Additionally, our method discovers effective FCIs on a specific instance, despite the challenging nature of identifying such cuts.

papers.title: PAC Reasoning: Controlling the Performance Loss for Efficient Reasoning
papers.authors: Hao Zeng, Jianguo Huang, Bingyi Jing, Hongxin Wei, Bo An
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress in complex problem-solving tasks. Despite this success, LRMs typically suffer from high computational costs during deployment, highlighting a need for efficient inference. A practical direction is to switch the LRM between thinking and non-thinking modes dynamically. However, such approaches often introduce additional reasoning errors and lack statistical guarantees for the performance loss, which are critical for high-stakes applications. In this work, we propose Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) Reasoning that controls the performance loss under the user-specified tolerance. Specifically, we construct an upper confidence bound on the performance loss and determine a threshold for switching to the non-thinking model. Theoretically, using the threshold to switch between the thinking and non-thinking modes ensures bounded performance loss in a distribution-free manner. Our experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method can save computational budgets and control the user-specified performance loss.

papers.title: An Online Multiobjective Policy Gradient for Long-run Average-reward Markov Decision Process
papers.authors: Rahul Misra, Rafa{\l} Wisniewski, Manuela L. Bujorianu
papers.abstract: We propose a policy gradient algorithm for multiobjective decision-making on continuous state spaces, in which the long-run average of a reward vector must be steered into a target set despite an adversarial disturbance, by scalarizing the reward along the direction prescribed by Blackwell's Approachability Theorem instead of tuning weights by trial and error. Existing approachability-based learning is confined to countable state spaces, because the scalarization is updated at the visits to a recurrent state, which on a continuous state space has probability zero. We update it instead at the returns to a set after a minimum number of steps, show that a geometric drift condition, uniform over the policy class, controls the cycle lengths while the policy is being learned, and replace the parallel learners of the existing algorithm by a single two-timescale actor-critic. We show that the distance to the target set is asymptotically bounded by the per-cycle remainder from Blackwell's condition, and decompose this remainder into the errors of the actor, the policy class, the direction tracking and the return set. We illustrate the algorithm on a heating, ventilation, and humidity control problem with adversarial weather and occupancy.

papers.title: A Simulation Framework with Guaranteed Error Bounds for Safety and Fuel-Efficiency Analysis of Vehicle Platoons
papers.abstract: Vehicle platooning is an important technology in modern transportation systems, offering significant improvements in highway traffic efficiency and fuel economy. Achieving coordinated behavior among vehicles in a platoon depends on wireless communication. However, packet losses in wireless communication can create critical safety issues when they occur together with sudden braking. In this paper, we propose a rigorous simulation-based method for studying such safety issues by analyzing the minimum inter-vehicle distance over time across control parameters that guarantee string stability. In particular, our method computes the exact distance at simulation time instants and guarantees that the change in distance between consecutive simulation time instants remains bounded. Therefore, the distances obtained at simulation times are representative of the continuous-time behavior, and the distances between those times can be accurately approximated. Our derivation relies on a lifted state representation and differential inequalities. For the proposed simulation method, we provide two approaches for selecting simulation times to ensure that the error in distance approximation remains within a given bound. We then extend our method to fuel-efficiency analysis, with guaranteed error bounds for calculating the average fuel savings of vehicles. Through an example involving a highway scenario with a merging lane, we demonstrate that among string-stable control parameter settings for a vehicle platoon, some perform better in terms of safety under simultaneous packet losses and sudden braking. We also identify control parameters that result in tradeoffs between safety and average fuel savings in a vehicle platoon.

papers.title: Correcting quantum errors one gradient step at a time
papers.abstract: Probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) lets a recovery fail with some probability, in exchange for higher fidelity when it succeeds. Prior PAQEC code searches keep the codewords orthonormal with penalty terms and tune the code without its best recovery. We propose a gradient method with three new parts. First, the codewords move on the complex Stiefel manifold, so they are orthonormal at every step without penalties. Second, every code is trained against its best recovery, which we solve for at each step rather than learn. Third, a fast Petz recovery that we can differentiate even for symmetric codes gets the search close, and the exact semidefinite program finishes it. We train a single five-qubit code over generalized amplitude damping noise. At weak noise ($\gamma = 0.1$, $p = 0.05$) and equal success probability, it has $23$ times lower infidelity than the permutation-invariant code of prior work, and $9$ times lower than that work's numerically optimized code. At equal fidelity it succeeds $91\%$ of the time, against $76\%$ for the permutation-invariant code.

papers.title: Elementary Quantum Gates from Lie Group Embeddings in $U(2^n)$: Spectral Geometry and Intrinsic Factorization Lengths
papers.authors: Antonio Falco, Daniela Falco-Pomares, Hermann G. Matthies
papers.abstract:
We study intrinsic factorizations of quantum gates using determinant-one unitaries supported on arbitrary two-dimensional subspaces of $\C^N$, where $N=2^n$. For $U\in U(N)$ write $r=\operatorname{rank}(U-I)$. When $r\ge2$, we characterize all factors that lower the active rank by two through traceless compressions of the Cayley transform on $\Ran(U-I)$. For the ordered active eigenangles $\vartheta_j\in(0,2\pi)$, existence is equivalent to $\vartheta_1+\vartheta_2\le2\pi\le\vartheta_{r-1}+\vartheta_r$. For $U\in SU(N)$, combining this construction with eigenangle merging realizes the classical reflection-length formula in two-level form: $\ell^{SU}(U)=\max\{
u(U),r-
u(U)\}$, where $
u(U)$ is the positive eigenangle sum divided by $2\pi$. On the full-rank open set, the age indexes $N-1$ connected components with constant intrinsic length. We place these factorizations within the spectral description of the dictionaries formed by faithful $SU(2)$ and $U(2)$ embeddings. For $n\ge2$, these dictionaries are Haar-null of Hausdorff dimensions $N^2-N+1$ and $N^2-N+2$; the former is compact and the latter dense. Distances to compact sectors reduce to eigenvalue matching. Further results concern ambient minimality of embedded geodesics and a first-order sharp spectral bound on coherence production.

papers.title: Multivariate Multicycle Codes for Complete Single-Shot Decoding
papers.authors: Feroz Ahmed Mian, Owen Gwilliam, Stefan Krastanov
papers.abstract: We introduce multivariate multicycle (MM) codes, a Koszul-complex formulation of abelian multicycle (AMC) codes, which are multidimensional scalar lifted-product codes over a finite abelian group algebra, that unifies bivariate bicycle, multivariate bicycle, abelian two-block group algebra, generalized bicycle, trivariate tricycle, and toric codes. MM codes are Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes defined from length-$(t+1)$ chain complexes, and for $t\geq4$ they possess metachecks for both types of checks, which can be used for single-shot decoding. We offer a framework that facilitates the construction of long-length chain complexes through the use of the Koszul complex. In particular, obtaining explicit boundary maps (parity check and metacheck matrices) is particularly straightforward in our approach. We also determine when an MM code encodes logical qubits, count the independent check relations not generated by its metachecks, and show that middle-degree codes with even $t$ have equal $X$ and $Z$ distances. This simple but very general parameterization of codes permitted us to efficiently perform a numerical search, where we identify several MM code candidates with high rates and high code distances. Examples of new codes with parameters $[[n,k,d]]$ include $[[96,12,8]]$, $[[144,12,12]]$, $[[486,24,12]]$, $[[630,70,9]]$, and $[[648,60,9]]$. For selected codes, we report confinement profiles and study single-shot and few-shot decoding under phenomenological and circuit-level noise. Our codes also include explicit collapsed 5D through 9D instances, and our 5D instances have check weights lower than those of recent small instances of quantum Tanner codes.

papers.title: Distribution-free certificate of similarity between distributions with blurred total variation distance
papers.abstract: Classical two-sample tests aim to determine whether two distributions are equal or not based on samples from each one. Even in an distribution-free setting, well-known methods such as the permutation test can provide statistical evidence that the two distributions differ. However, failure to reject equality does not necessarily establish that they are similar. In this work, we study the complementary problem of certifying distributional similarity with finite-sample confidence, without imposing assumptions on the underlying distributions. We show, however, that for continuous distributions, any distribution-free upper confidence bound on the total variation (TV) distance must be trivial with high probability, even if the distributions are identical. Thus, certifying similarity in TV with a distribution-free guarantee is practically impossible. We therefore examine the blurred TV distance, a relaxation of TV distance that enables us to quantify similarity after applying a common blurring operation while retaining the interpretation of TV. We construct distribution-free upper and lower confidence bounds on blurred TV, establish their finite-sample validity, and examine its properties in high dimensions.

papers.title: What Does Machine Learning Learn from Numerical Calabi--Yau Geometry? A Controlled Study on the Fermat Quintic
papers.abstract: We study polynomial regression of numerical metric errors on the Fermat quintic. A known hypersurface volume-ratio identity gives the exact reference $C-\log p_4$ relative to the induced Fubini--Study metric, where $p_4=\sum_i|z_i|^8$ on unit-normalized homogeneous coordinates. We optimize algebraic metrics at degrees $6,8,10,12$ while preserving finite Fermat symmetry, then fit their remaining logarithmic volume-form error. Regression splits and bootstrap draws keep the five roots of each sampled line together, with all compared teachers evaluated on common clouds. Warm-start replication correlations exceed $0.9997$ at $k=8,10,12$. Across degrees, source-derived modes fall short of target-specific fits, including in a post-hoc quartic check, but outperform random spans of matched rank in the tested libraries. Two independent random-invariant $k=10$ starts have residual correlations $0.768$--$0.803$, while their fitted cubic modes correlate at $0.979$--$0.983$ and retain useful calibrated cross-start prediction. Their fitted modes agree poorly with those of the principal warm-start teacher. Adding the phase-sensitive invariant $J_7$ improves prediction beyond the cubic modulus-only library for all seven warm-start teachers. The gain depends on the library: at $k=12$, a quartic modulus-only fit explains about 97--98\% of residual variance and the conditional interval for the added $J_7$ gain includes zero for both replicas under both measures. The gains therefore establish neither phase independence nor irreducible phase necessity; fixed-baseline augmentation preserves this distinction. The fitted components depend on the numerical protocol; global optimality and a universal finite-degree correction remain unestablished.

papers.title: Allure of Craquelure: A Variational-Generative Approach to Crack Detection in Paintings
papers.authors: Laura Paul, Holger Rauhut, Martin Burger, Samira Kabri, Tim Roith
papers.abstract: Recent advances in imaging technologies, deep learning and numerical performance have enabled non-invasive detailed analysis of artworks, supporting their documentation and conservation. In particular, automated detection of craquelure in digitized paintings is crucial for assessing degradation and guiding restoration, yet remains challenging due to the possibly complex scenery and the visual similarity between cracks and crack-like artistic features such as brush strokes or hair. We propose a hybrid approach that models crack detection as an inverse problem, decomposing an observed image into a crack-free painting and a crack component. A deep generative model is employed as powerful prior for the underlying artwork, while crack structures are captured using a Mumford--Shah-type variational functional together with a crack prior. Joint optimization yields a pixel-level map of crack localizations in the painting.

papers.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
papers.authors: Xavier Bekaert, Yannick Herfray, Lea Mele, No\'emie Parrini
papers.abstract: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincar\'{e} subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.

papers.title: Constrained and Composite Sampling via Proximal Sampler
papers.abstract:
We study two log-concave sampling problems: constrained sampling and composite sampling. First, we consider sampling from a distribution proportional to $e^{-f}$ on a convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, where $f$ is convex. Using an epigraph lifting, we reduce this problem to uniform sampling up to a one-dimensional exponential tilt over a convex set in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$. We then apply the proximal sampler to the lifted distribution. We develop an unbiased implementation of its restricted Gaussian oracle by using the cutting-plane method and rejection sampling, requiring only a separation oracle for $K$ and evaluation and subgradient oracles for $f$, without relying on projections or barrier functions.
  Second, we study composite sampling from $e^{-f-h}$, where $f$ and $h$ are closed and convex. This structure arises naturally in Bayesian inference, where $f$ represents data fidelity and $h$ encodes prior information. By applying an epigraph lifting to $h$, we reduce composite sampling to constrained sampling in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$, allowing us to build on the approach developed in the first part. This leads to a double lifting formulation in $\mathbb R^{d+2}$, for which we implement the proximal sampler using different combinations of subgradient and proximal oracles for $f$ and $h$. We establish mixing time bounds in R\'enyi and $\chi^2$ divergences for both problems.
  Finally, we revisit the convergence analysis of the proximal sampler from a variational perspective. Starting from variational formulations of its two half-steps as optimization problems over probability measures, we use a dynamic formulation of entropy-regularized optimal transport to recast them as optimal control problems. This allows us to derive their governing PDEs directly through the lens of optimization, without first analyzing particle-level SDEs.

papers.title: Exact Algorithms for Edge Deletion to Cactus
papers.abstract: We study two related problems on simple, un-directed graphs: Edge Deletion to Cactus and Spanning Tree to Cactus. Edge Deletion to Cactus has been known to be NP-hard on general graphs at least since 1988. We show improved exact algorithms for the former and a polynomial time algorithm for the latter.

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.authors: Hans Riess, Yujun Huang, Matthew Klawonn, Gioele Zardini, Matthew Hale
papers.abstract: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

papers.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry protected boundary modes in two-dimensional Potts paramagnets
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a class of one-dimensional boundary Hamiltonians arising from two-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases with $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry on a triangular lattice. Using a cohomology-based transformation, the lattice models for the edge modes are explicitly obtained, and their structure is shown to be governed by the arithmetic properties of $N$. For prime $N$, the boundary theory admits a formulation in terms of mutually commuting Temperley-Lieb algebras. For the composite values of $N$, the models exhibit hierarchical or factorized structures. We demonstrate that the phases can be understood in terms of primary models augmented by local defect degrees of freedom that partition the system into independent segments. Finally, the global symmetry is realized on the boundary in a non-on-site and anomalous manner, directly realizing the corresponding 't Hooft anomaly.

papers.title: The Gaussian data assumption does not always lead to the largest Cram\'er-Rao bound
papers.abstract: This lecture note addresses the common misconception that the Gaussian distribution always yields the largest Cram\'er-Rao Bound (CRB). We show that this property only holds under restrictive conditions: specifically, when the mean and covariance parameters are decoupled in the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), when the parameter of interest lies in the mean vector and when there are no additive nuisance parameters. Beyond this framework, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that non-Gaussian distributions can produce larger CRB.

papers.title: Stabilization of finite-energy grid states of a quantum harmonic oscillator by reservoir engineering with two dissipation channels
papers.authors: R\'emi Robin, Pierre Rouchon, Lev-Arcady Sellem
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze an experimentally accessible Lindblad master equation for a quantum harmonic oscillator, simplifying a previous proposal to alleviate implementation constraints. It approximately stabilizes periodic grid states introduced in 2001 by Gottesman, Kitaev and Preskill (GKP), with applications for quantum error correction and quantum metrology. We obtain explicit estimates for the energy of the solutions of the Lindblad master equation. We estimate the convergence rate to the codespace when stabilizing a GKP qubit, and numerically study the effect of noise. We then present simulations illustrating how a modification of parameters allows preparing states of metrological interest in steady-state.

papers.title: Structural interpretability in SVMs with truncated orthogonal polynomial kernels
papers.authors: V\'ictor Soto-Larrosa, Nuria Torrado, Edmundo J. Huertas
papers.abstract: Support vector machines (SVMs) can yield classifiers with similar predictive performance but different internal structures, particularly in the contributions of individual explanatory variables and their interactions. We introduce Orthogonal Representation Contribution Analysis (ORCA), a post-training methodology for SVMs constructed from tensor products of truncated Christoffel--Darboux kernels. The associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) admits a finite orthonormal polynomial basis in which the regularized component of the fitted decision function has an exact expansion. Squared expansion coefficients induce an additive decomposition of its squared RKHS norm. Based on this representation, normalized Orthogonal Kernel Contribution (OKC) indices quantify the fractions of the squared RKHS norm associated with total polynomial degrees, interaction orders, and input-variable contributions, both individually and through interactions of arbitrary order. ORCA summarizes these indices through joint structural maps, variable-specific displays, and comparisons of fitted classifiers. A controlled quartet of classification problems illustrates substantial structural differences under matched predictive performance. A double-spiral experiment compares five Jacobi kernels, while an application to the Vertebral Column data illustrates the method after cross-validated model selection. ORCA provides a quantitative characterization of the internal structure of fitted SVMs, revealing differences that may remain undetected by standard predictive performance metrics.

papers.title: Kill-Probability-Maximization Guidance: Breaking from the Miss-Distance-Minimization Paradigm
papers.abstract: Classical guidance laws aim at minimizing the miss distance, thus implicitly determining the minimum warhead lethality radius required against nominal targets. However, nonnominal targets or scenarios might render the designed warhead insufficient, causing a significant degradation in the single-shot kill probability (SSKP). We propose a guidance methodology that shifts the interceptor's objective from minimizing the miss distance to directly maximizing the SSKP, while taking into account the warhead's probabilistic lethality model. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the paradigm presented here modifies deterministic differential-game-based guidance laws using Bayesian decision theory. For this purpose, we obtain the saddle-point solution of the deterministic differential game whose objective is the SSKP. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate substantial SSKP improvement over the standard and recently introduced estimation-aware guidance laws, when tested against nominal and nonnominal evasively maneuvering targets.

papers.title: Layer-wise Geometric Approximation Rates for Deep Networks
papers.authors: Shijun Zhang, Zuowei Shen, Yuesheng Xu
papers.abstract: Depth is widely viewed as a central contributor to the success of deep neural networks, yet standard approximation results typically give error bounds only for the final output of a network. Inspired by classical multiscale expansions and multigrade deep learning, we give depth a scale-dependent interpretation by constructing a single network whose intermediate readouts approximate the target at successively finer scales. For any $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$ with $1\le p <\infty$ and any integer $N\ge2$, we construct a single network of width $3dN+2d+4$ with the same activation pattern in every hidden layer, using sine in the first two neurons and $\mathtt{ReLU}$ in the rest. For every $\ell\ge0$, the $L^p$ approximation error of the readout $\Phi_\ell$ at layer $\ell+4$ is bounded by $(2d+1)\omega_{f,p}(N^{-\ell})$, where $\omega_{f,p}$ denotes the $L^p$ translation modulus of $f$. Under the H\"older condition $\omega_{f,p}(t)\le Ct^\alpha$ with $C>0$ and $0< \alpha \le 1$, this estimate yields the geometric bound $(2d+1)C N^{-\alpha\ell}$.
